author: ymote
body:
The 14th runtime sweep. It pins makepad `main` d653bc44, Octoscript-Makepad 6cf2d90a (OSM #82 and #83) and App Hub 40abb23b (App Hub #191). It also carries the end of the per-app Splash runtime gates, under the ruling of 8 October 2026 (#450).

## What the runtime change means
- **makepad#117**: the isolate policy no longer gates an app's URLs, media, sockets or instruction budget. `network.hosts`, `images`, `web` and the budget become declarations.
- **makepad#118**: the runtime no longer refuses a `host.request` for a family the app did not declare. This is option (c), which the product owner confirmed directly. Nothing replaces it in App Hub's dispatcher. A host service that needs a grant checks it itself: the device service checks the app's grant and the person's device consent for every camera, microphone and location call, and the model (`Code::Capability`), audio, files, glance, device calendar, wasm and Gmail event services and the script-app tool executor check theirs. By a source read, mail, news and calendar have no check of their own. (Corrected after merge: an earlier version of this text listed model among them.)
- **What stays:** the storage jail, inert password fields, and the runtime's own checks on location, saved lists, the camera preview and `agent.notify`.
- **makepad#110–#116**: renderer, Android, Linux and TextFlow work.
- **App Hub #191:**
  - a runaway app tool handler still fails at once, through a captured-error sink;
  - `net` alone hands an isolate its network module;
  - it brings #186 (components under `wasm-components-v1`), #188 (`wasi:http` and `octosense:host` admission) and #190 (shared components) to this pin.

## The runtime overlay
The overlay is rebased from 32d6415f onto d653bc44: 34 patches, tree 0e7e0dac. `makepad-map-script-api.patch` is dropped, since makepad#113 merged it. Resolved by hand:
- **Settings patch, Android IME.** Upstream now defers `HideTextIME` (`pending_ime_hide`). `ShowTextIME` still skips a dismissed keyboard and publishes a new editor session, and now also cancels a pending hide. `HideTextIME` publishes the editor before deferring.
- **Settings patch, GL program cache.** The validation state (NeedsValidation, Supported, Disabled, and the probe of a fresh export) is applied to upstream's rewritten cache functions (`program_cache_path`, driver-keyed names).
- **`host-json-boundary` and `host-response-json`.** The capability pre-check they edited is gone. The raw-envelope test drops its refusal mode, because the runtime no longer builds that envelope.
- **`host-api-runtime-fixes`.** Its nested-callback test now has the host refuse the location sample.
- **`device-consent`.** It still adds `set_device_consent` next to `set_policy`. Its consent check in `service_allowed` still guards the runtime's own reads. Host methods are guarded by the device service.

## Other changes
- `video-api-smoke` no longer expects the runtime to refuse an unlisted URL.
- The host API lab's native acceptance (`desktop.yml native-host-api`):
  - a background location sample without consent is refused by App Hub's dispatcher (a foreground-only method from a background surface);
  - an undeclared microphone recording from a tool call is refused the same way (in the foreground, the audio service refuses it). Either refusal passes.
- Docs naming the release are updated: `phone/docs/build-tool.md`, `phone/docs/makepad-fork.md`, and the architecture and Mail docs' pins. `rom/docs/home-build.md` follows in its own PR, because a ROM path would need the two-run local gate. Dated evidence is untouched.

## Checks
- `cargo test -p makepad-widgets --lib` on the overlay: 319 passed and 5 failed. The 5 fail identically on plain makepad `main`.
- `cargo check --target aarch64-linux-android -p makepad-widgets` passes. The OpenHarmony check needs DevEco's C toolchain for `ring` and was not run.
- `python3 tools/setup.py --check --cargo` and `python3 tools/native_apps.py --check` pass.
- Local CI (`tools/ci-local.sh --only apps,desktop,phone --linux-host --offload`):
  - at a772b370: PASSED;
  - at d653bc44: one failure, the native lab text described above, now fixed (`tools/test-host-api-native.py` passes);
  - on this exact head: running, and I'll merge with `tools/ci-local-merge.sh` when it passes.

**Not run:** a phone or other device, Windows outside CI, and OpenHarmony.

author: tfausak
body:
- **What/why:** finishes the slot-reader consolidation #4906 started, so one map of what each slot names feeds every `Filter.Context`. Closes #4907
  - **One recipient map, one filler.** `Binding.recipientsBySlot` gives every recipient a slot names: targets of any count, group members as objects, and a key for every slot the environment bound. `Projection.framedBySlots` derives every slot field from it (objects, players, names, controllers, creature types, toughness, host controllers). So a slot holding only a player, an "up to" slot answered with none, or a slot CR 608.2b emptied answers an empty set, and `SameControllerAsBound` / `SharesCreatureTypeWithBound` refuse there. Only a slot nobody has answered yet widens.
  - **Routed through it:**
    - `Target.slotContext`, `Resolve.Slots.effectContext`, both intervening "if" checks and `Event.Match`'s bearer context.
    - `Mana`'s priced count.
    - The `Replacement` rows, `candidateContext` and `matchesPermanent`.
    - `Cost`'s pools. `Cost`'s slot map (40 signatures, plus the gate callers in `Cast`, `Activatable`, `Activate` and `Resolve.Effect`) now carries recipients rather than objects, so a cost criterion sees the announcement's player targets too. The board-blind `Filter.contextWithSlots` / `contextCrewing` are deleted in favour of `Projection.contextWithSlots`.
  - **`ModifyTarget`'s `each` re-frames.** The per-object freeze goes through `Resolve.Slots.effectContextNaming`, so the narrowed slot's names and toughness follow the one object. Before, only `slotObjects` was overridden.
  - **One exhaustive slot walk.** `Filter.overBoundSlotsWith` reports each slot with the arity its atom reads it at, and has no fallthrough. `boundSlots`, `renameBound`, `singularSlots` and `slotArities` all derive from it. `Resolve.Slots.filterSlotsOf` (the arity lint, nested `Count` filters included) and `CardSpec`'s clash lint both read it, so a filter reading a multi-target slot whole (`IsBound`) no longer offends. CLAUDE.md item 4 no longer lists `overBoundSlots` as a fallthrough site.
- **CR:** 601.2c, 603.4 / 608.2a, 608.2b, 603.7c, 701.10b, 110.2, 208.1.
- **Design calls:**
  - Each producer keeps its own slot map, and that is the only difference between them: announced (`Target`, intervening "if", `Cost`), legal (`effectContext`), captured (replacement rows, delayed triggers), paid (`Mana`).
  - Replacement rows still capture objects only (`ActiveReplacement.slots`), an elision the `slotPlayers` field's own note already records with its query. Widening it means a codec and game-state change.
  - `Activatable`'s payability aiming is still object-only (`recipientObjects`), as before.
  - `ControlledByBound` is read as one (`matches` answers only `Just [pid]`).
  - Item (2) is unchanged and deliberate: `boundDeparts` / `LoseControlOfBound` read a single object, a clash lint enforces that at load, and the pool's users (Ray of Command, The Deck of Many Things, Whippoorwill) are all single. No AtomicCards hit on 2026-10-09 for "when … those creatures die/leave" or "lose control of those/them". (e), the four single-object helpers over the whole-slot reader, changes what a group or a mixed slot answers, so it is filed separately as #4911.
- **Verified:** suite 13140 -> 13143 at the pre-merge head; 13143 again after merging origin/main (#4909), answered-empty mutation re-run red there. Mutations:
  - Slot keys naming no object dropped from `framedBySlots`' derived fields: TargetSpec "a slot holding bob refuses bob's Piker, so does a slot answered with none, and an unanswered slot admits it", expected `(True,True,True) == (False,False,True)` (re-run at 43768bc40).
  - Answered-empty keying dropped in `recipientsBySlot`: TargetSpec "… so does a slot answered with none …", expected `(False,True,True) == (False,False,True)`.
  - Players filtered out in `Projection.contextWithSlots`, with the now-empty key DROPPED (`Map.filter (not . Set.null)`; keeping it empty would stay green): TargetSpec "a pool whose slot holds bob refuses bob's Piker, and one with no such slot admits it", expected `(True,True) == (False,True)`.
  - `effectContextNaming` narrowing removed: TargetSpec "bob's Piker shares the narrowed Piker's name and bob's Giant does not", expected `(True,True) == (True,False)`.
  - `IsBound` walked at One: AbilitySlotLintSpec "a two-target slot read whole by a filter does not offend".
  - `filterSlotsOf` all-One: same assertion.
  - `ToughnessLessThanBound` emptied: "but one a filter reads as one object does".
  - `IsControllerOfBound` emptied: EffectLintSpec "a singular read inside a filter is caught".
  - Routing:
    - `candidateContext` slots emptied: DamageReplacementSpec "the Wall is gone as the fight's own resolution ends".
    - `Match` bearer bindings emptied: scenario "CR 400.7h …", `{"Life":{"player":"bob","life":16}}` failed; it was 20.
    - Cost pool slots emptied: ConjureSpec "both Calims stay in alice's graveyard".
  - The a–c tests are direct context tests, because no pool card writes these atoms at those positions. `Mana`'s priced route was not mutated.
- **Item-4 sites:** `overBoundSlots` is now exhaustive, so a new `Filter` constructor is compile-forced there. Deleted builders: every caller rewritten. Record updates `{Filter.slotObjects = …}` remaining: FilterSpec's pure context only (the `freezeFor` override is gone). `framedBySlots` writes every slot field, so no update can leave one stale.
- **Rules core cases on effect identity:** no.
- **Deferred:** #4911 (see above).

Automated, unattended Scout-mode pass by AIExpert, covering developments since the ledger's last scan (2026-09-17) through today (2026-10-10).

## What was added

**Ledger (4 new dated entries, each independently verified against primary sources where possible):**
- **Claude Code reads AGENTS.md natively** (v2.1.277, 2026-09-18) — verified directly against Anthropic's current docs. The two biggest coding-agent ecosystems (Claude, OpenAI/Codex) now read the same project-instruction file by default.
- **Claude Agent SDK caps subagent fan-out by default** — spawn depth lowered from 5 to 1, concurrency capped at 20 (verified directly from the SDK's own changelog). Self-referential: this is the exact mechanism AIExpert uses to delegate research.

Logged at deliberately low durability (same treatment as the prior model-wave entry) since most detail beyond Opus 5.5 rests on secondary sourcing, not a direct primary fetch.
- **Anthropic's three-tier Cyber Verification Program** (2026-10-06) — consolidates "Project Glasswing" into vetted Defense/Red Team/Specialized Access tiers for dual-use security capabilities.

**Playbook (2 new entries — the priority deliverable):**
- `unify-cross-tool-instructions-via-agents-md` — write project instructions once as AGENTS.md instead of once per vendor.
- `cap-subagent-fan-out-by-default` — design multi-agent workflows around the SDK's new default caps rather than assuming unlimited recursive delegation.

These are noted as open follow-ups in the relevant ledger entries' Status lines rather than asserted as fact.

No changes to `.claude/agents/ai-expert.md` or any governing instructions. No new tools/permissions granted. No merge — left for human review per the unattended-run publishing policy.

author: ceoloide
body:
## Problem and outcome

After #956 improved the circular-keepout approximation, the original false clearance violations in #954 were resolved, but inserting a trace around the refined obstacle could still fail. The spring-over routine could return a physically safe detour that the insertion checker rejected, leaving the board unchanged. A separate restriction also prevented detours around large convex keepouts when the search tree divided them into several sections.

This PR makes those detours insert successfully while retaining the refined circle geometry and the existing clearance checks. It addresses the [post-merge insertion report](https://github.com/freerouting/freerouting/issues/954#issuecomment-6086951498) and the request to test routing around the new geometry, not just its initial DRC result.

## What I found and changed

### 1. Rounded offsets could consume the detour's safety gap

Spring-over expands an obstacle to leave room for the trace and its required clearance. Previously, it combined the trace half-width and one half-clearance in a single expansion, then applied the second half-clearance. The insertion checker constructs its geometry with separately rounded expansions. Those operations are not interchangeable: `Line.translate` rounds the displacement along a coordinate axis.

For one reproduced tangent direction, `(-1951, 9808)`, with trace half-width 750 and half-clearance 1008, the old detour displacement and the checker's combined displacements both became 2821 internal units. The intended one-unit guard had disappeared. The shapes touched, so insertion rejected the path even though its analytical circle clearance was sufficient. The recursive spring-over check could still return that path because its centreline had no entrance points into the offset obstacle.

For non-octagonal tile shapes in the uncompensated branch, I now expand by half-clearance twice, then by trace half-width plus the existing one-unit guard. Keeping width separate preserves the separating gap through the rounded translations.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    A[Refined convex obstacle] --> B[Expand by half-clearance]
    B --> C[Expand by half-clearance again]
    C --> D[Expand by trace half-width plus one-unit guard]
    D --> E[Apply routing angle restriction]
    E --> F[Build detour and insert through existing checks]
```

The original report reproduced unrestricted angles, but a thinner trace also exposed the problem in 45-degree mode. The repair therefore happens before the bounding-octagon or bounding-box conversion used by restricted-angle routing. Existing box/octagon offsets and the compensated offset branch retain their established behavior.

### 2. Several index sections do not necessarily mean a non-convex obstacle

The spatial index partitions sufficiently large obstacles for efficient queries. A 6 mm circular keepout exercises that partitioning in the issue fixture, even though the whole keepout remains convex. Spring-over previously rejected any area with more than one search-tree shape.

For a partitioned `ObstacleArea`, the routine now obtains the area's convex decomposition. Only when it contains exactly one part does it recover that whole shape, apply the same compensation used before indexing, and construct the detour. Concave areas and areas with holes remain rejected by this fallback; using one index section or the outer hull would misrepresent their geometry.

The production change is confined to `TraceShover`. It does not change the circle approximation, spatial-index partitioning, global line rounding, clearance thresholds, or routing order.

## Regression coverage and edge cases

`Issue954CircularKeepoutInsertionTest` adds **75 cases** using the existing issue DSN. Positive cases require insertion to reach the requested endpoint, actual copper to exist, and end-to-end connectivity. They run comprehensive DRC through `DesignRulesChecker.getAllClearanceViolations()` before and after normalization and pull-tight. Circular cases also measure segment-to-circle clearance independently and check angle restrictions.

These assertions matter: an insertion that adds nothing can still leave a board with zero violations.

| Cases | Coverage and purpose |
| --- | --- |
| 60 circular detours | Unrestricted, 45-degree and 90-degree routing; both travel directions; 5 mm and partitioned 6 mm keepouts; three trace widths; central and offset approaches. |
| 3 oblique circular detours | 7°, 22° and 73° approaches; small and odd clearances (17, 2001, 3017 internal units); half-widths down to one unit. Exercises rounding-sensitive combinations. |
| 3 asymmetric convex polygons | The same oblique/clearance combinations on non-circular geometry, including partitioned shapes. |
| 1 partitioned rectangle | Verifies recovery of a whole convex obstacle also works for the established rectangular geometry path. |
| 1 pair of consecutive circles | Exercises recursive detouring and subsequent cleanup around more than one obstacle. |
| 3 circular copper areas | Same-net, foreign-net blocking, and foreign-net non-blocking behavior; traversable copper must not force a detour. |
| 4 negative controls | A genuinely invalid via clearance remains rejected on both copper layers; an endpoint inside the keepout inserts no copper; concave and explicitly holed obstacles are not treated as one convex shape. |

With `TraceShover` restored to upstream, **40 of the earlier 63 regression cases failed**. The final expanded candidate suite passes all 75. I also ran balanced and adversarial reviews. They prompted broader geometry coverage and identified a test-setup defect: component-owned keepouts could not be removed as the concave test assumed. That test now omits them before DSN loading and verifies both the obstacle inventory and the identity of the rejected obstacle. A mutation check confirmed it fails if the one-convex-part guard is relaxed. Supplemental sweeps passed 420 circular detour queries and 216 asymmetric-polygon insertions.

## Routing comparisons and downstream effects

I compared the candidate with upstream `853ce4f2` and stable v2.5.0 using identical explicit settings, one routing worker, and fresh user-data directories. The upstream comparator used the candidate executable with only `TraceShover` replaced by its upstream class, isolating this patch. The stable comparator used the v2.5.0 binary.

| Board / checkpoint | Upstream unrouted / DRC | Candidate unrouted / DRC | v2.5.0 unrouted / DRC |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Issue230, 10 routed items, repeated twice | 140 / 6 | 140 / 6 | 140 / 6 |
| Issue230, 25 routed items, repeated twice | 128 / 6 | 128 / 6 | 127 / 6 |
| DAC2020 BM02, routing plus one bounded optimizer pass | 0 / 0 | 0 / 0 | 0 / 0 |

Issue230 has 28 circular keepouts and starts with six fixed pin-to-pin violations. No comparison added violations. Candidate and upstream SES outputs were byte-identical at both repeated checkpoints and after BM02 optimization. The one-connection difference from v2.5.0 at 25 items already exists upstream. BM02 reached the same final optimizer score, 763.33, on all three versions. Additional matched DAC2020 BM01 and Corney Island Wireless checks preserved fanout board hashes and clearance counts; Corney Island Wireless completed with zero unrouted connections and zero violations.

The additional expansion allocates one temporary shape when this non-octagonal spring-over branch is used. Timings show no established performance trend: Issue230 candidate/upstream routing wall times were 4.99–5.19/5.36–5.56 seconds at 10 items and 8.29–8.47/8.30–8.40 at 25 items. BM02 candidate/upstream routing and optimizer times were 3.44/3.13 and 0.98/0.80 seconds respectively. Measured stage peak heaps remained below 150 MB. These are bounded comparisons, not a speedup or corpus-wide equivalence claim.

Normalization, pull-tight, net ownership, and copper-area obstacle flags are covered because a usable initial detour alone is insuffi

author: boadij
body:
Fixes #311
Fixes #338

## Summary

Prevent queued supervision messages from disappearing before Pi records their delivery, and keep Herdr pane identity aligned with the verified Manager role. Both fixes reuse existing coordination, session-history, and metadata contracts; no new persistent state or transport.

## Changes

- **Receipt-gated delivery:** Keep inbox records until the exact message is present in the recipient's complete Pi session history. Recheck after asynchronous authorization and before submission to avoid duplicate delivery; retain existing quarantine, lease, and generation safeguards.
- **Safe retries:** Suppress resubmission while Pi is busy or has pending messages. Retry an unreceipted message only when idle, after 1 second following settlement or a conservative 30-second fallback if Pi never emits `agent_settled`. Clear per-message tracking after acceptance or rejection.
- **Authorization:** Retain records when Manager/scope verification is inconclusive; continue rejecting definitively invalid assignments, identities, or lease generations.
- **Herdr identity:** Reassert Manager metadata after verified session restoration, clear obsolete Lead tokens, ignore stale queued reports, and record publication failures without affecting role authority. Reset error deduplication after a successful report.
- **Regression coverage:** Add receipt/authorization-race, retry-and-pending-message, stale-authority, Manager restoration, and metadata failure → success → failure checks to existing tests.

## Validation

Reported for follow-up HEAD `95566425aff24a6e067ef9a94d7b13b72ff4f8d9`:
- `npm test -- extension/supervision.test.ts` — passed
- `npm test -- extension/controller-api.test.ts` — passed
- `npm test -- extension/commands.test.ts` — passed
- `npm test -- extension/extension-contract.test.ts` — passed
- `npm run smoke -- manager-recovery` — passed
- `npm run check` — **926 passed, 0 failed, 1 skipped**
- `git diff --check` — passed

GitHub Actions **Validate** workflow at this HEAD also passed, including Ubuntu, macOS, Windows, package, and container jobs. External Review #2 found no merge-blocking issues; that review did not independently rerun the local test or smoke commands.

## Guarantees and limits

`message_staff` success acknowledges durable **enqueue**, not receipt. Inbox consumption now requires the recipient's persisted Pi message. Delivery remains recoverable rather than distributed exactly-once: the 30-second fallback (and crash recovery) can replay a message if Pi persists it unusually late. Herdr metadata remains best-effort presentation and never determines Manager authority.

The fixes address confirmed code defects, but do **not** conclusively establish the cause of the October 8, 2026 live incident.

## Summary

author: joeblau
body:
## Summary

Barge-in (#37) already marked a cut-short agent reply in the UI, but only in memory. After a relaunch, in history, in exports and on other devices the reply looked complete. This PR stores the mark.

- **SchemaV3 (3.0.0).** A copy of `SchemaV2` with one new optional attribute, `Utterance.endReasonRaw: String?`. It holds an `UtteranceEndReason` raw value: `interrupted` (the user said something new or continued their utterance), `bargedin` (barge-in) or `stopped` (the conversation was stopped mid-reply). It follows the pattern on main: copies of the `SchemaV2+*.swift` files, `BlauMigrationPlan.migrateV2toV3` as a `.lightweight` stage, and `CurrentSchema` moved to v3. `CloudKitCompatibility` already checks every schema in the plan and every step for additive-only changes, so the new tests use it for v3.
- **Writing the mark.** `TurnOrchestrator.abandon` marks every utterance it adds to `interruptedAgentUtterances` through a new **required** method, `TurnTranscriptRecording.markInterrupted(_:reason:)`. It is required so a wrapper can't drop the mark by falling back to a default. The mark goes on the same serial queue as the transcript writes, after the write of the heard part. It is written again after `conversation.item.truncated`, because when too little was heard to keep a whole word, that later write is the first one that stores the row. `ConversationStore.markEnded(utteranceID:reason:)` does the write, batched like a commit. Re-committing the row keeps the mark. `FeedingTranscriptRecorder`, `TopicTrackingTranscript`, `PersistenceTranscriptRecorder` and `ReplayTranscriptTap` all pass it on.
- **Reading the mark.**
  - The chat transcript and timeline history read it through `ChatLine.isInterrupted` (from `StoredUtterance.isInterrupted`). A line the app just recorded keeps the stored mark when it replaces the stored line.
  - The time-based rule still runs as the fallback for unmarked rows: rows stored before v3 or written by an older app version.
  - The Markdown exports (#78 conversation and topic renderers, Export Conversations, `Conversations.md` in Export All Data) end a cut reply with ` — *interrupted*`.
  - Export All Data's JSON gets an optional `endReason`. The key is left out when there's no mark, so the format version stays 1.
- **Docs.**
  - `docs/realtime.md`: Barge-in → "Not stored yet" is now "Stored", with a table of the reasons and the release requirement.
  - `docs/data-model.md`: new Schema v3 section, ER diagram, store API table, versioning steps, history and migration tests.
  - `docs/chat.md`, `docs/export.md`, `docs/privacy.md`, `docs/release.md` (the `CD_endReasonRaw` field, schema version 3.0.0 in the release history), `docs/sync.md` (new manual step 12) and the fixtures README.

> **Before release (manual, owner):** deploy the v3 schema to the CloudKit **production** environment before shipping any build that contains this change. The only change is one new field, `CD_endReasonRaw` (String), on `CD_Utterance`. Use the "Production schema deploy checklist" in `docs/release.md`, then set `BLAU_CLOUDKIT_PRODUCTION_SCHEMA` to `3.0.0`. Until then, upload runs of the release workflow fail at `release.py schema`.

Closes #160

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] A reply cut off by barge-in or by a new utterance is still shown as interrupted **after a relaunch**. Verified by tests on the Mac: `aBargedInReplyIsStillInterruptedAfterARelaunch` cuts a reply through the real `ConversationStore` on disk, reopens the store file and builds the chat rows from the store alone, with no live set. No user line follows the reply, so the time-based rule can't be what marks it.
- [ ] …and **on a second device**. The field syncs with the row and the chat reads it, but CloudKit sync between two devices was not tested (see below).
- [x] A v2 store migrates with no data loss (migration test). `MigrationV2toV3Tests` covers a checked-in `Fixtures/SchemaV2/Blau.store` and a store written during the test.
- [x] `docs/realtime.md` → Barge-in → "Not stored yet" is updated.

## Needs manual verification

- **CloudKit production schema deploy** (owner), as above. Not done here.
- **Second device:** step 12 of the sync manual test plan in `docs/sync.md`. Barge in on device A, stop mid-reply in a second turn, force-quit and reopen A, then open the conversation on B. Both replies should end in the interrupted dash, and in the CloudKit Console `CD_endReasonRaw` should read `bargedin` and `stopped`.
- **Development schema:** run a Debug build with `-BlauInitializeCloudKitSchema` and check that `CD_Utterance` gains `CD_endReasonRaw`. This needs an iCloud developer account and was not run.
- A real barge-in on a phone (VAD, echo guard, real Grok) writing the mark. On the Mac this was covered only through the orchestrator over fake sockets.

## Test evidence

All of these ran locally on a Mac, on the branch rebased onto `864caea`:

- `xcodegen generate`: project created.
- `make lint`: `swift-format.sh: 1095 Swift file(s) lint clean.`
- `xcodebuild … build -scheme Blau -destination 'generic/platform=iOS Simulator' -derivedDataPath .build/DerivedData CODE_SIGNING_ALLOWED=NO`: `** BUILD SUCCEEDED **`.
- `swift test` in `Packages/BlauKit`: every target passed (347, 442, 322, 256, 631, 397, 462, 11, 192 and 232 tests). Persistence and realtime include the new suites:
  - `Migration v2 → v3` and `SchemaV2 fixture` (v3 adds only `Utterance.endReasonRaw`, which is optional, a string and not encrypted)
  - `ConversationStore interrupted mark`
  - `Interrupted mark in storage` (orchestrator: `bargedin`, `interrupted`, `stopped`, each written after its row; no mark for a reply nobody heard or one that played to the end; the reopened-store test; a reply first stored by the server's transcript)
  - CloudKit compatibility for v3, a migration-plan check that every stage is lightweight between consecutive versions
  - chat rows from the stored mark, the renderer markers, and `endReason` in the JSON

  One earlier full run had a single failure in `ScriptedRealtimeServerTests.everyTurnGetsASpokenReply` (`latency.turn.totalCount == 3`). That test runs on real time against a scripted server. It passed in 8 separate runs and in two later full runs, so it looks like a timing flake under load, not something this change caused.
- App tests on a dedicated simulator (iPhone 17 Pro, iOS 26.5, created with `xcrun simctl create` and deleted afterwards):
  - `-only-testing:BlauTests`: `** TEST SUCCEEDED **`, 373 test cases passed, 0 failed (run before and after the rebase).
  - `BlauUITests/ChatTranscriptUITests`, `MarkdownExportUITests` and `TopicTimelineUITests`: 12 tests, 0 failures.

author: codemug
body:
The nit from the #608 review (ADM-18, refused writes leave no unhandled rejection): "document that mutate().then(onSuccess) with no rejection handler still leaks; a static pin would keep the count at zero."

## The limit of #608

`useMutation`'s `mutate` returns a promise that is marked handled before it returns, so `create.mutate(body)` in a click handler leaves nothing unhandled when the write is refused. That covers THAT promise only. `create.mutate(body).then(onDone)` (or `.finally(fn)`) derives a NEW promise that rejects with the same refusal and has no handler: an `unhandledrejection` (and a Playwright `pageerror`) per 422 or 409 again.

## What this adds

- `tests/ui/test_mutate_chains_end_in_a_rejection_handler.py`: reads every `*.js` and `*.jsx` under `ui/` with comments and string contents blanked, finds each `.mutate(...)` call by balanced brackets, follows its `.then(` / `.catch(` / `.finally(` links, and lists the call if the LAST link is neither `.catch(...)` nor a two-argument `.then(onDone, onFail)`. An `await` or `return` in front of the expression is the one exemption (the rejection goes to the enclosing async function or the caller, like awaiting `mutate` itself). The count is zero today: 55 call sites, 10 of them chained, all with `.catch`.
- `tests/ui/test_use_mutation_handled.py`: one V8 test of the premise (the promise `mutate` returns is handled; a chained `.then(f)` and a `.finally(fn)` are not; a `.catch` at the end of the chain is).
- `docs/dev/subsystems/ui-foundation.md` and a comment above `mutate` in `use-mutation.js`: the limit, how to write the chain, which test keeps the count at zero.

## Definition of done (AGENTS.md)

1. Backend: not applicable (console only).
2. UI: no surface changes; a comment in `use-mutation.js`, no behaviour change.
3. System tools: not applicable.
4. Docs: `ui-foundation.md` (above).
5. Unit tests: above.
6. E2E: not applicable, the browser behaviour is already watched by `tests/ui_e2e/test_refused_write_leaves_no_uncaught_error_journey.py`; this is a source pin.
7. Regressions: sweep below.

## Tests

There is no pre-fix tree to be red against (the count is already zero and no production behaviour changes), so the scanner is pinned on its own cases: 8 chains it must list (a one-argument `then`, a `then` after a `catch`, a `finally`, a multi-line chain, a `)` inside a string in the arguments, a trailing comma), 13 it must leave alone (a plain call, `.catch`, `.then(a, b)`, `await` and `return`, a call in a comment or a string or a template), the reported line, a quote in JSX text (`Don't`) that must not swallow the rest of the file, and a tree with one offender (listed by file and line).

Sweep on the head `c75dc9a7a` (main `de9f2d774`, team-locked pytest per directory): `tests/ui` 3839 passed (1 skipped, 1 warning: an anyio deprecation in starlette's test client), `tests/docs` 706 passed (2 skipped). ruff clean on the 2 changed Python files. Not run: `tests/ui_e2e`, `tests/e2e`, `tests/integration`, the wide suites (CI).

## Not changed, said plainly

- The `await`/`return` exemption is by the text in front of the call on the same line. A chain assigned to a variable and awaited on a later line (`const p = c.mutate(b).then(f); await p;`) is listed, which is the safe direction (it can be written `const p = c.mutate(b); await p.then(f)`); no such site exists today.
- The scanner masks a `'` or `"` string at the end of its line, so a quote in JSX text can only blank the rest of its own line; a call later on that same line would be missed. No file has that shape today: the raw text has 56 `.mutate(` and the scan sees 55, the missing one being the comment in `use-mutation.js`.
- The doc's "34 of the 57 call sites" figures are #608's and are not re-counted here (the scan sees 55 `.mutate(` calls in code).

## Hand-traced mutants (not mutation-checked by the author)

RED: the scan stopping at the first link (the `catch` then `then` case and the two-link cases); `finally` treated as a handler; a one-argument `then` treated as handled (every `then(onDone)` case); the `await` exemption dropped (the awaited and returned cases); comments not blanked (the commented-call case); strings not blanked (the `")"` case and the string/template cases); the bracket match counting a `)` in a string (same). Survivors, stated plainly: `.then(f, undefined)` counts as handled (two arguments) although it is not, and nothing in the tree writes it.

author: mrun25
body:
## TLDR
Problem this solves:
- When a call returns a plain dict instead of a ModelResponse (the native /v1/messages Anthropic path and the bridge stream wrappers), the result cannot carry _hidden_params, so litellm_model_name stays None in the standard logging payload
- Post-call deployment TPM/RPM accounting keys usage by the deployment model; with the name missing, the post-call increment misses the key the pre-call rate-limit check reserved against, so the deployment's counters undercount these calls

How it solves it:
- When the call succeeded and the response could not supply hidden params, the logging payload now backfills litellm_model_name from the call's deployment model - the same value update_response_metadata writes on the object path (Logging.model is provider-stripped and is deliberately not used)
- Failure payloads stay untouched, and a response object that carries its own _hidden_params keeps them

Fixes #45702

## Testing
- New regression tests: the plain-dict success test and the deployment TPM-key test each fail on unfixed main and pass with the fix; the failure-path and object-path guards pass on both
- llm_response_utils suite (150 passed) and test_litellm_logging.py show identical results with and without the fix; only pre-existing environment failures, unchanged either way

(Prepared with AI assistance; I reproduced the bug, wrote the fix and tests, and ran them myself.)

author: detail-app[bot]
body:
**Detail bug report:** [View on Detail](https://app.detail.dev/org_3377c26d-da48-4ccd-b83a-22c542f4fe83/bugs/bug_0d4021e2-50cb-4be6-a244-e715247ca757)

<!--
Thank you for your contribution!
Unless your change is trivial, please create an issue to discuss the change before creating a PR.
-->

### Describe your changes:

Fixes https://github.com/open-metadata/OpenMetadata/issues/35087

I worked on the stored-procedure name parser used by Snowflake, Oracle, and Redshift lineage because a `CALL`/`BEGIN` written inside a SQL comment was matched instead of the real statement, silently mis-attributing or dropping stored-procedure lineage.

#
### Type of change:
- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] Improvement
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to not work as expected)
- [ ] Documentation

#
### High-level design:

N/A — small change.

#
### Tests:

#### Use cases covered
- A commented-out `CALL`/`BEGIN` (`--` or `/* */`, single- or multi-line) preceding the real invocation no longer steals the match; the executed procedure's name is returned.
- A non-procedure query that merely mentions `CALL` in a comment (reaches the parser via Oracle's `%CALL%` substring filter) returns `None` — no lineage fabricated from a comment.
- Quoted identifiers (backtick `"..."` forms) and string literals are preserved by the comment strip (SQL-aware tokenizer, not a naive regex); a `--`/`/*` inside a string literal is not treated as a comment.
- Queries without comment or literal markers keep the regex-only path. Queries containing `--`, `/*`, a single quote or `$` use lexical masking. The existing large-SQL performance guard passes.

body:
The scheduled `Run soushuba qiandao` workflow failed in job `run` due to an unhandled `NoneType` access while parsing the credit response after posting actions. The failure path assumed stable XML/HTML structure and crashed when expected nodes were absent.

- **Root cause**
  - `SouShuBaClient.credit()` dereferenced `.string` from `cdata_soup.find("span", id="hcredit_2")` without checking for missing/empty nodes.

- **Code changes**
  - Added defensive handling for missing XML CDATA content (`root.text`).
  - Added null checks for missing `span#hcredit_2` and missing `.string`.
  - On malformed/unexpected response shape, return `None` and log warnings instead of raising via attribute access.

- **Behavioral impact**
  - Script no longer exits with `'NoneType' object has no attribute 'string'` when credit payload shape changes or is incomplete.
  - Existing success path for valid credit responses is unchanged.

```python
cdata_content = root.text or ""
if not cdata_content:
    logger.warning("Credit response has no CDATA content.")
    return None

hcredit_2_tag = cdata_soup.find("span", id="hcredit_2")
if hcredit_2_tag is None or hcredit_2_tag.string is None:
    logger.warning("Unable to locate credit field 'hcredit_2' in response.")
    return None
```

author: copilot
body:
The input plugin only exposed AMQP application headers via `include_headers`, with no way to surface standard basic properties (`content_type`, `content_encoding`, `message_id`, `priority`, `correlation_id`, etc.) that publishers rely on to signal metadata.

## Changes

- **New config params**: `include_properties` (bool, default `false`) and `properties_key` (string, default `"properties"`), mirroring the existing `include_headers`/`headers_key` pattern.
- **Record augmentation**: when enabled, the subscribe block attaches the AMQP basic properties to the record under the configured key:
  ```ruby
  record[@properties_key] = {
    "content_type"     => properties[:content_type],
    "content_encoding" => properties[:content_encoding],
    "delivery_mode"    => properties[:delivery_mode],
    "priority"         => properties[:priority],
    "correlation_id"   => properties[:correlation_id],
    "reply_to"         => properties[:reply_to],
    "expiration"       => properties[:expiration],
    "message_id"       => properties[:message_id],
    "timestamp"        => properties[:timestamp] ? properties[:timestamp].to_i : nil,
    "type"             => properties[:type],
    "user_id"          => properties[:user_id],
    "app_id"           => properties[:app_id],
    "cluster_id"       => properties[:cluster_id]
  }
  ```
- `headers` is intentionally omitted from this hash since it's already covered by `include_headers`/`headers_key`.
- `timestamp` is normalized to an epoch integer to avoid serialization issues with raw `Time` objects.

## Documentation & tests

- Documented `include_properties`/`properties_key` in README.md's input options table.
- Added `test_include_properties` and `test_properties_key` covering the new behavior.

author: mrbonha
body:
## ESCSUITE-234 — `/artist` and `/craft` without a trailing slash redirect instead of rewriting

`vercel.json` rewrote `/artist` to `/artist/index.html`, so the document URL stayed `/artist`. The hosted ARTIST bundle is inlined, so `import.meta.url` is the document URL and the decode-worker chunk resolved to `/decodeWorker-<hash>.js` — which the hub's SPA catch-all answered with `index.html` as `text/html`, and the worker failed to start. A deep path (`/artist/foo/`) did the same. Until ESCSUITE-254 this only chose which fallback ran; now that the worker decodes, anyone arriving by a typed or external link to `/artist` would silently lose background-tab export.

- **`vercel.json` gains `redirects`** (Vercel applies them before rewrites and before the filesystem): `/craft` → `/craft/` and `/artist` → `/artist/` as 308, and the deep paths `/craft/((?!.*\.[A-Za-z0-9]+$).+)` / `/artist/(…)` → the app root as **307** — temporary, so a browser never caches a deep path away forever if either app later gains a real sub-route; the negative lookahead keeps extensioned paths (the worker chunk itself) off the redirect. Query strings survive (the destinations carry none). The two now-unreachable bare rewrites are gone; `/artist/(.*)` and the hub catch-all stay.
- **`serve-dist.mjs` derives the redirects from `vercel.json`** the way it derives rewrites and headers (ESCSUITE-196): walked first, `Location` carrying the destination plus the original query, 308 or 307 from `permanent`. `serve-dist.test.mjs`'s drift guard pins each redirect, the query case and both statuses.
- **Production pin** `apps/e2e/tests/production/slashless-redirect.spec.ts`: `/artist` → 308 → `/artist/` (query kept), `/artist/foo/` → 307, the craft twins; loading `/artist` in the browser ends on `/artist/` and the worker chunk the page references is served as JavaScript; and the inverse — `/decodeWorker-<hash>.js` at the root is still the hub HTML, so the spec fails loudly if the derivation stops redirecting. 10 / 10 with `spa-fallback.spec.ts` on Chromium against `pnpm build:deploy`.
- Docs: root `CLAUDE.md`'s production-layout bullet, `apps/artist/CLAUDE.md`'s worker-chunk sentence. `.gitignore` gains the `AGENTS.md` Turborepo 2.11 writes on every build.

Infrastructure only: no app source, no changeset, no release. `pnpm test:scripts` 62. Review approved both verdicts; its two mediums (307 for deep paths, a mis-placed docs sentence) are in.

- **Session Usage:** the 5-hour usage window.
- **Session Clock and Session Name:** the Claude Code conversation.

So `Session: 42.0%  |  Session: 1hr 5m` reads as two facts about one session when they're about different things.

The 5-hour window already has a name here: Block Timer ("Shows current 5hr block elapsed time or progress") and Block Reset Timer ("…until current 5hr block reset window") call it the block. So the widget is named Block Usage, and the three 5-hour widgets now share a name in the picker. Session Clock, Session Cost and Session Name keep "session", which is the conversation.

Its label is `5h: ` rather than `Block: `, because Block Timer already prints `Block: 3hr 45m` for the block's elapsed time. A second `Block:` beside it would label two different numbers the same way. `5h:` says which window the percent is of, as `Weekly:` does.

## How

- **`usage-percent-widget.ts`:** the session kind's display name, label (`5h: `) and description change. Internal names (`sessionUsage`, the `session` kind) stay, since they follow the usage data's field names.
- **`docs/USAGE.md`:** the widget's current descriptions and keys say Block Usage. The README's past release notes keep the name the widget shipped with.
- **Not changed:**
  - Session Clock, Session Cost and Session Name;
  - every other widget's label;
  - how a label override is stored.

A note for review: #183 proposes a separate `block-usage` widget (the cost of the current block). This rename keeps the `session-usage` type, so the two could never collide in a config. Only their display names would overlap if both landed.

## Demo

Piped renders with the 5-hour window at 42% and a 1 hr 5 min conversation (made-up payload): Model, Block Usage, then Session Clock.

author: shanthg01
body:
P2 task 2.4 (decision 5): pure NumPy/SciPy white-box diode clipper, no ngspice. `pedals/*.yaml` and `derive.py` are untouched.

## Equations

Both configurations reduce to one nonlinear state equation for a capacitor voltage `v`:

`C v' = j(t) - G v - i_D(v)`, with `i_D(v) = Is(e^{v/(n_pos N Vt)} - 1) - Is(e^{-v/(n_neg N Vt)} - 1)`

- **Shunt** (RAT/DS-1 clipping stage): `v_in` → R → node, with C and the diodes to ground. `j = v_in/R`, `G = 1/R`, out = `v`.
- **Feedback** (TS808): ideal non-inverting op-amp, so `v- = v_in` and the R_gain–C_gain leg current `i_g` depends only on `v_in`. It is a *linear* source, `I_g = V_in · sC_g/(1+sR_gC_g)`, which reduces the two-capacitor circuit to one nonlinear state. The feedback network R_fb ∥ C_fb ∥ diodes carries `i_g`, with `v = v_out - v_in`. So `j = i_g`, `G = 1/R_fb`, `C = C_fb`, and out = `v_in + v`, which keeps the unity clean path.
- **Discretization:** trapezoidal rule at the oversampled rate: `v[n] + a·h(v[n]) = v[n-1] - a·h(v[n-1]) + a(j[n]+j[n-1])`, with `a = T/2C`. The left side is strictly increasing, so the root is unique. Newton–Raphson starts from a linear extrapolation and uses SPICE `pnjlim` step limiting per diode string, to `|Δv| < 1e-10 V`. The feedback source uses the same unwarped bilinear transform, so the linearised system is exactly the bilinear transform of the analog H(s).
- **Chain:** `pre` (base rate) → 4× (or 8×) upsample → solver → downsample → `post` (base rate) → `out_gain`. The resampler is the zero-phase Kaiser-sinc prototype from `dsp.oversample`, applied in float64 with `scipy.signal.upfirdn`. It matches the torch version to 1e-14 and is much faster than torch's float64 `conv1d`. Linear stages are s-domain transfer functions → `scipy.signal.bilinear`, with RC sections prewarped at their corner → `lfilter`. Op-amps are ideal.

## Modules

- `whitebox/devices.py` is a diode table keyed by part number, with Vt = 25.69 mV at 25 °C:
  - 1N4148/1N914 come from LTspice `standard.dio` (Is = 2.52 nA, N = 1.752).
  - 1S2473 is a flagged substitute that uses the 1N4148 values.
  - 1N34A and the red LED have no authoritative SPICE model. Their values were chosen to hit typical datasheet forward voltages (0.31 V at 1 mA; 1.68 V at 1 mA / 1.80 V at 10 mA).
  - Rs is recorded but not simulated.
- `whitebox/diode_clipper.py` contains `solve`, `ClipperCircuit`, `DiodeClipper(WhiteBoxModel)` and the public factories `shunt_clipper(...)` and `feedback_clipper(...)`, which wave 2 can use for DS-1 and RAT.
- `whitebox/linear.py` contains `AnalogFilter`, `rc_lowpass`, `rc_highpass`, `to_digital` (bilinear with optional prewarp) and the chain helpers.
- `whitebox/ts808.py` registers `@register_whitebox("ts808")`: the feedback clipper (R_fb + drive pot) → R_tone_lp/C_tone_lp low-pass → level-pot fraction. **Provisional**, like `derive.py`: the tone pot's active network, the buffers and the coupling caps are not modelled yet.
- `whitebox/bench.py`: run it with `python -m lstmabar.physics.whitebox.bench [--backend numpy] [--oversample 8]`.

## Validation (tests/physics/test_diode_clipper.py, about 1.5 s total with numba)

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| Small signal vs analytic H(s), 100 Hz–6 kHz (shunt at 1 mV; TS808 stage at mid and max drive) | worst error 0.016 dB (tolerance 0.1 dB) |
| Shunt peak at 20 V drive vs string forward voltage at the peak current | 1N914 ×1: 0.678 vs 0.680 V; ×2: 1.353 vs 1.359 V; LED: 1.789 vs 1.794 V |
| Feedback: max\|y − x\| at max drive, 1 V in | 0.48 V, below Vf(i_g,max) = 0.51 V (linear gain would be ~117×) |
| Symmetric diodes, even harmonics | about −306 dBc (numerical floor); tolerance −80 dBc |
| Asymmetric (1/2) diodes, H2 | −20.5 dBc (shunt), −24.6 dBc (feedback) |
| 4× vs 8× (TS808 stage, max drive, 0.05 / 0.5 V) | relative RMS difference −79 / −76 dB (tolerance −60); harmonics above −60 dBc agree within 0.003 dB (tolerance 0.05) |
| TS808 via `simulate`, 0.1 FS sine, THD at drive 0 / 0.5 / 1 | −23.4 / −19.0 / −16.9 dB |

Also tested: numba and NumPy backends agree to 1e-12, Newton converges on ±50 V steps, the level pot scales the output linearly, and RC prewarping puts −3.01 dB exactly at the corner.

The small-signal reference includes the diodes' zero-bias conductance. For the 1N4148-class pair this is about 9 MΩ, and at full drive (R_fb = 551 k) it lowers the gain by 0.5 dB against a "diodes removed" response. That is physical, so the reference keeps it.

## Throughput (TS808 at max drive, 1 thread, CPU-seconds, Windows laptop)

Real-time factor = seconds of 44.1 kHz audio per CPU-second, aggregated over the batch.

| Backend | Oversampling | B = 1 | B = 16 | B = 64 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| numba | 4× | 16–26× | 18.6× | 19.3–19.9× |
| numba | 8× | 9.1× | 8.1× | 7.6× |
| NumPy (fallback) | 4× | 0.04× | 0.3× | 0.9× |

The pure NumPy time loop misses the ≥10× target by more than 10×, because per-step NumPy overhead dominates. So, per decision 5, numba is added as an **optional `whitebox` extra** (`numba>=0.60`; it was already in `uv.lock` via librosa). The kernel is the same algorithm as a scalar Python function, `njit`-compiled when numba is importable, and `backend="auto"` falls back to NumPy otherwise. CI now installs `--extra whitebox` so the tests run on the fast path. Of the remaining 4× time, about 60% is the solver and about 40% is upfirdn resampling.

## Known limitations

- Ideal op-amp: no rails, slew or GBW. The TS808's JRC4558 bandwidth and the RAT's LM308 are not modelled.
- TS808 tone network, input/output buffers and coupling caps are not modelled yet, so the tone knob has no effect. The post-clip RC is treated as unloaded.
- The 1S2473 uses substitute 1N4148 parameters. The 1N34A and LED parameters are datasheet-fitted, not from SPICE models.
- Trapezoidal integration is not L-stable. Stiff diode conduction can ring at the oversampled Nyquist, which the decimation filter removes. The 4×/8× agreement shows it does not affect the audio band.
- The resampler's zero-extended edges disturb the first and last ~32 base-rate samples.

## Summary

**Fixes #146** — `backup/export` without an explicit path derived its destination from `time.Now().Unix()`, so two exports in the same second targeted the same `backup-<unix>.gbar` and `SaveAtomic` silently overwrote the first. Default-path exports are now serialized on a mutex and claim the first free destination, falling back to `-N` suffixes (`backup-<unix>-2.gbar`, …). The active-version path still hard-fails. `TestInstalledTamperingRejected` was updated: a tampered previous version no longer blocks boot, but rollback stays refused.

author: ludufre
body:
when the game asks for an MSU-1 track that is not on the card, the audio refill calls f_read with ff_sd_offload set. f_read returns early because the file is not valid, and the flag stays set. The next file read is then sent to the FPGA DMA instead of memory. On exit that read is fpga_pgm loading the menu core, and with the Xeno Crisis core loaded the DMA never finishes, so the MCU waits forever. On Mk.II it happened in about 1 of every 4 exits.

Tested on a Mk.II: 12 of 12 returns to the menu worked after the fix.

author: ganesh-403
body:
## Problem

Two point selections dispatched before the server acknowledges the first both carry the same interaction revision. The second can then be rejected as stale while its optimistic selection remains visible. Reproduce by dispatching two valid selections in the same browser task; the regression observes two outgoing revision-zero commands before this fix.

## Root cause and solution

The dashboard stamped every event from the last received signal state without coordinating outstanding commands. Serialize point selections in a bounded queue and release each intent only after matching canonical selection state and stream generation acknowledge the owned command. Stamp the next command with the observed revision, preserving ordered toggles and no-op acknowledgments.

Cancel pending intents when authority, data, specification, filter or page state changes, on a new command error, clear, navigation or disconnect. Valid spatial mutations supersede queued point intents. Reject invalid point events before the shell command bridge. Server revision and authorization checks remain unchanged.

## Tests and review

- Deterministic pre-fix regression: expected one transported command before acknowledgment; received two.
- Eighteen focused browser tests cover rapid selection, ordered toggles, no-op acknowledgment, source/global clear, stale authority, disconnect, prior-error recovery, canonicalization and layout. All 18 passed (42 assertions, 56 filtered out) at `78d03c398`; its hosted reports lane also passed.
- The current commit `bee692ca5` extracts the rapid-selection cases into a focused registration fixture, preserving the existing test command, names, setup and assertions. This fixes the hosted engineering-budget failure without increasing policy limits: TypeScript-test excess is now 9425 against the unchanged 9433 budget. Both TypeScript checks pass.
- After extraction, the local 18-case run passed 13 cases before a page-bootstrap timeout killed the browser and caused four further failures. A separate diagnostic execution of exactly those five failed/unreached cases passed (12 assertions, 6.68 seconds). The initial failed aggregate and raw diagnostic trace remain retained; this is not claimed as a clean 18-case run or root-cause clearance. Fresh hosted CI is running.
- Root directly reviewed all changed files, the extraction, event-bridge callers, optimistic controller and actual server acknowledgement behavior using the review-agent workflow. No unresolved findings.
- Native integration passed using clean binary `78d03c398` (production byte-identical to `bee692ca5`) and an isolated PostgreSQL/DuckLake instance with real Olist data. Three normal selections, three warmups and rapid A→B passed unchanged correctness assertions: two rapid requests, A superseded, B completed with two queries and the final typed B selection retained. Before/after governed totals matched 99,441 orders and 16,008,872.12 revenue. Browser/native cleanup completed; no stream, console or failed-response errors. Timing thresholds were disabled for this correctness-only check; no latency or performance acceptance is claimed.
- The earlier broad browser run failed after a required module request returned `ERR_NETWORK_CHANGED`; its 17-pass/54-fail/1-error result and cascade are retained, not counted as a pass. A separate captured `Promise was collected` error is tracked under FAI-1128; historical failures are not claimed resolved.

## Stack and limitations

Stacked on #959 at `2a3abee11` (which incorporates main `f8c2edc45`). This PR contains only the dashboard route and its registered DOM tests. The superseded local canonical run was interrupted after generation/APIGen when the hosted quality failure was identified; it is not counted as a pass. Fresh hosted CI remains pending before merge. Existing spatial-command concurrency is outside this bounded point-selection repair.

author: mui-muimui
body:
## 対応する Issue

Refs #456（候補 (3)「YUY2 → RGB の変換を GPU（シェーダー）へ」）

## 変更の要点

設計の詳細は `docs/design/video-pipeline.md` の「YUY2 → RGB を GPU で変換する（#456）」。

- **フレームの形式**: `VideoFrame` に `format: PixelFormat`（`Rgb24` / `Yuy2(ColorMatrix)`）を足した。GPU で変換すると決まっているときだけ、`FrameSink::push_yuy2` が偶数幅の YUY2 を回収済みの Vec へ写して積む（ロック・確保は増えない）。係数表（色空間・レンジ・映像調整）は CPU の経路と同じく積む時点で決めてフレームに持たせる。奇数幅とそれ以外の形式（NV12 / MJPEG / RGB24 など）は従来どおり RGB
- **描画**: UI スレッドは YUY2 のフレームを預け、映像より前に置いた `egui_glow::CallbackFn` が YUY2 を RGBA8 テクスチャ（幅は半分）で上げ、フレームバッファ経由で egui の映像テクスチャへ RGB を書く。egui がそのテクスチャを普通に描くので拡大縮小のフィルタも同じ。依存は増やしていない（`eframe::egui_glow` / `eframe::glow` の再輸出を使う）
- **見た目を揃える**: シェーダー（`src/video/shaders/yuy2_to_rgb.frag`）は CPU と同じ整数の式・同じ係数表。起動時に Y / Cb / Cr の全ての値を 6 つの係数表（素の 4 つと映像調整で大きく動く 2 つ）で GPU 変換して読み戻し、CPU と全画素一致したときだけ使う
- **RGB を要る側**: 録画は録画スレッドで `VideoFrame::rgb`（フレームの係数表で変換するので映像調整も従来どおり乗る）、スクリーンショット / クリップボードは保存スレッドの先頭で `into_rgb`。UI スレッドとフレームコールバックには置かない（例外は GPU → CPU の切り替えの前後に届いた数枚）
- **選び方**: 設定 `[video] convert = "auto" | "gpu" | "cpu"`（既定 auto）と「デバイス設定」タブの「映像の変換: 自動 / GPU / CPU」。デバイスは開き直さず次のフレームから効く。**プリセットには含めない**（画は同じで、使える GPU は PC で決まる。`docs/design/presets.md`）。環境変数 `CAPTURECARD_VIEWER_GPU_CONVERT=0` は開発者向けの A/B として残し、設定より優先
- **CPU へ戻す**: GL の失敗（版が足りない・コンパイル / リンク・自己診断・描画中の GL エラー・テクスチャ上限超え）は "gpu" でも戻す。auto のときだけ、ソフトウェア描画（GDI Generic / llvmpipe / Microsoft Basic Render Driver など）と、描画（swap を除く 1 フレーム）が到着間隔の 2 倍を超える状態が猶予 3 秒のあと 5 秒続いたときも戻す。**自動の切り替えは GPU → CPU の一方向・1 セッションに 1 回。** 「性能が戻った」で GPU へ戻す判定は持たない。戻るのは設定を変えて適用したとき（見張りの切り替えだけ取り消す）か再起動したとき。切り替えた次の `update()` で手元の最新フレームを CPU で描き直し、黒や前の画を残さない
- **見え方**: ログ（INFO / WARN）、「接続状態」タブの映像の欄（「YUY2 の変換: GPU / CPU（理由）」）、統計 OSD の「デコード」の行（GPU なら「デコード GPU (積むまで …ms、…)」、自動で戻したときはその下に理由の行）
- 閾値と猶予は `src/video/gpu_watch.rs` の定数で、理由は video-pipeline.md の「性能の見張り」。判定は純粋関数でテスト済み

## 検証

- [x] `cargo fmt --check`
- [x] `cargo clippy --locked --all-targets -- -D warnings`
- [x] `cargo build --locked --release`
- [x] `cargo test --locked`（1659 件）

実機確認: 未（キャプチャーボード・GPU のある PC が要る）。VM（VMware SVGA3D / Mesa 24.1、GPU パススルーなし）のフェイクデバイス 1080p60 で次を確かめた。

| 確かめたこと | 結果 |
|---|---|
| 起動時の自己診断 | `OpenGL 4.3 (Core Profile) Mesa 24.1.0、SVGA3D` で全画素一致、GPU の経路で映る（OSD「デコード GPU (積むまで 0.75ms…)」） |
| 表示までの遅れ（到着→テクスチャ更新、30 秒の debug ログ） | CPU（`CAPTURECARD_VIEWER_GPU_CONVERT=0`）: 平均 9.94ms / 最大 34.97ms、取り込む前に上書き 173 枚 → GPU: 平均 1.32ms / 最大 17.07ms、上書き 27 枚（2 回目 1.32ms / 17.43ms、17 枚） |
| GPU と CPU の画面のピクセル（ウィンドウを PrintWindow で取り込み、OSD とフレーム番号を除く映像域 607,200 画素） | 既定の色設定で差 0、BT.601・フル・明るさ 20・コントラスト 30・彩度 -40 でも差 0 |
| シェーダーのコンパイル失敗（一時的に壊して確認） | WARN を出して CPU の経路で映る |
| 見張りの発火（一時的に閾値を 0 にして確認） | 起動から 8.1 秒（猶予 3 秒 + 5 秒）で WARN を出して CPU へ切り替わり、映像は流れ続け、OSD に「GPU の変換を止めて CPU へ戻した: 描画が映像に追いつかない」 |
| 見張りの誤発火 | 通常の閾値で 40 秒流して発火しない |
| `convert = "cpu"` | ログ「CPU で行う: DisabledBySetting」、経路は高速パス |
| 録画（YUY2 のまま届くフレーム） | 一時的に旗を既定で立てて、`#[ignore]` の録画テスト 4 件（`session_stopped_by_size_change…`、`recorder_replay_buffer_prepends…`、`recorder_without_replay…`、`recorder_save_replay_writes…`）が通る |

## 人間が dev で確認すること

PR はマージせず、ブランチの exe で実機（YUY2 で開けるキャプチャーボード、GPU のある PC）を確かめる。統計 OSD を出しておく。手順は `docs/MANUAL-TEST.md` の「YUY2 の GPU 変換（#456）」にもある。

1. 既定のまま起動すると、OSD の「デコード」の行が「デコード GPU (積むまで …ms、…)」になり、「接続状態」タブに「YUY2 の変換: GPU（シェーダー）」が出る。ログに「自己診断で CPU の変換と全画素が一致、OpenGL …」が出る
2. OSD の「表示までの遅れ」の平均を、環境変数 `CAPTURECARD_VIEWER_GPU_CONVERT=0` で起動したとき（CPU、1.4.0 と同じ経路）と比べる。GPU のほうが小さい（1.4.0 の実機は平均 5.3ms）
3. 設定画面 > デバイス設定タブの「映像の変換」を「CPU」にして「適用」すると、映像が途切れずに OSD の「デコード」の行が「デコード 3.xxms (…)」（GPU の文字が無い形）に変わる。「自動」に戻すと「デコード GPU …」に戻る
4. GPU と CPU（または 1.4.0）で色が同じ。色空間・色レンジ・明るさ / コントラスト / 彩度を動かすと、GPU のままでも同じように追従する
5. GPU のまま録画・スクリーンショット・クリップボードへのコピーをして、色が画面と同じ
6. 数分流し、最小化して戻す・ウィンドウの大きさを変える・設定画面を開くを挟んでも、ログに「YUY2 → RGB の変換を CPU で行う（GPU へは、…）」の WARN が出ない（見張りの誤発火が無い）

## 判断を仰ぐ点

- **"gpu" の意味**: 依頼の「"gpu" を選んでいても 1 の失敗時は CPU へ倒す」に合わせ、"gpu" は性能による切り替え（ソフトウェア描画・見張り）だけを外し、GL の失敗では CPU へ戻す形にした
- **見張りで戻したあとに設定を変えて適用したら取り消す**: 依頼の「設定を変えて適用し直すかアプリを再起動するまで GPU へは戻さない」に合わせた。GL の失敗は設定を変えても取り消さない（同じセッションでは GPU を試さない）
- **見張りの時間の取り方**: eframe の `IntegrationInfo::cpu_usage`（`update()`・テッセレーション・描画のコールバックを含み、swap の待ちを含まない）を使った。CPU 側の時間なので、GPU の実行時間そのものは入らない。ソフトウェア描画は描画を swap まで遅らせることがあるので、`GL_RENDERER` の文字列でも見分けている
- **ファイルの行数**: `src/video/frame_sink.rs` が 853 行（dev の時点で 828 行）、`src/app/mod.rs` が 835 行（同 818 行）で、800 行の目安を超えたまま。`frame_sink.rs` はデコーダ任せ・MJPEG・RGB24 の受け口とそのテストを別ファイルへ分ければ 800 を切れるが、移動を混ぜると差分が読みにくくなるので別の PR にしたい



<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **新機能**
  * 設定ダイアログで映像変換方式を「自動」「GPU」「CPU」から選べるようになりました。自動設定ではGPU変換を優先し、利用できない場合や描画が遅い場合はCPUに切り替わります。
  * 統計OSDと接続状態に、現在の変換方式やCPUへの切り替え理由を表示します。
  * GPU変換でも、画面表示・録画・スクリーンショットの色を従来のCPU変換と同等に保ちます。
  * 映像変換方式は設定ファイルに保存されますが、プリセットの適用対象には含まれません。

<!-- end of auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->
## レビュー対応で挙動を変えたもの（0891de5）

- GL のエラーの判定: 変換の前に積まれていたエラーを読み捨ててから見る。egui などが残したエラーを拾って、そのセッション中ずっと GPU が止まるのを防ぐため
- 切り替えのとき: GPU から CPU へ切り替わる時点で、預けたまま描かれていないフレームを捨てる。CPU で描き直したテクスチャを古いフレームが上書きしうるため
- 見張りの閾値: 「到着間隔の 2 倍」と「32ms」の大きいほうにした。120fps 以上の映像では、垂直同期の待ちだけで 2 倍を超えて誤って発火しうるため

author: aluuriel
body:
## Summary
- **New `typecheck` job in `Build`:** mypy as a ratchet. The existing code has 877 errors (with `--check-untyped-defs`), so mypy can't gate merges directly. `tests/static/mypy-baseline.txt` records those errors by file, code and message, with no line numbers, so moving code doesn't churn the baseline. The job fails:
  - on any error that isn't in the baseline;
  - when baseline errors disappear, until the baseline is shrunk (`tests/static/mypy_ratchet.py --update`). The count only goes down.
- **`--check-untyped-defs` is required:** without it, mypy doesn't look inside unannotated functions, which is most of the backend. In a test without the flag, a typo'd attribute (`Machine.infoReadyy`) in a new function went unnoticed; with the flag, the job fails on that line.
- **mypy is pinned to 1.18.2** and installed with `uv run --with`, so `uv.lock` isn't touched. A new mypy release changes what it reports, so bumping it means regenerating the baseline.

## Findings in the baseline
Most errors come from the code style (static methods without `@staticmethod`, attributes created at run time). Real ones I checked:
- `wifi.py:1092` and `wifi.py:1150` read `health.connected`, but `WifiHealthStatus` only has `link_connected`; that line raises `AttributeError`.
- `imager.py:374-376` writes `notification.responses`, but `Notification` keeps its options in `respone_options` (sic), so the options the imager sets are never shown.
- `profile_converter/references.py:26`: `get_reference_kind()` calls a `set_reference()` that doesn't exist (it has no callers).

## Validation
- `uv run --with mypy==1.18.2 python tests/static/mypy_ratchet.py`: no new errors (877 in the baseline).
- Added a function using `Machine.infoReadyy` to `api/action.py`: the ratchet reports `api/action.py:48 ... has no attribute "infoReadyy" [attr-defined]` and exits 1.
- `uv run flake8 tests/static`, `uv run black --check tests/static`

author: m-jerez
body:
Milestone 1, step 1.7

`scopeId()` in `@multifront/core` gives the same `data-v-*` id plugin-vue gives on its own, in dev and in production. Every target uses it later: React (M3) and Svelte (M6) stamp it, the Vue target (M4) hands it to plugin-vue's `componentIdGenerator`.

## What changed

- `packages/core/src/scopeId.ts`: `scopeId(relativePath, source, production)` = first 8 hex chars of `sha256(relativePath + (production ? source : ''))`, the call plugin-vue 6.0.8 makes (`node:crypto` `hash`). Exported from core.
- `packages/e2e/build/lib/build.ts`, the Build area helpers:
  - `withNodeEnv(mode, run)`: pins `NODE_ENV` around `run`, then restores it. plugin-vue picks its dev or production id from it, and Vitest only sets `test` when the shell has none.
  - `buildApp(root)`: the production `vite.build()` `vue-reference.spec.ts` ran inline, returns `{chunks, css}`.
  - `exportedScopeId(code)`: the `__scopeId` value of a component module.
- `vue-reference.spec.ts` moved onto the helpers, its checks unchanged.
- `scripts/lib/env.mjs`: `NODE_ENV` row in `REGISTRY` (scope `internal`). The legend now says `internal` = set by the scripts or a tool they run, which also fits the existing `CI` row.
- Docs: `docs/spec.md` 3.3 says the path is relative to the **Vite root** (was "package root"), like the milestone, plan.md and plugin-vue. Milestone 1.7 `- Status: done`. Todo moved to `docs/done/`.

## Tests

- `packages/e2e/build/scope-id.spec.ts` (Build area), real plugin-vue with no `componentIdGenerator`, on a `copyApp('vue-reference')` copy:
  - production: the `__scopeId` of a real `vite.build()` equals `scopeId('src/Reference.vue', source, true)`;
  - development: the `__scopeId` from a real `createServer()` + `transformRequest('/src/Reference.vue')` equals `scopeId(..., false)`;
  - the dev and production ids differ.
- No new CI infra: Node and the root devDependencies only, inside `pnpm devx test`.
- Checked by hand: with `production` ignored in `scopeId`, the dev test and the "differs" test fail. All 4 Build tests also pass with `NODE_ENV=production` set in the shell.

## Orchestrator decisions

- Spec 3.3 says "Vite root" (decision rule 1: the milestone doc wins).
- One shared `build/lib/build.ts` for the production build; `vue-reference.spec.ts` keeps its checks.
- No fuzz test: the only oracle compares sha256 with sha256; the real plugin-vue checks pin the input shape.

## Review

- Fixed: `NODE_ENV` in `REGISTRY`, spec wording of the e2e include glob, derived return type instead of `BuiltApp`, `withNodeEnv` instead of `let` + try/finally, `css: string[]` instead of an unread `fileName`, duplicate checks dropped from the production test, dev test pins its own `NODE_ENV`.
- Not taken: moving the production check into `vue-reference.spec.ts` (step 1.7 puts it in `scope-id.spec.ts`); validating `relativePath` in `scopeId` (plugin-vue hashes any path, so a guard could only make the ids differ).
- Comment pass: 3 JSDoc lines shortened in `build.ts`, committed as `chore(comments): …`.

No unrelated findings.

author: jiunshinn
body:
Closes #96.

`<SideTools key={deviceSession.revision}>` remounted the whole tool column every time the device-session store published, which happens at least twice per device switch. Each remount:
- collapsed every open section;
- dropped anything typed into a panel;
- tore down and recreated polls and the logcat `EventSource`;
- left the accessibility flag, which lives in `AppShell`, out of sync with the collapsed section.

## Changes

- **`SideTools` is no longer keyed.** Panels already refresh their own device data when the session changes:
  - the orientation, theme, font, network, foreground and accessibility polls are keyed by the session revision;
  - the route and session panels poll every second;
  - the accessibility panel clears its nodes while a switch is in progress.
- **`LogcatPanel` follows the session.** Once a *different* session has settled (serial and generation known, not transitioning), it clears the old device's lines and resubscribes if it was streaming. Transitional snapshots are ignored, so a switch reconnects once.
- **New Playwright test**, "a device switch keeps open tool sections open": open Session and Location, switch device through the device list, and both stay expanded. It fails on `main`'s UI (`aria-expanded` becomes `false`).

## Validation

### Automated

- `bun run check` passes: 627 tests, coverage floors, all three type checks, the Vite build, README sync, and the package smoke test.
- `bun run --filter serve-emu test:browser`: 6 Playwright tests pass, including the new one.

### End to end on two real emulators and a browser

Setup:
- AVDs `dev` (`emulator-5554`) and `serve-emu-e2e` (`emulator-5556`), both booted headless with `agent-device boot --platform android --device <name> --headless`.
- Real `serve-emu -s emulator-5554`.
- In Chromium: open Network, Font Size, and Logcat, start logcat, then click `emulator-5556` in the device list.

| After the switch | `main` | this branch |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Network / Font Size / Logcat sections | **all collapsed** (`aria-expanded` `false`) | all still expanded |
| Network panel | unmounted | shows the new device's state (`on (wifi enabled, data enabled)`) |
| Logcat panel | **unmounted**, stream stopped | `Streaming • 248` lines from the new device; the buffer was cleared (the first line is the new logcat's `--------- beginning of main`) |

While validating this, the second emulator was hit by #121: a 0-byte cached scrcpy jar made the switch fail with `[scrcpy] Aborted`. The evidence points to the cache not being crash-safe (no `sync` after `push`/`mv`), and I added it to #121. The stale file was removed before the runs above.

body: boonza sitemap structure had its own copies of PPc, MOc, the grid-cube voxelization and the ligand-volume overlaps, with fpocket's thresholds (4 A; 3 A, 0.5, 0.2) written out a second time. It now calls boonza.pockets.overlap's ppc, moc, grid_pocket and volume_overlap, so both commands judge a pocket by one definition and cannot drift apart. Its output is unchanged: pockets.csv identical, byte for byte, before and after, for an apo structure with --holo (1QIF with 1ACJ) and a holo structure with --ligand (184L, I4B), in Martini 2, Martini 3 and SIRAH. overlap.grid_pocket now voxelizes every point at once (in chunks of a few tens of MB), and both it and the ligand voxels take unique voxels by one integer key per row instead of np.unique(axis=0): the same voxels in the same order, 4-7x faster (2,000 points on a 2 A grid 169 ms to 43 ms; 20,000 points 2.0 s to 0.31 s), which boonza pockets traj's enclosed cores get too. New tests compare grid_pocket with the one-point-at-a-time loop (1, 1.5 and 2 A grids, points on and off the grid) and the integer-key unique with np.unique. tests/test_pockets.py, test_sitemap.py and test_sites.py: 136 passed, 1 skipped (the fpocket build); both ruff commands pass.

## Summary Adds inline previews for every file type on the file detail page (`/files/:id`), plus a **Preview** item in the file card ⋯ menu that opens that page. The page reuses the existing presigned-URL endpoint `GET /api/v1/files/{id}/download`. **No changes to file-service, the gateway or DynamoDB.** ``` FileCard (click | ⋯ Preview) → /files/:id → size 0 → "This file is empty" resolvePreviewKind(mimeType, name) // extension fallback only for "" / application/octet-stream unsupported → fallback card (name, size, MIME, Download) // pptx, legacy Office, binaries gated kind && size > 104_857_600 → "Large file (N MB)" + "Load preview" image|pdf|text|markdown|csv|audio|video|zip|docx|xlsx → lazy renderer(url, retryWithFreshUrl) first load error → refetch presigned URL once (expired links); second → "Could not load preview" + Retry/Download ``` - **Bucket CORS (root-cause fix):** the `otterworks-files` bucket had no CORS rule, so the browser blocked text preview's `Range` requests and the old code fell back to iframing the whole file. Added `put-bucket-cors` in `scripts/localstack-init.sh` and `aws_s3_bucket_cors_configuration.files` + `files_cors_allowed_origins` in `infrastructure/terraform/modules/storage`. The rule allows GET/HEAD and the `Range` header, and exposes `Content-Range`/`Content-Length`. Presigned signatures are still required. - **Renderers:** - text/code: first 500,000 bytes via `Range`; html is shown as source. `LineNumberedText` renders a line-number gutter plus the content as two `
` blocks, so the DOM size stays fixed no matter how many lines there are. The old per-line rows took 8.6 s for a 690 KB log; this takes about 250 ms.
  - markdown: `react-markdown` with `skipHtml`; images replaced by their alt text; Rendered/Source toggle in `?view=`.
  - csv/tsv: `papaparse`; draws at most `MAX_TABLE_ROWS` (1,000) data rows and shows `Showing first 1,000 of N rows`.
  - zip: `@zip.js/zip.js` reads only the end of the archive via Range GETs (no HEAD, because presigned URLs are signed for GET); lists up to 1,000 entries.
  - docx: `mammoth`, output cleaned with `DOMPurify`.
  - xlsx: SheetJS CE `0.20.3` from `cdn.sheetjs.com`, because the npm copy is stale and has advisories; sheet tabs in `?sheet=`; up to `MAX_TABLE_ROWS` rows.
  - audio/video: native players.
  - svg: `` only.
  - The heavy renderers are lazy chunks; the main bundle grew by about 1.4 kB gzip.
- `components/files/file-preview.tsx` is replaced by `components/files/preview/*`. Adding the Preview item to `FileCard` changes no props.
- File-service's existing access behaviour and the planted admin-service bug are intentionally untouched.

## BDD & verification

- BDD requirements + AC → BDD traceability: [`docs/bdd/file-preview-bdd.md`](../blob/workshop-inline-file-preview/docs/bdd/file-preview-bdd.md). 35 ACs map 1:1 to BDD-01…BDD-35; no AC is unmapped.

author: thomask33
body:
## Summary

When an Anthropic server tool (web search) runs between two thinking blocks, Xum now turns thinking replay off for the rest of the context segment, using the existing replay receipt from #5994. Before this change, the next turn replayed the later thinking block against a prefix that Xum never sends again. On accounts that enforce the prefix check, that request gets a 400 and pays one signature repair. Elsewhere the API drops the block.

Part of #5887. The issue stays open: full native replay of server tools is a separate decision (see "Not in this PR").

## Background

Preserved thinking binds each replayed thinking block to everything before it. In one step the API returns `thinking, server_tool_use, web_search_tool_result (encrypted_content), thinking, tool_use`. The SDK replays exactly that within the turn.

Xum stores the server tool differently, so history cannot rebuild it:

- The persisted `dynamic-tool` part has no `providerExecuted` (the `tool-call` case in `StreamManager` never copies it, and `MuxToolPartBase` has no such field). `providerExecuted` exists only on the `tool-call-end` event.
- `stripEncryptedContent` removes `encryptedContent` from the result before storage.

The next turn therefore sends the server tool as a client `tool_use`/`tool_result` pair. The thinking after it is bound to the native blocks, so it cannot be valid.

## Implementation

`StreamManager` only (+42 lines). Nothing new is persisted.

- The `tool-call` stream case records the call ID in an in-memory set when `providerExecuted === true` on the Anthropic Messages wire (`isAnthropicMessagesModel`).
- When `appendPartAndEmit` stores a reasoning part and a recorded server tool's part is in the row, it sets `initialMetadata.anthropicThinkingReplay = "off"`. The receipt rides on the partial write that every reasoning append already schedules. The existing receipt readers (`messagePipeline`, `commitPartial`, the continuous-compaction rebuild) then strip Anthropic thinking for the rest of the segment.
- The helper checks the parts, not only the ID set, so a retry that drops parts also drops the trigger. On a miss it clears the set, so the parts scan runs at most once per server-tool call, not once per reasoning delta. Today every retry path keeps existing parts, so reaching that stale-ID case takes a test-only reset. The bound holds anyway.

## Validation

All tests use the real `HistoryService` and the real `@ai-sdk/anthropic` / `@ai-sdk/openai` SDKs with scripted SSE. The next turn is built through `assemblePromptPayload`.

- A server tool between thinking blocks: the committed row carries the receipt. The next request body has no `thinking`/`redacted_thinking` blocks. Every `tool_use` is answered by the next message, and no `tool_result` is left over. The answer text is kept.
- Receipt timing and crash: the first partial on disk that holds the bound thinking already has the receipt. That exact partial, committed through `commitPartial` and reloaded, gives the same clean request.
- Continuous compaction: `rebuildContinuousPrefix` over the committed row shape matches `assemblePromptPayload`, carries no signed thinking, and keeps both tool pairs.
- Controls: a client-tool-only turn writes no receipt and replays every block as returned. A server tool with no thinking after it writes no receipt. A provider-executed tool before reasoning on the OpenAI Responses wire writes no receipt.
- Scan cost: a server-tool part dropped by a reset, then 50 reasoning deltas, gives at most one parts scan (50 before the fix).

Each behavior test failed before its fix. Mutations confirmed the guard tests: without the receipt, without the Anthropic guard, and without the stale-ID drop, exactly the matching test fails.

## Risks and known limits

- **Tradeoff:** after such a turn, Anthropic thinking replay stops for the rest of the context segment. That costs prompt-cache reuse of the thinking blocks, not correctness. The preserved-thinking docs list removing every thinking block as a valid edit.
- **Client-pair limit:** with thinking dropped, the request still sends the server tool as a client `tool_use`/`tool_result` pair named `web_search`. That is the shape Xum has sent after every web search turn since that code shipped. This PR neither introduces nor worsens it, and no issue reports a rejection. The scripted fixtures prove the strip, not upstream acceptance of the client-pair shape.
- Regression surface: Anthropic turns that use server tools. Other providers and client tools are unchanged (covered by the controls above).

## Not in this PR

Full native replay (persisting `providerExecuted` and `encryptedContent` so history sends `server_tool_use` + `web_search_tool_result` in the original order) is being prototyped and measured locally (history size and input tokens), for a user decision. #5887 stays open for it and for the text-first reorder audit.

body:
**Draft, opened only to run CI.** Nothing merges until the operator says so.

## Why this exists

The only live publisher is `pages-app`, which deploys from `main` and only when the whole of `ci.yml` passes. On the current head of `claude/redesign-20261008` (`e34841f`, PR #126) the required battery has **eight red gates** — `word-saved-answer`, `format-check`, `lint`, `corridor-lint`, `later-encounters-integration`, `assessment-written-section`, `record-live-chromium`, `record-live-webkit` — plus the Corridor-gate decks job (committed `study*.html` / `deck-*.json` outputs no longer match `build.py --frozen`). Merging that head would trigger a deploy that skips itself.

This branch is a clean fast-forward of `claude/redesign-20261008` plus Sol's 52 round-5 commits. Its `docs/redesign/r5/REVIEW.md` reports a repaired build but states it skipped PR/CI for local-only delivery and *does not claim the gate passed*. No GitHub CI has ever run on it. This PR is the cheapest way to find out.

## What happens next

- CI runs here (~3h for the battery). Sol's further pushes re-run it automatically.
- If it goes green, the operator merges → `pages-app` verifies again (~3h) → the app is on the phone.
- If it goes red, the failing gates are named here, not discovered after a merge.

## Not changed by this PR

Nothing in the tree. This is `claude/r5-strict-20261010` exactly as pushed.
