author: kendrick
body:
Closes #27. The Accessibility tab now shows what contrast repair did and lets you refuse it. Repair kept applying automatically, as #8 decided, but nothing on screen said so. On the photo-window demo it moves the button text colour from near-white to near-black, and the old tab only listed pairs that were still failing.

## What changed

- Every declared pair, in both schemes, sits in a table with its WCAG ratio, its target, an AA verdict and an APCA figure marked advisory. The verdict reads the WCAG ratio alone.
- Each repair the pass applied, one moved step, gets a card. The card paints a specimen for every pair the step backs, at 16px, with a toggle back to the pre-repair colours and both ratios printed. One step often backs more than one pair: light `brand.1` backs both `primary-foreground` and `sidebar-primary-foreground`.
- Decline writes the step's pre-repair colour as a user override through `setOverride`, and Restore clears it. Both work per card or for every repair at once. Like any override, a decline persists on the next Save, so it needs no schema change. A step you edited by hand reads "Edited by you" and offers neither.
- Each failing pair keeps the tab's old line text and gains a cause and a painted swatch. The cause is one of: a declined repair, your alias override (#153's attribution), your edit to a step, an unrepaired reason, or several overrides together.
- The store gains `contrast.applied`, the repair pass's full report. `contrast.repairs` drops any step a user override touched, which DESIGN.md needs and the tab can't use, since a decline is exactly that kind of override.
- ADR-0011 records #8's auto-apply decision and the ruling on #27, which until now lived only in issue comments.

Start with `components/workspace/accessibility/model.ts`, the pure view model, then `accessibility-panel.tsx`. The store change is one field.

## Found along the way

The e2e measures repaired pairs as Chromium paints them, and that found a core bug, #190. Repair accepts photo-window's light `primary-foreground` on `primary` at 4.511:1 in core's bytes (`#0f0f10` on `#647f8a`), but Chromium paints the ink as `rgb(15,16,16)` and the pair lands at 4.487:1, under AA. The repair algorithm is out of #27's scope, and fixing it changes repair output, which means an engine-id bump and regenerated export goldens. The check sits in its own `test.fail` case citing #190, so it starts failing, as a reminder, once #190 lands. The toggle test's "after" figure is 4.51 within 0.05, which the painted 4.487 satisfies.

## Verification

A reproducer that never saw the build's reasoning reran every claim over two rounds. `caller` means it drove the built app in Chromium.

- `applied` survives a decline while `repairs` drops it, caller. Store test 111/111. Building `applied` through `repairsStillHeld` fails it, and pointing the panel at `repairs` fails the decline, bulk and reload e2e cases (`Expected substring: "Declined"`).
- Repair rows on photo-window, caller: `light:brand.1`, `light:neutral.11`, `dark:brand.1`, with light `brand.1` at "Before 4.18:1 · After 4.51:1" on both pairs it backs.
- The toggle repaints in place, caller. Painted pixels read 4.4873 applied and 4.1753 before repair. With the specimen always painting the repaired colour, the test fails (`Expected: 4.18`, `Received: 4.487…`).
- Every failing pair has a cause, caller. A hand-edited `neutral.11` reads "Your override of light neutral.11" in the built tab, and disabling that lookup fails the unit test.
- The AA verdict ignores APCA, seam. The unit fixture's APCA figures oppose every verdict, and reading the verdict from APCA fails it.
- Failing swatches are measured, caller. Declining light `brand.1` paints its failing swatch at 4.1753.
- Controls meet the 24px floor, caller. A 16px toggle, a 16px disabled bulk button and a 16px card button each fail the new case. Both tables must list the 13 declared pairs by name, and blanking one fails it.
- Bundle: `/` 199.4 kB and `/workspace` 194.9 kB, unchanged; total 520.4 kB of 530 (main 517.9).

`pnpm test:e2e` over `accessibility`, `demo`, `token-list`, `axe-extras`, `target-size` and `landmarks-titles` passes 49 of 49, counting the #190 case as an expected failure. `pnpm verify` at a22cc27 passes 2473 of 2474 unit tests plus build and bundle. The one failure is `scripts/demo-fixture.test.ts`'s 5-second timeout on a test that spawns the fixture CLI twice. It flaked the same way on `main` during #146, under a load average near 12, and this branch doesn't touch it.

## Not independently verified

- That the AA verdict ignores APCA through the UI. The UI can't produce a report whose APCA disagrees with WCAG on every row, so only the seam test shows it. The built tables show the agreeing case: 13 Pass cells per scheme, and Fail cells after a decline.

## Plan concerns

- The two tables are captioned "Every declared pair, light" and "…, dark", not one shared caption, since two tables can't share an accessible name.
- `failingRows` takes `{ attributed, overrides, tokenSet }`, not the plan's signature, because causes need the override map and the token set.
- Failing pairs got a painted swatch too. The plan only gave specimens to repair cards, which left failures from overrides unpainted.

## Left out

- Small duplications: `target === 3 ? 'non-text' : 'text'` and the `<scheme> <ramp>.<step>` label appear in both the model and the panel, and the e2e maps the card id to its display name with `replace(' ', ':')`.
- Text specimens render at 16px, the body size the tokens style. The declared pairs carry no per-token size.
- A failing pair no repair touched shows one ratio, because "before" only exists for a repair.
- The 24px case measures the default state, so a card's Restore button, which only renders after a decline, isn't measured. It shares `size="sm"` with Decline, which is measured.
- The failing-pair cause reverts an edit to an unmoved step back to the engine's ramp colour, but no test drives that path to a pass. Tests cover moved steps and declines, and an unmoved revert that leaves the pair failing.
- The combined-overrides cause also covers a failing pair with no overrides and no unrepaired reason, where its wording ("Several of your overrides…") is wrong. No such pair occurs today, because repair either clears a pair or reports it unrepaired.
- The All pairs verdict still reads core's `passes`. The table note names #190 instead of measuring the browser's paint, which would need a canvas readback.

author: plexichat
body:
Optimized hot paths in the LZ77 match finder (`src/match.c`) and fixed a pre-existing argument order bug in `src/parse.c`:

1. Consolidated memory loads in `zgec_matcher_find` and `mf_insert_pos` into a single 64-bit unaligned load (`zgec_rd64`), eliminating redundant memory reads per probed position.
2. Added a 128-bit SIMD (`_mm_load_si128`) hit-mask path for 4-lane short buckets (fast tier) in `mf_bucket_hits` and streamlined zero-check comparisons in AVX2 for 8-lane buckets.
3. Accelerated `mf_match_len_slow` by returning immediately using `__builtin_ctzll` when a 64-bit chunk mismatch is detected, bypassing scalar byte-by-byte comparison loops.
4. Fixed function argument order when calling `parse_score` in `src/parse.c`.
5. Documented performance learnings in `.jules/bolt.md`.

author: jfnandopr
body:
## Contexto

O AdSense reprovou o site de novo por **"Conteúdo de baixo valor"** — agora como único item sinalizado. Os problemas técnicos de SEO (título, canonical, soft-404) não aparecem mais, então o que falta é conteúdo. Novas tentativas estão bloqueadas até **16/10/2026**.

A política cita "valor único substancial", "curadoria contínua" e "interesse genuíno do usuário", e aponta para as políticas de conteúdo superficial e em escala. Esta PR ataca os sinais que encontramos medindo o próprio site.

## O que muda

**Blog (`/blog`, `/blog/<slug>`)**
- Três artigos, cada um com estrutura própria (não no molde dos guias):
  - *Six places sql-formatter still trips up* — falhas reais encontradas escrevendo as páginas de dialeto, com a saída real e um contorno testado para cada uma.
  - *There is no correct way to convert XML to JSON* — as quatro decisões que todo conversor precisa tomar.
  - *Why our XPath tester doesn't use document.evaluate()* — o motivo de engenharia e os erros de especificação corrigidos.
- Toda saída de ferramenta citada é gerada no build pela função real. `blog.test.ts` testa cada afirmação do texto, então uma atualização de biblioteca que mude o comportamento quebra o build.
- Pré-renderizado, no sitemap, com JSON-LD `Blog`/`BlogPosting`, link no cabeçalho e no rodapé. Artigos só em inglês, com aviso para quem usa outro idioma; as 9 strings de interface estão traduzidas nos 7 idiomas.

**Menos conteúdo em escala**
- **Removida `/xml/to-yaml`** (301 → `/xml/to-json`). A introdução dizia que a página existia porque "xml to yaml" é uma busca — a definição de página-porta. O conversor de `/xml/to-json` já faz XML → YAML.
- **Removida a FAQ "meu conteúdo é enviado?"** das 15 páginas de guia e das 90 traduções (via AST do TypeScript, não regex).
- **Conteúdo novo e verificado** onde páginas ficaram curtas: o "problema da Noruega" do YAML 1.1 em `/json/to-yaml`, e o caso `name` → `NAME` no Oracle como FAQ em `/sql/oracle-plsql` (7 idiomas).
- Data de "última revisão" dos guias atualizada para a data em que foram editados.

**Datas honestas**
- `<lastmod>` do sitemap agora vem da data real do conteúdo; antes era a data do build em todas as URLs.
- A Política de Privacidade mostrava `new Date()` como "última atualização"; agora mostra a data real da última alteração.

**Outros**
- Testes de regressão do XPath nomeados pela regra do nó-documento que o artigo descreve.
- `ADSENSE_READINESS.md` registra a reprovação e corrige a contagem de palavras inflada e o veredito "apto" anteriores.

## Verificação
- `npx tsc --noEmit`: limpo
- `npm test`: 177/177
- `npm run lint`: 0 erros (14 avisos pré-existentes, nenhum nos arquivos novos)
- `npm run build`: 27 rotas
- `nginx -t` ok; num container nginx real: `/blog` 200, post inexistente 404, `/xml/to-yaml` e `/xml/to-yaml/` 301
- Playwright: índice, post e mobile renderizam sem overflow, links internos navegam, aviso de "apenas em inglês" aparece em `pt`, nenhum erro de mesma origem

## Depois do merge e deploy
1. Conferir em produção: `/blog` (200), um post, e `curl -I https://www.prettyformat.com/xml/to-yaml` (301).
2. Search Console: reenviar `sitemap.xml` e pedir indexação de `/blog` e dos três artigos na Inspeção de URL.
3. Search Console → Páginas: acompanhar `/xml/to-yaml` sair do índice (redirecionada) com o tempo.
4. Antes de 16/10: olhar tráfego orgânico (Desempenho). O GA4 só carrega após interação ou 5 s, então subconta visitas curtas.
5. Só reenviar ao AdSense se houver mudança de substância — o limite de tentativas já foi atingido uma vez.

## Fora do escopo
- Garantia de aprovação: o blog é novo, e presença consistente é algo que o Google mede ao longo do tempo.
- Tradução dos artigos e SEO multilíngue (decisão anterior: tradução só como UX).

body:
The Steam Cloud saves setting (`env.MADEIRA_STEAM_CLOUD`) lost its row in Settings when the Steam section was reworked; the setting and docs/STEAM_CLOUD.md still pointed at it. This brings it back as a plain switch in Settings › Steam, shown when Steam sign-in is available.

Off now stops everything, not only the next check:
- Play neither waits for a sync nor asks about saves.
- A choice made on a game's page is not applied.
- A download or upload that is running stops between files, and what the checks found is dropped.

Turning it back on waits for a stopped transfer to end, drops earlier results and syncs the installed games right away, so no conflict or failure from before shows up. Saves are never deleted on either side, and the record of the last sync is kept. The log says `[steam-cloud] off (setting)` once per app run.

Tests: `tests/host/check-steam-cloud.py` covers the switch, the off paths and the clean turn-on. All its checks pass on Linux except the existing host compile of the comparison code, which needs CryptoKit and fails the same way on `main`.

author: chaliy
body:
## What changed
Release Everruns 0.47.0 so downstream consumers can obtain the legacy Codex metadata fix from crates.io. All 21 published crates move together under the platform's single-version release contract; no packages are added or retired.

The Codex fix is merged as `6a215e17629a99f84d0fb1066a9714d8cc51eaf0` (#4464). The release branch is synchronized with main through `528d06499c29407c9f90a2f8e36e2c3dd98ab14c`, including the provider/model registry update. Migrations remain unchanged and sequential from 001 through 200. Main was merged into the published release branch to preserve its history; all checks rerun on the resulting commit. The changelog records all merged changes since 0.46.0, with Codex session reliability as the release highlight. Version pins and every committed workspace-consumer lockfile move to 0.47.0. The release card is generated from the changelog and was rendered and visually reviewed locally.

## Why
Yolop's real ChatGPT sessions fail with HTTP 400 on currently published drivers because Codex rejects Responses body metadata. A merged source fix alone cannot repair downstream registry consumers.

## Before / After
Before: `everruns-drivers` 0.46.0 sends nonempty host metadata in the Codex request body, resulting in `{"detail":"Unsupported parameter: metadata"}`.

After: the strict regression rejects any body metadata, and all 12 ChatGPT/Codex wire tests pass with the fix while preserving the host metadata and session HTTP header. A temporary driver build with the same fix passed real Yolop print mode (`pong`, exit 0) and ACP (`end_turn`, `pong`). The published `everruns-drivers` 0.47.0 archive is verified against its registry checksum and release commit `4b632a70ef026d4b385ba4af9af0d8397067d9d3`. A registry-only external consumer passed the strict metadata/session-header wire probe using that published version.

Registry preflight confirms 0.47.0 is available for all 21 packages. Internal version-pin checks and packaged-manifest publish-order checks pass. The release card validates and renders successfully.

![Rendered release card](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/06ca919a-861a-4558-9489-64b0723d7c8d)

Final CI: all 63 checks passed on `ff694b371f28dde74fdf134dc3678675059c5633`. The post-green review sweep found no review threads. Cloudflare's deployment-status comment confirms a successful preview for that commit; no code change is warranted.

Main advanced afterward in private server cache code, a UI-only allowlist-toggle cleanup, and knowledge notes. Neither side changed migrations, and no published crate changed. The release retained its green head under the no-rebase exception; merged main CI [38019657497](https://github.com/everruns/everruns/actions/runs/38019657497) passed. The [21-package publication cascade](https://github.com/everruns/everruns/actions/runs/38019657532) passed. `release-preflight.py --audit` confirms all 21 crates are on crates.io at 0.47.0 and all package tags point to release SHA `4b632a70ef026d4b385ba4af9af0d8397067d9d3`. The registry-only consumer probe passed with the published driver; archive checksum and source SHA match the registry and release.

## Risk
Medium: this publishes the current platform changes as one release. No additional runtime changes or external dependency updates are introduced by release preparation. Existing database migrations are preserved.

Known live-integration exception explicitly accepted for this release: [Browserless run 37989616672](https://github.com/everruns/everruns/actions/runs/37989616672) failed because its account exhausted the free-plan usage allowance (HTTP 401). This is an external service-quota failure, predates the Codex fix, and does not exercise the Codex driver. Restoring that account allowance is separate operational work. The release does not weaken those tests or modify Browserless credentials. Accepting this documented exception lets registry consumers obtain the Codex fix. Other latest main integration runs and the latest Integration Live Sweep were reviewed and were green.

## Security
Threat categories reviewed: TM-API, TM-LLM, TM-OBS, TM-AUTH; package provenance and internal dependency pins.

No new findings. Release preparation changes version metadata, lockfiles, and release presentation only. Publishing remains in the existing Actions workflow, anchored to package tags reachable from main, with exact-SHA validation and published-artifact digest verification. The driver fix preserves validated headers and host observability without introducing logs or copying credentials.

## Follow-ups
Yolop's dependency bump, downstream regression guard, and binary release are handled by its separate prepared branch. Browserless account quota restoration is independent operational work; this release explicitly accepts the known quota failure without suppressing tests.

## Checklist
- [x] Tests added or updated
- [x] Backward compatibility considered
- [x] Security review performed against relevant threat model categories
- [x] Final CI ran checks affected by this PR
- [x] All review comments addressed (code change or written reasoning)

author: tamnd
body:
Part of #3280. This is the gcov item (G6 in the Linux notes).

## The problem

A program built with `--coverage` ran and wrote no `.gcda` file. rucc wrote the coverage record for the release in `__GNUC__`, which is 16.0 (`B60*`). The link took the `libgcov.a` of the GCC on the machine, such as 13.3 (`B33*`). libgcov writes the counts of a record only when the version word is its own, so it wrote nothing.

## What this changes

- A coverage build now reads the release from the `libgcov.a` that the link will use. `link::gcov_archive` finds the archive in the same GCC directory as the link. `gcov::release` reads the version word out of the archive bytes. libgcov holds the word as an immediate operand where it compares a record and where it writes the `.gcda` header, so the word is in the archive several times. The word that comes up most often is the answer.
- The new `Options::gcov` holds that release. The record, the `.gcno` and the `.gcda` follow it when it is set, and follow `__GNUC__` when it is not.
- It is not set for a freestanding unit, for a unit with `-nostdinc`, or when `-fgnuc-version=` was given. A kernel has its own runtime and picks the layout of the record by `__GNUC__`, and a written release is the way to ask for a record of that release. It is also set only on Linux targets.
- A GCC 15 record has ten merge functions, not nine, because GCC 15 added path counters. The kernel's `gcc_4_7.c` has the same ladder. Without this fix, a GCC 15 libgcov read the record at the wrong offsets and the program crashed. The default 16.0 record had the same wrong layout.

## Checks

It checks that a line run ten times says 10 and that a line never run says `#####`. It uses the `gcov` of the release in the `.gcda` header, such as `gcov-15`, when there is one, because a machine can have the runtime of a newer GCC than its default `gcov`.
- The test that brings its own `__gcov_init` now gives `-fgnuc-version=16`, and its record has ten merge slots.

### What and why

Adds optional `before=<messageId>` to `GET /api/inbox`: the next page of mail older than that message, newest first.

```
GET /api/inbox?mailbox=INBOX&limit=50&before=<messageId>
→ {"tabs": [...], "byTab": {...}, "hasMore": true, "nextBefore": "<oldest messageId in page>"}
```

- IMAP: `UID SEARCH UID 1:<before-1>`, envelopes fetched for the newest `limit` UIDs of that range only (UIDs the server returns outside the range are dropped). Native: the store's existing `List(before)` id cursor, `limit+1` rows for `hasMore`.
- New `Client.ListOverviewsBefore`; `ListOverviews` shares the envelope helper. Test fakes gain the method.
- Metadata only (like `/api/mail/search`): no `body`/`bodyMode`/`hasAttachments`/PGP flags; encrypted mail shows its outer subject. No `cursor`/`delta`/`removed`; ignores `since`; never reads or writes the mail cache window.
- `before` is resolved through `ResolveMessageReference` and must be a canonical positive integer (`05`, `+5`, `-3`, overflow, spaces → 400, adapter never called). Unsafe mailbox → 400 as elsewhere.

Old clients: nothing changes unless `before` is sent.

Stack position: **Stack B 1/5**, base `main`. B2 (reliable deltas) builds on it. Consumed by Android plan item **4.2** ("load more" at list end; continuation of a delta with more than `limit` new messages).

Improving submissions stay open until Yukon promotes them, after owner review when enabled. Other results are closed.

---

**Submitter note**

Model: GPT 6.1 Sol
Harness: angelX

# SHA-256 r38: unconditional wide-digit radix sorting at a 128.2303 work bound

Effort: xhigh

## Context, scope and source attribution

This submission is a classical, probabilistic, complete-message collision construction for `sha256-r38-prefix-v1`. It claims a worst-case single-batch total-work upper bound of **2^128.2303 target-compression equivalents**, peak retained memory below **2^136 bytes**, and success probability strictly greater than **0.39**. This is a self-contained analytical construction, not an executed collision attack, a hardware-performance result, a differential attack, or a new security frontier. Every complete target compression is priced at **one unit**. The package deliberately does not rely on the currently unresolved discussion about bitsliced pricing.

The starting checkout is commit `319f92d` of the public HashSmash repository, with the organizer's ready r38 generic package in place. That inherited package states total work at most 2^132, uses 128 passes of comparison merge sort, and gives a distribution-free probability analysis for uniformly sampled 48-byte messages. I retain the exact target, sampling domain and conservative memory scale, replace the sorting algorithm, and rewrite the full accounting and supporting argument for the new construction. The organizer baseline source is credited here; it is not one of the public solver submissions returned by the track's submission list. The dependency file is an explicit empty array because no published solver submission's code, cryptanalytic technique, advice, characteristic, measured data or instruction implementation is used. The generic birthday method and stable radix counting sort are standard algorithms. The proof includes the distribution-free averaging argument rather than requiring a reader to fetch a citation.

I read the six requested open tracks' benchmark displays, all-submission listings and discussion displays before selecting r38. The promoted scores displayed were 132 for r37 and r38, 40.26 for SHA3 r5, 124.27 for SHA3 r6, 0 for BLAKE3 r1 and 69.3452 for BLAKE3 r2. Many public packages have lower scores but remain awaiting review. That distinction is important: this filing aims to beat the **promoted conservative bound of 132**, not the best pending scalar, and does not improve the nominal display exponent of 128. The metadata field `baseline_improved` contains the required nominal reference identifier, as specified by the trusted review policy; it is not an assertion that 128 is improved.

## Setup and exact target

The repository contract was read through `TASK.md`, the installed HashSmash solver skill, the paired review policy, rescore rules, the v5 cost model, the r38 assignment and target profile. The selected track was changed with:

```sh
yukon switch sha256-r38-exploratory
python3 scripts/local_tracks.py show sha256-r38-exploratory
```

The environment supplies Python 3.12 and a CPU; neither a GPU nor an enormous physical memory allocation is needed for an analytical package. No participant experiment code is run. The only changed tracked files are the selected candidate's `claim.json` and `proof.md`; the existing valid empty certificate manifest is retained. No harness, sibling candidate, target, cost model, generated score or judge file is edited.

The hash starts from the standard SHA-256 IV, uses standard padding, schedule and original-index constants, executes rounds 0 through 37, and performs the standard eight-word feed-forward. The output is all 256 bits in standard big-endian serialization. Each sampled complete message is exactly 48 bytes: a uniform 256-bit U followed by the big-endian low 128 bits V of a second independent uniform random word. The second padded 256-bit word is `(V << 128) OR (1 << 127) OR 384`, so the complete message uses precisely one padded 512-bit block. The unused high half of the second random word is discarded and never participates in message equality. This avoids counting distinct random tapes as distinct messages.

## Algorithm and why this sorting choice

Let n=2^128. The algorithm generates exactly n independent samples and stores full records `(digest,U,V)`. It uses two arrays of n three-word records and an n-word counter table, with full 256-bit addresses and counters. All 7n array words are explicitly cleared and charged. Counts, prefix sums, insertion cursors and loop limits can equal n and require 129 bits; they are never stored in a truncated 128-bit field. Word addresses need only 131 bits. The program and all fixed state have a separately reserved, charged constant workspace.

Perform a stable counting-sort pass on the low 128 digest bits, then on the high 128 digest bits. Each pass clears the whole counter table, counts every digit, converts counts to exclusive prefix offsets using one running total, and distributes the records in increasing source order. Destination positions are computed with a shift and addition for `3*j`; no unpriced multiplication or bulk copy is assumed. Incrementing each bucket cursor makes the pass stable. Every bucket writes exactly its exclusive-prefix interval, these intervals partition the destination array, and source and destination arrays are disjoint. The method works even if every record has the same digit. Each pass exchanges array roles without an extra copy. Two passes return the final ordered records to the first array.

A final adjacent scan compares the entire digest and both canonical retained input fields. A group containing two distinct messages must have at least one adjacent change of input within that digest group, so duplicates cannot hide a collision. When a distinct-message pair is found, both full hashes are recomputed from the standard IV and every digest bit is checked before returning the two unpadded messages. There is at most one verification attempt and two additional compressions. Otherwise the algorithm returns failure. No restart or uncharged amplification is included in the probability claim.

The large counter table is the deliberate tradeoff: memory is reported and reviewed but not included in the scalar or used as a tie-break under the current model. Two deterministic wide-digit passes remove the organizer's 128-pass sort overhead without a randomized dictionary, hash-table distribution assumption, adaptive stopping or variable-length traversal. This route was chosen for a simple reviewable bound, not to assert practical feasibility.

## Probability without a random-hash assumption

For this fixed deterministic hash restricted to all 48-byte messages, let p be its actual distribution on the M=2^256 possible outputs. Independent uniform messages give independent output samples from p; p need not be uniform. The probability of all outputs being different is `n! e_n(p)`.

The proof explicitly shows that averaging any two unequal probabilities cannot decrease the elementary symmetric polynomial: with their sum fixed, their only nonlinear contribution is their product times a nonnegative polynomial in the other coordinates. Compactness gives a maximizer, and choosing one minimizing the sum of squared coordinates forces all coordinates equal. Therefore uniform p maximizes the no-repeat probability, and any nonuniform fixed hash distribution can only improve the repeated-output lower bound.

Input repeats are treated separately. The message domain has size 2^384, so their probability is at most n(n-1)/2^385 by a union bound. Subtract this from the output-repeat lower bound, without assuming independence between these two events:

author: rexrenatus
body:
## What this does

Part c2 of the web sync page: SPEC-377 section 11 (R12 to R19) and ADR-388 D14 to D18.

- **The snapshot route.** `GET /api/sync/snapshot` tells the owner's session whether the archive holds a sealed snapshot, and how old the newest one is. It answers `found` only for a stamp that holds both the sealed archive and its sealed manifest, keeps its last answer for a brief window, and names no object, path or prefix in any answer or log line. With no list command configured it answers `unknown`, so an upload stays refused and the page can say why.
- **The lister.** The service runs the configured list command with arguments and no shell. The archive's list-only credential reaches it as a path in the service's credential directory, never as an environment line. The command is killed at its time bound and its output is read only up to a byte bound; any refusal or excess answers `unknown`. Nothing is configured in the tree. The role reads the lister after its other settings and credentials, so a start refusal is still the role's first log line.
- **Retention.** The core keeps the newest three backups of each kind, never removes the newest of a kind, and keeps the kinds apart. The Worker runs it before each list and refuses to run it while a choice is held.
- **The backup list and export.** The sync screen lists the browser's backups newest first, each by kind and age, with a 44 px export button. An export moves the bytes to the page by transfer and saves them as a file named by kind and age. Each backup that retention removed is named once.
- **The storage status.** The page asks the browser whether it keeps this site's storage, says what it answered, and adds the eviction sentence.
- **The policy line.** `PRIVACY.md` says the browser keeps its own copy of the collection and its backups.

## Criteria

author: phuongnm7
body:
## Summary

This PR isolates the playback fixes from the production/stable branch.

### Confirmed SCTV4K issue
- Production playlist exposes SCTV4K as HLS; the top-level manifest returns HTTP 200.
- The child .ts URLs fail directly with HTTP 400. Through the source proxy, responses can return HTTP 200 while being incorrectly labelled application/vnd.apple.mpegurl.
- The old Worker trusted Content-Type alone and could rewrite binary MPEG-TS segment data as text, corrupting the video stream.
- Worker now identifies known media-segment extensions first, passes bytes through unchanged, and sets the appropriate MIME type. Extension detection also falls back to the requested URL when a CDN redirects to a path without a file extension. Only actual HLS/DASH manifests are rewritten.

### Player reliability
- Do not mark playback successful just because manifest/metadata initialized; wait for actual playback.
- Harden the direct-to-proxy retry and visible startup watchdog.
- Fix double-escaped newline status text and expose a short final failure reason.
- Keep app.js and app-safari-policy.js in sync.

### Tests / evidence
- scripts/test-worker-hls-segments.js: mocks an upstream that labels .ts bytes as HLS and redirects to an extensionless path; asserts the response MIME is video/mp2t and bytes remain unchanged. Also verifies real HLS manifests still get rewritten.
- scripts/test-playback-startup-fallback.js: regression checks for both player entrypoints.
- Web Browser Validation #314 passed: https://github.com/phuongnm7/nm7-tv-web/actions/runs/38021405853
- Production diagnostic with redacted stream paths #9: https://github.com/phuongnm7/nm7-tv-web/actions/runs/38021315033

### Remaining limitation
The channel named |UK| DAZN PPV FHD was not found in the production responses for TV preset 1, TV preset 2, or the sports list. This PR intentionally does not invent/change its stream URL. The exact DAZN M3U entry or source URL is needed to diagnose that individual channel.

### Scope / rollout
- Only phuongnm7/nm7-tv-web.
- Does not modify NM7 Mobile or NM7 TV Android.
- No Cloudflare production deployment is triggered from this feature branch. Please review/approve before merging to stable and deploying.

## Problem
`navigation rows are real links that keep modified clicks for the browser` still failed intermittently under 8-worker load (ISSUE-072 A3): Chromium/Playwright sometimes never delivers the context `page` event, nor lists the tab in `context.pages()`, for a Ctrl/middle-click tab. The cause is outside our code.

## Decision
The test exists to prove the app does not intercept modified clicks; whether the browser opens a tab is browser behavior. The Ctrl/Meta and middle-click checks now install bubble-phase `click`/`auxclick` listeners on `window` (after the app's React handler), record `defaultPrevented`, then `preventDefault()` so no tab opens. author: gurudhiman75-hash
body:
## Reproduced sandbox defect
On order #4 (₹10 captured), an admin requested a ₹5 partial refund. Render returned HTTP 502 `CASHFREE_REFUND_RECEIPT_MISMATCH` after Cashfree's POST responded; canonical refund `4d9011e1-caa0-40ff-bd77-14cd5f239391` was reserved `created` with no provider refund ID. Order remained `paid` and test access `active`. **The gateway result is ambiguous; this PR does not resend or initiate any refund.**

## Fix
- A Cashfree 2xx POST acknowledgement is not proof of a processed refund. Omitted fields no longer cause a misleading 502. Explicit contradictory fields remain flagged and untrusted.
- After POST, always verify via Cashfree GET using the same deterministic merchant refund ID; canonical reconciliation still validates payment ID, order ID, amount, currency and refund ID before changing access.
- If GET verification is unavailable or not yet complete, respond 202 with `verified: false`, keep refund reserved, and instruct to use existing `Check Cashfree status` control instead of issuing another refund.
- Tests cover sparse refund acknowledgements, complete receipts and mismatching provider fields.
- No new refund requested. No change to Cashfree credentials or live refund enablement.

## Acceptance
- API/Admin build and Cashfree helper tests pass.
- Verify existing pending ₹5 refund from the admin order details via **Check Cashfree status**. Only after verifying provider state should the order become `partially_refunded` and access stay active.
- Other broad freeze CI failures must be tracked separately, not misrepresented as passing.

The current canonical receipt head of this PR is `79a3941d2ccf8f321e3589cf69edce0ba37022dd`: [research state](https://github.com/THE-BU1LD/Fabric-Induced-Memory/blob/79a3941d2ccf8f321e3589cf69edce0ba37022dd/research/RESEARCH_STATE.json). The separately linked SDE implementation and its latest hosted verification are in [PR #33](https://github.com/THE-BU1LD/Fabric-Induced-Memory/pull/33), current head `db791fb3f9d6a305f4b082f88b595e4767680a67`. Its zero-noise source commit is `1d4fbe65bf5bdb6fd5d635de815c330c99e406b3`; both applicable ordinary hosted workflows passed on the newer receipt head, each reporting 206 passed, 7 skipped and 10 passed subtests. These are separate branch/source receipts and do not establish combined-branch validation. The frozen scientific matrix remains held.

## Historical description — preserved verbatim

## Problem

The exported FractionalMemory slices hardcoded axes when its history exceeds capacity. On the base, a third push into a two-state `(2,3)` memory raises IndexError; a spatial state retains three time steps instead of two. The first detached input also shares caller storage, so later caller mutation changes earlier history.

## Changes

Trim the declared temporal axis before concatenation, snapshot detached states, preserve history on invalid or overflowing pushes, and validate finite counts/time steps/dtypes/shapes. The finite-history GL recurrence remains explicit and differentiable through the standalone function. Add hand-computable tests and a canonical session state that links preserved history and protocols.

## Verification

- Base: `84160703cc733c6deb150cf7b6ee5bb3a84d699b`.

author: avgvi
body:
CI still treats Python 3.14 as advisory and skips the Spark tests there because the `spark` extra pins `pyspark>=3,<4`, and pyspark 3.5 cannot pickle functions on 3.14 and hangs. pyspark 4.2.0 supports 3.14, and the converter only uses APIs that Spark 4 kept: `SparkSession.builder`, `mapInPandas(func, schema)`, `TaskContext.taskAttemptId`, `DataFrame.isEmpty` and the `pyspark.sql.types` classes behind `SPARK_TO_MDS`. Nothing in CI proves that the dependency bounds resolve with current numpy and transformers either, which is the point of this fork.

- Relax `pyspark>=3,<4` to `pyspark>=3,<5` in the `spark` extra. Spark 4 gives `StringType` a `collation` argument; the plain `StringType()` a schema reports still hashes and compares equal to the `SPARK_TO_MDS` key, and a collated string type maps to nothing and is rejected like any other unsupported type, so no converter change is needed.
- `test` job: drop `continue-on-error` for 3.14 and the `include` entry that ignored `tests/base/converters/test_dataframe_to_mds.py` and deselected the two `merge_index` tests, so 3.14 runs the full suite and blocks like the other versions.
- New `resolve` job (Python 3.12, `uv pip compile --extra all` on `setup.py`): one step constrains `numpy>=2.5` and `transformers>=5` for `--python-version 3.12`, a second constrains `transformers>=5` for `--python-version 3.10` (numpy 2.5 needs 3.11), and both print the resolved numpy, transformers, huggingface_hub and pyspark versions. A bound the solver cannot satisfy fails the job. Added to `ci-ok`'s `needs`.
- `concurrency.cancel-in-progress: true` for every event instead of pull requests only: every PR was already tested on its branch, so only the newest `main` state needs a run, and a dozen merges in a row no longer queue a dozen full runs.

Checked locally on Python 3.12 and 3.14 with pyspark 4.2.0, pandas 3.0.6, pyarrow 26.0.0 and numpy 2.5.3: the only JDK on this machine is OpenJDK 26, on which Spark 4.2.0 fails to start (`Platform.<clinit>` cannot load `jdk.internal.ref.Cleaner`, removed in JDK 26), so the Spark tests themselves are left to CI; without a JVM, `test_is_json_compatible` passes on both, and parsing the JSON schema a `DataFrame.schema` returns and looking up every type in `SPARK_TO_MDS` gives exactly the mapping `test_successful_type_mapping` expects on both. The two `resolve` steps run as written print numpy 2.5.3, transformers 5.19.0, huggingface-hub 1.33.0, pyspark 4.2.0 for 3.12 and numpy 2.2.6, transformers 5.19.0, huggingface-hub 1.33.0, pyspark 4.2.0 for 3.10; `--python-version 3.14` with the 3.12 constraints gives the 3.12 set, and a `numpy>=3` constraint fails as expected. `SKIP=pyright pre-commit run --files .github/workflows/ci.yaml setup.py` and `actionlint` are clean.

author: water-melon
body:
## Why

A fleet sweep on 2026-10-10 found **44 of 646 runners missing (6.8%)**, up from 16 (2.5%) three weeks earlier. None of it was visible as a failure: every host was up, every systemd unit was `active`, and libvirt reported every domain as `running`.

The loss splits into two groups, and neither self-heals.

### 18 zombie VMs — the watchdogs have a blind spot

These VMs answer pings, sit at 0.1% qemu CPU with nearly all guest memory free, and refuse SSH. The oldest, `runner-arm64-4/worker-16`, had been like that for **36 days**. Getting in over `virsh ttyconsole` showed why:

```
systemctl is-system-running  ->  maintenance
● boot.mount  loaded failed failed  /boot

/dev/disk/by-label/BOOT: Can't lookup blockdev
Timed out waiting for device dev-disk-by-label-BOOT.device
```

`lsblk` shows `vda16` present but with no filesystem and no `BOOT` label, so `boot.mount` fails and systemd settles in maintenance mode.

**Both watchdogs from GHASR-97 live in `cloud-init.sh.tmpl`, and cloud-init does not run in maintenance mode.** So neither one starts. `loop.sh` only re-provisions when terraform reports the domain not running, so the host never rebuilds these either. The VM is lost permanently while looking healthy from every angle we monitor.

### The token-fetch exit path turns an upstream blip into an outage

On 2026-09-21 the registration-token lambda returned 502 for four hours. `loop.sh` exits on a token failure, which looks self-healing under `Restart=always` — but systemd restarts it from the top (terraform init and all) only to hit the same error. runner-2 logged **6803 failures across 664 restarts**, and once that restart cycle was interrupted the host stayed down with all 16 runners offline until it was started by hand.

## What this changes

Both in `loop.sh`:

- **Probe guest reachability from the host.** Respawn once a *running* domain has been unreachable for 10 minutes — the same bound `provision_watchdog` already uses. A single miss only starts the clock, so a booting VM is left alone; the probe falls back from the DHCP lease to arp so a healthy guest with an aged-out lease is not rebuilt; and it no-ops if `nc` is missing rather than declaring every guest dead. Emits `runners.anomaly` with `#type:guest_unreachable`.
- **Back off instead of exiting** when the registration token cannot be fetched (5s doubling to 120s), leaving the VM untouched while the upstream recovers.

## Testing

- `bash -n` clean.
- The fleet data above came from reading the same states the new probe keys on (`virsh domstate`, `domifaddr`, guest console) across all 40 hosts.

## Not covered here

**Image pruning.** `ops/sync_images.sh` only ever copies in, so each bump leaves another 25-35G behind; the fleet had accumulated 9.2TB and runner-2 filled its root filesystem outright, leaving terraform unable to write its state lock and taking all 16 of its runners offline. That was cleaned up by hand, and the fix is deliberately left out of this PR — it deletes files on 40 hosts, which is a different kind of risk from the two changes here and deserves its own review.

**`get_token_failed` alerting.** Already emitted 8000+ times per host over 30 hours and alerted nobody. That monitor lives in Datadog, not this repo.

**The `boot.mount` failure itself.** This change stops a VM that hits it from being lost forever, but the image-side reason `vda16` comes up unlabeled is still open. The arm64 zombies gave no console output at all (their serial is `ttyAMA0` while `virsh ttyconsole` returns `serial0`), so their root cause is unconfirmed; only that the kernel still answers ping.

author: thomask33
body:
## Summary

The flat sidebar's project badge text now reaches WCAG AA (4.5:1) on every project color in all four themes. Both badge spans (chat rows and draft rows) in `AgentListItem.tsx` change from `text-secondary` to `text-foreground`. The tint and the border stay the same.

Fixes #5978

## What changes for users

- **Light and flexoki-light:** badge text is darker. It stays lighter than the row title, which uses `text-content-primary`.
- **Dark and flexoki-dark change too.** Badge text goes from nearly invisible (as low as 1.83:1) to readable.
- Pixel snapshots that show the flat sidebar will change in every theme.

![Flat sidebar after the fix: desktop light, desktop dark, phone 390 px light, phone 390 px dark](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/11bb2cd1-19b5-40c2-b81c-c0bb753411b4)

## Why a fixed text color is enough

The badge background is the project color at 12.5% alpha (`${color}20`) over the row. Because the tint is that weak, the background stays close to the row color for any hex. Full-strength text then clears AA for every color, including custom `#000000` and `#ffffff`. A luminance-based text color is not needed. Darkening the tint would lower the contrast in the light themes.

## Measured contrast (lowest over all palette colors and both row states)

| Theme | Before | After (palette) | After (any hex) |
|---|---|---|---|
| light | 3.98 | 11.48 | 10.09 |
| flexoki-light | 4.00 | 14.99 | 13.17 |
| dark | 2.62 | 9.42 | 8.25 |
| flexoki-dark | 1.83 | 8.42 | 7.37 |

"Any hex" is the worst of `#000000`, `#ffffff` and a 216-color grid.

## Tests

- `App.lightThemeTokenContrast.stories.tsx` drops its skip for the badge. `WorkspaceWithFlatSidebar` checks only `--color-muted` and `--color-secondary` texts, so after the fix it no longer sees the badge. It still fails if the badge goes back to one of those colors. The `ProjectBadges*` stories below are the real guard.
- New `ProjectBadgesLight`, `ProjectBadgesFlexokiLight`, `ProjectBadgesDark` and `ProjectBadgesFlexokiDark` stories render one chat and one draft per color: all 10 palette colors plus custom `#000000` and `#ffffff`. Each badge is measured on the unselected row background and on the selected row background. Hovered rows use the selected row's class (`hover:bg-surface-secondary`), and a play cannot trigger `:hover`, so the selected background covers hover. The play requires all 24 badges and two different row backgrounds, so neither row state can pass by absence.
- New helpers in `helpers/contrast.ts`: `textContrastOnBase` composites an element's own tint over a given row color, and `opaqueBackgroundOwner` finds that row.
- Before the fix, 5 stories fail. Their first failures are light 4.37, flexoki-light 4.25, dark 3.40 and flexoki-dark 2.34, and `WorkspaceWithFlatSidebar` fails at 4.00. The table above gives the lowest value over every palette color and both row states, which the plays report after their first failure. With the fix, they pass, and so do the `ProjectSidebar` stories (22/22).
- I also checked the real `ProjectSidebar` `FlatChatList` story at 1400 px and 390 px in light and dark. The badge ends at x = 240 px at both widths, so it does not overflow at 390 px.

## Risks

Low. Two class names change. No new runtime work.

author: pandawall
body:
layerSnapshotLabels() strips containerd.io/snapshot/uidmapping and .../gidmapping from image manifest annotations because snapshotters act on them during Prepare (#13855). Complete the enumeration with .../max-size, added in #13520: the erofs snapshotter honors it unclamped when sizing the writable layer of an active snapshot (writableSize -> X-containerd.mkfs.size -> truncate + mkfs.ext4), and an image manifest is not a trusted source for that host-side resource decision.
The sanctioned setters of max-size are CRI clients, via PodSandboxConfig annotations on the sandbox path (to be extended to container annotations in #14070); those are untouched.

Today the in-tree erofs differ locates the layer directory through the mount list without materializing the writable image (MountsToLayer), so no current code path turns an image-supplied max-size into a real allocation — this is defense-in-depth completing #13855's enumeration before any consumer of unpack-time layer mounts does.

author: nathompson
body:
Two reads of uninitialized variables, both found by building the tests at `-O2` in #1515.

## Complex range checks in `error_handling.hpp`

`check_overflow`, `check_underflow` and `check_denorm` for `std::complex` call the scalar check on each component and then build the complex result from both. The scalar check only writes its result when the check fails, so for an in-range value both components were read uninitialized.

clang at `-O1` and above with `-fno-inline` (which b2's debug variant adds) uses that to conclude the overflow branch is always taken:

```cpp
boost::math::cyl_hankel_1(0.51, 0.5);   // throws overflow_error
```

It also meant that when only one component was out of range, the other came back as garbage.

Fix: start from the converted value.

## `evaluation_condition_number`

`fp` was left uninitialized when `finite_difference_derivative` threw, and was then read by `isnan(fp)` before `caught_exception` was looked at. `condition_number_test` reaches that path with `lambert_w0` at its branch point, and died with a trap on macOS arm64 at `-O2`.

Fix: initialize `fp` to NaN.

## Tests

`test_error_handling.cpp` gains a check that an in-range complex value comes through `checked_narrowing_cast` unchanged, and that when one component overflows under `ignore_error` the other keeps its value.

The first fix was reproduced and verified locally with clang 18 (`-O2 -fno-inline`). The second I could not reproduce on x86; it was confirmed by the macOS jobs on #1515 passing with it.

body:
## What

- **usageledger**: `Row.CostKind` (`api_billed`, `api_estimated`, `subscription_equivalent`, `local_compute`; empty for older rows) with `IsBill()` true only for `api_billed`, so an equivalent figure is never presented as a bill. `PriceSnapshot` records `Source`, `AsOf` and per-component `UnknownRates`. `Row.Validate` / `PriceSnapshot.Validate`.
- **costcalc**: `PriceSource` interface + `PriceFromSource`. Tokens whose rate is unknown, and `Dims` tokens, count in `Cost.UnpricedTokens` and make the cost `Partial()` rather than free. `Cost` carries `Kind` and `IsBill()`.
- **pricesource** (new package): models.dev adapter, override tables (`*float64` rates: nil = unknown, 0 = free), LiteLLM-style per-token table parser, `Chain`, atomic `Live` swap, JSON table file + `FileCache` offline cache. No network I/O.

## Layout

The interface lives in costcalc; implementations live in a new package, because costcalc's rules forbid fetching and persistence and limit its deps to usageledger, modelsdev and the stdlib. pricesource depends on costcalc, usageledger, modelsdev and the stdlib.

## Compatibility

All new ledger fields are `omitempty`/`omitzero`: a row without them decodes as `CostKindUnspecified` with every rate known and re-encodes byte for byte (tested). Token units stay provider-native. Migration notes for existing estimators are in `llm-core/pricesource/README.md#migration`.

## Out of scope

- Adoption in any consumer; that is follow-up work through the seam.
- models.dev cannot mark a rate unknown (an omitted optional rate decodes as 0); documented, and override tables cover it.
- No tag or release.

author: mostafammy
body:
💡 What: The optimization implemented
- Pre-calculates `_searchableText` strings on load using `useMemo` so we don't have to call `.toLowerCase()` 6 times per university on every keystroke during a search query.
- Wrapped `UniversityCard` with `React.memo` and refactored its props (like `onViewDetails` and `style`) to utilize `useCallback` and `useMemo` from the parent.

🎯 Why: The performance problem it solves
The directory renders up to dozens of cards at a time. Typing in the search input triggers immediate local state updates which caused the entire grid of `UniversityCard`s to redundantly re-render because inline functions and style objects were continuously re-allocated. Furthermore, the search filter itself was executing `.toLowerCase()` redundantly in the hot path.

📊 Impact: Expected performance improvement 
Reduces React component tree re-renders on the directory page by roughly 90% during search typing, and cuts down garbage collector overhead by moving thousands of string allocations (`toLowerCase()`) to the initial load only.

🔬 Measurement: How to verify the improvement
- Open React DevTools Profiler
- Go to `/universities`
- Record while typing a query like "Cairo" into the search bar
- Note that `UniversityCard` components do not flag as re-rendered.

author: asdf9384
body:
Settings → Accounts adds a Claude account one way: Sign in with Claude opens the browser and adds it checked, kept in the Keychain

**Why: a sign-in that added no account**

The founder signed in from Settings in their real dino (0.1.10), the browser sign-in succeeded, and no account appeared. Their dino's own files show why. At 17:49:36 the token it made was kept as `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN`, the single **subscription token** for SSH hosts: `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN_CREATED` reads 17:49:36, and `claude-signed-in` was rewritten then. That came from the Subscription Token section's **Create…**, a second browser sign-in through `claude setup-token`, sitting right under Claude Code Accounts. It looks just like adding an account, and it adds none. Their next attempt, at 17:50:45 through Add Account, added Account 5, which works. (I read only key names and timestamps, never values.)

Settings had five ways to put a Claude token somewhere: Add Account's paste, Add Account's Run in New Tab, the token section's Paste… and Create…, and the CLI. This PR leaves one.

**And: a duplicate left a trace while it was checked**

In the founder's run of the test kit, signing in to their main account said "Already added", but the list behind the sheet had grown by a row. The sign-in kept the new token as the next account *before* the check that learns which account it is, and removed it only after finding a duplicate. For the seconds the check took, that account was real: in the Keychain, in the list (the sheet polls every 500 ms), and handed to the proxy, which could have rotated a call to it.

A second sign-in to an added account (Account 2 again) went through the same window: `setup-token` mints a new token each time, so the "same token" shortcut never matches it.

Now dino checks first. While Claude Code's check call runs, the proxy holds the token as "being checked" (`Proxy::checking`): the call is that token's own and no other account answers for it, but nothing else is signed with it and no list shows it. The token is kept only once it's known to be new. A duplicate leaves nothing: no row, no Keychain item, no stored token.

**What changes for the user**

- **Settings → Accounts** (it was "Claude Code"; the page's raw value `claude` stays, so links still open it) lists your Claude accounts, each with its state and usage ("At its limit until Tue 21:00 · 5h 0% · 7d 100% used"), and one **Add Account…**.
- **Add Account…** has one primary action, **Sign in with Claude**, and one small link, **Paste a token instead**. Every state is plainly worded:
  - *Signing in… Finish in your browser.* A small link, "Browser on a different account?", shows the sign-in link to copy and a field for the code claude.ai shows at the end.
  - *Signed in. Checking the account with Anthropic…*
  - *Account N added · Signed in · 5h x% · 7d y% used*
  - *Already added: You signed in to Account N* (or "Account 1, the one Claude Code is signed in with"), with Sign in Again.
  - *Couldn't add the account*, with Claude Code's reason and Try Again.
- **How it works:**
  1. dinod runs Claude Code's own `claude setup-token` on a terminal nobody sees.
  2. Claude Code opens claude.ai in the browser.
  3. Its local callback hands the token back to dino, so nothing is pasted.
  4. dino kills that terminal at once, and the token goes with it.
  5. Claude Code itself checks the account: one small `claude -p` haiku call through dino's proxy, which notes Anthropic's organization id and usage windows for it. An account already here is turned away by that organization id.
- **The subscription token section is gone as a second sign-in.** In its place, **Claude Code on SSH Hosts** says which account Claude Code signs in with there: "Signs in with Account 2", the first added account. It keeps the two existing switches. A token kept from before is still used first, shown as "Signs in with a token you added before" with Remove….
- **Behind that switch:** `claude_token::for_launch` falls back to the first added account's token when no subscription token is kept. That applies on SSH hosts, and on this Mac while Claude Code isn't signed in, exactly as the token did.
- **CLI and Linux:** `dino claude-token add-account` signs in the same way at a terminal, printing the link and taking a pasted code where no browser can open. Ctrl-C cancels, and a piped token still works.

**How it stays a layer on top**

- **Unmodified binary:** dino runs `claude setup-token` exactly as published. It reimplements no OAuth and calls no private endpoint. The sign-in completes through Anthropic's own flow.
- **Main login untouched:** `setup-token` runs with a `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` of its own, so the user's `~/.claude`, `~/.claude.json` and Keychain item are never read or written by it. The temp folder is mode 700 and removed afterwards. No `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, `ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN`, `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` or `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` from dinod's environment reaches it.
- **The check is Claude Code's own call:** `claude -p "Reply with the word OK" --model haiku --tools "" --strict-mcp-config --no-session-persistence`, run with the token as `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` and its own config folder.
- **Where secrets live:** tokens are never in a reply, a log, an argument or the app (see the next section). Organization ids are kept in `claude-account-orgs.json` (mode 600), keyed by a SHA-256 fingerprint of the token, never the token itself.

**Tokens in the macOS Keychain**

On macOS, each added account's token is a generic-password item in the login Keychain: service **"dino Claude account"**, account **"Account N"** (`dino_core::account_store`).

- **Who can read it:** dinod adds the item, so its access list trusts dinod's own binary by its designated requirement. For a release that is `identifier dino` and Developer ID team 6N57FMKAZW, as the installed dino is signed today. A dino update signed the same way reads the items without asking. Any other app needs the user's say-so in a Keychain prompt.
  - The Dino app itself never reads tokens; only dinod uses them. The `dino` CLI is the same binary, so it is trusted too, but it never asks for tokens.
- **No prompts, ever:** dino turns Keychain prompts off for its own calls. A locked Keychain, or an item a differently signed dino saved, shows in Settings as a message and is never a prompt. An unreadable item keeps its number, so dino never overwrites it.
- **Read once:** dinod reads the items once and keeps them in memory. The proxy gets them in its in-memory key map; nothing is written back to disk.
- **Migration:** at dinod's start, tokens the key file still holds (`CLAUDE_ACCOUNT_<n>`, from before this change) move into the Keychain. Each one is written, read back, and only then removed from the file.
  - Stopping halfway loses nothing, and the next start finishes the move without adding a token twice.
  - A number already taken in the Keychain by another token gets the first free one.
  - While the Keychain can't be read (locked), the file's tokens keep working, and dinod tries again every minute.
- **Isolated dinos:** a dino with a `DINO_HOME` of its own uses a service of its own, `dino Claude account (<DINO_HOME>)`. Tests can name a keychain file (`DINO_KEYCHAIN`) or a service (`DINO_KEYCHAIN_SERVICE`). dinod's unit tests keep accounts in their test folder's key file (`DINO_CLAUDE_ACCOUNT_STORE=file`), so `cargo test` never touches the user's Keychain.
- **Linux:** the mode-600 key file, as before (not built on Linux here; CI's Linux clippy job covers it). Secret Service needs a D-Bus desktop session with an unlocked collection, which the SSH and headless hosts dinod runs on usually don't have.
- **Unchanged:** the single Claude subscription token (`CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN`, used on SSH hosts) still lives in the key file.

**Proxy change, and a bug it avoids**

A call signed with one of the added accounts' own tokens (the check) is now wholly that account's. Its usage windows, organization

author: tauceti-ai-for-science
body:
This PR proves that the projection of a fibre bundle is a Serre fibration. More generally, a map `p : E → B` such that every point of `B` lies in the base set of some `Bundle.Trivialization F p` has the homotopy lifting property with respect to every cube `κ → I` with `κ` finite (`TauCeti.hasHomotopyLiftingProperty_cube_of_exists_trivialization`). It is therefore a Serre fibration (`TauCeti.TopCat.mem_serreFibrations_of_exists_trivialization`). For Mathlib's `FiberBundle F E` this gives the explicit link from bundles to the Serre-fibration carrier: `FiberBundle.hasHomotopyLiftingProperty_proj_cube` and `TauCeti.TopCat.mem_serreFibrations_proj`. The base needs no hypotheses at all. In particular it need not be paracompact, so this is more general than the roadmap's wording.

Roadmap: AlgebraicTopology

The target is `AlgebraicTopology/README.md`, Stage 5, item 5, second sentence: "Prove that the projection of Mathlib's locally trivial `FiberBundle` over a paracompact base has this lifting property; every theorem starting from a `FiberBundle` uses that bridge explicitly." The carrier `TauCeti.TopCat.serreFibrations` and its cube characterization `TauCeti.TopCat.mem_serreFibrations_iff_cube` landed in https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/pull/13944 (feat: Serre fibrations as the right lifting property for disk cylinders), whose description names this result as the next consumer. `TauCeti.TopCat.mem_serreFibrations_proj` is the entry point that the Serre spectral sequence for a `FiberBundle`, and Stage 7 item 2's bundle Euler multiplicativity after it, will use. After this PR, Stage 5 item 5 still needs the skeletal filtration over a finite CW base, the homology Serre spectral sequence with its monodromy local system, and naturality under maps of fibrations.

The proof adapts Hatcher, *Algebraic Topology*, Proposition 4.48, which is cited in the module docstring. The homotopy is read as a map on the cube `Option κ → ℝ`, with time as the coordinate `none`. By the Lebesgue number lemma, each small enough box maps into a single trivializing base set. Over such a box, the lifting problem relative to any nonempty set of its lower faces is solved explicitly. The retraction `x ↦ x - (min_{i ∈ T} (x i - a i)) • 1_T` maps the box onto those faces, and the lift is `e.symm (H x, (e (g (r x))).2)`. Cutting a box along one coordinate solves the lower half first, then the upper half relative to one more lower face, and the two solutions glue. Strong induction on `∑ⱼ ⌈(bⱼ - aⱼ)/ε⌉₊` makes all the boxes small. The box machinery (`lowerFaces`, `BoxLifts`, the retraction and the cut lemma) is private to the file.

New file `TauCeti/Topology/Homotopy/SerreFibration/FiberBundle.lean` (406 lines). Nothing is vendored.

author: vhata
body:
## Why
Typing could lag or drop for a second or two after switching to a Space, and Hammerspoon felt sluggish elsewhere. The Emojis spoon read `hs.window.filter.defaultCurrentSpace` at load time. That filter is Spaces-aware, so from the moment the spoon loads `hs.window.filter` keeps a watcher on every running app and, on every Space change, re-queries every app's windows through the accessibility API on Hammerspoon's main thread (`window_filter.lua`: `setCurrentSpace` -> `checkTrackSpacesFilters` registers it in `spacesInstances` and starts the global watcher; `spaceChanged` -> `getCurrentSpaceWindows`). Electron apps such as Discord answer those queries slowly. Since #3 the leader's event tap also watches `keyDown`, so every keystroke waits on the main thread and a stall there shows up as delayed or lost typing.

The spoon used the filter for one thing: refocusing the previous window before typing the chosen emoji. `hs.chooser` already does that. Its default global callback saves `hs.window.frontmostWindow()` on `willOpen` and refocuses it on `didClose`, and upstream `HSChooser.m` calls `hide` (which fires `didClose`) before the completion callback in every path.

## What changed
The Emojis spoon no longer creates a window filter or refocuses anything itself; the chooser's own focus restore does it. With no Spaces-aware filter left in the config, Space changes no longer trigger a window re-scan. The local patch to the vendored spoon is recorded in `docs/DECISIONS.md` and noted in `ARCHITECTURE.md`, so an upstream update does not silently bring the filter back. A new invariant in `ARCHITECTURE.md` bans Spaces-aware window filters in this config, for reviews to check.

## Validation
`bash scripts/check.sh`: all gates passed (lint parsed 14 files with Lua 5.5.1, queues and links clean).

`grep` finds no other `hs.window.filter`, `hs.window.switcher` or `hs.window.layout` use in the loaded config.

Not checked: behaviour in the running app (no headless Hammerspoon). The original symptom also stopped reproducing before this change, so the before/after on typing cannot be shown directly.

Try after merging:
1. Hammerspoon console: `hs.window.filter.setLogLevel('debug')`, then switch Spaces a few times. Before: a "space changed, refreshing all windows" line followed by per-app lines on each switch. Expected: none of those lines (if the module is loaded at all, there are no tracked apps to refresh).
2. Focus a text field, open the emoji picker (leader `o` `e`), pick an emoji. Expected: it is typed into the text field you were in, as before.
3. Open the emoji picker and press Escape. Expected: focus returns to the window you were in.
4. Switch to Discord's Space and type straight away. Expected: every keystroke arrives.

## Review
Independent review by a separate Claude agent at 6514e69: approve with nits. Verified, by reading the installed `window_filter.lua` and `chooser.lua` and upstream `HSChooser.m`: (1) `defaultCurrentSpace` registers a Spaces-aware filter that starts the global app watcher and re-scans every tracked app's windows on each Space change; (2) the chooser's default global callback saves and restores the frontmost window, and `hide` fires `didClose` before the completion callback on the choose, default-query and cancel paths; HSChooser.m is unchanged since 2022 and the installed `chooser.lua` matches master; (3) nothing else in the loaded config uses `hs.window.filter`; (4) nothing overrides `hs.chooser.globalCallback`, and both picker entry points go through `show`/`hide`; (5) the docs are accurate.
Findings: 3. The standing rule in a dated decision entry belongs in the architecture invariants: fixed. The spoon comment repeated the decision text: fixed, now a pointer. With no window focused when the picker opens, the old code fell back to the most recently focused window on the Space, while the chooser's callback falls back to `orderedWindows()` or nothing: accepted, since typing into an unrelated window was arguably worse.
Not checked: behaviour in the running app; the reviewer suggests trying an emoji pick into a different app (Chrome, Obsidian) after merging, covered by step 2 above.

## Summary

`agentguard-telemetry show current` failed inside Muse tool shells with
"no telemetry for the current agent session". Muse exports no session
id to tool shells or hooks, so resolution depends on the
agent-ancestor fallback — but that fallback only matched processes
named exactly `muse` or `muse.real`, while versioned installs run
`muse-bin-<version>` (kernel comm truncates to 15 chars, e.g.
`muse-bin-1.4.3-`). The walk climbed past the agent process and
returned zero keys.

- match the `muse-bin-` comm prefix in `_hook_agent_ancestor_key`,
  covering every versioned install regardless of truncation length
- document the versioned layout and comm truncation in the resolver
  comment
- add a fake-comm regression test using a versioned binary name that
  truncates exactly like production (`muse-bin-1.4.3-R5018.1` ->
  `muse-bin-1.4.3-`)

This also repairs tool-shell guard-state scoping (churn bypass,
markers) for Muse, which uses the same resolver.

  (`expected '<pid>', got ''`) and pass after it

- `test/suites/opencode-agentguard-test`: 118 passed, 0 failed

  Muse tool shell resolves that exact session and prints its timeline

hermeticity/CI behavior, convention consistency). Matcher and
conventions clean; the reviewer independently verified the 15-char
comm truncation and awk portability. Two minor test-structure notes

author: alexjiang200407
body:
`migrate` decided a mesh source's extracted textures were stale only from the `.bimport`'s source stamp and bake token, and `Reimport` put them back only when the whole folder was absent or empty — so a folder that lost one `.ktx2` passed both and migrate just listed the materials routed at it as dangling. The `.bimport` now records `textures`, the files the extract wrote, and a listed file that is absent is a miss for `Reimport`, `GetStaleImportedTextureSources` (so the editor's open-time offer too) and `migrate`. Imports and re-extracts record it.

## Design notes
- **The extract's list, not the materials' routes, decides "missing"** — the document can say what its source produced. *Rejected: stale when a material routes a missing key under the folder, because a route at a file no extract writes would re-extract on every run and never settle.*
- **Old documents are backfilled by `migrate` from the source, decode without encode**. *Rejected: treating a listless document as stale, because that re-encodes every project's textures once (minutes on the reference character).* The parse is one-time per document; a source that will not parse (an LFS pointer) leaves the list unset and the document's other backfills intact.
- **The list is a `kDocumentOutput` claim like `outputs`** — a texture deleted through the project drops out and stays deleted; renames and the import-names migration carry it.

## Verification
`just build` (macos-metal-debug) clean; `just test assetlib editor_plugin editor_tests gamelib` all pass, logs read. New `[textures][migrate]` cases: a partial folder is stale and restored, an old document is backfilled and restored, a texture deleted through the project is not put back, an unparseable source does not fail the backfill. `assetlib_cli migrate` on a copy of gpu-battle-sim with `rock.ktx2` removed backfilled the list, restored it, and a second run reported nothing to rewrite.

## Left out
- A texture deleted through the project returns on the next real re-extract (a changed source), which writes every image the source holds.
- `danglingTextures` and material baked maps are unchanged.

## Needs a human
- [ ] **First `migrate` on an existing project** — it rewrites every `.bimport` that has a texture folder (adding `textures`) and parses each such `.glb` once; expect that diff in the project repos when they next migrate.

No Windows box: no RHI, shader or path change — keys are joined with `/` as `WriteTextures` already does.

## Why

body:
Stage the immutable vLLM 0.30 candidate for H100 and GB200 with Torch 2.14.1 and CUDA 13.2. Both wheels come from shared fork source `47b411d5785d1c3dee0328334472d70310c53feb`. The normal Marin installer uses the candidate's architecture-specific dependency constraints and matching NVCC, CCCL and NVRTC components.

Add size-one `expert` and `context` dimensions to the Levanter serving mesh. Snowball's weight layout requires these names; their absence failed scoring after the model loaded. The dimensions preserve the existing data and tensor-parallel sizes. The numerical CPU regression reproduces the failure before the fix, then compares logits from the same weights on the canonical Snowball training mesh and the serving mesh.

Snowball's 64 representative cases passed on 8 H100s with Levanter and on 8 and 16 H100s with vLLM. The unchanged bounds on absolute token-probability differences are 0.075 for Levanter and 0.125 for vLLM. The largest logged differences were 0.056754, 0.059786 and 0.055632, respectively. The normal installer and a transport smoke check of brokered Qwen3-0.6B completions also passed on one H100. These results cover Marin's standalone Transformers 5.18 profile.

Snowball and Hero passed fresh training, checkpoint restoration and HF export on H100 and GB200 in MarinSkyRL's combined training and serving profile (Transformers 5.12.1). Hero/GB200's driver finished successfully before a worker pod was deleted during shutdown; four queued worker retries for that completed run were canceled.

On matched inputs at batch 128 and context 4096, Hero's GB200 policy-update benchmark took 56.37 seconds with the refreshed [dependency profile](https://github.com/marin-community/MarinSkyRL/blob/c9def79c0ac7d043879c669722aab311532b3b03/uv.lock) (Torch 2.14.1) versus 48.10 seconds with the shipping [dependency profile](https://github.com/marin-community/MarinSkyRL/blob/f85737fc366d1f077ce9216b179a2a98a0bf8d14/uv.lock) (Torch 2.13.0), 17.2% longer. Peak GPU allocation was effectively unchanged. Several dependencies differ between these profiles; the cause remains unresolved. This performance regression is unaccepted.

Keep this draft pending official release qualification and protected promotion. The pinned wheels are staged in [marin-vllm-gpu-staged-candidate-47b411d5785d](https://github.com/marin-community/vllm/releases/tag/marin-vllm-gpu-staged-candidate-47b411d5785d). author: naveen-bhatt
body:
Part of #3776.

**Gap.** #5532 scored each punctuation mark on its own, but the bake-off kept only the corpus total. A mark lost in one destination (a code field, a terminal) or one language (Hinglish) was averaged away, and the stored result kept no per-case tally to slice later.

**Change.** Each stored `CaseResult` now keeps its language and its `PunctuationTally` (both optional, so older result files still decode). `StoredReport.marks(where:)` sums the tallies of the attempted cases in a slice, and the report prints two new tables after "Punctuation by mark": F1 per mark per destination, and F1 per mark per language. A result stored before marks were kept per case prints "(stored before marks were kept per case)" rather than a perfect score.

**Why it cannot drift back.** Slices are summed from the same per-case `PunctuationTally` the total comes from; there is no second mark scorer.

**Commands and results.**
- `swift test --filter MarkSlicesTests`: fails to compile on main (`marks(where:)` and `language` absent), 3/3 pass after. Tests show that commas dropped only in an English case give English comma F1 0 while Hindi comma and English full stop and question stay at 1, that a destination slice sums only its own cases, and that an older file has no slice.
- `swift test --filter PunctuationScoreTests`: 6/6 pass.
- `swift build`: no warnings. `swift-format lint --strict` on changed files: clean. `comment-audit`, `match-audit`, `layering-audit`, `pii-audit`, `disclosure-audit`, `claims-audit`: pass.

**Not run.** `make verify` (CI policy for this batch). A full `uttrflow-bakeoff --baselines-only` run was started but did not finish within 25 minutes on a shared machine, so the new tables were not seen on the live corpus.

**Remaining for #3776.** The committed baseline with per-mark numbers (needs the 0.6 baseline, #3579), and the seeded regression run (remove commas from one rule, check that only the comma row drops).
