author: santi-rl
body:
Un login que verificaba la contraseña anterior podía generar una sesión válida después de un reset concurrente, porque el JWT recibía un `iat` posterior al restablecimiento. SC-11 vincula las sesiones nuevas al hash exacto verificado mediante una versión HMAC opaca, relee la cuenta y valida ese vínculo en autenticación obligatoria y opcional.

Nivel 2 por autenticación. Sin migraciones, dependencias, cambios fiscales ni pasos nuevos. Conserva SC-08, revocación temporal, cuentas inactivas, correos legacy, roles, asignaciones y recuperación administrativa/por consola.

Las sesiones legacy válidas mantienen su compatibilidad temporal. Una sesión legacy ya afectada antes del despliegue no puede distinguirse retrospectivamente; el contrato documenta este límite. Un reset posterior a la relectura puede producir una respuesta con un token ya revocado, que el siguiente control backend rechaza. La reversión de código reabre SC-11; se prefiere una corrección hacia adelante.

Validación:

- Cinco carreras deterministas en PostgreSQL descartable con sesiones independientes: reset durante bcrypt, después del commit de login y timestamp de reset asignado antes de leer la credencial, con transacción aún abierta. Contraseña vieja rechazada, nueva válida; ambos controles de autenticación incluidos.
- SQLite/ASGI: reset administrativo y por consola durante bcrypt, desactivación/borrado concurrentes, campos malformados, privacidad del token y compatibilidad legacy, incluidos tokens emitidos después de un reset anterior.
- Suite completa local backend con PostgreSQL: 1.926 aprobadas, cobertura 75,04 % (mínimo 69 %), una omisión por falta de permiso de Windows para crear symlinks en un test de soporte. Las 56 integraciones PostgreSQL pasaron; CI Linux debe cubrir también ese caso sin omisiones.
- Frontend: 291 tests, umbrales de cobertura, tipos, lint y build verdes; E2E: 39; scripts: 30.
- Smoke real local: Alembic, API, PostgreSQL y preview Vue verdes. Auditorías pip y npm sin vulnerabilidades conocidas.
- Autoreview autorizado para este corte: Codex gpt-5.6-sol high, P0–P2, escaneo TruffleHog de entradas congeladas y cada pack, aislamiento y web deshabilitada; scoped-clean, sin hallazgos. Dos particiones del mismo corte, sin rondas adicionales ni cambios posteriores en sus fuentes.
- QA de esta unidad: recorridos reales ASGI de login/reset/me con cuentas sintéticas y los mismos emisores/permisos; no hay cambios visibles de pantalla. El QA contable del candidato completo mantiene su puerta separada.

Matriz documental:

| Fuente | Resultado |
|---|---|
| VISION.md | Revisada; sin modificación, sin fricción adicional ni nueva política. |
| ROADMAP.md | Revisado; futuro y orden conservados, incluida la indicación sin prioridad «Olvidé mi contraseña». |
| CHANGELOG.md | Agregado el comportamiento SC-11 en Unreleased. |
| current-status.md | Cierre de código y continuación por ensayo/QA exactos, sin acreditar producción. |
| development-portfolio.md | SC-11 implementado; política de contraseñas y olvido mantienen alcances separados. |
| sc-11-login-reset-design.md | Contrato, invariantes, carreras, límites legacy y recuperación. |
| security.md / índice agentes | Vínculo de tokens y diseño SC-11. |
| docs/api/README.md | Semántica de login/reset concurrentes y compatibilidad, mismas rutas/status/schema. |
| manual-qa.md | Recorrido sintético reutilizable y carreras reservadas al harness. |
| Dossier v0.3.8 | Incluido SC-11; continúan respaldo/ensayo, QA del rango y decisiones de release/despliegue. |
| README / backend README / manual usuario / soporte | Revisados: comandos, recuperación y acciones del usuario conservados. |
| testing / calidad / CONTRIBUTING / overview | Revisados: mismas puertas, harness y arquitectura; evidencia de esta corrida aquí. |
| Checklist fiscal / ARCA / notas WS / setup | No aplica al diff de autenticación: no modifica emisión, certificados, fechas, numeración, permisos por emisor ni infraestructura de instalación. El checklist acumulado del candidato permanece. |

No se accedió a producción, no se emitió CAE y no se incluyeron datos ni evidencia privados. La integración aprobada no crea una release ni despliega.

Cierre de integración (10/10/2026):

- [CI del PR](https://github.com/Santi-RL/FactuFlow/actions/runs/38030525940): siete checks verdes sobre `4ed902d37c98e27f41e19504925951a7228911db`.
- Squash integrado en main: `0bcc4c2e303b526fddfecef30e98fcf09ff12eef`. Árbol idéntico al head revisado: `d0057b621e5f59bed50705bad5baae27952ff002`.
- [CI de main](https://github.com/Santi-RL/FactuFlow/actions/runs/38031608099): siete checks verdes sobre ese SHA exacto. Tanto PR como main aprobaron 1.927 pruebas backend sin omisiones, cobertura 75,04 %, 291 frontend y 39 E2E.
- Rama temporal local y remota eliminada tras aprobar main. Checkout main limpio y sincronizado, sin divergencias.
- Siguiente puerta del candidato: ensayo aislado de actualización/recuperación con las imágenes del SHA exacto, QA contable del rango y preflight/respaldo aplicables. Tag/release y despliegue mantienen sus decisiones separadas.

author: caomengxuan666
body:
Closes #1156

## 实测驱动的逐项处置表

| # | 疑点 | 实测结论 | 处置 |
|---|------|----------|------|
| 1 | `uninstall` 的 y/N 确认不读管道 stdin | **证伪（本分支已修复）**。工作树构建实测：`echo y \| wpm uninstall jq` 正确确认并卸载；`n`/EOF 中止且不删文件。0095bab（已在 origin/main）改为 `std::getline(std::cin, ...)`。#1154 事故中的旧发布版二进制早于该提交 | **already-fixed** + 回归测试钉死行为（管道 y / 管道 n / EOF 三例） |
| 2a | `install --force` 未在 help 的 install 说明中出现 | **属实**。`--help` 的 install 行仅写 "install one or more packages"，Options 段的 `-f, --force` 未说明可重装 | **fixed**：help install 行补 "use --force to reinstall or overwrite" + 测试断言 |
| 2b | 重装时被锁文件静默跳过仍报成功 | **证伪（现状已正确）**。实测锁住 `usr/bin/jq.exe`（无 FILE_SHARE_DELETE 打开）后：`install --force` → exit 1 + `wpm: failed to install ... being used by another process`；`uninstall -y` → exit 1 + `failed to remove`，removed=0 failed=1。#1154 实测的"报成功但文件未变"根因是下载缓存键不含版本（疑点 3），非锁文件跳过 | **already-correct**（补锁文件回归测试，install/uninstall 各一，断言非零退出） |
| 3 | 缓存键不含版本 | 本 PR **不处置**（修复进行中，关联 #1154 的 PR 负责），见 issue 备注 | **defer**（归属 #1154） |
| 4 | `outdated` / `index update` / `install` 索引副本不一致窗口期 | **属实且比"窗口期"更严重**。`outdated` 用本地索引版本 vs 远程索引版本：一旦 `wpm index update`，本地==远程，此后**永久**报 "all installed packages are up to date"，即使磁盘上仍是旧版（receipt 里记录的实装版本为 1.0.0、远程 2.0.0 时仍报无更新，已实测复现） | **fixed**：`outdated` 改以 install receipts（`.wpm/installed/*.json`，且校验 destinations 仍在磁盘）为已装版本来源，无 receipt 的旧式安装回退到本地索引；`outdated` 从此不依赖本地索引副本。+回归测试 |
| 5 | automation 友好性：`-y` 覆盖、`--json` 缺失 | `-y`：**已生效**——唯一交互提示是 uninstall 确认，`-y`/--yes 任意位置解析均跳过（实测 `wpm -y uninstall jq` 与 `wpm uninstall jq -y` 等价）；GNU/apt 惯例上 `-y` 不应隐含 `--force` 重装，维持现状。`--json`：install 缺失（实测输出人读文本）、list 已有 | **fixed（分层交付第一批）**：`install --json` 输出单一 JSON payload（schema 1、results[]、failed，状态机 installed/already_installed/would_install/not_found/not_installable/preflight_failed/download_failed/error，errors[] 内联），全部人读进度走 stderr，下载进度条在 --json 下禁用；`already_installed` 按 apt 惯例 exit 0。附带 `index update --json` 输出 payload（且命令内自动刷新不再向调用方 stdout 泄漏第二个 JSON 文档）。+回归测试（含 stdout 纯净性断言） |

## 实现说明

- `outdated`：receipts 优先（`receipt_install_records`），本地索引回退仅覆盖无 receipt 的历史安装；比较基准从"本地索引副本"改为"磁盘实装版本"，疑点 4 的不一致窗口整体消除。
- `install --json`：`install_package` 增加 `json_result` 出参，全部退出路径经 `finish()` 记录结果；`preflight_install_destinations` 增加 messages 出参供 payload 的 errors[] 使用；`download_artifact`/`extract_archive`/`copy_artifact_files`/`create_package_shims`/`create_package_aliases`/`cleanup_legacy_flat_artifacts`/`refresh_index_once`/`update_index` 增加 json 路由参数。
- `wpm restore` / `install --from` 走同一 `install_packages` 通道，自动获得 --json 支持。

## 测试

- `tests/winuxcmd-tests.exe --gtest_filter=wpm.*`：**50/50 通过**（41 存量 + 9 新增，覆盖管道 y/n/EOF、-y 跳过提示、help force 文案、锁文件 install/uninstall 非零退出、outdated 在 index update 后的 receipt 锚定、install --json 精确 payload 与 stdout 纯净性、index update --json payload）。
- `--gtest_filter=winuxcmd.*`：28/28 通过。
- 端到端手工探针（file:// 索引夹具、锁句柄、管道）：全部符合预期，过程见 PR 描述（构建于 VS18 + Ninja，`-DBUILD_FFI=OFF`，pcre2 复用主仓缓存）。

## 后续（不在本 PR）

- 按 AGENTS.md 的跨仓同步要求，新增/变更的 i18n key（`command.wpm.custom_help` fallback、`command.wpm.error.download_failed_generic/copy_failed/shim_failed/alias_failed`）需在 `unixwin/winuxcmd-i18n` 补 zh-CN 目录并 bump VERSION；本 PR 先落英文 fallback。
- 疑点 3（缓存键不含版本）由 #1154 的修复承接。

author: s3ntin3l8
body:
## Summary
- Bundle tree rows get archive and delete icons (on hover/focus; hidden for single-document bundles, which the bundle actions already cover). Both go through a confirm dialog and a toast; removing the active `?doc=` clears the param so the pane falls back to the lead.
- New `useDocumentAction()` calls the existing `POST /triage/documents/{id}/dismiss` and `DELETE /triage/documents/{id}`; it refetches instead of dropping the bundle from the cache.

## Backend fixes needed to make that safe
- Archived documents no longer get confirmed into the case: `confirm_bundle` skips `DISMISSED` docs, as do sub-group initialisation, cover-letter selection, batch analysis (`analyze_batch` + `batch_analyzer`) and `get_bundle_by_batch_id`. The feed, sub-group `doc_ids` and the lead doc already derive from non-dismissed docs, so the lead is re-picked automatically (now covered by a test).
- Doc delete returns 409 `in_flight` while a stage is running/retrying and hard-deletes its ActionItems (as the batch path does).
- Deleting a cover letter detaches its enclosures first. `Document.children` is `cascade="all, delete-orphan"`, so without this the ORM would silently delete the enclosures without their cleanup.
- `DocumentService.delete_document` removes the batch's `raw_source_path` file when it drops the batch with its last doc (also benefits `DELETE /documents/{id}`).

No API schema change, so `make api-types` produces no diff.

## Test plan
- [x] `make lint`, `make test` (2010 passed), `make frontend-test`
- [x] New unit tests: archived doc excluded from confirm, lead re-picked, doc delete in-flight / action items / cover-letter / last-doc raw file; integration: archive one doc of two, delete refused in flight; vitest: per-doc archive confirms and calls the doc endpoint, clearing `?doc=`

P1 follow-ups (apex): the last of the three. It re-copies react #64's shared files and ports its member fixes, so they work against express 2.1.0 (#100).

**Changed behaviour**
- **A member already gone.** Staff and member paths, removal and role change are all covered.
  - The member is recognised by express's `member_not_found` code. On older APIs it falls back to a 404 with "Member not found".
  - The dialog shows "That member is no longer in this tenant.", as react does, waits for the refetched list, and moves focus to the Members heading.
- **Last-owner checks count owners the way express does.**
  - On the Staff page (the platform tenant), only active owners count (`user.active !== false`).
  - On a customer tenant, every owner counts.
  - This applies to Leave, Remove and role change. Express's 409 stays as the safety net.

**Maintainer changes**
- **Byte re-copies from react 9d46e88**, checked with `cmp`:

author: krzysztof-cieslak
body:
# Wrapper-free generic Option boundaries

Option of a type variable can now use the existing boxed None sentinel. Its payload arrives in standardized uniform representation, so it cannot collide with that internal sentinel. Generic lookup bodies remain shared, with no type specialization.

Cross-scheme conversions change only the None sentinel; owned Some payloads pass through. Unannotated data inspections force the standard layout, including generic results instantiated at concrete Float and nested Option types. First-class, captured and data-slot boundaries retain their normal conversions.

## Matched measurements
CPU 1, three interleaved before/after/OCaml passes of 21 measured executions after two warmups. Workload sources and peers are unchanged; answers match.

| Workload | Before / after time | After / OCaml time |
|---|---:|---:|
| FibMemo | 1.017× | 1.356× |
| GameOfLife | 0.999× | 1.145× |
| OptionEval | 1.006× | 0.736× |
| OptionPath | 1.297× | 0.714× |
| OptionTreeFind | 1.001× | 0.526× |
| GraphBFS | 1.011× | 0.709× |

OptionPath improves about 30%. Other controls are near flat or modestly faster; FibMemo remains an open gap. Initial cross-scheme handling exposed a crash in the existing generic-combinator regression; correct sentinel conversion and standard-layout constraints fix it. Earlier measurements using temporary standard wrappers for cross-scheme conversion remain archived.

## Validation
257 Core, 539 RC and 401 codegen cases pass, along with 20 existing niche cases and 11 new cross-module generic-Option cases. Tests cover Float/function/tuple payloads, nested Some/None layers, collection storage, repeated captures and allocation-flat cross-scheme forwarding. All embedded standard-library contracts, 90 native cases, 35 HTTP cases, 22 bundle cases, 23 backend incremental cases, stream/daemon stdin and opaque/pattern regressions pass. All 20 Perceus guards pass. Workspace build, all-target/all-feature Clippy, formatting and diff checks pass.


Fixes #586.

Measurements: https://gist.github.com/Krzysztof-Cieslak/1f15aeb078058f278258c918846090c8#file-generic-option-sentinels-md

author: leonam-daris
body:
**Causa raiz:** a stack separou o hbbs/hbbr do painel e o painel enviava os comandos para 127.0.0.1 (`connection refused` em 21115/21117). O hbbs só aceita comandos vindos de 127.0.0.1.

**Correção:** encaminhador `nc` no contêiner `servidor` (portas internas 21125 e 21127, não publicadas) + patch 0018 na API (`NEXTEC_SERVER_CMD_HOST=servidor`) + prazo de leitura de 3 s para comandos de gravação.

Testado com contêineres separados: h, aur (ler e gravar), u, tb em hbbs e hbbr; servidor reinicia e o painel volta sozinho; servidor parado mostra mensagem clara. A alternativa `network_mode: service:servidor` foi testada e descartada: reiniciar o servidor deixa o painel sem rede.

**Aplicação:** recria o contêiner `servidor` (entrypoint novo), então o acesso remoto cai por alguns segundos no redeploy. Fazer em horário de pouco uso.

body:
## 背景 `Deploy to Aliyun OSS` [#79](https://github.com/fit2cloud-dev/fit2cloud-docs/actions/runs/38021260440) 失败的根因已由 [#145](https://github.com/fit2cloud-dev/fit2cloud-docs/pull/145) 修复（`community_faq.md` 第 74 行裸 `<参数>`）。 但那条坏内容是 **`auto-community-faq` 工作流自动生成的**，人工只修文档不堵源头，下周一还会复发。本 PR 从生成链路侧根治。 ## 现有链路的漏洞 ``` 芝麻群聊 → community_faq.py → commit 到 chore/weekly-community-faq → 自动开 PR → 人工合并进 main → 手动触发 Deploy → npm run build 💥 到这里才发现 ``` 坏内容在**前面所有关口都没被拦住**： 1. **脚本零 MDX 防护**：`_render_entry` 把模型输出的 `body` 逐行原样落盘，现有后处理（`_strip_trailing_citation`、空行收敛）全是排版层面，没有一行做词法安全。 2. **CI 无门禁**：`.github/` 下搜遍没有任何 MDX 校验（根目录 `check_mdx.js` 写死单文件、既不在 CI 也没接 `npm` scripts）。内容 PR 不跑 build，**build 校验只在手动触发的发布工作流里** —— 等于「先合进 main、发布时才知道炸了」，代价是整站发不出去。 3. **生成的工作流每周定时自动开 PR**，人审只看 diff、没有编译结果可看。 ## 修复 给生成链路补**三层护栏**（按你的选择：只做脚本侧 A 层）： ### 1. 提示词层 —— `PASS2_SYSTEM` 新增硬性要求第 7 条 禁止裸尖括号占位符 / 裸 HTML 标签 / 裸链接；真实的尖括号写法必须包进反引号或代码块。 ### 2. 转义层 —— `sanitize_entry` / `sanitize_mdx_text` 把代码块与行内代码之外的裸 `<`、`{` 转义成 HTML 实体（`<` / `{`），**渲染结果与原文一致、内容不丢**。 覆盖 `title` / `new_section` / `question` / `body` / `see_also` **全部**会落到页面的字段。特别说明 `new_section`：它会变成 `## 标题` 行，最初漏掉它就会出现「逐条校验通过、整页构建失败」的盲区（实测已补上）。 ### 3. 校验层 —— `ensure_mdx_safe_entry` / `mdx_compile_check` - **逐条**：按最终渲染形态用 `@mdx-js/mdx` 真实编译。**原文能过就原样保留**（避免误伤仓库里合法的 JSX），过不了才转义挽救，转义后仍不过则丢弃该条。 - **整页**：写回页面前再校验一次，不通过返回**退出码 5** 且**不写入页面**。 ### 关于兜底路径（关键） workflow 的 sparse-checkout 只取 `.github/` + md，**不含 `package.json` / `node_modules`**，跑不了真实编译，所以设计了纯正则兜底 —— 且**必须做增量**：只报「新页面比原页面多出来」的危险模式。 原因是实测出来的：仓库现有文档本就大量使用**合法 JSX**（`
`、`
` 等），绝对扫描在 `jumpserver-docs` 的 198 个文件里**命中 160 个、全是误报**。拿它当闸门会每周把自动化自己拦住。改成按模式计数相减后，存量合法写法自动抵消，**自比对误报 0/198**。 ### workflow 侧 把退出码 5 单独成码（原方案复用退出码 4 = 大模型失败，会把排查方向带偏），并输出具体指引。 ## 验证 实测用 `@mdx-js/mdx` 真实编译，覆盖全部字段与危险写法： | 用例 | 原始 | 护栏后 | |---|---|---| | `title` 裸标签 `配置 <域名> 怎么填？` | FAIL | PASS | | `question` 裸标签 `报错 <错误码>？` | FAIL | PASS | | `body` 裸标签 `在<参数>中配置` | FAIL | PASS | | `see_also` 裸标签 `详见 ` | FAIL | PASS | | `new_section` 裸标签 `5 <新增> 小节` | FAIL | PASS | | `body` 花括号对象 `{display:"block"}` | FAIL | PASS | | `body` `
` 标签 | FAIL | PASS | **零误伤**（应原样保留，全部 `未改动=True`）：代码块内尖括号、行内代码 `` `<域名>` ``、比较运算 `a < b`、纯汉字花括号 `{参数}`、合法 JSX `
x
`、超链接 `[文档](/a/b)`。 **增量检测误报**：自比对 0/198 个文件；新引入裸标签条目命中 1 处、合法 JSX 与代码块内标签命中 0。 **现有页面**：`jumpserver-docs/faq/community_faq.md` 编译通过（修复前为 `FAIL: Expected a closing tag for <参数>`）。 ## 改动范围 - `.github/scripts/community_faq.py`：+267 / -7 - `.github/workflows/auto-community-faq.yml`：+15 / -8 纯 CI 链路改动，**不触碰任何文档内容**，对站点渲染无影响。 > 注：workflow 与脚本需在 `fit2cloud-dev/fit2cloud-docs` 内生效，合并后即对本仓库的定时任务生效。 ## 未做的部分（供决策） - **B 层（全仓库 MDX lint + PR 门禁）**：能兜住所有内容 PR（不只社区 FAQ），本次未做 —— 你选择了只做 A 层。 - **C 层（部署工作流 build 预检）**：收益最低（已经炸了之后报错更清楚），未做。 - 另外发现一个**独立**的问题：`deploy-oss.yml` 只有手动触发，内容 PR 不跑 build，所以本次这类问题本质上只能靠「合进 main 后发布时」暴露。若不打算做 B 层，建议后续考虑给部署 workflow 加个 `pull_request` 触发的纯 build 校验 job。

body: Adds offline sqlite journal commands open, show, manual-close and fills without broker connectivity. Manual records are USER_DECLARED_UNVERIFIED; writer requires --record-only, private database stored outside repo, symlinks rejected, malformed commands do not create an orphan file. Includes direct SQLite path hardening and tests for partial closes, idempotent fill replay, conflicting duplicate fill, oversell, timestamps and 0600 file permissions. Local Python 224/224 PASS, Ruff critical rules PASS, Graft wiring build/check PASS, Jev evidence-bounded labeling PASS. Signed commit 49a2832 GitHub verified, PStack interrogate guidance read-only consulted, independent reviewers NOT_RUN. CI exact-head pending; mandatory native Alibaba OCR NOT_PASS. No Derayah statements independently verified, OPRA feed, broker order submission, iPhone alert delivery or real options backtest. Stacked on Draft PR #26; do not merge until governance gates. --- ## Summary by cubic Adds an offline SQLite journal for manually recording long-option positions and sell-to-close fills, without any broker connectivity. All records are labeled `USER_DECLARED_UNVERIFIED` with `broker_execution_verified=false`. - New `journal_cli` commands: `open`, `show`, `manual-close`, and `fills`. - Writes require `--record-only`; the CLI never submits orders or contacts the broker. - Rejects symlinked databases, paths inside the repo, and malformed commands that would create orphan files; sets 0600 permissions on the database. - Supports partial closes, idempotent fill replay, and rejects conflicting duplicates and oversells. - Added direct SQLite path hardening in `position_store.py` plus regression tests for all safety boundaries. Written for commit 49a2832a7d9544b20d16af7749a8e5d4f2f902c7. Summary will update on new commits.

author: milo-devbot
body:
Adds optional authentication. It stays off by default, so existing installs behave as before.

## Modes and env vars

Configured only through environment variables, so nothing in the UI can turn it off. Startup fails with a clear message on invalid combos: password mode without a password, proxy mode without trusted proxies, a password set while auth is off, guest access with auth off, a malformed hash or CIDR.

- `ORBITDASH_AUTH`: `none` (default), `password` or `proxy`
- `ORBITDASH_PASSWORD` (hashed with argon2id at startup) or `ORBITDASH_PASSWORD_HASH` (argon2 hash)
- `ORBITDASH_SESSION_DAYS` (default 30, 1 to 400)
- `ORBITDASH_GUEST`: `none` or `view`
- `ORBITDASH_PROXY_HEADER` (default `Remote-User`)
- `ORBITDASH_TRUSTED_PROXIES`: IPs/CIDRs, IPv4 and IPv6. Required for proxy mode. In password mode it enables `X-Forwarded-For`/`X-Forwarded-Proto` from those proxies.

Hash CLI: `bun run hash-password`, or `docker exec -it orbitdash bun server/cli/hash-password.ts` in the image. It prompts twice without echo (or reads stdin) and prints the hash plus a compose-escaped (`$$`) copy.

## What is protected

- Every `/api/*` route needs access, including SSE `/api/events`, icons, wallpapers and backups.
- Open: `/healthz`, `/readyz`, `/api/health`, `/api/auth/session|login|logout`, and the SPA assets and `index.html`.
- Unauthenticated calls get `401` with `{ error, auth }`. Guests asking for more than reads get `403` with the same shape.
- Backups (export, snapshots, import) always need a full session.
- The same-origin guard still runs first, auth routes included.
- Trust decisions use the socket address (`server.requestIP`, passed as Hono env), never `X-Forwarded-For`. A proxy header from an untrusted peer is ignored and logged as `auth.proxy_header_ignored` with the peer address.
- Guests get services without status check targets, since those can hold credentials.

## Sessions, cookie, rate limit

- Random 32-byte tokens. Only a SHA-256 is stored, in a new `sessions` table (migration 10).
- Sliding expiry, written at most hourly. The cookie is renewed when it slides.
- Cookie: `HttpOnly`, `SameSite=Lax`, `Path=/`. `Secure` over direct https or `X-Forwarded-Proto: https` from a trusted proxy.
- `auth_state` holds the argon2 hash in force (a plain password is hashed into it) and a random credential id, reused while the configured password still matches, so sessions survive restarts. Each session stores that id, so a new password ends old sessions. Neither table is in backup exports.
- Logout deletes the session, and open event streams check their session on each keep-alive and close once it ends.
- Login is limited to 5 failures per 15 minutes per client IP, with `Retry-After`. Each attempt counts before the argon2 check, so parallel guesses can't bypass the limit, and empty passwords cost a full verify.
- Errors are generic. Failed attempts are logged with the IP, never the password.

## Frontend

- `AuthGate` asks `GET /api/auth/session` first. The last answer is cached in localStorage, so the first paint and the offline shell aren't blocked.
- The sign-in screen is a lazy `SignInScreen-*` chunk: logo, dashboard name, password field with show/hide, inline error with a shake, and a rate-limit countdown. Proxy mode shows "Not signed in" with Try again.
- Global 401/403 handling lives in `src/lib/api/client.ts`. A dropped event stream rechecks the session too, so an expired session returns to sign-in cleanly.
- Guests get the dashboard read-only: no add, edit layout, settings, theme or edit palette actions, no service dialogs, and a Sign in button in the header (password mode).
- Settings gets an Account section: Sign out in password mode, the user name in proxy mode. Signing out also clears the service worker's cached data.
- Bundle: the entry gained about 1.2 kB gzip. It's offset by making the toaster lazy (which also took Radix Toast out of `vendor-*`: 29 to 19.6 kB gzip, budget lowered to 75/23 kB) and by loading the service form builder on first save. Entry 22.5 to 22.8 kB of 23. No budgets raised; CSS is at 89.9 of 90 kB raw, noted in `docs/bundle-size-budget.md`.

## Try it

```bash
ORBITDASH_AUTH=password ORBITDASH_PASSWORD=dev ORBITDASH_GUEST=view npm run dev:server
npm run dev
```

README has an Authentication section with compose examples for password mode, Authelia/Authentik and Tailscale Serve.

## Checks

`format:check`, `lint`, `typecheck`, `test:unit` (501), `test:integration` (480), `test:coverage` (all three gates), `test:e2e` (6), `build`, `bundle:check`: all pass.

New tests:

- bun: config parsing, CIDR (v4, v6, mapped), sessions, rate limiting, the mode × guest × method × route matrix, proxy trust, cookie flags, stream closing on logout, and the hash CLI
- Vitest: sign-in screen, auth gate, guest header/app/settings, client challenge handling
- Playwright: a second `auth-password` project running its own backend (port 3002) with password auth. It covers sign-in, a wrong password and sign-out.

author: bibekshrestha
body:
- **WeChat retries:** when ZXing and full-size WeChat find nothing, WeChat runs again on 1024 and 512 px copies. Its CNN detector is scale-sensitive. On BoofCV's benchmark this lifts zxing → WeChat from 1,008 to 1,017 of 1,232 codes (81.8% → 82.5%, all in glare/bright spots/damage) with no false reads. Average time goes from 68 to 94 ms per image; the extra cost only lands on images that would otherwise fail.
- **BarcodeDetector last:** if WeChat also fails, the browser's own detector gets a pass where it exists. Chrome on Android uses Google's barcode model and Chrome on Mac uses Apple Vision. It runs on the device under the scan deadline. Results show "Browser detector" and no version or ECC level, because browsers don't report them.
- **Regression:** `glare-024` (read by the 1024 px retry) and `glare-036` (512 px retry) join the fixtures; `readCodes` mirrors the new order. Node can't run BarcodeDetector, so that pass was checked in Chrome only.

body:
## Summary

Removes unit tests whose code paths are already exercised by existing vdiffr snapshots, replaces plot-internals checks with visual snapshots, and drops the R >= 4.5 test guard.

### Removed (covered by existing snapshots)

| Test | Already covered by |
|---|---|
| `ggbarstats` "one-sample expression output" | "checking one-way table - without NA" snapshot (renders the one-sample subtitle) + `extract_stats()` text snapshot |
| `ggbetweenstats` "subtitle output works" | "specific geoms removed" snapshot (same data, default subtitle) + `extract_stats()` text snapshot |
| `ggcoefstats` meta-analysis `expect_s3_class()` check | "meta analysis subtitle and caption" test builds the same plot and makes stronger assertions |
| `pairwise.alpha` between- and within-subjects tests | "between/within - parametric - stricter alpha" snapshots render the same filtered brackets and the `α = 0.001` label |

To keep a custom `pairwise.alpha` covered on both branches, the within-subjects "stricter alpha" snapshot now uses `pairwise.display = "ns"`. The between-subjects one still covers the significant branch.

The two helpers that only the `pairwise.alpha` tests used (`signif_comparisons()`, `pairwise_seclabel_text()`) are removed too.

### Converted to visual snapshots

These tests reached into layer indices, `aes_params`, or built layer data to check what gets drawn:

- `ggcoefstats`: stats label colours stay aligned after filtering labels
- `ggcoefstats`: tidy data without statistic inputs draws no stats labels
- `ggcorrmat`: caption marks p-values as unadjusted with `p.adjust.method = "none"` (moved into the "changed defaults" block)
- pairwise brackets stay above negative outcomes

I checked each new SVG by hand: the brackets sit above the data at three levels, only the firebrick/forestgreen labels remain, no labels are drawn without a statistic, and the caption shows `p unadj.`.

### Kept on purpose

- Subtitle-equality tests that pass `digits`, `conf.level`, or `type = "np"` (bar/pie, scatter, histo, dotplot). No snapshot exercises those arguments with the subtitle shown.
- The `ggwithinstats` missing-data tests. They check exact row and group counts, which a snapshot would only show indirectly.
- `.ggsignif_adder()` finite-positions test and the helper unit tests.

### R version guard

`tests/testthat.R` no longer checks `getRversion() >= "4.5.0"`, because `DESCRIPTION` already requires R >= 4.5.0. The Linux/macOS restriction stays. AGENTS.md is updated to match.

## Drive-by cleanup

- Tidied section headers in the touched test files: renamed "expected warnings" to "expected errors" for an error test, fixed a missing space and an overlong rule, updated a stale header, and added a header for the bracket tests.

## Verification

- Full suite via `testthat::test_local()` with `NOT_CRAN=true` on R 4.6.1: 80 blocks, 0 failures. Existing snapshots match locally.
- `air format . --check` and `lintr::lint_dir("tests")` are clean.

body:
## Sintoma

A instrução do worker manda gerar o grafo do código no próprio checkout (`project_knowledge_context`). Em 10/10/2026, nenhum dos 67 worktrees do Concursa tinha `graphify-out`; o único grafo era de 16/09, de um checkout em `staging`. Instrução que pede um passo de preparo não era seguida.

Desde 10/10 existe um grafo da main gerado fora do card, de hora em hora e sem LLM, e o comando `historico.py impacto` (arquivos da candidata, commits do trecho, consumidores e relação com a extração).

Pedido do Maikol em 10/10/2026: "Sim, aplique tudo nessas condições". Esta é a parte do fork da fase 2 do grafo.

## Mudança

Em `kanban.delivery.project_knowledge.projects.<projeto>`, duas chaves opcionais:

- `graph_path`: caminho do grafo compartilhado. Com ela, o contexto do worker aponta o grafo pronto, dá o comando de consulta com `--graph` e diz para não gerar grafo no checkout.
- `impact_command`: comando de impacto, com `{repo}` trocado pelo checkout do card. Com ela, o contexto manda rodar o comando antes de classificar domínio e impacto.

Projeto sem as chaves recebe a instrução de antes, sem diferença.

## Prova

- `tests/hermes_cli/test_nfos_project_knowledge.py`: teste novo (projeto com grafo compartilhado recebe o grafo pronto e o comando de impacto com o próprio checkout, sem a instrução de `extract`; o outro projeto segue igual). Os 3 testes que já existiam passam.

## Entrada e volta

Entra desligado. Liga pondo as duas chaves no `config.yaml` do perfil, no projeto `concursa-ai`:

- `graph_path: /srv/projects/Concursa_ai/historico-commits/grafo-codigo/graph.json`
- `impact_command: python3 /srv/projects/Concursa_ai/historico-commits/historico.py impacto --repo {repo} --candidata HEAD`

Volta: tirar as chaves. O contexto do worker é montado a cada execução.

## Purpose

Fix claims in the CSV and flat file processing page that do not match the behavior of `ballerina/data.csv` 1.0.0, and document options that were only mentioned in passing.

- Remove the claim that fixed-width files are supported. The module parses delimited data only.

- Correct `skipLines`: it counts data rows from `1` after the header, and the string form accepts a single range such as `"2-4"`. The previous `"2-4,7"` example fails at runtime, and `skipLines: [0, 1]` implied zero-based numbering.

- Document the `encoding` option for non-UTF-8 input, with an example.
- Document the `FailSafeOptions` and `FileOutputMode` fields, with a file-logging example and its log output.

author: johnwang688
kensac
body:
## What

Asks ("complete the assessment", "respond to the offer") were rows in `action_items`, which `sync_action_items` kept in step with the mail by re-reading every application on every matcher run and after every correction. They are now derived when read, by `mail.pipeline.action_items`:

- An ask comes from each message's current event on its current application.
- It is closed by the first later event on that application that settles it, or by the person's latest answer being `done`.
- Its id is the id of the event that asked.

What a person answers is now stored in a new append-only table, `event_answers`, with these columns: `event_id`, `question` (status|action), `answer` (accepted|dismissed|done|reopened), `actor_user_id`, `note`. A reopen is an answer, and the closing answer stays readable beneath it. Status proposals use the same table and stop using `suggestion_responses`. The history page now shows ask closures with their neighbours, which the in-place table could not do.

Removed: `sync_action_items`, the matcher's per-application loop and its "items opened/resolved" counts, and `reply_to_recruiter`. A recruiter approach is attached to no application (`UNATTACHABLE_KINDS`), so it could never ask anything. On production it had 73 rows, all closed by the sweep.

## Migration 09397cf6c3d1 (additive)

The migration creates `event_answers` and copies `suggestion_responses` into it: 8 rows on 2026-10-10, all `accepted`. Nothing is copied from `action_items`, because no person ever closed or reopened an ask. All 217 closures without a settling event were the sweep's own "no longer part of this application". Both old tables stay for now. A later migration will drop them, after every server has stopped writing them, and will first copy any answers made during the roll. The migration revises 98ace4b3fc55, the same parent as #898's 54630f36d8b8, so whichever merges second needs re-parenting.

## Same open asks (production, read-only, 2026-10-10)

| Kind | Stored open | Derived open | Both |
|---|---|---|---|
| complete_assessment | 146 | 146 | 146 |
| respond_to_offer | 140 | 140 | 140 |
| schedule_interview | 44 | 45 | 44 |
| send_information | 195 | 197 | 195 |

Every stored open ask is derived open. The 3 extra asks had been closed by an event that is no longer current on the application: the closing message was later reclassified or moved (events 4379 and 58779). By the current-row rule they are open again.

## API

Response shapes are unchanged, and `openapi.json` changes only in two docstrings. The frontend reads `id`, `kind`, `settles_on`, `due_at`, `event_id`, `resolved_at`, `resolution` and `resolved_by_event_id` from pipeline actions (`lib/job-tracker/types.ts` `PipelineActionItem`), and all of them are still served. Ask ids are now event ids, in `/user/actions/{id}/resolve|reopen` and in the queue's `action:<id>`. A page loaded before the deploy holds old ids. Such an id gets a 404 on its next click and is correct after a reload.

## Tests

- `tests/test_mail_pipeline.py`: an ask is derived, closed by a later event, not closed by an earlier one, moves with its message, and is closed and reopened by appending.
- `tests/test_api_pipeline.py`: the resolve and reopen endpoints, a 409 on reopening an ask that an email settled, and a 404 for another person.
- `tests/test_decision_inbox.py`, `tests/test_resolve_queue*.py` and `tests/test_devseed.py` now run on derived asks. The queue oracle reads the asks through the same function the queue does, which matches how both previously shared one SQL statement.

author: lexrus
body:
## Summary

Syncs the `cupthread-api` skill with the published public image-delivery contract for `GET /api/v1/files/{key}`, which now supports an optional integer `width` query parameter requesting a square thumbnail (verified against the live `openapi.json` and the SaaS implementation).

### What the skill doc now documents

- **Fixed width set.** Only `16, 32, 36, 56, 64, 72, 80, 112, 128, 160` can create transformations; any other value (non-numeric, zero-padded, or out of set) fails with `400 {"error": "Unsupported image width"}`.
- **WebP-or-original responses.** When the platform image-optimization flag is enabled and the original is PNG/JPEG/WebP, a width-hint response is a WebP thumbnail (width×width, center-cropped, quality 85). When optimization is disabled, unavailable, fails, or exhausts its monthly transform budget — and for GIF originals — the original bytes are served as the fallback.
- **Two cache lifetimes.** Every width-hint response — thumbnail *or* original fallback — carries `Cache-Control: public, max-age=300` (five minutes). Requests without the hint keep the canonical policy, and the edge cache key stays the object key, so query-string rotation and unrelated query parameters do not multiply cache entries.
- **Stale cache policy fixed in passing.** The row still claimed `Cache-Control: public, max-age=60`; the published contract (and SaaS #649) moved canonical originals to `public, max-age=86400, immutable` with a 15-second negative cache on missing keys. The row now matches.
- **Client guidance.** Decode by the response `Content-Type` (`image/webp` when transformed) rather than inferring the format from the URL extension, and treat public image URLs under `/api/v1/files/` as opaque — preserve path and query string instead of reconstructing them.
- **PRIV-19 avatar reads.** Thumbnail hints apply only to API-origin managed URLs (`<PUBLIC_BASE_URL>/api/v1/files/…`), are appended to the stored URL with an always-present fallback to the original URL; `imagedelivery.net` / images-delivery-host URLs pass through untouched.

No CLI code changes are needed: the CLI neither fetches nor serves public images, and it provides no thumbnail helper, so the issue's helper guidance is documentation-only here.

## Test plan

- New `TestAPISkillIssue204WidthHints` pins every marker above in `skills/cupthread-api/SKILL.md` and rejects the stale `max-age=60` policy plus undocumented width values, so future edits cannot silently desync the skill the way earlier API-sync issues did.
- `go build ./...`, `go vet ./internal/cmd/`, and the full `go test ./...` suite pass; the modified test file is gofmt-clean.

author: mgradwohl
body:
## Description

### Problem

ThreadSanitizer sometimes reports a data race in `LazyBackgroundReadTest.AThrowingReadIsTheFailedResult`. The `ts-test-read` worker frees a `std::runtime_error`'s message while the UI thread reads `e.what()` in `LazyBackgroundRead::takeFinished()`. It happened about 1 to 2 times in 2000 runs, and it failed the Heavy Checks `sanitizers (tsan)` job on #1677 (run 38028428563), which blocks performance PRs.

### Severity

LOW for users: there is no real memory-safety bug. HIGH for the conveyor, because a flaky sanitizer job blocks unrelated PRs.

### Root Cause

This is a false positive caused by an exception object crossing threads. A read that threw escaped its `std::async` worker. `std::async` stored it as an `exception_ptr`, `future::get()` rethrew it on the UI thread, and `takeFinished()` read `e.what()` there. The message buffer of a libc++ `std::runtime_error` is reference-counted inside libc++abi (`__libcpp_refstring`), which is not TSan-instrumented. The atomic refcount does order the worker's free after the UI thread's read, but TSan can't see that ordering, so it reports a race.

### Fix

No exception object crosses threads any more:

- The worker lambda now calls a new `readOrFailed()`. It catches the exception on the worker thread, copies `e.what()` into a `std::string` there, and returns the plain Failed `Result`. Only that value goes through the future, and TSan understands the future's synchronization.
- A throw that isn't a `std::exception` (`catch (...)`) becomes Failed with `"unknown error"`.
- `takeFinished()` keeps a catch-all for the one thing that can still escape the worker: a `bad_alloc` while the Failed result is being built. That path never reads the exception's message.
- The Failed status and the message text are unchanged for `std::exception` throws.

Connections, Modules and Open files all use `LazyBackgroundRead` and have no copies of this pattern, so this one change covers them.

## PR Size

Small: 48 insertions and 5 deletions in 2 files.

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)
- [ ] New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality)
- [ ] Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to change)
- [ ] Documentation update
- [ ] Build/CI improvement

## Checklist

- [x] I have read the [CONTRIBUTING](../CONTRIBUTING.md) guidelines
- [x] My code follows the project's coding standards
- [x] I have run `clang-tidy` and addressed any warnings
- [x] I have run `clang-format` on my changes
- [x] I have run `pre-commit run --all-files` or installed pre-commit hooks
- [x] I have added tests that prove my fix/feature works
- [x] All new and existing tests pass
- [x] I have updated documentation as needed

## Testing

### Validation

New test: `LazyBackgroundReadTest.AReadThrowingANonStdExceptionIsTheFailedResult` (the `catch (...)` path).

**TSan** (WSL, `tsan` preset, clang-22/libc++, private `FETCHCONTENT_BASE_DIR` under /tmp, repo `tsan.supp`, `halt_on_error=0`):
- `LazyBackgroundReadTest.*` (8 tests) with `--gtest_repeat=3000`: **0 TSan reports**, all passed. Before the fix the rate was about 1 to 2 per 2000.
- `LazyBackgroundReadTest.*:ProcessOpenFilesViewTest.*:ProcessModulesViewTest.*:ProcessConnectionsViewTest.*` (30 tests: the original 29 plus the new one) with `--gtest_repeat=500`: **0 TSan reports**, all passed.

**Windows** (`win-debug`):
```
cmake --preset win-debug
cmake --build build/win-debug      # all targets
ctest --preset win-debug           # 100% tests passed out of 4340
```
- `tools/clang-tidy.ps1` on `test_LazyBackgroundRead.cpp`, which includes the header: clean.
- `tools/clang-format.ps1`: no changes.
- `pre-commit` on the touched files: passed.
- `linux-tidy.sh` on the touched files: exit 0.

### Issues

Fixes #1685

### Risk

Low. Behaviour is the same for every read that returns or throws a `std::exception`. The only new behaviour is that a non-`std::exception` throw now gives a Failed result. Before this change it escaped `takeFinished()` uncaught.

## Additional Notes

`ServiceActionsView`, `StartupActionsView` and `SystemInfoPanel` also use a `std::async` worker whose exceptions are caught on the UI thread. They are outside this issue's scope and haven't shown TSan reports, but they could get the same treatment in a follow-up.

author: kucell
body:
## Why this change exists
Previous v1.15.4 release attempts completed dry-run but could not publish: the manual form demanded release_pr, exact SHA, canonical Decision ID and Waitpoint ID. This is a system-design failure for one-owner publication, not user misconfiguration.

## Proposed UX
Actions → npm Release → branch `main` → **Publish the prepared current version** checkbox → Run workflow. No manual PR/SHA/governance ID entry; package version from checked-in package.json, dist-tag `latest`. Unchecked means safe dry-run.

## Security contract
- The new `verify-owner-dispatch.cjs` only accepts `workflow_dispatch`, repo `Kucell/cortex-agent`, ref `refs/heads/main`, actor **and GitHub event sender `Kucell`**, an explicitly checked publish input, valid committed package name and SemVer, numeric GitHub run id, and verified remote main SHA equal to triggering SHA. GitHub API denied, stale branch or invalid input fails closed.
- Run the gate **three times**: before tests, before Git tagging, before npm publication. Existing frozen install, M-040 tests, real CLI tests, npm pack, registry collision detection, tag/main immutability and OIDC trusted publish steps remain.
- No npm token. Preserve existing automatic owner-comment (`issue_comment`) release with **canonical Decision/Waitpoint** gate. `CORTEX_AUTO_RELEASE_ENABLED=false` still disables comment automation; does not prevent explicit owner workflow dispatch.
- Write an audit receipt to the workflow artifact containing actor, repository, version, committed SHA, run ID; this is accurately labeled `github-owner-workflow-dispatch`, **not** a fake canonical Cortex Decision or Waitpoint.
- **This PR introduces an alternate governance authorization policy** for the single-maintainer project. Do not merge/enable without the corresponding independently reviewed governance policy exception and explicit owner acceptance. It is not a cosmetic UI-only change.

## Acceptance
- CI release-workflow contract tests, owner/non-owner/branch drift tests, M-040 and CLI regressions on exact PR head.
- Governance policy confirmation that an authenticated GitHub owner `workflow_dispatch` constitutes release consent on this owner-operated project, with required source/actor/side-effect audit; no false canonical governance records.
- No publish until merged, safe dry-run on resulting main and owner dispatch with checked publish; verify actual npm `cortex-agent@1.15.4` plus git tag and GitHub Release.

Related activation tracking: #58. npm Trusted Publisher workflow filename **unchanged** (`npm-release.yml`).

author: haranishi
body:
## What and why

Three ways a small EPS/PS/AI program could freeze or crash the import through a stitching function (`/FunctionType 3`) in `shfill`:

1. **No cap on the stops.** For a stitching function whose pieces are all linear, `gradient()` made one stop per `/Bounds` entry (`linear_points`), and every stop calls `eval`, which rebuilt `Bounds` and copied the whole `Functions` array on each call: O(N²). A program that builds 40,000 bounds in a loop (a few operations each) took 11 s, and the import is synchronous. The non-linear case was already capped at 32 samples.
2. **A function that refers to itself** (`F /Functions [ F ] put`) made `linear_points` recurse until the stack overflowed, which aborts the process (`vectorcraft_engine::guard` cannot catch an abort). `eval` already stops at depth 8; `linear_points` did not.
3. **Shared children.** The depth limit does not stop a tree of shared references: `Functions` arrays of 1025 references to one child, three levels deep, are 1025³ visits for `linear_points` from a tiny file (it did not finish in 60 s).

What changes, in `crates/eps/src/import/graphics.rs`:

- `MAX_STITCH_STOPS = 1024`: more bounds, or more than 1025 pieces, and the function is sampled (33 stops) like any other function. Up to 1024 bounds keep their exact stops, so ordinary gradients are unchanged.
- `linear_points` takes the depth (it gives up past 8, as `eval` does) and a visit counter shared by the whole recursion (it gives up past 2 × 1025 visits; a well-formed stitch of linear pieces needs at most 1026). `Functions` is length-checked before it is copied.
- `eval`'s stitching branch reads `Functions` through the borrow and copies only the piece it recurses into, instead of the whole array on every call and at every live recursion level.
- Not changed: the interpreter's op budget (`MAX_OPS`) still does not account for the work `eval` does on large arrays. I left that as it is.

## How it was tested

Five new tests in `tests_generators.rs`. They assert stop counts and outcomes; there is no timing.

- `gradients_stitched_from_linear_pieces_keep_or_sample_their_stops`: 3 bounds give the exact 5 stops; 1024 bounds give 1026; 1025 bounds are sampled (33). Before the fix the last case gave 1027 stops.
- `a_stitching_function_with_one_piece_but_many_bounds_is_sampled`: 2000 bounds on one piece give 33 stops (2002 before).
- `a_gradient_with_a_functions_array_past_the_cap_is_sampled`: 1026 pieces with 1000 bounds give 33 stops (1002 before).
- `a_stitching_function_that_refers_to_itself_is_rejected_not_crashed`: the import returns, keeps what was drawn before the error and reports it (before the fix the process aborts with SIGABRT).
- `a_deeply_shared_stitching_function_is_sampled_not_walked`: 1025 references to a child, three levels deep, are sampled at once (before the fix it did not finish in 60 s).

`cargo xtask ci` passes after rebasing onto the current `main` (all 7 steps, 145 tests in `vectorcraft-eps`).

## Checklist

- [x] `cargo xtask ci` passes (fmt, clippy, tests, assets, brands, layers, wasm).
- [x] No panics in shipped code: no `unwrap()`, `expect()`, `panic!`, `unreachable!`, `todo!` or
      `unimplemented!` outside tests, and no unchecked indexing on data from files, parameters or
      messages. Errors are returned as `Result` and shown to the user
      ([why and how](https://github.com/storytold/vectorcraft/blob/main/docs/development.md#robustness-vectorcraft-never-crashes)).
- [x] Clean-room: nothing copied from Adobe products or GPL/AGPL code ([AGENTS.md](https://github.com/storytold/vectorcraft/blob/main/AGENTS.md)).
- [x] Every new asset has a row in `ASSETS.md`. (There are no new assets.)

author: miili
body:
Replaces `distance_weights.py` with a `station_weights` module that follows the module pattern of the triggers: a `StationWeights` base class, one subclass per weighting, selected by `"weights"` in the configuration. Supersedes #46.

## Station weights

| `weights` | Full weight | Taper | Defaults |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `StationDensityWeights` (**default**) | The closest `plateau_stations` independent stations | Gaussian, σ = half the distance of `taper_stations` independent stations, at most `max_taper_ratio` × the plateau distance | 3, 8, 1.0 |
| `DistanceWeights` | The `required_closest_stations` closest stations | Gaussian, FWHM `distance_taper`: `"mean_interstation"` (twice the mean interstation distance, the weights of main) or `"nearest_neighbor"` (6 × the median distance between neighboring sites) | 4, `"mean_interstation"` |
| `LogLogisticWeights` | The closest `plateau_stations` independent stations | `1 / (1 + (d / (taper_scale · d_plateau))^taper_exponent)` | 4, 1.8, 4 |

**Independent stations:** each station counts as a number of independent stations, `1 - (k - k_min) / k_max` with the Gaussian kernel density `k` of the neighboring sites (kernel width: the median distance between neighboring sites) and the lowest and highest density of the available stations, `k_min` and `k_max`. An isolated station counts as one, a station in a dense cluster as a fraction of one; sensors within 50 m share a site and count as one together. Campi Flegrei's 18 stations count as 11.1 independent stations, Mount Spurr's 20 as 13.8.

**Taper cap:** a gap in the network (Mount Spurr: local stations within 32 km, regional beyond 79 km) puts the `taper_stations` far away and stretches the taper across the gap. `max_taper_ratio` caps σ at the plateau distance; without a gap it rarely binds (Campi Flegrei: σ = 0.77 × the plateau distance in the median). With σ = the plateau distance, the weight halves at 2.2 × the plateau distance, where the mean phase confidence of small events halves on the playground.

## Breaking changes

- The default station weights change: `StationDensityWeights` instead of the distance weights. `"station_weights": {"weights": "DistanceWeights"}` gives the results of main (`just compare`: `B is identical to A` on campi-flegrei, spurr-2024 and norcia-2016).
- The configuration key `distance_weights` is now `station_weights`; the alias `spatial_weights` is gone too. Configurations and run directories with these keys do not load anymore. `OctreeSearch(distance_weights=...)` is now `station_weights=...`.
- `qseek.distance_weights` is removed, with `weights_exponential`; `weights_gaussian` moved to `qseek.station_weights`.
- With fewer than two station sites (a single station, or all sensors co-located), `DistanceWeights` give all stations full weight.

## Calibration and results

Calibrated on the playground and a synthetic benchmark: the nearest neighbor factor (2–8), plateau and taper stations (3–5, 6–16), the taper cap (0.75–1.5, none), the log-logistic scale (1.8–2.6).

Playground, `MADTrigger` `mad_factor` 10 (detections / well constrained (≥ 8 picks, Norcia ≥ 20) / RMS / catalog / epicenter offset):

| | campi-flegrei | campi-flegrei-2025-02 | spurr-2024 | norcia-2016 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `StationDensityWeights` | 954 / 524 / 0.282 s / 45 / 216 m | 8189 / 3799 / 0.278 s / 210 / 295 m | 2457 / 1140 / 0.338 s / 229 / 409 m | 4279 / 3874 / 0.325 s / 1026 / 668 m |
| `DistanceWeights` (main) | 732 / 521 / 0.284 s / 45 / 241 m | 6379 / 3750 / 0.278 s / 209 / 280 m | 1758 / 1046 / 0.349 s / 228 / 416 m | 3732 / 3602 / 0.310 s / 1013 / 635 m |
| `DistanceWeights`, `"nearest_neighbor"` | 750 / 525 / 0.286 s / 45 / 238 m | 6614 / 3772 / 0.280 s / 209 / 293 m | 2210 / 1070 / 0.318 s / 230 / 348 m | 3972 / 3747 / 0.314 s / 1020 / 648 m |
| `LogLogisticWeights` | 800 / 520 / 0.286 s / 45 / 229 m | 7092 / 3800 / 0.284 s / 210 / 332 m | 2226 / 1127 / 0.364 s / 230 / 416 m | 4166 / 3829 / 0.321 s / 1025 / 653 m |

Synthetic benchmark, recall of events with ≥ 6 picks at 2 false detections per hour (observatory with co-located sensors / regional with sub-array / Campi Flegrei / Mount Spurr / Norcia / small, 7 stations / nodal line of 40 stations 30 m apart + 8 permanent):

| | Obs. | Regional | CF | Spurr | Norcia | Small | Nodal | Location change |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `StationDensityWeights` | 0.86 | 0.38 | 1.00 | 0.86 | 0.34 | 0.74 | 0.69 | −3 to 5 m |
| `DistanceWeights` | 0.65 | 0.23 | 1.00 | 0.76 | 0.22 | 0.78 | 0.84 | 0 m |
| `DistanceWeights`, `"nearest_neighbor"` | 0.60 | 0.38 | 1.00 | 0.78 | 0.27 | 0.76 | 0.52 | −2 to 1450 m |
| `LogLogisticWeights` | 0.80 | 0.38 | 1.00 | 0.78 | 0.30 | 0.74 | 0.30 | −2 to 5 m |

Known limitation: with a dense nodal array, the median distance between neighboring sites is the array spacing; the density kernel (and the `"nearest_neighbor"` taper) get narrow. `DistanceWeights` with `"mean_interstation"` stay the better choice there (0.84 against 0.69). A per-station kernel width would address it in a follow-up.

## Memory

The interstation distances are needed only by the density-based weights and the `"nearest_neighbor"` taper; they are computed lazily, as float32 in blocks of rows, and the station density is computed in blocks of rows without copying the matrix. Total peak memory of the independent station counts: 86 MB for 3000 stations, 243 MB for 6000, with the 36 MB and 144 MB matrix resident during the search. The playground results are unchanged (`B is identical to A` for the default on campi-flegrei, spurr-2024 and norcia-2016). `DistanceWeights` with `"mean_interstation"` compute the mean interstation distance as main does, in O(n²) Python calls; unchanged from main.

## Docs and tests

- `docs/configuration/station-weights.md` replaces the distance weighting page (redirected): independent stations, choice of the weights, the results above, figures of the weights and of the taper cap at Campi Flegrei and Mount Spurr.
- `test/test_station_weights.py`: Gaussian distance weights (from main), both distance tapers, independent stations and co-located sites, plateau, taper cap, log-logistic taper, the three models on a clustered network, station subsets, single station and co-located sites, a second `prepare` with other stations, configuration. `test/test_search.py` locates a synthetic event with each weighting on a network with a dense cluster. 272 tests pass.

_Requested by **Shubhanshu** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_011qDT8Q1c7gDodDspnZeS1d?thread=cmsg_011qDT8Q1c7gDodDspnZeS1d3ESZstozdDLt6GH5UN5rc7)_

Before: at Study, 3,948 verses (12.7%) had no theme of their own and none through links, so the Themes tab showed only a quiet line for them.

After: at Study and Deep, those verses show what Nave's Topical Bible (1896) lists them under. For example, Genesis 2:6 shows "Nave's Topical Bible (1896) lists this verse under Mist · Meteorology and Celestial Phenomena". Each heading is a button that opens that subject in Ask the Bible. A verse Nave's cites only as part of a passage gets a passage row instead: Genesis 2:22 shows "Part of a passage Nave's lists under Creation (Genesis 2:1–25)". 80.4% of those verses now get a row, and 775 (2.5% of the Bible) keep the quiet line. Simple is unchanged: it keeps the quiet line and never loads Nave's.

Nave's never becomes a theme. It adds no verses or roots to any theme. Only its subject headings are shown, never the text of its entries.

How:
- **One shared reader** (new `crates/atlas-cli/src/naves.rs`). Ask the Bible's Nave's parser moved out of `ask.rs`, so Ask and the Themes rows read the table the same way.
- **Cut entry fixed.** The table's "JESUS, THE CHRIST" entry stops at 32,767 characters, a spreadsheet's cell limit, partway through a reference ("Head of every man 1CO 1"). Ask was filing all of 1 Corinthians 1 under it. The build now drops the cut line and logs it. Ask's output is otherwise byte-identical: only that topic loses 24 verses of 1 Corinthians 1.
- **Which headings show** (`config/naves-display.json`, checked by the build):
  - Only subjects about a concept. People, places and names are left out, using the same open name lists the app already pins: Theographic, OpenBible.info, STEPBible capitalised glosses, and words the KJV and BSB always capitalise. A `show` list lets through 28 concepts the name lists mistake for names, such as Sin, Sabbath, Passover and Holy Spirit.
  - 143 subjects are hidden, each with a reason:
    - 1896 headings that read as slurs today;
    - old senses that now mean something else, such as Abortion (miscarriage) and Infidelity (unbelief);
    - meta lists such as Types and Quotations and Allusions;
    - subjects too broad for one verse, such as God and Jesus, the Christ.
  - A `fix` list corrects 14 references the table edition mistyped. These fixes apply to these rows only. Ask's own subject list is unchanged.
- **Data:** `naves/<Book>.json`, 66 files, 754 KB raw and 262 KB gzipped. One book's file loads at Study only, and only for a verse no theme reaches.
- **Web:** `web/src/data/naves.ts` and `VerseThemes.tsx`.
  - Up to 3 headings show, then "+N more", which opens in place. Up to 2 passage rows.
  - Deep adds a source line that links to the Nave's card on the Sources shelf.
  - Closing Ask returns focus to the heading that opened it.
- **Checks:** atlas verify gains checks:
  - every subject number and title matches Ask's;
  - no hidden title appears;
  - the cut-entry pin;
  - pins such as Genesis 2:6 (Mist), Genesis 2:22 (Creation passage), 1 Samuel 17:43 (never Dog (Sodomite?)) and Joshua 13:16 (no misread Moon);
  - a Study coverage floor.
  The new naves.rs has 12 unit tests.
- **Review:** this went through code, data and browser review. The browser review covered desktop and phone, light and dark, Simple, Study and Deep. All 13 confirmed findings were fixed. `sources.json`, NOTICE.md and the Sources shelf card now say what is shown.

Checks: after merging the latest main (word forms and the Ask chains), make data passes 3,041 verify checks. Clippy (stable 1.99), cargo test, make wasm, npm run typecheck and npm run build pass.

author: dirkjink
body:
## Summary

The OSV dependency scan has been red on `main` since 2026-10-02. The cause is `tools.jackson.core:jackson-core`/`jackson-databind` **3.1.5**, which the Spring Boot BOM 4.1.1 manages and which arrives through the optional `logstash-logback-encoder`. All seven advisories are fixed in **3.1.7**, and no Boot patch release with that version exists yet.

This PR imports `tools.jackson:jackson-bom` 3.1.7 into `dependencyManagement` before the Boot BOM, the same pattern as the other pinned BOMs. The property is `jackson3.version`, so Dependabot keeps it current.

## Advisories and exposure

| Advisory | CVSS | Precondition |
|---|---|---|
| GHSA-7hhh-6rmp-j9qf | 7.5 | parsing untrusted JSON via `DataInput` |
| GHSA-p6pp-m3f8-5c89 | 7.5 | number-string validation of untrusted input (ReDoS) |
| GHSA-cxp5-3px4-pw24 | 7.5 | deserializing into `@JsonIdentityInfo` collections |
| GHSA-q4xh-88c3-wmh7 | 7.5 | deserializing `Duration`/`XMLGregorianCalendar` |
| GHSA-wv8q-qhhj-9h54 | 7.5 | `@JsonTypeInfo(Id.NAME, defaultImpl)` with untrusted type ids |
| GHSA-gx83-3vf8-gh7j | 5.6 | `@JsonTypeInfo` on a `Comparable` property |
| GHSA-wjgm-6hv5-3cvf | 5.3 | binding `Path` from untrusted JSON |

**No exposure in tabellarium:** all seven need Jackson to parse or deserialize untrusted JSON. The shipped code contains no Jackson reference, and the `LogstashEncoder` only writes JSON. Consumers are unaffected either way, because the encoder dependency is optional and applications that add it manage their own Jackson. The pin fixes our build, our tests and the SBOM the scan reads.

The test-scoped `com.fasterxml.jackson.core:jackson-databind` 2.21.5 is affected as well. It is deliberately not pinned: it is test scope only, not in the SBOM, and it will move with the next Boot update.

## Test plan
- [x] `mvn dependency:tree`: `tools.jackson.core:*` resolve to 3.1.7, `jackson-annotations` unchanged at 2.21
- [x] `cyclonedx:makeBom`: SBOM lists 3.1.7
- [x] OSV API: no advisories for 3.1.7 / annotations 2.21 (3.1.5 as control still affected)
- [x] `mvn verify` green locally (includes the logstash-encoder tests)
- [ ] CI "Dependency vulnerability scan" green

Drop the pin once the Boot BOM manages Jackson ≥ 3.1.7.

body:
## Monitoring: die DB-Session läuft in UTC (R-0218)

- **Spec:** Roadmap R-0218 (Kurz-Ledger ohne Spec)
- **Heavy:** linux-full — `run.sh integration` auf einer Pool-VM, wie bei R-0209: Der Stack fährt Postgres mit `TZ=Europe/Berlin`, genau den Fall, den der Listener abfängt. `agent_monitoring` fährt die Engine des Monitorings im Container, `stack-pytest` den neuen Test gegen das Postgres des Stacks (T2).

### Tasks

- [x] **T1 — Monitoring-Engine: jede Verbindung setzt ihre Session auf UTC (R-0218)**
  - Evidenz: run.sh[quick] monitoring: 4 passed, 0 failed, 14 skipped · contracts: 1 ok @fdf8e8aa 2026-10-10T09:35:17+02:00
  - Review: Review am Ende (Kurz-Ledger, Opus)
- [x] **T2 — `stack_pytest.sh`: der neue Test läuft im integration-Layer gegen das Postgres des Stacks (R-0218)**
  - Evidenz: run.sh[quick] scripts: 6 passed, 0 failed, 12 skipped @77815da5 2026-10-10T09:47:44+02:00
  - Review: Review am Ende (Kurz-Ledger, Opus)
- [x] **T3 — Nachbesserung aus dem Review am Ende: DEVELOPMENT.md nennt die vier Pflicht-Tests von stack-pytest (R-0218)**
  - Evidenz: run.sh[quick] scripts: 6 passed, 0 failed, 12 skipped @8c4f6938 2026-10-10T10:30:49+02:00
  - Review: kein neuer Review (Nachbesserung, Aufsicht 2026-10-10)

### Befund vorab (Explorer, Opus)

Im Monitoring hängt heute kein Schreiber und kein Leser an der Session-Zeitzone.
- Alle Zeitspalten sind naive `timestamp`, und alle Defaults sind `timezone('UTC', now())`.
- Die Python-Schreiber nutzen `utcnow_naive()`.
- Die Cutoffs für Cooldown, Retention und Maintenance werden naiv in Python gebildet, ohne SQL-`now()`.
- Die Ausgabe läuft über `iso_utc`.
- Altzeilen in Ortszeit aus der Zeit vor v0.40 bleiben, wie sie sind. Der Wechsel ändert keinen Wert und keine Antwort, in keine Richtung.

Eine Datenmigration ist nicht nötig. R-0218 ist Härtung gegen künftigen Code.

### Verifikation

- **Beweis vor dem Fix (origin/main@d4515a1e):** Die Monitoring-Engine wurde gegen die eigene Test-DB geprobt, in einer TEMP-Tabelle mit Rollback. Ohne `PGTZ` wie mit `PGTZ=Europe/Berlin` gilt `SHOW TimeZone = Europe/Berlin`, und ein aware 12:00Z wird als `14:00` gespeichert.
- **Neuer Test `test_db_session_utc.py`:** Er lief von Hand, nur diese Datei, gegen die eigene Test-DB. Vor dem Fix `2 failed` (`'Europe/Berlin' == 'UTC'`, `stored 2026-10-10 14:00:00`), danach `2 passed`.
- **`verify.sh monitoring --strict` (task-close T1):** `522 passed, 12 skipped`. Ohne Postgres-`DATABASE_URL` skippen sich dort auch die beiden neuen Tests, wie beabsichtigt.
- **`stack_pytest_test.sh`:** `17 passed, 0 failed`. task-close T2 (`verify.sh scripts --strict`) ergibt `run.sh[quick] scripts: 6 passed, 0 failed, 12 skipped`, diff-scan und docs-pairs clean.
- **Gesamt-Schnellcheck:** `run.sh quick --strict` ergibt `run.sh[quick]: 18 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped, 14 test-skips, 0 reruns`. Die zwei Test-Skips mehr als zuvor sind die neuen Tests ohne Postgres.
- **Heavy linux-full, Pool-VM, `iter.sh integration --strict` auf a1ca2f81:**
  - `run.sh[integration]: 8 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped, 0 test-skips, 0 reruns`.
  - Darin `stack_pytest: 4 passed, 0 failed`, mit `monitoring-session-utc` → `2 passed` gegen das Postgres des Stacks (TZ=Europe/Berlin), und `agent_monitoring (push pipeline)` grün.
  - Danach `reap.sh`; `vm.py list` zeigt 0 eigene VMs.
- **Merge-Probe gegen origin/main@128b7fb5 (#113):** `git merge-tree` meldet keinen Konflikt.

### Review

**Review am Ende (Opus): approve.** Drei nits:
1. `DEVELOPMENT.md` (Kommentar zum Schritt stack-pytest) zählte noch drei Pflicht-Tests auf. **Behoben als T3** auf Anordnung der Aufsicht, ohne neuen Review: `run.sh[quick] scripts: 6 passed, 0 failed, 12 skipped`, diff-scan und docs-pairs clean.
2. Nicht behoben: `scripts/tests/run.sh` ist ein Harness-Pfad und gehört nicht in diesen Branch. Sein Kommentar sagt noch „three tests“, und `test_skip_is_required` kennt `test_db_session_utc` nicht. Ein Skip in einem lokalen `--strict`-Lauf mit Postgres-`DATABASE_URL` fiele dort also nicht auf; abgedeckt ist er heute über stack-pytest auf der Box.
3. Nicht behoben: Der Kommentar in `.github/workflows/ci.yml` zum `DATABASE_URL` des Monitoring-Jobs war schon vorher veraltet.

Die nits 2 und 3 betreffen Harness-Pfade; die Aufsicht trägt sie als Roadmap-Zeilen ein.

author: kanywst
body:
Follow-ups from the Claude review on #21.

- `refreshWiFi` execs `iw link` (with one retry) and `iw scan dump`, each with a 4s timeout, so it can block for about 12s. It ran inline in `EvictLoop`, which delayed flow eviction and shutdown behind a hung `iw`. It now runs on its own 15s ticker goroutine started by `EvictLoop`.
- `parseIWScanSecurity`: an RSN element advertising `FT/PSK FT/SAE` but no plain `PSK` was labelled `WPA3_SAE`. It is now `WPA2_WPA3_PSK`. This only affects the label; it never produced a false open-network warning.

`go test ./...` and `golangci-lint` pass, and a new table case covers the FT-only AP.

body:
<!-- CURSOR_AGENT_PR_BODY_BEGIN -->
המסך הראשון שואל איך מתחילים, בשני כרטיסים. «אני יודע מה אני מחפש» פותח חיפוש ואת כל הסינונים במסך אחד. «עזרו לי לבחור» נשאר שאלה אחת בכל מסך. שני המסלולים חולקים אותה בחירה.

כל כרטיס: כותרת גדולה, שורה קצרה על מה שמקבלים, ואיור קו דק בצבע הכחול של האתר. אין תיבות מזויפות ואין פסים צהובים. האיור נכנס פעם אחת. בלי תנועה הוא נשאר קבוע.

«תארו מה צריך» שולח אל `/api/noamSiteCompanion` באותו אתר, עם אסימון reCAPTCHA מהלקוח `noam-bot-client.js` (המפתח הציבורי מגיע מ־`GET /api/noamBotConfig`). אם השרת עונה `NOT_ACTIVE`, 404, או כל כשל אחר, מוצג «נועם AI עוד לא פעיל. אפשר להמשיך לבחור ולהדפיס.» והכפתור נפתח. הבחירה וההדפסה נשארות.

על אותו ענף, אחרי הסקירות של `afee3d2` ו־`e699fbe`:

- למסך הפתיחה יש ריווח צדדי: `.route-gate{padding:22px 18px 12px}`.
- לחיצה על כרטיס מסלול לפני שהקטלוג נטען נשמרת, עם שורה «טוענים את הקטלוג…», וממשיכה כשהרשימה מוכנה.
- במסלול המהיר, בחירה שהחיפוש מסתיר נשארת כצ'יפ ונספרת בנפרד. המונה הוא מה שנכנס להדפסה.
- בטלפון, «הצגת הדף המסומן» יושבת בסרגל תחתון גם במסלול המהיר.
- על צ'יפ של בחירה מוסתרת יש × גלוי. לחיצה עליו מסירה את הבחירה מההדפסה.
- `searchHiddenSelected()` מחשב מחדש רק כשהחיפוש, הבחירה, או הסינון שקובע את הרשימה משתנים. ציור מחדש של המסך לא סורק שוב.

ההודעה בפאנל נועם AI («אפשר להתחיל ממפגש ראשון…») ירשה את ברירת המחדל של הדפדפן, כי הפאנל הפתוח יושב על `html` ולא על `body`. עכשיו הגופן של האתר מתחיל ב־`html`, וכל הפאנל — הודעות, צ'יפים, שדה וקפתורים — יורש אותו (`Heebo`, ואז `'Arial Hebrew'`). אותו ירושה גם בשאר מסך המורים ובאשף. כותרות Secular One ו־Amatic SC נשארו. הערת ההדפסה וגובה המדידה שלה לא השתנו.

תמונות הכרטיסים נחתכות מאותו חלון שורה לבן של ההדפסה, ואז נצמדות לדיו של הסעיף עצמו: שורת התשובה (המקפים) וקצה הסעיף הבא יורדים, הגובה גדל לפי התוכן עד 180 פיקסלים, ויש ריווח סביב הסימנים. ההדפסה המסומנת לא השתנתה.

## דף מצומצם אחד, עם תשובות

הדף המצומצם כבר לא מדביק כל דף מקור עם כותרת משלו. סעיפים מכמה רמות נאספים לדף אחד: כותרת אחת (בס״ד, נושא, שם/כיתה/תאריך), סדר לפי רמה ואז מספר שאלה, הוראת השאלה פעם אחת לפני הסעיף הראשון שלה, בס״ד ועמוד N מתוך M בכל עמוד. בסוף בא «תשובות»: התשובה הסופית נחתכת מעמוד «תשובות סופיות» של דף המקור. אין תשובה במקור — השורה היא «אין תשובה במקור».

הדף המסומן (המקור המלא) לא השתנה. אותו צייר רץ במסלול המהיר ובאשף.

## «תארו מה צריך» על נקודת הקצה של האתר החדש

הפאנל הצף (`#noam-site-companion`) קורא לאותה נקודת הקצה דרך אותו לקוח. כשל בפאנל המורים נשאר על המשפט הרגוע. רמזי (`worksheet-viewer-noam.html`) לא נגע. הטופס כבר לא קורא ל־`my-site-2`. הוא קורא ל־`POST /api/noamSiteCompanion` דרך `NoamBotClient`, והגוף כולל `message`, `page`, `teacher`, ו־`botVerification` (`recaptcha-v3` + token). בשרת הסטטי אין עדיין את הנתיב, אז נרשם בקונסול `NOAM_TEACHER_SUGGEST_FAILED BOT_CONFIG_UNAVAILABLE` והמסך מראה רק את המשפט הרגוע.

## מרווח כתיבה, תשובות לפי דיו (`0047a1b`)

שלושת החוסמים מהסקירה של `d67cfc7` תוקנו ב־`0047a1b` ונשארו: מרווח כתיבה עד התווית הבאה, תשובה לפי דיו, ו־9א פעם אחת בבית.

## חפיפה ותשובה לשורה שלה (`c914bb3`)

מוזג על `headless/astro-poc-baseline` (`fef1acb`, כולל PR 96). בלי קונפליקט.

- חפיפה בין שני דפי מקור לא מלבינה את הסעיף המוקדם. בתערובת של נועם (רמה א׳ 1א, 1ב, 2א, 18א, 18ב, 19א, 20ג + רמה ב׳ 1א) שורת שאלה 1 ו־«12, 18» מודפסות, וגם 1ב. שני עמודים, והתשובות נארזות בלי עמוד שמחזיק תשובה אחת.
- כל תשובה נחתכת משורת התווית עד התווית הבאה. דיו שנוגע בקצה החלון ואינו על שורת התווית נזרק. בזוויות, 4א הוא ∡PKQ ו־∡QKR, בלי ∡ABC של 5ב. רמה ב׳ 1א הוא הפתיחה של (x+3)², בלי «16 ב. 36 ג.».
- `0d548c` ו־`050b9c`: בלוק הכותרת של המקור (שם, כיתה, תאריך) לא נכנס מתחת לכותרת שלנו. 3א, 3ב ו־3ג מודפסים.
- בית `871fe9`: 9א פעם אחת, הבית שלם.
- תמונת כרטיס נעצרת לפני השורה הבאה. כשיש שרטוט, שורת השאלה מופרדת ומודפסת גדול יותר, בתוך אותה תקרה של 180px ומכסת הגדלה 1.5.

## תשובות בגודל טבעי (`4568069`)

החוסם של `c914bb3`: התשובות כבר לא מוגדלות ל־72px. הן בגודל הטבעי (לכל היותר ×1.3), כמה מהן באותה שורה, ותערובת נועם יוצאת שני עמודים. רמה ב׳ 1א (`x² + 6x + 9`) יושבת בעמוד 2 עם שאר התשובות.

- סריקה מחדש של 449 הדפים: 30,278 סעיפים, 13 בלי תיבה (חזרה מה־28). אות סעיף שמוזכרת בלי תווית נפרדת חוזרת לזיהוי הקודם.
- `0d548c` 3ב הוא שורת ההזזה, `050b9c` 3ג הוא שורת הכלל. החיתוך נעצר בסיכה של הסעיף הבא.
- רסיס אות שנוגע בקצה התשובה ומופרד ברווח לבן יורד.
- כרטיס זוויות 2א: שורת השאלה גדולה מעל השרטוט. 4א עדיין שורה קטנה.

## גופן Heebo על כל הטקסט בפאנל (`aa8085b`)

המשפט «אפשר להתחיל ממפגש ראשון בפירוק לגורמים לכיתה ט׳, לבחור שאלות קיימות, ולסמן אותן על דף המקור.» נכתב ל־`#noam-site-companion-answer` בתוך `#noam-site-companion`. אין shadow DOM. אותו קובץ ב־`public/` ובשורש.

כל צומת בפאנל, כולל צ'יפים שנוספים אחרי הפתיחה, נועל `font-family: Heebo, 'Arial Hebrew', Arial, sans-serif !important`. בפריוויו ב־390×844, `getComputedStyle` על האלמנט הזה הוא Heebo, והדיו זהה לקובץ Heebo העברי המוטמע (0 פיקסלים הבדל). מול Georgia/Times יש הבדל.

## רק הסעיף שנבחר, והודעה רגועה אחת (`aa9876b`)

סקירת `aa8085b`: שני החוסמים.

- חיתוך של סעיף לבד נעצר בסיכה או בתווית של הסעיף הבא. שורה קודמת שרק נוגעת לא נמשכת פנימה. שרטוט מסומן, כמו הבית, עדיין נפתח מראש השרטוט. רמה ב׳ 10ב, 16ג ו־20ג, ופיתגורס 2ב, בלי התווית שלפניהם. סריקה של 30,536 סעיפים בחטיבת הביניים: בכל חיתוך יש את התווית שנבחרה, ותווית אחרת נשארת רק כשהיא בתוך שרטוט משותף.
- כל כשל של נועם AI, בכל דף, מראה «נועם AI עוד לא פעיל. אפשר להמשיך לבחור ולהדפיס.» הסיבה נשארת בקונסול.

## בלי רסיס שכן, בלי קו אפור, וכרטיסים קריאים (`33a84e9`)

- חלון התשובה נעצר לפני תווית של סעיף אחר. הריפוד של 2 נקודות לא נכנס לאות הבאה, וחיתוך הדיו לא גדל בחזרה מעבר לחלון. בפירוק לגורמים, 2א נעצר אחרי «3», 19א בלי «ב» נגרר, ו־7ג בלי «ד». סריקה של 449 דפי חטיבת הביניים (29,812 סעיפים עם תשובה): אף תווית מנוקדת של סעיף אחר לא נכנסת לחלון.
- קו הפרדה אפור דק מהמקור (בהיר, כמעט ברוחב החלון, עד 3 פיקסלים) נמחק רק ברשימת התשובות. הדיו השחור נשאר. דף המקור המסומן לא משתנה.
- כרטיס פיתגורס 3א לא חותך אות מהשורה שמעל. זוויות 2א: השרטוט (הזווית, החץ והאותיות) נשאר חתיכה אחת. זוויות 1א ו־4א נפרדים לטקסט ולשרטוט וגדלים לגודל קריא, בתוך תקרת 180 פיקסלים.

author: ali-issa
body:
## Summary

- Adds the catalog family. `@netvark/catalog-core` holds the catalog model, `toPublicCatalog`, and `diffCatalogs`. `@netvark/pg-catalog` replays migrations into a throwaway PostgreSQL and writes `catalog.ts`, `public-catalog.ts`, and the Kysely types. `drift` compares a live database with the committed catalog.
- The resource packages derive everything from this catalog, so it has to be exact and deterministic. PGlite 18 and a PostgreSQL 14 server write byte-identical files for the same migrations.
- CHECK constraints become rules a client can enforce with the database's verdict, and stay `null` when no rule is exactly equivalent.
- The `pg-catalog` CLI runs extraction, the CI check, and drift from a `netvark.config.ts` that `defineExtraction` checks as it loads.
- One commit per issue. `rules --check` (#19) waits for the Zod schemas from the resource epic and lands with it, so this PR leaves #15 open.

Part of #15.

## Test plan

- [x] #16: the design, spec, and ADR are checked against the PostgreSQL system catalogs.
- [x] #17: unit and reader tests pass on PGlite and with `CATALOG_PG_URL` against PostgreSQL 14.19. The catalog e2e suite matches the hand-reviewed expected files. The Bun, Deno, and workerd smoke runs pass.
- [x] #17: a real 115-table production schema extracts deterministically on PGlite.
- [x] #18: the recognizer is tested on the exact text PostgreSQL 14 and 18 deparse. Rules agree with the database's verdict on values around every bound, on PGlite and PostgreSQL 14.19, and every accepted pattern matches the same input in both engines.
- [x] #18: on GitLab's current schema, 1,579 of 1,884 CHECKs become rules, with no disagreement across 23,120 probed values. Every CHECK left without a rule was reviewed by shape.
- [x] #69 (found by the GitLab run): GitLab 17.11's schema now extracts to identical bytes on PGlite and PostgreSQL 14.19, and the contacts fixture covers a foreign key to a partitioned table.
- [x] #21: every row of the Kysely type mapping is held against node-postgres on PostgreSQL 14.19. Each insert alternative is accepted and reads back with the select type, and the values the types leave out are refused.
- [x] #21: the contacts application writes and reads every table through Kysely with the generated types, plain and with `CamelCasePlugin`, on PGlite over a socket and on PostgreSQL 14.19.
- [x] #21: the types for the 115-table production schema and for GitLab's 1,093 tables compile against Kysely with typed queries. The production schema's camelCase keys match its existing generated types for all 115 tables, and the run showed those existing types are wrong for `int8`, `tsvector`, and `vector` columns.
- [x] #21: on GitLab, the 17 names `CamelCasePlugin` cannot map back are reported in one `camel_case_mismatch`.
- [x] #20: drift finds no differences between the contacts application and its committed catalog on PGlite over a socket and on PostgreSQL 14.19, also as a role with only `CONNECT` and `USAGE`, and reports exactly the column, policy, and CHECK a hotfix changed. It runs on Bun and Deno too.
- [x] #20: GitLab 17.11's 846 tables and the 115-table production schema, loaded into PostgreSQL 14.19, show no drift against the catalogs PGlite extracted. A hotfix on the GitLab copy shows exactly its three objects.
- [x] CI passed on 73f8700, including the Kysely type table, the Kysely e2e, and drift on PostgreSQL 14 and 18 servers, and drift on Bun and Deno.
- [x] #22: every validation message of `defineExtraction`, every usage error, and the CLI's output and exit codes are tested, with extraction on PGlite and drift on PGlite over a socket. Mutating any exit code, the config directory, strict parsing, or a validation rule fails a test.
- [x] #22: the built bin, run as a package manager runs it, writes the contacts files byte for byte, fails `--check` on a hand edit, and reports drift on PGlite over a socket and on PostgreSQL 14.19. A TypeScript configuration loads where Node.js strips types and fails with directions where it does not.
- [x] #22: installed with npm from packed tarballs, the bin extracts the 115-table production schema (TypeScript configuration, pgvector, camelCase types) and GitLab 17.11, passes `--check`, and shows no drift against PostgreSQL 14.19 copies. After a hotfix it shows exactly the changed objects. Bun and Deno give the same output and exit codes, and GitLab 17.11 with camelCase exits 2 listing its 15 names in one message.
- [x] #22 (found by the real-world run): connection failures now give the driver's or the server's reason, such as a refused connection or a missing database, and still never the URL.

author: chreece
body:
> **Merged to master 2026-10-10** at `51b6946d1e937300389bac5d85e058765e7518cd` after 45/45 offline A40/protocol checks passed on the maintainer's Debian server. This includes explicit profile write guarding and power-off state safeguard. Full Style/blueprint pytest suites did not run because the server lacked dependencies and the assistant environment could not fetch the repository. The last A40 power-off regression test was added after the 45-test run and is not independently executed. Merge was a conservative choice for a read-only profile, **not** a claim of complete test or A40 hardware validation. Issue #5 remains open for capture-backed write support. Release `2026.10.10` is not yet published.

## Why

Issue #5 supplied the full Home Assistant diagnostic for an Aura A40 running V56. It **already establishes successful identification, common 8D11/8D22 BLE communication, protocol v1, eight state queries, and the observed Optical/Music/volume-13 state**. We should make those state values useful without asking the nontechnical reporter for Bluetooth captures.

**The provided diagnostic contains no A40 control/SET frames.** Hardware-safe write mappings cannot be inferred from eight successful GETs. This PR deliberately implements read-only support and leaves A40 write commands disabled.

## Changes

- Dedicated `aura_a40` model profile (not `generic_common`), with *no* `wire_features` or CONTROL source map.
- Strict A40 INFO source decoding for Optical, Bluetooth, AUX and USB. Optical INFO `01` is directly observed, the other three are app-derived plus corroborated by flags and official hardware documentation. No unsupported HDMI/ARC fallback in runtime state decoding.
- Ordinary visible A40-only status sensors: Volume (V56 100-step raw), Input and Sound mode, in English/German/Greek. Existing read-only media-player state retained.
- Distinct readable versus verified writable features in diagnostics and the Capabilities sensor.
- **Safety fix:** `_async_write_verified` now enforces per-model verified write authorization at the BLE dispatcher, not merely in Home Assistant UI visibility. Direct media-player services cannot bypass the Aura A40 write lock.
- Sanitized V56 diagnostic fixture, eight new tests, updated protocol documentation and release metadata `2026.10.10`.

## Evidence

- Reporter: #5 (no additional testing required)
- [ULTIMEA A40 inputs](https://support.ultimea.com/hc/en-us/articles/38299427461273-Multiple-Connection-Methods-for-the-Aura-A40-Soundbar): Optical, AUX, Bluetooth and USB, no HDMI
- [ULTIMEA V56 notes](https://support.ultimea.com/hc/en-us/articles/41571846052249-Aura-A40-APP-OTA-Upgrade-V56): 100-level volume

## Validation and safety

- Locally run focused design contract: **4 passed**.
- Eight new repository regression tests supplied, including the actual read-only sensor values and a direct device-write rejection test, explicit source read mapping, and D70/D80 regressions. Source/fixture integrity checks passed.
- **Second full-suite attempt blocked (2026-10-10):** `ultimea-full-20261010-114748.tar.gz` confirms no existing Python environment with `pytest`, `PyYAML` and `Jinja2`. **No tests were executed in that attempt.** This is a test-environment issue, not a test failure. Do not ask the reporter or maintainer to repeat a dependency discovery check.
- **Independent source review:** every current device-level D80 write feature is present in D80's verified mapping; A40 remains write-disabled by the dispatch guard. This is static review, not a substitute for the unexecuted Style/blueprint pytest suites.
- **Verified on a Debian 13 homeserver, October 10, 2026:** `python3 -u scripts/a40-offline-smoke.py` reports **45 PASSED, 0 FAILED, 0 SKIPPED**, plus integration compilation and JSON validation PASS. Uploaded report: `ultimea-a40-offline-20261010-113937.tar.gz`. The preceding full-test attempt stopped at `pip` dependency download *before any tests*, with no code failure. **Complete Style/blueprint pytest suite and A40 hardware write tests remain unrun.** The PR is kept in draft pending the full-suite decision. Commits carry `[skip ci]`, honoring no GitHub-hosted full tests.
- Zero A40 outgoing write commands added. No change to the existing D80/D70 SET allow-lists.

Closes no issue: #5 should remain open for separately verified write support.
