author: k1moradi
body:
## Problem

Our Firefox diagnostic correlator only counted X11 INCR terminator acknowledgements **globally**. An acknowledgement for a different requestor, property, clipboard generation, or reused XID could misleadingly appear alongside the right Firefox transfer. The first-chunk generation check also matched a string prefix (e.g. `start_generation=5` also matched `50`).

## Change

- Retain the raw cross-transaction `incr_terminator_ack_count` for diagnostic context, but add an explicitly scoped `incr_terminator_ack_correlated` and `incr_terminator_ack_ns` only when exactly one acknowledgement matches the first PNG request's **requestor XID, property, start/current/terminator generation, and `state_match=1`** before later XID reuse or format-list change.
- Match chunk generation by numeric equality, not substring; require the current generation as well.
- Retain the Xlib `send_result` of an issued X11 SelectionNotify as evidence (never call it browser receipt).
- Add offline regression cases for unrelated clients, stale generations, duplicate acknowledgements, reused XIDs, missing `state_match`, and requestor attestation gating.
- Preserve the caller's global `XAUTHORITY` when starting the private test harness; the child `xdpyinfo` probe receives its own explicit authenticated environment. A fully mocked offline test confirms no Xvfb or clipboard process is spawned.
- Document actual Codex-reported native Qt6/52-patch/29-test offline results, clock-domain boundaries, and a possible private-Xvfb X-Resource v1.2 PID lookup as a *future, conditional* Firefox XID attribution method. No live X11 queries were added.

## Remaining gates

The browser runner is a **browser leg**, not a complete peer/owner orchestrator. A successful INCR terminator ack is stronger **X11 protocol evidence**, not a trusted Firefox paste event or PNG File. XRes must be available on the isolated private Xvfb and each returned PID independently matched to the caller-attested Firefox process tree; no guessed Firefox XID is accepted.

## Tests and safety

All changes are metadata-only Python test helpers/docs. No production xrdp/chansrv patch changes, service operations, installed-binary changes, physical display, clipboard, Xvfb/Firefox runtime, RDP sessions, or deployment. This draft stacks on PR #31 and does not modify Codex's host validation paths or PR #32.

## Verified final offline CI

- Final head: `bf0721cef788d67226fec0922beb4d843cea61d1`.
- [GitHub Actions 38039039604](https://github.com/k1moradi/xrdp-console/actions/runs/38039039604): **19/19 CTests passed**, Linux job 114175425660.
- The Firefox classification unit exercises unrelated/stale/duplicate INCR acknowledgements, requestor/property reuse, exact generation comparison, and the browser attestation gate. It also fully mocks the private Xvfb launcher to verify the caller's `XAUTHORITY` remains unchanged; **no X11 process is started**.
- Codex's 52-patch replay, 14-unit chansrv native link, 29 fresh xrdp unit checks, and C++23 Qt6 helper compile are **separate host-reported results**; this PR does not rerun or modify them.
- Still pending: proof that X-Resource v1.2 is supported by the future private Xvfb; a verified Firefox X11 requestor mapping; an authorized private Firefox A/B and real macOS screenshot acceptance.

| `Sancti/01-23o` | 2024-01-23 | Emerentiana: Collect/Secret `Emerentiánæ` (genitive), Postcommunion `Emerentiána` (ablative); original English/French `Emerentiana`/`Émérentienne` |
| `Sancti/02-15` | 2024-02-15; 2027-02-15 | Martyrs Faustinus and Jovita: `Faustíni et Jovítæ` (genitive pair), exact complete dual placeholder `N. et N.` / `N. and N.` |
| `Sancti/03-04cc` | 2024-03-04 | Pope Lucius I: `Lúcium` (accusative after `per beátum`), English Lucius / French Lucien |
| `Sancti/05-25o` | 2027-05-25 | Pope Urban I: French `Urbain`; already named in Latin and English |
| `Sancti/05-26o` | 2027-05-26 | Pope Eleutherius: `Eleuthérium` (accusative), English Eleutherius / French Eleuthère |
| `Sancti/06-19o` | 2027-06-19 | Martyrs Gervasius and Protasius, named as a pair in English Collect, Secret and Postcommunion |

### Implementation
- The **existing** `ao-boot-4ef16d2b0e26d68c.js` source owner applies these mappings to commemorations **after their exact source identity is resolved**, before adding them to the composed Mass.
- Only explicitly authorized source path + prayer section + language combinations are substituted. Latin grammar is per individual prayer, never a universal `N.` replacement. Unrecognized owner/source cases remain unresolved and are not declared certified; missing-case or half-pair matches in a known owner throw instead of fabricating text.
- `tests/mass-proper-composition-integrity.mjs` executes the **actual production function**, validating original language forms, six owner boundaries, paired names, rejection of unapproved sections and preservation of already named text.
- `tests/calendar-1962-rogations-commemoration-e2e.mjs` checks **real composed prayers** on all seven original dates, correct commemoration owner, absence of leftover `N.`, and the named forms for each pertinent oration.
- `tools/calendar/proper-source-batch-100.mjs` makes **any** unresolved name occurrence in the unchanged deterministic first-100 Proper sample a CI failure (new exit code 7), while retaining Latin/EN/FR completeness gates.

author: caomengxuan666
body:
## Non-cfg-layer Windows-hardcode audit

Sister of the cfg-gate audit (#492). Scope: Windows assumptions that live **outside** `cfg(windows)` gates — strings, defaults, docs, product behavior. Classification: **(a)** legitimate Windows-native code behind cfg gates — kept; **(b)** Windows assumptions wrongly active/visible on non-Windows builds — fixed; **(c)** stale/dangling docs & copy — fixed. Report-only items were deliberately not touched (see footer).

Base: origin/master @ 61dd62f5. Windows behavior byte-identical (unix-arm additions or cfg(windows)-scoped text only).

### Fixed in this PR

| # | Location | Class | Finding | Disposition |
|---|----------|-------|---------|-------------|
| 1 | `src/expand/tilde/tilde.rs` — `home_value()` | b | USERPROFILE fallback (`env_vars.get("USERPROFILE")` + `env::var("USERPROFILE")`) ran un-gated; a stray USERPROFILE exported by cross-platform tooling would hijack `~` on unix once HOME is unset. Ledger E9 revision planned this gate ("随 getpwnam 改造一并") but it never landed. | cfg(windows) gate; unix arm returns `""` — identical to today's unix behavior (HOME unset + no USERPROFILE). The pre-existing `windows_home_value_prefers_home_before_userprofile` test was already cfg(windows). |
| 2 | `src/main.rs` — `print_identity_disclosure()` (`--help`) | b | Native-persona branch unconditionally printed `switch: unset RUBASH_IDENTITY (or set any other value) to return to msys` — false on non-Windows builds where `current_identity()` is hardwired Native (`identity.rs:42-50`). | Platform-split: unix prints `persona: native (honest-native; non-Windows builds are always native)` and `switch: n/a (RUBASH_IDENTITY only selects personas on Windows)`. Windows msys/native text unchanged. |
| 3 | `src/main.rs` — `print_identity_report()` (`--identity`) | b | Same defect: unix reported `RUBASH_IDENTITY=native; honest-native` (implies the var was set) and the msys-default switch line. | Platform-split: `non-Windows build; honest-native` + n/a switch line. Windows text unchanged. |
| 4 | `src/build_info.rs` — `version_appendix()` (Windows `--version` note) | c | Note pointed users to `docs/platform-support.md` — **the file does not exist** anywhere in the repo; both test assertions anchored the dangling path. | Repointed to `README.md, Identity and Compatibility` (where the persona contract actually lives); `src/build_info.rs:107` + `tests/cli_tests.rs:4146` assertions updated. |
| 5 | `README.md` — Quick Start / Build from Source | c | `> Full functionality requires Windows today.` directly contradicted the Platform status section 130 lines above (Linux native runs verified in WSL, macOS CI-green). | Replaced with an accurate cross-platform note. |
| 6 | `README.zh-CN.md` — 从源码构建 | c | `> 完整功能当前需要 Windows。` — same stale claim. | Replaced (kept Chinese to match the file). |
| 7 | `README.md` — Identity section, default-persona bullet | c | Presented the MSYS persona as the unqualified default; non-Windows builds never take it. | Added the qualification matching `identity.rs` module docs (non-Windows builds always report honest-native). |

### Verified correct — no change needed (a-class spot checks)

| Location | Check |
|----------|-------|
| `src/executor/external_inner.rs` — `materialize_required_windows_env` | `#[cfg(windows)]` real body + `#[cfg(not(windows))]` no-op (ledger E8 fixed). SystemRoot/WINDIR/ComSpec copies at :287 also `#[cfg(windows)]`. |
| `src/executor/path.rs` — `apply_required_windows_child_environment` | cfg pair, unix side no-op. |
| `src/executor/path.rs` — `windows_command_processor()` (`C:\Windows\System32\cmd.exe` fallback) | Only reachable under `is_windows_batch_file()`/`is_windows_powershell_script()` which embed `cfg!(windows)` and return false on unix. |
| `src/executor/init.rs` | HOME-from-USERPROFILE seed (:106), TMPDIR+HOME backslash rewrite (:449), TMPDIR injection (:541) — all `#[cfg(windows)]` (ledger E4/E19 fixed). |
| `src/executor/path.rs` — `standard_path()` | cfg!(windows) arm + unix `confstr(_CS_PATH)` (ledger E5 fixed). |
| `src/executor/path.rs` — `has_path_separator` / `shell_path_to_process` | cfg-split; unix treats only `/` (ledger E7 fixed). |
| `src/executor/lookup_paths.rs` — `/usr/bin/mv`, `/bin/{cat,ls}` suite bridge | `#[cfg(windows)]` (ledger E2 fixed). |
| `src/executor/identity.rs` | Fully platform-aware: unix uname(2)/MACHTYPE/OSTYPE arms; MSYS persona unreachable off-Windows. |
| `src/locale.rs` | `platform_collate` cfg pair; windows-sys import gated. |
| `src/proc_vfs.rs`, `src/fd/windows_impl.rs`, `src/console_readline.rs` | Whole-file/function cfg(windows) gating with unix counterparts. |
| `src/executor/local_helpers.rs` — `safe_temp_dir_string()` | Unix arm `/tmp` (rubash#232). |
| `src/executor/job_builtins.rs` — `fc` default `vi`; `script_driver.rs` PS1 default `\s-\v\$ ` | GNU-correct defaults on all platforms, not Windows hardcode. |
| Hardcoded `C:\...` / `System32` literals | All in `#[cfg(windows)]` bodies, doc comments, or `#[cfg(test)]` fixtures. |

### Reported — deliberately NOT changed

| Location | Class | Finding | Why not fixed here |
|----------|-------|---------|--------------------|
| `src/bin/bash.rs` + `Cargo.toml` `[[bin]] name="bash"` | b (release-layer) | E20 stands: `locate_shell()` probes only `niu.exe`/`winuxsh.exe`, so on unix the shim always exits 127; worse, unix builds ship a `bash` binary that can shadow the system bash in PATH. Ledger routes this to the C2 release batch (two-part: platform-split probe names + unix release stops installing the shim). | The probe-name half alone would make the shadowing *quieter* (silent forward instead of loud 127) while the release half is pending — a product/packaging decision for the captain. Recorded as a known gap in `docs/host-contract.md:73`. |
| `src/executor/support_names.rs:763` — `executable_extensions()` | b (benign today) | Un-gated PATHEXT/`;`-split helper; sole caller (`lookup_paths.rs:139`) is cfg-gated. Ledger E7 revision recommends renaming to prevent future misuse. | Rename churns an executor-facing name; zero behavior gain today. |
| Display-path `.replace('\\', "/")` normalizations (`external_finish.rs`, `lookup_paths.rs`, `init.rs`, `external_file_builtins.rs`, …) | b (cosmetic) | Ungated; on unix a legal filename containing `\` renders lossily in display paths. | Display-only, and the sites sit in/next to the executor hot path (#242 conflict zone) — report only per audit constraints. |
| `~` with HOME unset expands to `""` (all platforms) | semantic | GNU keeps the word verbatim (`echo ~` prints `~`). | Cross-platform semantic deviation, not a Windows hardcode; touching it changes suite-visible behavior. |
| Bare `~` has no unix getpwuid fallback (ledger E9 follow-up) | semantic | HOME unset + USERPROFILE absent → `~` is empty instead of passwd home. | New libc surface, belongs with the tilde semantic fix above. |

### Verification

- `cargo fmt` clean.
- `cargo check --lib` (x86_64-pc-windows-msvc): clean.
- `cargo test --lib`: **642 passed; 2 failed** — `builtins::pwd::tests::logical_mode_reports_posix_drive_pwd_by_default` and `executor::path::tests::virtual_system_root_operand_resolution_keeps_option_b_and_legacy_verbatim`; **both fail identically on pristine origin/master** (WSL-interop environment-dependent assertions, e.g. expects `/mnt/c`), i.e. pre-existing, no new failures.
- `cargo check --lib --target x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu`: clean (unix arm compiles).
- Linux/macOS `cargo test --lib` runs: pending CI on this PR (no local linux toolchain for test execution).

Conflict hygiene: no changes in cfg-gate audit territory (#492), lexer word/scanner (#462 neighborhood), or the executor hot path (#242 neighborhood).

The old H1 read like a list of keywords. The new one opens with the main benefit (no falling needles) and still has «ёлка» and «макраме» for SEO. «На стену» and «ручная работа» now live in the paragraph.

author: muralis456
body:
## Summary

This change closes stale-derived-result gaps in the production replan strategy:

- A cheaper-flight replan refreshes budget and itinerary after flight options change.
- A hotel upgrade refreshes budget and itinerary after the hotel result changes.
- Removing expensive attractions rebuilds the itinerary from the pruned checkpoint state without rerunning research and repopulating removed attractions.
- Adding a destination invalidates destination-dependent flight, hotel, research, weather, budget, and itinerary results.
- Adds regression coverage for these dependency invalidation rules.

## Validation

- GitHub Actions Maven package/test workflow: **passed** on the latest head commit.
- Branch created from `main`; PR remains open for review.

## Remaining production hardening

This PR does not claim to solve external-provider idempotency/reconciliation. Those require provider-aware operation IDs and reconciliation for ambiguous outcomes. Role differentiation remains least-privilege (`USER`) until an authoritative authenticated role source is available; no client-supplied role should be trusted.

body:
## 変更内容

セキュリティ調査で見つかった「一般ユーザーがブラウザから直接コイン・預金・株・馬券・レース結果などを書き換えられる」問題への第1段階の修正のうち、**アプリ・通知 Worker・derby-runner の変更**です。**Firestore Rules の変更は別PR（第1段階B）** にしています。

**このPRだけではブラウザからの直接書き込みはまだ防げません**（Rules は従来どおり）。安全な移行のため、順番は次の通りです。
1. このPR（A）をマージ → Worker が本番に公開され、アプリが Worker 経由で動くようになる
2. 本番で正規の操作（賭け・精算・預金・株・ログインボーナス・名前変更など）が動くことを確認
3. 第1段階B（Rules ロックダウン）をマージ → ブラウザからの直接書き込みを禁止

この順番なら、移行中に正規ユーザーの操作が壊れません（A の時点では Rules が緩いままなので、Worker 経由の書き込みも従来の直接書き込みも成功します）。

### サーバー側（notify-worker/worker.js）
`POST /economy` を追加。本人の ID トークンを検証し、**自分の `users` だけ**を操作します。残高・株価・締切・オッズ・レース結果・払い戻し額は、すべてサーバーで計算・確認します（ブラウザから送られた値は使いません）。

- 預け入れ・引き出し・緊急融資・返済
- 株の売買（株価は `market/current` のサーバーの値）
- ログインボーナス（日本時間で1日1回）・追加ボーナス・初期コイン
- 馬券の購入（受付中のレース・締切・券種・馬・金額・残高を確認。手動レースの `betCount` も同じ書き込みで加算）
- レース結果の生成（発走後・まだ無いときだけ。サーバーが作ったものでない結果は移行後に信用しない）
- 精算（結果とオッズからサーバーが払い戻しを計算。固定オッズ方式も山分け方式も）
- 名前変更の経済項目の引き継ぎ（`from`・`to` がどちらも自分のときだけコピーして `from` を消す）

読んだときの更新時刻を条件にしたまとめて書き込みで、競合は読み直してやり直します。オッズ・結果・払い戻しの計算は `derby-odds.js`（アプリ・derby-runner と同じ）と一致することをテストで確認しています。

### アプリ（script.js）
預金・引き出し・株の売買・融資・返済・ログインボーナス・追加ボーナス・初期コイン・馬券の購入・レース結果の生成・精算・名前変更の経済項目の引き継ぎを、すべて Worker 経由に変更しました（ブラウザからの直接書き込みをやめました）。画面・操作・メッセージは今まで通りです。

### derby-runner（自動開催・精算）
- 締切後に作られた馬券・中身が正しくない馬券は払わない（外れとして精算し、理由を残す）
- 移行後（`SERVER_RESULTS_FROM` 以降）は、サーバー以外が作ったレース結果を信用せず作り直す

## テスト

- `notify-worker` 単体テスト：115 OK / 0 FAIL（うち `/economy` の新規 22 件：銀行・株・ボーナス・馬券・結果生成・精算〈固定オッズ・山分け〉・名前引き継ぎ・初期コイン・不正な入力・権限・同時更新・オッズ一致）
- `derby-runner/validation.test.mjs`：6 OK / 0 FAIL（締切後・不正な馬券を払わない／サーバー以外の結果を信用しない）、PR で走るテストジョブを追加
- Emulator + 実 Worker + アプリ（第1段階B の Rules ロックダウンと合わせて）の e2e：9 OK / 0 FAIL
  - 初期コイン・ボーナス・ログインボーナス、預金・引き出し、株の売買、馬券購入、結果生成・精算（払い戻しがコインに反映）、名前変更の引き継ぎ、ブラウザからの直接改変（コイン・預金・株・馬券・結果）が拒否される
- 回帰（Emulator + Playwright、Worker を起動して実施）：読み取り削減 7、PR #37 追加 7、PR #37 エラーの区別 17 すべて 0 FAIL。ゆうダービーの演出（リプレイ）e2e：賭け・リプレイは成功
- 未確認：ゆうダービーの「ライブ演出中に結果が出る」部分の e2e は、テスト環境で開催時刻を実時間に合わせる必要があり、タイミングが不安定なため確認しきれていません（賭け・結果生成・精算の経路は上記の e2e・単体テストで確認済み）

author: kiziltepehakan
body:
🚨 **Severity:** MEDIUM
💡 **Vulnerability:** The logger class in `src/logger.js` previously emitted the raw payloads and arguments directly to `window.console` when debug mode was enabled. This could lead to developers inadvertently exposing sensitive data (auth payloads, API tokens, passwords) to the client's browser console, posing a significant risk if clients save or share logs.
🎯 **Impact:** Exposure of sensitive user credentials, session tokens, or API keys directly to the browser console.
🔧 **Fix:** Introduced a generic `sanitize` function in the logger that intercepts all outgoing console logs. It traverses incoming plain objects/arrays (handling circular references via a `WeakSet` safely), replacing values associated with common sensitive keys (`password`, `token`, `secret`, `credential`, `key`, `auth`) with `[REDACTED]`. It respects binary structures, Dates, and standard primitives.
✅ **Verification:**
1. Confirmed local changes to `src/logger.js` and `.jules/sentinel.md`.
2. Verified the local build script runs correctly (`npx webpack --mode=production`).
3. Ran existing test suites via `npx jest` to ensure no regression was introduced.

body:
## 코드 변경 (이 PR)

`infra/monitoring/docker-compose.yml`
- `ports: 127.0.0.1:3000` → `3000:3000`. 서버 안에서만 받던 걸 ALB 가 닿게. 외부 노출은 보안 그룹 `k6-sg` 가 ALB 에서 오는 3000 만 허용해서 막습니다
- `GF_SERVER_ROOT_URL=https://grafana.moyeota.p-e.kr`. 없으면 로그인 리다이렉트·공유 링크가 `localhost:3000` 으로 만들어집니다
- 관리자 비밀번호 기본값 `admin` 제거. 환경변수가 없으면 기동 자체가 안 됩니다(`${GRAFANA_PASSWORD:?…}`)

`infra/monitoring/up.sh` (신규)
- 파라미터 스토어 `/moyeota/monitoring/GRAFANA_PASSWORD` 를 읽어 `docker compose up -d`. k6 서버 역할(`ec2-ssm-role`)로 읽히는 것 확인했습니다
- 나머지 비밀(`PG_EXPORTER_*`)은 서버의 `.env` 그대로

`README.md` 모니터링 절: 주소, 기동 방법, 공유는 Viewer 계정으로

## 콘솔 작업 (코드 밖, 머지 전후 무관)

- [x] ACM 와일드카드 `*.moyeota.p-e.kr` 발급
- [x] 가비아 `grafana` CNAME → ALB
- [ ] 대상 그룹 `moyeota-grafana-tg` (HTTP 3000, 상태 검사 `/api/health`), 대상 k6-ec2
- [ ] 리스너 443 에 와일드카드 인증서 추가, 규칙: 호스트 `grafana.moyeota.p-e.kr` → grafana-tg
- [ ] `k6-sg` 인바운드 3000, 소스 = ALB 보안 그룹

## 머지 후 k6 서버에서

**사전 1회**: k6 서버에 AWS CLI 가 없습니다(SSM 에이전트는 snap 이라 별개). `up.sh` 가 없으면 안내 메시지를 내고 멈춥니다.

```bash
apt-get install -y unzip && curl -sS https://awscli.amazonaws.com/awscli-exe-linux-x86_64.zip -o /tmp/awscliv2.zip && unzip -qo /tmp/awscliv2.zip -d /tmp && /tmp/aws/install
```


```bash
cd /root/Backend && git pull && infra/monitoring/up.sh grafana
docker compose -f infra/monitoring/docker-compose.yml exec grafana grafana cli admin reset-admin-password "$(aws ssm get-parameter --name /moyeota/monitoring/GRAFANA_PASSWORD --with-decryption --query Parameter.Value --output text)"
```

기존 Grafana 는 `.env` 의 비밀번호로 한 번 떠 있어서 환경변수만으로는 안 바뀝니다. 리셋 한 번이 필요합니다. 

Prometheus(9090)·Loki·Tempo 는 그대로 내부. 인증이 없습니다.

author: vadimsidoryk
body:
The Test bench window now starts with a goal written in words. Everything below it is kept in `lab.json` until the building is demolished.

- **Goal:** an agent writes the first cases from it. The goal's words choose the metric the window leads with: tokens, time or quality. A large **Run all cases** button runs every case.
- **Settings:**
  - the scheme's AI tool and tier;
  - the bare harness's AI tool and tier;
  - the spend limit per case;
  - a blind judge that scores both results 0–10, shown to it in random order.
- **Cases:**
  - an agent writes them, or you add one by hand with its title, input and the building it goes into (when the chain has several ways in);
  - **Test this case** on each;
  - the last result shows Δ time, Δ tokens and Δ quality against the bare harness.
- **What to change:** an agent reads the code, the roads and the last tests, then proposes changes to code, roads, prompts or settings. Ticked proposals become tasks for an Agent pool or go down the bench's roads.
- The shipped cases and reviews move into a fold below. It starts open while the lab has no cases of its own.
- **Backend:**
  - `realm/lab_cases.py`, `gui/lab_runs.py`;
  - `orkcraft bench chain --cases-file --bare-tool --bare-tier`;
  - a single building runs as a chain of one, and every one of its events counts as coming back;
  - a case can go into External listeners as a mail.
- **Fix:** concurrent saves of `lab.json` no longer share one temp file.

Tests:
- `tests/test_lab_cases.py`, `tests/test_gui_lab.py`, a new case in `test_bench_kits` and a browser test all pass.
- The full suite passes; `test_wiki_quality` failed once under load and passes when run alone.
- All 61 browser tests passed after the fix: the three older bench browser tests had failed once before the shipped fold was opened by default, and the 4 bench tests pass on a re-run.

author: finanzinstitut
body:
## Why "can't add" happened
- The friends screens rebuilt only once after a button press, before the server had answered, and never again. Requests, acceptances and messages therefore only showed up after reopening the screen. The screens now watch a revision counter and rebuild live.
- The first long poll had no feed version, so it couldn't notice changes for up to 25 s. `/friends` now returns `version`.
- Name lookup fell back to `api.minecraftservices.com` only when `api.mojang.com` refused Cloudflare. Before that, existing names came back as "no player by that name".
- The status line sat underneath the "Try again" button.

## New: group chats
- Create a group from your friends with multiple selection, write in it, invite more friends, and leave.
- Members only see messages sent since they joined.
- The last person to leave deletes the group.
- Worker: `chat_groups`, `group_members`, `group_messages` and `/groups/{create,invite,leave,message}`. `/poll` delivers `groupMessages` with `gcursor`.

## Other changes
- The Mojang handshake is a direct `services().sessionService().joinServer(...)` call. The signature is identical across all four versions.
- Offline profiles get a clear message instead of "handshake failed".
- Failed sends are pulled back out of the chat, with the reason shown.
- History loaded at startup no longer counts as unread.
- Enter sends a request.
- Lists scroll and fit a normal window size.

## Tests
- Worker: `node --test`, 31/31.
- In-game end-to-end against a local worker on **26.3, 26.2, 26.1 and 1.21.11**. The flow:
  1. Add someone by name.
  2. Accept an incoming request.
  3. The friend shows up live.
  4. Chat both ways.
  5. Create a group with two friends; all three write in it.
- Mixin audit OK on every version.

## After merging
The worker needs a redeploy via "Deploy friends worker" so the new tables and endpoints are live. The schema only uses `CREATE … IF NOT EXISTS`, so existing data is kept.

Path

> - two-bot-next is the Together We Own Discord bot, written in Rust, running as one always-on container
> - The gateway subsystem commits a durable checkpoint after every dispatch in `apply_dispatch`
> - A failed checkpoint stops the dispatch worker and is recorded on `operation`, but had no metrics counter, unlike every sibling failure surface
> - Silent worker-stopping failures cannot feed the planned M2.1 alert rules
> - This pull request adds a bounded-label checkpoint-failure counter following the dispatch-drops pattern
> - The benefit is that every checkpoint commit failure is now an alertable exposition series

## Linked Issues or Issue Description

No public issue exists. The `apply_dispatch` Err arm in `crates/bot/src/gateway.rs` records checkpoint commit failures only on `operation`; sibling surfaces (events, REST, voice, DB errors, send admissions, dispatch drops) all increment saturating bounded-label counters in `crates/core/src/metrics.rs`. This PR closes that observability gap with a stage-labeled counter. Related but non-overlapping: #703 names reaction events in the gateway metrics allowlist (different series, no shared lines).

## What Changed

- Added the gateway checkpoint-failure counter name, `stage` label, and every allowed stage value to the metrics-doc conformance pin.

- Added `two_bot_gateway_checkpoint_failures_total{stage}` with the `CHECKPOINT_FAILURE_STAGES` allowlist (`pre_commit`, `commit`) in `crates/core/src/metrics.rs`, including exposition and saturating increment
- `apply_dispatch` in `crates/bot/src/gateway.rs` tracks the failure stage and increments the counter on every Err arm entry; failure causes are never labels
- Added exposition unit tests for bounded increments and hostile-label collapse, and pinned the new series in the `/metrics` HTTP test
- Documented the counter row and label allowlist in `docs/metrics.md` with the M2.1 alert-threshold hook
- Fixed the `gateway_worker_community_facts_drain_failure_warns_and_commits` fixture pin (`1` to `2`): the gate-clearing `MemberAdd` buffers `member_joined` (via `on_join`) plus `rules_accepted` (via the instant `on_gate_cleared`) since member_joined capture landed on main, and the merged-in test still pinned one. Same stale pin is currently on main; this PR carries the repair.

## Verification

- `cargo fmt --all -- --check` passes via the installed toolchain path; `git diff --check` passes.
- Focused test `python3 scripts/cargo_cache.py run -- test -p two-bot-core --test metrics_docs` was refused because no idle below-budget cache slot was available; no direct Cargo fallback was used. Hosted CI is the verification path.
- Pre-review: 4/5 at `75ba1870`; covered the metrics-doc counter/label/stage pins and Rust arm syntax; not covered: Cargo compilation/focused test (cache admission refused); fast tier: formatting and whitespace checks passed.

## Risks

- Low risk. Additive counter only; no behaviour, schema, or alert-rule change. Fixed-cardinality exposition (two stages); hostile labels collapse to `commit` with no new series.

## Model Used

- Initial feature implementation: Meta Muse Spark (`muse-spark-1.3-contributor`), xhigh reasoning; code and shell tools.
- Follow-up conformance-pin fix: OpenAI `gpt-6-luna`; code edit and shell tool use. Context window and reasoning mode were not provided.

## Summary

- Twelve `GQAPagedFwdOp` decode rows set the page pool to the table width, so every request's table points at the same pages and the KV cache stays in L2. The pool is now batch times width, so each request draws its own pages, as in serving.
- Two decode rows with a cache length of 4001 put the cache end inside a key tile, on 64- and 256-row pages.
- The twelve labels are kept, so their nightly history steps up once: these rows now measure KV read from HBM.
- `MHADecodePagedWithKVCacheFwdOp` serves SM89 with `GQADecodePagedKernel`, which zeroes the value rows past the cache end. SM90 picks the warp-specialized kernel, so no CI test reached that zeroing. An `sm89` test now runs the partly-filled-cache check on one request whose cache end cuts a key tile.

Part of #2500.

author: akreit
body:
## Summary
The map page now has **one search box** that searches both saved Only Paws places and **any place on Google Maps** (issue #12).

- **`src/app/components/map/MapSearchBox.vue`** (new): an accessible combobox.
  - The input has `role="combobox"` with `aria-expanded`, `aria-controls` and `aria-activedescendant`; the dropdown is a `listbox` of `option` items.
  - The dropdown is grouped into **Saved places**, each with its category icon, and **Google Maps**.
  - Keyboard: ↑/↓ move with wrap-around, Enter selects, Escape or a click outside closes.
  - 48px rows, max 50vh with scrolling, full width in the panel on mobile.
  - It shows loading and empty states, and a quiet *"Google place suggestions unavailable"* note when Google fails.
- **`src/app/composables/usePlacesSearch.ts`** (new) uses only the **new Places API**:
  - `AutocompleteSuggestion.fetchAutocompleteSuggestions` with one `AutocompleteSessionToken` per typing session; the token is reset after a selection.
  - Results are biased to the current map bounds, falling back to a 20 km circle around the center.
  - On selection it calls `placePrediction.toPlace()` and then `fetchFields` with the full details field list (`PLACE_DETAIL_FIELDS`).
  - Any failure (library load, request, key or API not enabled) is caught and sets `placesUnavailable`, so nothing breaks in the UI.
  - No legacy `Autocomplete` widget or `PlacesService` anywhere. **Map clicks on Google POIs now also use Places API (New)** (`new Place({ id }).fetchFields(...)`), replacing the legacy `PlacesService.getDetails` path in `useMap.ts`, which has been removed. Search picks and POI clicks share one details mapper in `utils/google-place.ts`, so both prefill website, phone and hours.
- **`src/app/utils/map-search.ts`** (new, pure):
  - Builds the dropdown model, up to 5 saved and 5 Google results.
  - Drops Google suggestions that match a saved `googlePlaceId`.
  - Provides the keyboard index helpers.
  - Maps `Place` and saved `Location` to the existing `GooglePlaceDetails`.
- **`map.vue`:**
  - **Search:** a debounced search (300ms, at least 2 characters) runs the saved-places search and the Google suggestions in parallel; stale results are discarded. Category chips still filter saved results and markers. Clearing the input restores the normal listing.
  - **Saved result:** the map pans and zooms to 16, and the existing preview card opens with "Open in Only Paws".
  - **Google result:** the map fits the place's viewport (or pans and zooms to 16) and drops **one temporary blue pin**, which is distinct from the category pins and removed when the card is dismissed. The existing `MapPlacePreviewCard` and **prefilled Add-location flow** are reused: name, address, lat/lng, `googlePlaceId` and an inferred category. If a saved place already has that `googlePlaceId`, the card offers to open it instead.
- **`map-markers.ts`:** `getSearchResultMarkerIcon()`, a solid blue pin.
- **`MapPlacePreviewCard.vue`:** the "Add this place…" hint is hidden when the place already exists.

## ⚠️ Google Cloud requirement
The Maps key must have **"Places API (New)"** enabled, and allowed if the key restricts which APIs it can use. The existing Maps JavaScript API alone isn't enough. This now applies to **both** the search box **and map clicks on Google POIs**: the click-a-POI → preview card → Add flow fetches details through Places API (New) too.

Without it:
- the search box still works for saved places and shows the quiet "unavailable" note;
- clicking a Google POI shows the "Could not load details" error instead of the preview card.

Confirm the production key allows Places API (New) before merging.

## Testing
- `npm run lint`, `npm run typecheck`, `npm run format:check`: clean.
- `npm run test:unit`: 27 files, 251 tests passing; coverage is 95% lines and 88% functions. New tests with a mocked `google.maps`:
  - `map-search.spec.ts`: grouping, caps, dedupe, wrap-around index, mapping.
  - `usePlacesSearch.spec.ts`: suggestion mapping, token reuse and reset, bias fallbacks, plain-literal bias, error flag and recovery, `fetchFields` fields.
  - `MapSearchBox.spec.ts`: ARIA, keys, click, Escape, outside click, minimum length, loading, empty and unavailable states.
  - `map-markers.spec.ts`: the new pin.
- **Local headless Chrome** (`nuxt dev`, seeded DB, placeholder Maps key):
  - Typing "park" shows *Saved places → Cubbon Park Dog Run* plus "Google place suggestions unavailable".
  - ↓ highlights the option and sets `aria-activedescendant`; Enter closes the dropdown and opens the preview card with "Open in Only Paws"; Escape closes it.
  - The Google request reaches Places API (New) and fails only with `API key not valid`, as expected with the placeholder key.

  Screenshots: `places-search.png` and `places-search-selected.png` are saved on the agent box but not attached here (the CLI can't upload images).
- **Bug found by that run and fixed:** location bias was passing `mapStore.bounds`, a Google `LatLngBounds` wrapped in a Pinia/Vue reactive proxy. Google's library threw `Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'lat')` before even calling the API. The bias now sends a plain `{north,south,east,west}` literal, with a test.
- **Vercel preview** (`only-paws-45xizrdxb`): Ready; the migration step was correctly skipped (`VERCEL_ENV=preview`). `/map` and `/api/locations` return 200, and the new combobox is in the served HTML.
- **Not verified:** real Google suggestions, the viewport fit and the blue pin with a real key. The preview is behind Vercel Authentication, and the key may not allow preview domains. Please check on the preview or after deploy: type a place name, pick a Google result, and use "Add".

## Notes
- The "already saved" check for a picked Google place uses the currently loaded saved results. During a text search those are narrowed to matches, so a saved place whose text doesn't match the query can show "Add" instead of "Open". This is harmless: `POST /api/locations` looks up a known `googlePlaceId` and returns the existing location instead of creating a duplicate (`src/server/api/locations/index.post.ts`), so the unique constraint is never hit. *(Corrected: an earlier version of this note wrongly said it would hit the unique constraint.)*
- No dependency, server, schema or `nuxt.config` changes.

Implemented with Claude Code and reviewed before opening.

Closes #12

author: jarviisha
body:
The agent pane takes the design proven in `labs/ui-labs`: its transcript, its edgeless composer and its menus. Every feature the lab does not draw is kept and redrawn in the lab's language. Where the person preferred the app's own UI, it stays, and the lab's Departures table says so.

## Transcript

- **A reading column of 44rem** in 1rem text with 1.6 leading. Wide content scrolls inside its well, so the old rule of "100 mono columns of a diff" is gone.
- **Wells are filled and have no edge.** The copy buttons and the line and height caps stay.
- **A thought is its own block.** So are answered permissions and questions: activity clusters hold tools only.
- **What runs opens, and closes when it is done.** The plan stays open. The reader's fold always wins, including on a running cluster. Folds keyed by position are dropped on resume, because a resumed transcript is numbered afresh.
- **The prompt bubble takes the lab's shape and fill.** It keeps the app's thumbnails and *not sent*.
- **The running line is an accent spinner.** It keeps the turn clock, the running-task count and the status.
- **A finished turn ends on a footer.** It reads *Processed in 1m 12s*, and its Copy takes the closing paragraph.
- **The transcript has a scrollbar** on the panel's edge, ending at the composer.
- **The adapter's `[Request interrupted by user…]` chunk is now a notice**, *Interrupted*, instead of a prompt the person never typed.

## Composer

- **No edge.** A `raised` surface and a two-layer lift set the card off; it has a contrast test in `theme.rs`.
- **No line is ever added to the card.** A refusal is Send's tooltip, and a failed paste is a toast on the window it happened in.
- **The chips:**
  - Fast is a toggle when its two choices read as on and off.
  - The effort has a chip and a menu of its own, beside the model's.
  - *Stop* is solid danger with its word, and *Queue* is outlined.
  - The strip under the card stacks the branch over the mode when narrow.
- **Each chip's menu opens just above the chip**, without the chip's tooltip, and follows it when the chip moves. Completions and the attachments list still span the stack. Menus show 6 rows, then *N more*, and have no footer of keys.
- **Staged files rest above the card in one row.** A file and an image share one chip. A row too long fades out where it is cut, beside *Show all N*.

## Pinned cards

- **The app's own permission and question cards stay**, as the person preferred them to the lab's.
- **One card is pinned at a time, the oldest.** A line under it says how many more wait. The next card takes its place and the caret once the first is answered.
- **A permission's command scrolls inside a bounded box**, with no *Show all*.

## Docs

- Root `DESIGN.md` describes all of the above. It is back under its line budget: the workflow launcher's detail now lives only in `docs/workflows.md`.
- `labs/ui-labs/DESIGN.md` closes the Departures rows the app now matches and adds rows for what the app does on purpose.

## Checks

- `make clippy CLIPPY_EXTRA="-- -D warnings"` is clean, and `make fmt` was run.
- `cargo test --locked --workspace --no-fail-fast` passes. Locally, `documents_are_written_in_english` trips on an untracked `localDocs/` note that CI does not have.
- The lab's tests pass.
- The menus were driven in a headless session: *Mention a file*, a model pick and a mode pick.
- *Attach files…* is not exercised: it opens the desktop's native dialog.

- Deny interactive question/plan-confirmation tools in headless tasks and use Bun's lower-memory mode.
- Handle a slow read-only idle check with a bounded five-second confirmation window, one-second attempts, and retries only for that GET timeout. Never resubmit the model prompt; protocol errors, process exit, cancellation and shutdown failures still fail. A deployment-host trace observed this GET taking 3869 ms.
- Keep the authorized trial 512 MiB / repository 768 MiB test delivery targets in separate strict image-provenance fields. The earlier repository OOM at 512 MiB remains a failed result. General self-host defaults/ceilings, CPU/PID/swap/network/credential/provider-call limits and production are unchanged; trial deadline 300 seconds and repository 900 seconds.

## Verification

Current fixed head: 203dba346599560f2c9d7732e44287b851b887da.

- The final three-file idle-wait delta passed both independent Standards and Spec review with zero actionable findings, 26 focused completion/image-delivery tests and diff check. The slow-query regression was observed failing on c444 and passing after the fix. Late idle, repeated timeouts, non-timeout protocol failures and process exit remain negative regressions.
- Baseline c444bc7e547ce6ef07afd520b861152bbd8dd0c3 passed frozen npm run release:verify: 923 unit tests (918 pass / 5 platform skips), 99 scripts, 393 source Web plus 3 built Web checks, 5 integration and 9 e2e, both Git-less npm installation checks, and zero reported vulnerabilities. All eight c444 CI checks passed, including actual trial 512 MiB / repository 768 MiB containers and both guarded CPU modes. These are baseline evidence, not substituted for current-head CI.
- The unchanged UI passed ten Chromium/WebKit ordinary-pointer flows (desktop, short/narrow desktop, phone and tablet), Codex/DSH local pause/resume, exact targets, drafts/Chat, staged GitHub setup and no-login-flash checks; six-size WebKit example/onboarding coverage and an independent native Safari preview passed. No existing login tabs or real repositories were modified.
- An isolated c444 host run with a dependency observer passed completed final response, strict idle validation and clean SIGTERM closure in about nine seconds, with one fake-model call and zero real calls. The earlier uninstrumented c444 host failure remains recorded; this success does not establish its exact cause.

## Delivery

The final uninstrumented 203d candidate passed one controlled real-model acceptance on the deployment host: exact configured sf-qwen35-4b, one upstream request, final answer valid, normal container exit and cleanup in 14.253 seconds, no user database/live-service/production change. No further provider acceptance calls are needed. All current pull-request CI checks passed; the duplicate push Windows job failed an unchanged 1000-file Git stress fixture with code_git_unavailable, while the same head's pull-request Windows suite passed (815 unit pass, 0 fail). The existing candidate workflow performs the canonical fresh release gate once before artifact delivery. Merged as d62837f158e2d9bbccece1ff82609f69bd0bae96, with its Git tree verified identical to reviewed head 203d. body:
## Summary

Lands the framework-optional split: express and fastapi become **optional** — the core SDK installs and imports without either — and node conformance becomes **verifiable** for any server, including self-hosted ones built without this SDK. Closes the architectural follow-up from #102/#104.

## Issue Reference

Closes #104

## Changes

### TypeScript — express as optional peer
- `express` moves from `dependencies` to `optional peerDependencies` (`^5.3`) — fresh installs no longer pull it
- Server construction lives at **`@betekk/canvastekk-workflow-sdk/express`** (subpath export); the root bundle ships **zero** express imports (proven by dist grep)
- `BaseNode.createApp()` is now **async** (lazy adapter load); core-safe structural `CreateNodeAppOptions` in core, express-typed version on the subpath
- `auth.ts` express types replaced with structural equivalents — the emitted core declarations resolve without `@types/express`
- `express` retained in devDependencies (tests exercise the adapter)

### Python — fastapi as the `[fastapi]` extra
- `pip install canvastekk-workflow-sdk` no longer pulls fastapi; `[fastapi]` extra provides it (`[serve]` still provides uvicorn)
- `create_node_app` / `create_multi_node_app` / `NodeAuth` keep their import paths and resolve **lazily**; without the extra, access raises a guided `ImportError` naming `[fastapi]`
- Proven by `tests/test_lazy_server.py`: subprocess with `sys.modules["fastapi"] = None` — core import + `__all__` intact, guided errors raised
- Note: fastapi/pydantic resolve string annotations (PEP 563) against module globals at registration — the lazy path publishes the imported names via `globals()` at first entry (documented in code + LEARNINGS)
- CI: `poetry install -E fastapi` (3 sites in ci-python.yml)

### Route verifier — the enforcement half
- New `conformance.py`: `verify_node(base_url)` probes **GET /health** (200), **GET /manifest** (200 + `WorkflowNodeManifest` validation), **POST /execute** (malformed payload must 4xx) — framework-free (httpx), so self-hosted nodes are judged by the same contract
- `register_node(..., verify=True)` refuses registration with a per-route report when any probe fails (opt-in; default unchanged)
- CLI: `python -m canvastekk_workflow_sdk verify <url> [--api-key KEY] [--timeout S]` — per-route PASS/FAIL, exit 0/1
- node-builder skill template (bundled + mirror) installs `[fastapi,serve]`

## Breaking changes (both carry **BREAKING** via commit subjects)

- TS: root-entry import of `createNodeApp`/`createMultiNodeApp` → `@betekk/canvastekk-workflow-sdk/express`; `node.createApp()` returns a Promise
- TS: consumers pinning express get it as a peer they must install
- Py: deployments relying on the SDK to transitively install fastapi must add the `[fastapi]` extra
- Python import paths are unchanged (lazy, not relocated); Python consumers otherwise unaffected

## Quality Checks

Gated per PLANS/PLAN-104.md Trace — `RE-GATE (post-rebase final tree) tier=full` (rebased onto main post-#106; package.json union-resolved, lock regenerated):

- Python: `poetry check` + `--lock` green, `ruff` clean, `pytest` **833 passed** (9 new: conformance pass/fail modes, registration refuse/accept/require-invoke-url, CLI exit codes, lazy-server subprocess proof)
- TypeScript: `npm audit --omit=dev` 0, build OK, `vitest` **378 passed**, `eslint` clean, `tsc --noEmit` src+tests clean
- Dist laziness: root bundle 0 express refs; `/express` emits js/cjs/d.ts
- Skill mirrors byte-identical (`skill-mirror-guard`)

## Files Modified

- TS: `package.json`, `package-lock.json`, `tsup.config.ts`, `src/express.ts` (new), `src/index.ts`, `src/base-node.ts`, `src/auth.ts`
- Py: `pyproject.toml`, `poetry.lock`, `__init__.py`, `app.py`, `auth.py`, `router.py`, `conformance.py` (new), `registry.py`, `__main__.py`, `tests/test_lazy_server.py` (new), `tests/test_conformance.py` (new)
- CI: `.github/workflows/ci-python.yml`
- Docs: node-builder `SKILL.md` ×2, `PLANS/PLAN-104.md`, `LEARNINGS/*` (1 new entry)

## Checklist

- [x] No manual version bump (release workflow owns it)
- [x] Deferred: none from #102 — all three follow-ups (#104/#105/#106) land this run

author: flavioprogramador
body:
- Gargalo encontrado: Na listagem de recorrências de agendamento (`AppointmentRecurrenceViewSet.list`), a serialização de cada objeto `AppointmentRecurrence` executava consultas SQL N+1 repetidas para calcular `occurrences_count`, `completed_count`, `next_occurrence_id` e `next_occurrence_at`.
- Causa: DRF chamava métodos no gerador de relacionamentos (`obj.appointments.count()`, `.filter().count()`, `.filter().first()`) sem verificar o cache `_prefetched_objects_cache`, ignorando o `prefetch_related("appointments")` já configurado na queryset. Além disso, `_next` era invocado duas vezes por item.
- Alteração: Em `AppointmentRecurrenceSerializer` (`backend/apps/scheduling/api/serializers/recurrences.py`), `occurrences_count`, `completed_count` e `_next` passaram a verificar `_prefetched_objects_cache` para a relação `appointments` e calcular contagens/próxima ocorrência em memória quando prefetched. O resultado de `_next` também foi memoizado por instância do serializer para evitar chamadas redundantes.
- Medição antes e depois: Em uma listagem com 5 recorrências, a quantidade de consultas SQL foi reduzida de 22 consultas (2 base + 4 por item) para 4 consultas constantes (membership, count de paginação, listagem de recorrências e prefetch de consultas), eliminando a escala N+1 conforme a lista cresce.
- Validações executadas: `python manage.py check`, `python manage.py makemigrations --check --dry-run`, `pytest` (660 testes backend passando), `npm run lint`, `npx tsc --noEmit` e `npm run build` (frontend compilado sem erros).
- Riscos restantes: Nenhum. O comportamento, ordenação, tipos de retorno e isolamento multi-tenant/organização permanecem estritamente inalterados.

Root cause: decision_snapshot_guard calls sanitize_real_alerts(), which rewrites candidate-evidence-envelope.json. The publisher restored canonical HEAD bytes before the guard, then generated a hash from the sanitized worktree file while insisting the unchanged HEAD blob had that hash. The safety check failed with GENERATION_COMMITTED_INPUT_HASH_MISMATCH.

Fix: preserve the safety-sanitized envelope, classify it as locally generated for provenance validation, and atomically publish it alongside real-alerts and decision-generation. Extend pipeline integrity ownership audit to require this file and add 3 regression tests. No BUY threshold relaxation, no research-to-Telegram alerts, no automatic trades.

Validation: CI tests and follow-up real publisher run required.

author: skchiew-bot
body:
## What this adds (tests only, no product code changed)
- **Approvals at the same moment:** three people approve a two-level policy change at once. Exactly two levels are approved, in order, by two different people; the third request is refused.
- **Publishing at the same moment:** two reviewers publish the same knowledge draft at once. It is published exactly once.
- **Drained provider in the retry path:** when the first telephony provider refuses a dial and the only other one is drained, the call fails rather than going to the drained one. Once that provider is restored, the same refusal is retried there.
- **Drained voice provider:** a drained voice provider is skipped for new calls, its real health stays untouched, and it is used again once restored.
- **Change-log late answer:** in the browser, a slow answer for an old filter is held back until after the filter changes. It never mixes into the new view.

Each test was checked against deliberately broken code (L-010) and fails without its protection.

**Exception:** the policy-approval race test still passes when the policy lock is removed. The `UNIQUE (version_id, level)` constraint also stops two approvals of one level, so the test proves the outcome, not that particular lock.

## Lessons
New guards added to **L-001** (requests that arrive together) and **L-011** (old data must not overwrite new).

## Still open
- **Intermittent file failure:** twice in about 19 full runs, one test file was marked failed even though every test in it passed. It was `tests/resilience.test.ts` once and `tests/control-actions.test.ts` once.
  - It doesn't reproduce on demand: 8 runs in a row came back green while I was trying to capture it.
  - Measured setup and teardown are fast (setup under 1.5 s, database drop under 0.3 s), so a hook timeout is unlikely.
  - My best guess is an unhandled error raised after a file's tests finish, but the error text hasn't been captured, so that is unconfirmed.
  - No test was skipped, retried or relaxed to hide it.
- **Not covered yet:** the premium-pricing path with a drained provider, and a drain racing a dial.

## Review
No independent review: this PR only adds tests and lesson guards.

Comprehensive ArtCraft Watcher hardening tracked under #1.

- Atomic, deduplicated event/state updates and accurate `changes_found`.
- POST-only authenticated crawler, bounded GitHub retries/timeouts, validation of upstream payloads, isolated per-app failure streaks, and recovery of abandoned runs.
- Database-backed scheduled tick and local-hour idempotency, including DST fallback; safe manual rechecks.
- Health RPC, hourly alert evaluation, explicitly private RLS policies, and operational logging.
- Deno lint/type checks and HTTP tests, disposable PostgreSQL transaction/rollback/deduplication tests, smoke checks, dependency update monitoring, and operational recovery documentation.

## Production deployment and verification (2026-10-10)
- **Live:** all 10 hardening migrations applied in order; `crawl-artcraft` Edge Function **v20** deployed with the prior **v19** source retained locally for rollback.
- Read-only preflight and post-deploy smoke checks passed; live data and installed version fields were preserved.
- Supervised crawl #15 succeeded with 7/7 apps, 14 new events and no errors.
- Supervised repeat crawl #16 succeeded with 7/7 apps and **zero duplicates**.

author: maikolb
body:
Owner instruction relayed by the coordinating session on 2026-10-10: "Não perguntar ao dono vale pra todos os projetos. As correções no NFOS são pra tudo. Todos os projetos. Só em workflow que é no projeto em si."

## Problem

1. The owner question was refused only where a project set `owner_questions: false` (Concursa). Read-only replay on the real boards, 2026-10-10 07:21 UTC: 8 human questions open outside Concursa, the oldest for 32 days.
2. A maintenance pause lost its owner when its repair obligation left through a human question. Measured the same day: 11 open pauses, 2 with no pending obligation (`dovcrm` `t_e49b4951`, `conferencia-folha` `t_56d65bd8`), both answered with `action: human`. Three ways out without the deferral:
   - `review_owner_questions` and `review_maintenance_human_decisions` create a successor whose context is only `{supersedes, ...}`; a `continue` on it resolves as a common decision.
   - on a board without a portal the human reply resolves the obligation directly.
   - `reconcile_maintenance_recovery` never issues it again because the deterministic id already exists (`if decision: continue`).
   The card stays `blocked/awaiting_principal` with an open pause, no decision and no reminder.
3. The sweep recognised a requester question only by `public_message`. Two of the eight open questions were recorded before the decide wrote `public_message` and are addressed to the requester ("PERGUNTA para Jhonatan", `ccm-web` `t_57b12eeb`, `conferencia-folha` `t_b52998e4`). A universal sweep would have returned them to the Principal as owner questions.

## Change

- `_owner_questions_refused` refuses in every project, also when the configuration cannot be read. Only an explicit `owner_questions: true` (project or `kanban.delivery`) turns the question back on; no project sets it.
- `OWNER_QUESTION_REFUSAL` no longer speaks of one project (it mentioned the student, the PDF and US$ 2). It states the conservative path: no spending, no budget grant without an authorization already on record, no credential the card does not have, partial delivery with what is pending.
- `_asked_to_requester`: a question recorded before `public_message` is read by the `PERGUNTA para <human_to>:` prefix the decide itself writes. An addressee that is not the owner stays as it is; no prefix counts as an owner question.
- `_carried_pause`: both sweeps hand `maintenance_recovery`, `maintenance_deferrals` and `dependency_declarations` to the successor, and a card under a pause is not unblocked.
- `reconcile_maintenance_recovery` issues the obligation again for an open pause that no pending or human decision carries (`PAUSE_OBLIGATION_REISSUED_20261010`).
- Principal and worker instructions no longer send anyone to the owner.

## Replay on the real boards (read-only)

| Card | Open for | After this PR |
|---|---|---|
| `dovcrm` `t_1462760a`, `t_f7e2059e` | 2.7 days | back to the Principal; AI provider, account and cost cap: no spending without an authorization on record |
| `dovcrm` `t_47aa7110` | 1.6 days | back to the Principal; corporate access |
| `dovcrm` `t_e49b4951` | 1.5 days | back to the Principal with the repair obligation of pause 967; card stays blocked |
| `conferencia-folha` `t_56d65bd8` | 1.7 days | back to the Principal with the repair obligation of pause 15 (budget exhausted); card stays blocked |
| `project-factory` `t_caaa3f10` | 32 days | back to the Principal and unblocked. Its text says the card is a permanent bus that must stay blocked: someone has to give it another resting state |
| `ccm-web` `t_57b12eeb`, `conferencia-folha` `t_b52998e4` | 17.6 and 9.4 days | stay: asked to the requester |

## Tests

- `tests/hermes_cli/test_nfos_owner_questions_universal.py` (new, 14 cases). Before the change 6 of the first 8 failed. The successor carrying `maintenance_recovery` (review finding A1) is `test_owner_question_that_was_a_pause_repair_keeps_the_pause_owned` and `test_maintenance_human_question_that_was_a_pause_repair_also_carries_it`.
- 16 suites written before this rule ask with a plain `action='human'`: 78 of their tests fail under the new default. They test the machinery behind a human question, which the requester question still uses, so they opt in with the fixture `owner_questions_allowed`. `test_nfos_no_owner_questions.py` and `test_nfos_wait_successor.py` were adapted instead.
- Local run (Windows), 22 suites plus `tests/e2e`, before bringing main in: 366 passed, 10 skipped, 1 failed. The failure is `test_nfos_worker_shutdown::test_existing_native_command_can_flush_within_the_recorded_exit_grace`, a timing test: on a clean main (`a255011b92`) it passed once and failed twice on the same machine.
- After merging main (`a255011b92`, with #302 and #303): universal, no-owner, wait successor, backoff, requester deadline, laboratory wait, public messages, markers and guard: 101 passed, 1 failed. That one is a test #303 added which asks the owner with a plain `action='human'`; it now uses the fixture and passes. Ruff clean.

## Release

Three markers. Conferences for `check_release`:

```python
d.OWNER_QUESTIONS_DEFAULT is False
hasattr(d, '_carried_pause') and hasattr(d, '_asked_to_requester')
'PAUSE_OBLIGATION_REISSUED_20261010' in inspect.getsource(repair.reconcile_maintenance_recovery)
'The owner is never asked, in any project' in ' '.join(r.principal_instructions().split())
```

## Not enforced by code, not proven

- Spending is instruction only: `grant_iteration_budget` accepts the Principal without checking an owner authorization. A code gate there is an owner decision and another PR.
- What the Principal does with the six returned questions shows only after activation.
- The first tick after activation supersedes the six owner questions at once: six requests to the Principal in the same tick.

author: jackvdp
body:
Sign-in state now lives in one place and components reach it through `useAuth()`. This also adds sign out.

## Why

After the sign-in work, the session was spread across three places:

- A `useState` in `App.tsx`, reaching the forms as an `onSignedIn` prop passed through `LoginScreen`.
- The device id, as module state in the API client, which the login code overwrote when the server returned one.
- The access token, which nothing handed to the API client, so a protected call could not send it.

## What changes

- **`auth/session.ts`**: holds the session, which is the tokens plus the device id they are bound to. It is a small store outside React, with `getSession`, `setSession` and `subscribe`.
- **`auth/useAuth.ts`**: `useAuth()` returns `{ session, signIn, verifyCode, signOut }`. It is how components read the session and the only code that changes it.
- **`api/client.ts`**: reads the device id and access token from the session and sends `Authorization: Bearer …` once there is one. It no longer keeps a device id itself.
- **Forms and `App.tsx`**: use the hook. The `onSignedIn` props are gone, and `LoginScreen` takes no props.
- **Sign out**: a button on the placeholder home screen, calling `POST /api/admin/auth/logout`.
- **`auth/login.ts` → `auth/authApi.ts`**: renamed now that it also has `logout`. Its functions only talk to the server. Where the server names a device id, they return it, and `useAuth` applies it.

## Why there is no provider component

The API client runs outside React and needs the token for request headers, so the session cannot live only in component state. `useAuth` subscribes to the store with `useSyncExternalStore`, which gives every component the same session without an `<AuthProvider>` in the tree.

## Things to know

- **Sign out does not wait for the server.** The user is signed out locally straight away, and a failed logout request is ignored. If it fails, the server session lingers and the next sign-in asks whether to take over from the other device.
- **A new device id after sign out.** The next sign-in gets a fresh one, as the web app does.
- **Still in memory only.** Reloading the app signs you out. Persisting the session is a later change, and it now has one place to go.
- **Not in this PR:** token refresh, handling a 401 on a protected call, and tests. The mobile app has no Jest setup yet.

## Testing

- `npm run typecheck -w @nomos/mobile` and Prettier pass.
- Exercised in a headless browser against the web build, with replies mocked in the shapes the web app reads:
  - Sign in, then sign out: the logout request carries the token and the session's device id, and the sign-in screen returns without waiting for the reply.
  - Sign out when the server refuses the logout.
  - Signing in again uses a fresh device id and sends no token.
  - A device id returned by the server is the one the session uses, including through the one-time-code step.
  - The existing flows: signed in elsewhere, wrong code, resend, and going back.
- A made-up user still gets "Invalid credentials" from the dev API, with no `Authorization` header sent while signed out.
- The sign-in screen renders on the iOS simulator.
- A real sign-in and sign-out against the dev API have not been confirmed.

body:
…unding

Pure :engine addition; nothing outside the two new files is touched.

RpEngine.kt (commonMain):
- RpEngineConfig: every magnitude in one tunable data class, so a balance pass retunes without touching RankLadder's 19 thresholds (RD4 "independent of threshold constants").
- computeBaseDelta: base by outcome + opponent-strength term + symmetric tier-difference term. Sign comes only from outcome — the raw sum can overshoot past zero (a King 15 ordinals above a weak table sums negative), so clampToSign stops it AT zero. Without that, winning at a much weaker table would cost RP.
- withMixedTierAdjustment: identity stub, the RD5/RD6 seam S48 replaces.
- finalRpDelta: GM6 single authority — every input first, then ×0.5 for MINI once, then round. FULL is multiplier 1.0 and a round no-op.

roundDelta implements OPEN-3 (ties AWAY from zero) explicitly because neither library does: java.lang.Math.round is half-up toward +inf (-7.5 -> -7), and kotlin.math.round is ties-to-EVEN (4.5 -> 4, -4.5 -> -4). The latter contradicts the closed rule's own stated cases (+9 -> +5, -9 -> -5, since 9 * 0.5 = 4.5), though the plan's insertion contract names it. Pinned by two mandatory guards in the test.

16 new tests; full :engine:jvmTest 235 / 0 failures; JS target compiles.

## O que mudou (1.4.2, código 62)

Pedidos do Caio de 10/10 (prints no tema Heitor):

- **Favoritos saiu de Bibliotecas**: o atalho já existe no menu Você, então não aparece mais repetido.
- **Menu Você na ordem pedida**: Favoritos · Bibliotecas · Meus pedidos ─ Configurações · Trocar usuário · Sobre ─ **Apoie o CGFLIX**. No modo off-line, os 3 primeiros continuam escondidos.
- **"Apoie o CGFLIX" em destaque**: coração preenchido em rosa `#ec4899`, igual nos dois temas e fora do tom monocromático, no Você e nas Configurações. O texto passa a ser: "O CGFLIX Lite é grátis e vai continuar grátis. Se você gosta de usar, pode dar uma força para manter o projeto."
- **Minha conta (foto e senha)**: o topo do Você (foto, nome e "Minha conta: foto e senha") abre a tela nova. A foto vem da galeria do sistema, sem pedir permissão, e é enviada como quadrado de 512 px em JPEG (`POST /UserImage`, em base64); há também "Remover foto". A senha pede atual, nova e confirmação (`POST /Users/Password`). Se a senha atual estiver errada, o app avisa que várias tentativas bloqueiam a conta. Testado no Jellyfin 10.11.11 com o `teste-cgflix`.
- **Ícone do app acompanha o tema**, como no Telegram: com o tema Heitor, o ícone fica verde; com Isis ou automático, roxo. São dois `activity-alias` no manifesto (`IconeIsis`, ligado por padrão, e `IconeHeitor`). A troca só acontece quando o app sai da tela (`CgflixAppIcon`).

Ficam para etapas separadas: as capas verdes das bibliotecas no Heitor (geradas no servidor).

## Como testar

1. Instalar o APK do PR por cima da 1.4.1.
2. Abrir **Você** e conferir a ordem e o coração rosa no fim. Tocar nele abre a tela de apoio.
3. Em **Configurações**, conferir o coração rosa em "Apoie o CGFLIX".
4. Em **Bibliotecas**, conferir que o cartão "Favoritos" não aparece mais.
5. Tocar na foto/nome no topo do **Você**: trocar a foto pela galeria, conferir que ela aparece no Você e no site; remover. Trocar a senha (errar a atual uma vez para ver o aviso); o app continua conectado e o site pede login de novo.
6. Mudar o tema para **Heitor** e sair do app (botão início). Em alguns segundos, o ícone na gaveta fica verde. Voltar para Isis e sair: o ícone volta a ser roxo.

## Riscos
- Trocar a senha derruba as outras sessões da pessoa (site, TV, outros celulares): é o comportamento do Jellyfin. O app avisa na mensagem de sucesso.
- O Jellyfin bloqueia a conta depois de várias senhas atuais erradas seguidas; só o admin desbloqueia.

- Na atualização a partir da 1.4.1, a entrada do launcher muda de `MainActivity` para o alias. Alguns launchers podem tirar uma vez o atalho fixado na tela inicial; aí basta fixar de novo.
- O launcher demora alguns segundos para mostrar o ícone novo depois da troca.
- Em alguns aparelhos (Samsung e Xiaomi), trocar o ícone pode fechar o app ou sumir com o atalho fixado. Por isso a troca é feita com o app em segundo plano, e não no toque.
- `MainActivity` continua `exported` (sem intent-filter) para o `am start -n` do CI de telas.

Fix mounted components retaining their first selection through the native `useSelector` subscription callback. The stable subscription shares a V8 closure context with the first snapshot callback, keeping its inline selector and Component render alive. Construct the snapshot callback in a separate factory so its captured inputs have their own lifetime. Subscription identity/cleanup, snapshot caching, comparison behavior, and concurrent selection ownership remain unchanged.

Also shorten the three private selection-cache keys (`owner`, `snapshot`, `selected` → `o`, `s`, `v`), since property names survive consumer minification. Comments retain their meaning; public sources/options/types and all eight state fields are unchanged.

Found while investigating [Router #8657](https://github.com/TanStack/router/pull/8657). A Store-only production GC regression fails on the alpha and passes with this fix. author: zihanghe13123
body:
The 23 Python tests that still failed on Windows in the release gate after #29. One of them pointed at a defect in the product; the others were tests that assumed something Windows does not do.

## The defect: a turn's change list on Windows

At the end of a turn the change ledger reads each touched file again and compares it with the bytes captured before the first edit. On Windows that read did not ask for binary mode, so Windows opened the file in text mode: `\r\n` came back as `\n`, and the read ended at the first `0x1A` byte. For any file with `\r\n` line endings:

- a file edited and then edited back was listed as changed;
- every line counted as changed, not only the edited ones (60 added for 51 edits in the gate's run);
- the stored "after" copy had lost its carriage returns.

The read now asks for binary mode where the platform has one. macOS and Linux are unchanged. This accounts for 6 of the 23.

## The tests

| Tests | What was wrong | Change |
|---|---|---|
| 1 turn-change integration test | Compared stored copies with `\n` bytes after writing the file with `write_text` | Writes `\n` explicitly. A second test that passed on Windows only because of the defect gets the same change |
| 2 turn-change store tests | Check a guarantee the store gives through directory handles, which it does not use on Windows | Skipped on Windows, like their neighbours |
| 2 turn-change store tests | One injected its failure into a function Windows never calls; one compared two moments with a clock that ticks every 15.6 ms there | Inject into the removal the platform uses; use `perf_counter` |
| 3 desktop session tests | Read a writer's lock file while it was held, which Windows refuses | The snapshot records such a file without its bytes |
| 3 desktop session tests | Made a session media directory by hand; Windows keeps media through its native library and refuses a directory it did not make | Add media only where the store takes a plain directory. The native path has its own tests |
| 1 delegate history test | Relies on a file's change time, which Windows does not report | Skipped on Windows |
| 2 worker execution tests | `pwd` is sent to WSL on Windows, and the runner has no distribution; a later check looked for a Windows path in JSON text | Print the working directory with the Python that runs the test; undo the doubled backslashes before comparing |
| 3 browser tests | Looked for the heading "Example Domain" in the text of `example.com`, which the page no longer has | Look for the word "example" |

Three tests are skipped on Windows as a result; each skip names the reason.

## Verification

- Whole Python suite and `ruff check agent tests scripts` on macOS, and `pyright` on the changed source file for macOS, Linux and Windows analyses.
- The defect and its fix were checked on macOS under an emulation of three Windows behaviours (the store's path-based mode, text-mode reads, `write_text` storing `\r\n`). Without the fix it gave the same failures as the gate; with it, only tests that Windows skips were left. A new test applies the text-mode rule on other platforms and fails without the fix.

- The release gate was run on this branch. Its first run left 2 of the 23 failing: the worker test's command now ran on Windows, and a later check looked for a Windows path inside a tool result's JSON, where its backslashes are doubled. The last commit fixes that check. On the second run the gate passed on Windows (6,794 tests, none failed) and on Ubuntu (7,484).

author: gmgauthier
body:
## Repro (m2 at a3ef188)

1. New document, type `one two`.
2. Select `two`, Ctrl+B.
3. Select `one`, Ctrl+C.
4. Caret between `t` and `wo`, Ctrl+V.

The pasted `one` is drawn bold and saved bold (`\pard\f0\fs22\b0\i0\ulnone one \b tonewo\par`). Each pasted character carries two format tags, `fmtSans220000` and `fmtSans221004`, and the tag created later in the document wins. With the bold typed first, the same paste comes out plain. Screen, `capture()` and RTF all agree, so the result is wrong but the file isn't damaged. All six cases from the report are in `/workspace/paste-repro`.

## Cause

GTK gives text inserted inside a tag's range that tag too. A paste or drop of this document's own text then goes through `insert_range`, which copies the source's tags on top, so the pasted characters end up with the surrounding run's fmt tag plus their own. `finish_pending()` only applied the typing format when a segment had no "foreign" tag. In every other case it left the text alone, both tags included. It also never counted the newline before a paragraph as a surrounding tag, so a paste at the start of a paragraph doubled the same way.

So the doubling comes from GTK's inheritance plus the source tags. The typing format is not applied on top of pasted text. The code just never removed the inherited tag.

## Fix

- `finish_pending()` records, through `signal_apply_tag`, the character formats applied over the new text during the user action: the source's tags copied by a paste or drop, or Replace's format. It keeps exactly those. Text that got none (typing, or plain text from another program) takes the typing format, as before.
- Every character format now goes on through the new `MainWindow::set_fmt(from, to, tag)`, which removes every other fmt tag on the range first. It is used in `finish_pending()`, `tag_line_breaks()`, `apply_run_edit()` (bold, italic, underline, size, font) and Replace. No `apply_tag(format_tag(...))` call is left outside it. `replace_buffer()` (load, undo, redo, styles) inserts at the end of the buffer, where GTK adds nothing.
- DEVELOPMENT.md, M2: one line for the rule, with the plain-`one`-inside-bold-`two` example.

## Tests (committed on their own first, failing on m2)

`tests/test_paste_format.cpp` (`paste-format`, 87 checks, real key events). Each case checks the text, what GTK draws, what `capture()` records, and `assert_single_format_tag()`.

- The six report cases: bold into plain, plain into bold, 16 pt into 11 pt, across a paragraph end, and both with bold typed first.
- Plain text from another program (`Gtk::Clipboard::set_text`) into bold: it takes the caret's format.
- Paste into an empty last paragraph, at the start of a run, at the end of a run mid-paragraph, and at the start of a paragraph.
- Drag and drop within the document, both ways. A GTK drag can't be driven under Xvfb, so the test replays GtkTextView's own calls: `insert_range_interactive` in one user action, then `delete_selection`.
- Undo and redo of a paste (Ctrl+Z / Ctrl+Y), Ctrl+B on and off over a pasted range, and Heading 1 then Normal over it.

On m2 plus the tests (05ff728), 27 of the 87 checks fail. Doubled tags show up in bold-into-plain, plain-into-bold, bold-first-plain-into-bold, start-of-paragraph, drag-plain-into-bold and the paste/undo/bold/style cases built on plain-into-bold. With the fix, all 87 pass.

### The one-tag check, for #42's undo fuzz

- Rule: `int writeit::first_doubled_format_tag(const Glib::RefPtr<Gtk::TextBuffer>& buffer, std::string* why = nullptr)` in **`src/format_tags.hpp`** (in `libwriteit_core`). It returns -1 when no character has more than one `fmt*` tag or more than one `para*` tag. Otherwise it returns the first such offset, and `*why` names the character and its tags. These are the same two prefixes the fuzz's `MainWindowProbe::doubled()` counts today.
- Check.hpp wrapper: `assert_single_format_tag(buffer)` in `tests/format_tags_check.hpp`, which is one `CHECK`.

This PR leaves #42 alone. Whichever of the two lands second should change `tests/test_undo_fuzz.cpp`'s `after_edit()` from `if (MainWindowProbe::doubled(*w_) >= 0) ++doubled_actions;` to fail on doubles:

```cpp
std::string why;
if (writeit::first_doubled_format_tag(MainWindowProbe::buffer(*w_), &why) >= 0)
  fail("two format tags on one character: " + why);
```

It also needs `#include "format_tags.hpp"`.

## Runs (fresh `meson setup`, -j2)

- Normal, `xvfb-run -a meson test -C build`: 41 OK, 3 expected fail (the guard tests), 0 fail, 0 skipped.
- ASan+UBSan with sanitize.yml's options (`-Db_sanitize=address,undefined`, its ASAN/UBSAN/LSAN options, `--timeout-multiplier 4 --num-processes 2`, slow suite included): 41 OK, 3 expected fail, 0 fail, 0 skipped.
- `scripts/lint.sh`: ok (32 files).
- `/workspace/paste-repro` built against this branch: all six cases give 0 doubled characters. Pasted text keeps its source format (`one ToneWO`, `oneTWO TWO`, `OtwoNE two`, `ONE twoONE`, 16 pt kept).

## Still open (no doubled tags, but noted)

Pasting from one Write-It window into another arrives as plain text, because each window has its own tag table, so it takes the caret's format. Bold `two` pasted into a plain run in another window comes out plain. That is the "another program" rule, not "keeps its own format". It needs a rich-text clipboard target, so it's out of scope here.


## Round 2: paragraph format on a multi-paragraph paste

### Repro (Bug Basher)

`aaaa` (Normal), `bbbb` (Block Text, Heading 1 or a bullet item), `cccc` (Normal). Copy from after `aa` to after `cc`, then paste into the middle of `cccc`. The pasted `bbbb` loses its paragraph format:

- Block Text comes out Normal and loses its 1" indent.
- A bullet item stops being a list item.
- Heading 1 loses its style but keeps its outline level and size.

Those characters carry two `para*` tags (`first_doubled_format_tag()` returns 15). m2 has the same bug.

### Cause

The same GTK behaviour as for character tags. Text inserted inside a paragraph gets that paragraph's tag, and `insert_range` copies the source's para tags on top. `finish_pending()` only cleaned the text after the last pasted newline. So whole paragraphs, and the paragraph closed by the first pasted newline, kept both tags, and whichever tag was created later won.

### Rule

Paragraph format belongs to the paragraph's end, its newline, as in Word:

- Each pasted paragraph end brings the format of the paragraph it was copied from, so a paragraph copied whole keeps its style, indents, alignment and list membership.
- The paragraph that the paste's first copied end closes starts with the landing paragraph's text. It takes the format of the paragraph it was copied from, not the landing paragraph's.
- The text after the paste's last end joins the paragraph it lands in and keeps that paragraph's format.
- A paste with no paragraph end changes no paragraph format.
- No character carries more than one paragraph tag.

Example: copying from the middle of a Heading 1 through a Block Text paragraph into the middle of a Normal one gives Heading 1, Block Text, Normal.

Sources:

- Current Word: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/answers/questions/5116871/copy-paste-with-keep-source-formatting-does-not-wo
- Word 97 file-format spec: paragraph properties live in the paragraph mark.
- KB Q176314 and Q185824.
- The paste rule is also stated in Mac Word KB Q24413, *Running Microsoft Office 2000*, and Word 2003 Help.

Nobody has tried this in a real copy of Word 97 yet.

### Fix

- `finish_pending()` now records the para tags applied over the new text, as it already did for fmt tags.
- Every paragraph the insertion touches is set through `MainWindow::set_para(from, to, tag)`, which removes every other para tag on the range first.
- When the first joined paragraph changes style, the landing paragraph's own text in it follows the new style the way applying a style does (`restyle_run`). Without this, that text would be 11 pt plain inside a Heading 1 and would r

body:
The updater previously activated a new Skills runtime without checking whether its detected consumers could satisfy the target runtime’s prerequisites. A Sumi installation without the dedicated path reader could therefore become blocked after the launcher switch.

Declared targets now run their own bounded, read-only checker before activation. The checker reuses the existing consumer detector and Sumi resolver; refusals preserve the old runtime, launcher bytes, configuration and session receipts, while retaining the artifact-bound prepared rollout receipt. Unsupported contracts and invalid responses fail closed. Undeclared legacy targets remain compatible and explicitly report unverified status.

Validation: 16 focused activation tests (12 new prerequisite cases and four existing upgrade/rollback controls), 13 existing consumer detector tests, typecheck, target bundle build and built-ins-only import checks passed in a network-isolated synthetic HOME. The pre-fix regression proves that the old updater resolved activation when the helper was missing. Exact seven-file staged credential scan passed with no findings, skips or errors.

The full package build also passed against the retained development closure. That is compilation coverage: producer verification correctly refused the retained MCP SDK 1.31.0 because the standalone lock requires 1.30.0. A fresh standalone frozen install subsequently passed with the lock unchanged, managed seven-day policy enabled, and no host dependency or credential projection; producer verification (233 nodes, 646 edges), typecheck and the full build passed against that matching graph. The no-tag release workflow’s candidate/archive gates remain pending. The separate release metadata commit prepares version 0.10.62 and records the behavior in the changelog; it does not publish it. The same 16 version-sensitive tests and fresh frozen producer/typecheck/build also pass at 0.10.62.

First installation from Skills 0.10.61 must independently run the exact candidate reader under the reviewed retained-installer procedure before switching PATH; its older updater does not implement this check.
