body: ## What changed **Android app** - Capacitor project in `android/` (app id `app.blank.player`, minSdk 24, target 36), with generated icons and splash. Build with `npm run android:apk`. - Android back button closes the topmost overlay, then goes back a page, then minimizes the app. - Phone layout: two-column album grid, two-row player with a seek bar, and safe-area insets. - Inter is bundled instead of loaded from Google Fonts, so it also works offline. - **Lock screen and notification player.** A native media session and foreground playback service show the current song, cover art and previous/play-pause/next controls (with seeking) on the lock screen and in the notification shade. Playback also keeps going with the screen off. Android 13+ asks for notification permission the first time a song plays. - **Reopening the app.** The app now accepts the third-party sign-in cookie and saves cookies when it goes to the background. If the server rejects the saved sign-in, the app returns to the sign-in screen instead of staying "signed in" with every request failing. - Tapping no longer shows the blue highlight, and text selection is off on touch devices outside inputs. - Removed the "Line-synced" chip and the "Lyrics from ..." credit from the lyrics view. **Offline** - Right-click (long-press on Android) a song, an album or a search result and choose **Make available offline**, or **Remove download** if it is already saved. - Audio, cover art and the lyrics found for the song are saved together in IndexedDB. Opening lyrics for a downloaded song reads the saved copy first. - The last library snapshot and the last signed-in user are kept, so the app opens with no connection. Songs that are not downloaded are greyed out while offline. - Downloaded songs show a badge, with a progress ring while downloading. **Settings** shows how much space downloads use and has **Remove all downloads**. - The hosted web build gets a small network-first service worker so it can also reopen offline. The Android app doesn't use it. ## Notes - The APK is debug-signed, so it can be installed directly. A release build needs your own keystore. - Android's origin `https://localhost` is a trusted domain in Neon Auth. - The Android-only changes (media notification, cookie handling) compile and package, but I could not run them on a device or emulator here. The web side was tested in headless Chrome. ## Testing - `npm test` passes (13 tests), `npm run build` passes, and the debug APK builds and verifies.

author: stokuj
body:
Closes #110

## What

The wiki screens (sidebar, Page view, Edit, History) now read and write Pages through the real `/api/wiki/pages/` API from #108 instead of the in-memory fake. Errors a real backend returns (400, 404, 409, 5xx) have clear UI states. Things with no backend yet stay on a trimmed fake store: Agent candidates (chat), Profile and Proposals. Generate and Proposals are hidden until M3.

| Area | What |
|------|------|
| **API layer** | New `src/api/wiki.ts` (list, get, versions, save with `base_version`, create book). `url()` checks the Page path against the backend `PAGE_PATH` pattern before any request, so a crafted link cannot reach other `/api` endpoints. `apiErrorMessage()` in `client.ts` turns an `ApiError` into one UI string |
| **Types / hooks** | `PageSummary` (list, no `content`) vs `Page` (+ `content`, `version`); `Paginated<T>`. Hook names unchanged; `useSavePage` takes `{ content, baseVersion }`; `useGeneratePage` removed |
| **Screens** | Editor: 400 shows the backend message, 409 shows "page changed" + Reload. It keeps its own `base_version` and text across background refetches, so a refetch cannot hide a conflict or wipe typed text. Page: 404 → "Page not found." (no retry), other errors → "Could not load this page.". Sidebar: alert when the list fails. History: newest 20 Versions, labels from `total`; "Could not load history." when the list fails. "Yes, add" uses the real `POST`. `pagePath` accepts a trailing `/` and a missing `.md` |
| **Fake store** | `store.ts` keeps only candidates, profile and proposals. The frontend `.md` fixtures are deleted; the prod bundle has no page bodies |
| **Backend** | Frontmatter shape check (`description`/`author`/`status`/`book`/`universe` as text, `sources`/`verified`/`generated` shapes) moved from the SPA's `validateEdit` into `okf.validate`. It now also protects future Agent writes. Frontend `validateEdit`/`checkShape`/`TEMPLATES` removed |
| **Tests** | `src/test/mockWikiApi.ts`: an in-memory `fetch` mock of the wiki API serving `backend-django/wiki/fixtures` (the same files `seed` loads), with a 409 rule and per-request overrides. New tests cover the error states, the path guard and the two refetch cases. Vite `server.fs.allow` is limited to `frontend/` + that fixtures dir |
| **Docs** | Spec and plan for #110, plus `ARCHITECTURE.md` status line, `CLAUDE.md` "Co to jest" and layout, and a `GOTCHAS.md` note on `fs.allow` |

## Why

M2 needs the wiki usable on real data. Done when: (1) after `seed`, sidebar, Page view and History show database data; (2) a saved edit is a Version in History; (3) 400 shows the backend message, 409 asks to reload; (4) no Proposal or Generate entry point is reachable; (5) Vitest covers the error states with a mocked `fetch`. Spec: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-10-110-wire-wiki-api.md`, plan: `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-10-10-110-wire-wiki-api.md`.

## How to test

- ✅ `make verify` on `3826088` + CLAUDE.md commit: ruff clean, backend 133 passed, OpenAPI schema test OK, `tsc`, ESLint, Prettier clean, Vitest 108 passed (13 files), build OK
- ✅ `npm run build` + grep: no fixture page bodies in `dist/`
- ⚠️ Not run: manual browser check (`manage.py seed`, `make dev-up`, `npm run dev`, edit a Page, see the Version in History)
- Review: ready with notes. Each task was reviewed (spec + quality), plus a final whole-branch review: 0 Critical/Important left. Findings fixed along the way: client-side path traversal, `fs.allow: ['..']` exposing `infra/.env` to the dev server, a background refetch wiping the editor or hiding a 409, and Reload during an outage overwriting text. `devkit:adr-guardian`: no violations

## Risks

- Frontend tests depend on the backend fixture layout (`backend-django/wiki/fixtures`). Renaming that dir breaks Vitest, and CI will catch it.
- The backend shape check is slightly stricter than the old SPA one (PyYAML 1.1: unquoted `status: yes` is a bool and is rejected, with a "quote it" message).
## Rollback

Revert the merge. No migrations.

## Contract impact

safe: `PUT/POST /api/wiki/pages/` now also return 400 for wrong frontmatter shapes (same `{content: [msg]}` format). No other API, schema or env change.

body:
## Work package

None: this is a fix to WP-07 (jobs) under D-37 (one database). You chose option 1 on Oct 10. Decision **D-62**.

**Requirements:** NFR-07, NFR-14

## The problem

Previews and e2e run as the demo family in the **production** database (D-37). So production's scheduled jobs worked on it too:
- the goal reconcile every 5 minutes;
- day close and chore planning;
- reminders.

A job could land in the middle of an e2e step and leave its mark. On PR #38, `goals.spec` failed twice in a row: "Movie night" had already been reached once before it began. The likeliest cause:
- `admin-day.spec` checks off Leo's bed and takes it back a few seconds later;
- for those seconds, Leo is at 19 of 19;
- chained e2e runs were starting at about :X5:39, which put that window right on the reconcile at :X6:00.

## Decision to look at (D-62)

- **Every job skips the demo family.** It is test data. Its tests run what the jobs do themselves:
  - the Goals page evaluates goals;
  - "Pay bonuses now" applies the bonus rules;
  - the reminders job runs on the e2e runner against a mocked push service.
- **`household.is_demo` marks it.**
  - The seed sets it (the seed deletes and recreates the demo household).
  - The migration sets it on the demo household already there, so jobs stop at this deploy, not at the next reseed.
- **Only the server, the seed or a migration can change the mark.** A parent can't turn their own household's jobs off, or the demo family's back on (`private.guard_household_demo`).
- **The trade-off:** between e2e runs, the demo family's days aren't closed and its plan doesn't roll forward. Every e2e run reseeds it, so a preview opened the day it is built is current. A preview opened days later shows the old days unclosed.
- **System Health** says so for the demo family: "The background jobs leave the demo family alone, so here they show as not run yet. In a real household they run on schedule."

## What changed

- **Database** (`20261010090000_demo_household.sql`, additive):
  - `household.is_demo boolean not null default false`;
  - the demo household is marked;
  - `trg_household_demo` refuses a change from a signed-in user (`42501`).
- **Jobs** (`lib/jobs/store.ts`): `households()` lists every household but the demo family. This is the one list every HTTP job runs over. `purge_history` (SQL) only trims logs and stays as is.
- **Seed:** the demo household is inserted with `is_demo = true`.
- **System Health:** the note above, for the demo family only. The page reads the flag on its own and treats a failed read as "not demo", so a page served before the migration still works.

## Docs updated in this PR

- [x] `docs/05-backlog.md`: v0.8.52 (no work package changes status) and a "later fix" line under WP-07
- [x] Affected artifacts, plus a row in `04` §I (0.8.52):
  - `00`: D-62
  - `01` v0.8.33: §5.6 and §9.5
  - `02` v0.8.25: §3.1
- [x] `python3 docs/check_traceability.py --docs docs --tests .` passes (0 errors, 0 warnings)
- **Numbering:** the docs are numbered after #38 (D-61, 0.8.51). If this merges first, I'll renumber.

## Verification

- **Local gates** (from main):
  - unit: web 297, rules engine 63, ui 79; the job schedule check;
  - pgTAP: 777, including `250_demo_household` (10) and two more in `012_demo_family`;
  - UI suite: 110/110;
  - format, lint (only the existing warning), typecheck, docs build and layout;
  - the migration classifies as additive; the seed loads.
- **pgTAP `250` (10):**
  - every household is marked demo or not, and a new one is not;
  - a parent still renames their household, but can't mark it;
  - a demo parent can't unmark the demo family;
  - an update that leaves the mark alone goes through;
  - the server, the seed and a migration can change it.
- **`012`:** the seed marks the demo family, and a real household stays in the jobs.
- **Unit** (`lib/jobs/store.test.ts`): the job store lists every household but the demo family.
- **On the preview** (`health.spec.ts`): the demo household is marked after the reset, and System Health shows the note.
- [x] CI gates green (checks, database, build) on `771c8bc`
- [x] e2e green on the preview (`771c8bc`): 92 passed, no retries, DEV-05 p95 910 ms. This run's `admin-day` missed the reconcile's minute, so it is not yet proof of the fix; that comes with the first run after the deploy.

**A caveat on this PR's own e2e run:** the job filter is app code, so production skips the demo family only once this is deployed. Until then, this PR's e2e still faces production's jobs, and `goals.spec` can still hit the race if a run lines up with the reconcile. The proof is the first e2e run after the deploy.

## Deferred

Other e2e flakes seen on #38's three runs, which this doesn't touch. I've put them to the owner rather than widen this PR:
- `board-shop.spec` (celebration not seen);
- `devices.spec` (DEV-05 p95 at 5.8 s on a slow preview);
- `offline.spec`;
- the `wishlist.spec` retry.

author: agluszak
body:
## Summary

`compat/kernel32.h` and `wiz8_windows.h` are deleted; everything they provided has a native home. Follow-up commits address review feedback: Win32-shaped SDL wrappers are gone rather than renamed, and runtime deadlines moved to a 64-bit monotonic model.

**SGP clock manager.** `timer.cpp` kept `guiCurrentTime` as a startup-relative snapshot refreshed per frame via `UpdateClockManager`, but callers only wanted a millisecond stamp. The manager (`Initialize/Update/ShutdownClockManager`, `guiStartupTime`/`guiCurrentTime`, `TIMER` typedef, dead unit macros) is gone: `GetClock()` → ticks, `SetCountdownClock(d)` → `ticks + d`, `ClockIsTicking(t)` → `TimeUntilDeadline(t)`. Save files store remaining ms and re-arm on load.

**kernel32.h removal.** `w8_clock_us`/`w8_get_ticks` decls live in `compat/native.h` (visible everywhere via the forced `compiler.h` include). `RECT`/`POINT` → `SGPRect`/`SGPPoint`, `HWND` → `SDL_Window*`, `BOOL`/`DWORD`/`LONG`/`UINT` → `bool`/`UINT32`/`INT32`, `FILETIME`/`SYSTEMTIME` → `wiz8::DiskFileTime`/`CivilTime` (deleting `SetSaveSlotCalendar`), `MAX_PATH` → `std::string`, `VK_*`/`LOWORD`/`HIWORD` → `src/sgp/input.h`, unqualified `min`/`max` → `std::` forms.

**Window layer (review P1).** Video2.cpp called `W8Video*` wrappers through Win32-named macros. `ShowWindow`/`OpenIcon`/`SetFocus`/`CloseWindow` are now direct `SDL_ShowWindow`/`SDL_RestoreWindow`/`SDL_RaiseWindow`/`SDL_MinimizeWindow`/`SDL_HideWindow` calls and `SetCursorPos` → `WarpGameMouse`. The `W8VideoClientToScreen` no-op and the always-`{0,0,640,480}` translation arithmetic were dead code — deleted along with the unreachable out-of-window cursor branch, `g_system_cursor_visible`, write-only `g_window_rect`, and never-assigned `g_render_window`. `W8VideoGetClientRect` remains as the 640×480 design-space adapter; the forwarding functions and the identity `native()` cast are gone.

**Timing model (review P1).** `w8_get_ticks()` returns 64-bit milliseconds derived from `w8_clock_us` — still the single injectable clock runtime tests drive. Stamp/deadline fields widened to `uint64_t` across input timers, combat/main-game-screen countdowns, portrait and sound scheduling, path/mouse/UI timers, and `InputAtom.uiTimeStamp`, so plain `<=` comparisons are correct everywhere (previously `guiLeftButtonRepeatTimer <= uiTimer` was wraparound-unsafe) and `0` remains an unambiguous "disabled" value. Wraparound workarounds deleted: mousesystem's `+0x7fffffff` fix-up, soundman's rollover branch, Environment's wrapped-elapsed ternary. Layout-pinned exceptions keep 4 bytes: serialized `savant_hack_tick`/`bela_cycle_tick` (32-bit wrap-tolerant diff) and `item_group_seed`; `saved_remaining_ms` stays `UINT32` on disk.

**Behavior note:** deadlines read the live monotonic clock, not the once-per-pump snapshot — a countdown can now expire mid-frame rather than at the next event iteration. Also includes a test-harness fix: `runtime_load-game` constructs `Game` before reading the fixture so a missing asset root reports skipped rather than failed.

#### Follow-ups not in this PR

Per review, deliberately deferred: SGP input rewrite (VK double-translation → typed actions + SDL text input), `SGPRect`/`SGPPoint` → `SDL_Rect`/`SDL_Point` in native code, surfaces consolidation onto SDL blitters, and `compat/native.h` + `-fshort-wchar` removal (broad modernization, own change).

#### Test plan

- [x] `cmake --build --preset linux` clean
- [x] `ctest` — 33/33 pass; 8 `runtime_*` tests skip without GOG assets (`runtime_load-game` now skips correctly)

author: kreneskyp
body:
Refs #157.

`make ci` ran its four `cargo test` lanes directly, so a suite that ran zero tests printed the same `test result: ok.` as one that ran and passed. They now run through `cargo xtask test-suites <lane> <cargo test args>` (`xtask/src/test_suites.rs`), with the original cargo arguments and order unchanged.

- Suites are identified from `cargo test --no-run --message-format=json` (target source file, plus `doctests` for a library's doc-tests). The run's `Running ... (<executable>)` and `Doc-tests <crate>` headers are mapped to them by executable path and library name. A header that maps to nothing fails.
- Only counts are read from the text: first `running N tests`, last `test result:` between two headers, and they must agree. Missing or malformed lines fail.
- Each lane declares its legitimately empty suites with a reason (`LANES`). An undeclared zero-pass suite fails. A declared one that passes tests, or does not run, fails. A built test executable that never ran fails.
- `cargo` runs as a child process, so a build or test failure exits with cargo's own code and skips the suite check. There is no pipe whose status could be lost.

Declared-empty inventory comes from the retained QSL#670 gate log; both workspace lanes listed the same 16 suites. The two `-p` lanes declare none.

No existing FR/NFR owns a CI empty-suite guard, so this adds no spec text. That is a spec gap for the owner.

Checked locally: fmt, clippy `-D warnings` on xtask, `xtask string-edge`, `cargo test -p xtask` (115 pass, including 21 for the guard and 4 end-to-end runs of real cargo on a fixture project), `make -n`.

Not yet run: the full `make ci` aggregate, so the declared inventory is unproven against the live tree. Review and the merge gate remain.

body:
## Summary

Adds `.github/workflows/release.yml` following mcvs-general-action's [docs/auto-release.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/schubergphilis/mcvs-general-action/refs/heads/main/docs/auto-release.md), pinned to v0.9.0.

**Why:** releases are tagged by hand today, so merged fixes and features wait until someone cuts a tag, and the version bump is a manual call. With this workflow every `feat:`/`fix:` merge is released automatically, with the version derived from the commit messages.

On every push to `main` it creates the next semver tag and a GitHub Release from the Conventional Commits since the latest tag (`feat!:`/`BREAKING CHANGE:` major, `feat:` minor, `fix:`/`perf:` patch, otherwise nothing). The current latest tag is `v0.2.1`, so the next release builds on that.

Commits are already linted as Conventional Commits (`lint-commit` in `general.yml`).

It also adds a 7-day `cooldown` to the Dependabot updates, so a newly published version waits a week before Dependabot proposes it.

**On merge:** no release yet. `main` has no `feat:`/`fix:`/`perf:` commits since `v0.2.1`, and this PR's own `ci:` commit does not bump the version, so the next `feat:`/`fix:` merge cuts the first automatic release.

author: zillic
body:
Plan phase 8 item 2: the measure definitions left after the ANY-maze audit (TODO §16).

Source: ANY-maze's "A detailed description of the ANY-maze measures" (Version 4, 30 May 2024, https://www.any-maze.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/01/a-detailed-description-of-the-any-maze-measures.pdf). Every definition change has a `tests/test_anymaze_definitions.py` case citing its section and page.

## What was done

**Activity (2.23–2.30)**
- New `Behaviour.activity` flag: tick "This behaviour counts as activity" on the Key page. It applies to keys with a duration only.
- New `AnalysisSettings.activity_definition` with three values:
  - `mobile_or_keys` (ANY-maze): mobile, or doing a behaviour that counts as activity.
  - `keys`: ANY-maze when immobility is not detected.
  - `pixel_change`: the previous definition.
- Files saved before the option load as `pixel_change`. New experiments (`AnalysisSettings.for_new_experiment()`) use `mobile_or_keys`, and so does Restore defaults.
- With ANY-maze's definition, activity no longer needs a motion value, so it also works on imported tracks and per zone.

**Rotations and turning**
- Partial rotations (2.34–2.36): new measures `Partial rotations`, `… clockwise` and `… anticlockwise`. A partial rotation is a turn of the body of at least the *Partial rotation angle* (90° by default) during which no rotation was completed. A turn ends when the animal turns back by more than the rotations' reset angle, and it counts where the turn stopped.
- Angular velocity is now the absolute turn angle divided by the test (or period) duration, as the 2.37 note defines it.

**Zone and sequence measures**
- Undefined averages: new setting `undefined_averages` with values `blank`, `zero`, or `""` (the earlier values). It covers the measures the PDF lists for this option: 3.12, 3.28, 3.30, 3.33, 3.52, 3.55, 3.76, 5.5, 5.9 and 5.12.
- Initial heading error (zones, points, and the water-maze template): new Heading error settings.
  - The heading runs from the first position to the position after 1 s of mobility, or to the first position further away than a chosen distance.
  - Positions while the animal is immobile are ignored.

**Heat-map points (4.17–4.19)**
- `PointOfInterest.heatmap` can be `time`, `freezing`, `immobile` or `rearing`. In each test the point is placed at the hottest spot of that heat map, and all its measures use that spot.
- It reports X, Y and *approximate time at point*.
- The heat-map array code is now shared with the Heat maps view (`occupancy.occupancy_map`).

**I/O measures**
- Encoders per zone (8.x): time turning, reversals, clockwise / anticlockwise / half / quarter rotations, minimum RPM, mean RPM, and mean RPM while turning.
- Analogue signals per zone: time of max and min (9.4 / 9.5) and the integrals above / below baseline (9.14 / 9.15).
- Syringe pumps per zone (17.1 / 17.2): volume infused and withdrawn.
- RAPC (2.54–2.56): with 12 inputs given `index=1…12`, the results give type 1 errors, type 2 errors and the door sequence.
- Photobeam arrays (11.x): digital inputs sharing `detector=<name>` (time-out set with `timeout_s=`).
  - A beam broken again before another beam is not counted.
  - Each counted break starts or extends a bout of movement that lasts the time-out.
  - Beams already broken when the test starts are ignored.
- Events (21.x): a When statement's *Record as the event* notes each time its event happens during a test (kind `event` in the I/O log). The results give `Event <name>: count` and `latency (s)`.
- Investigation zones: per-zone key measures and virtual switches count while the animal investigates the zone (6.x, 22.x). These are the only devices for which the PDF says "investigating"; the other devices keep zone membership, as the PDF describes them.

**GUI**
- Key page: "This behaviour counts as activity" checkbox.
- Protocol ▸ Analysis: the activity definition, Partial rotation angle, "An average of nothing is", and a new Heading error section.
- Apparatus point properties: a location combo (fixed, or one of the heat-map bases).
- Procedure editor: "Record as the event" on When statements.
- Results table: new categories for the RAPC, pump, movement-detector and event measures.

**Docs:** USER_GUIDE covers the Protocol tab, Apparatus, Keys, the When options, the I/O channel options, I/O results and §9 Measures. It also states each definition kept as ours, and why Good / Poor tracking quality is not available.

## Decided differently / open

**Old results that change. These are corrections to ANY-maze's definitions:**
- Angular velocity: it was turn angle / time mobile; now turn angle / test duration (2.37).
- Approximate time at point: it was the moment the animal was closest to the point; now the time spent there, read from the heat map (4.19). Two assertions in `test_io_point_extras.py` that pinned the old reading were updated.
- Initial heading error: immobile positions are now ignored (3.60 / 4.12). The result is unchanged when the animal is mobile throughout its first second.
- Per-zone keys (with *Split the scored behaviours by zone*) and virtual switches in investigation zones now count while the animal investigates the zone (6.x, 22.x).
- Activity and undefined averages do **not** change for existing experiments: they keep the earlier settings until changed.

**Choices where the PDF gives no definition or no default:**
- The partial-rotation algorithm (the PDF says "beta") and its 90° default angle.
- Approximate time at point: the smoothed heat-map value × 2πσ², so that a stay on the spot counts in full.
- Heat-map point X / Y are in units, not pixels as in ANY-maze. The spot comes from the whole test, while the approximate time is given per period.
- Heat-map points can be based on position, freezing, immobility or rearing, not on keys.
- Movement-detector time-out of 1 s.
- RAPC errors are also given per period (the PDF says nothing about time periods); a chamber in which no door was opened shows as `-` in the door sequence.
- Pump volumes are in ml, like our whole-test pump measures (ANY-maze uses µl).
- Kept as ours, with the choice stated in the guide: turn angle mobility gate, heading error denominators, "moving towards" outside only, freezing time in a zone by frames.

**Not done:** ANY-maze's Good / Poor tracking quality (2.51). The PDF describes it only in words; there is no formula to reproduce.

## Tests
- New tests:
  - `tests/test_anymaze_definitions.py`: 14 cases (activity; old and new experiment defaults and file compatibility; partial rotations; angular velocity; undefined averages; heading error options; heat-map points; investigation zones; encoder in zones; analogue and pump in zones; RAPC; beam repeats; event measures).
  - `tests/gui/test_definitions_gui.py`: 4 cases.
- `uvx ruff@0.11.13 check manymaze`: 87 findings, identical to 2b75dc0.
- Full suite on macOS (offscreen): **1084 passed, 2 skipped**.

## What's new

Based on Grok's "morning path" prompt, the owner's "Patch 2" and a render.js Grok wrote, all checked against the code.

### Morning path
- **Opens on VITALS.** STATUS is one tap away.
- **Cards in today's order.**
  - The urge decoder comes first while its timer runs or after a craving of 6+ (today's or yesterday's).
  - The chem-free streak comes first the day before a milestone ("Day 7. Tomorrow: +150 XP.").
  - Otherwise the order is check-in, streak, urge decoder, so the streak stays in sight under the field report.
  - All three cards are always there. The streak card moves here from STATUS; the Lifetime total stays on STATUS.
- **Sliders start from the last check-in.** It's shown above them ("Yesterday · energy 4 · sleep 3 · craving 7"), so a day like yesterday is one tap. The INT training shows under the button.
- **Folded after logging.** The check-in becomes one line, a **FIELD REPORT** built from the state, and a **NEXT** step:
  - The report covers sleep low, craving high, INT training, dailies left, trials due and the chem-free day.
  - NEXT is a trial that's due (Go opens it) or else the daily left longest (Go opens QUESTS).
  - **Edit check-in** opens the check-in again.
- **Check-in first.** Until the check-in is logged, QUESTS, ITEMS, MAP and LOG are dimmed, and a tap shows "Check-in first: VITALS". STATUS, VITALS and the urge decoder stay open. Settings → Morning turns it off on this device.

### Skill sources (STATUS)
- **Tap a skill** to see where its points came from and what's still to come:
  - **Earned:** quests done, books, journal entries, urges ridden out.
  - **Coming:** open quests that give it.
  - A short line under each skill shows the next one coming or the latest earned.
- **The − / + buttons are gone.** Skill points come from rewards only.

## Changed from Grok's text and file

- Training is 300 XP a point, not 100.
- SURVIVAL is a skill, so it's shown read-only on the urge card after a ride-out.
- The check-in folds when it's logged; there is no separate "close morning" tap.
- The UI stays in English, like the rest of the app.
- The lock is a setting, and it stays off if the phone's storage can't be read.
- From the render.js, I left out:
  - its second tab lock, which ignored the Settings switch;
  - its `<div>`s inside a `<button>`.
- Its journal and urge sources needed `award()` to record skill points in the history, so that's added.

## Data

- No new saved block and no new XP path.
- `vitalsToday()` now fills a new day's levels from the last check-in instead of 5 (`lastCheckIn()`).
- `award()` adds `data.skills` (for example `"KNOWLEDGE:3,FINANCE:1"`) to each history event that gave skill points. It fits the events' existing shape (strings ≤ 200, ≤ 8 keys), so backups keep it and no migration is needed. Older events have none.
- The lock setting is a per-device `localStorage` key, like the power-on screen setting.

## Checks

- `node --test`: 258/258 pass.
  - `tests/morning.test.js`:
    - the card order
    - sliders filled from the last check-in
    - the field report, including the streak
    - the next step
    - the lock refusing a tab tap
    - a hostile name
  - `tests/skills.test.js`:
    - sources counted once
    - backups keep `data.skills`
    - skill buttons and detail, with escaping
    - the tap toggles without changing the skill
  - `tests/history.test.js` now expects `data.skills`.
- Tested live in Chromium with Playwright, with no errors:
  - the morning path end to end
  - each card order
  - the Settings toggle
  - on STATUS: 8 skill buttons with no steppers; a tap opens Earned / Coming and keeps focus; a second tap closes it; no sideways scroll

author: flouss
body:
## What

A Gmail or Microsoft account connected over OAuth never got its own colour. Every one of them kept the column default (`colorIndex = 0`), so they wore the same dot in the sidebar and the same corner mark on every message row, which is the one job that mark has.

## Cause

`AccountCreator::create()` hands out `colorIndex` from the lowest free palette slot, but `OAuthAccountLinker::upsert()` builds its `Account` without going through it.

## Fix

- `upsert()` assigns the lowest free slot to a **new** OAuth account, via `AccountCreator::freeColorIndex()` (made public; it was already pure).
- A reconnect finds the existing row and leaves its colour alone.

## Tests

`OAuthAccountLinkerColourTest`, with expected slots derived by hand (a user with a password account in slot 0: the first OAuth account takes 1, the next takes 2). It fails before the fix (every OAuth account stays 0). Mutation-checked a second baseline too: assigning the colour outside the "new account" branch repaints a reconnected account, and the reconnect test fails. `AccountOrderIsNotIdentityTest` still passes. PHPStan clean on the touched files.

It goes through `upsert()` by reflection, because `link()` also seeds aliases and registers push against the real provider.

Not changed: OAuth accounts connected before this keep slot 0. No migration; the changelog says so.

author: maxh
body:
The demo plan's step 7, first scenario: the paper's suddenly foolish administrator. Slow reasoning turns his basic questions into elevated risk, and his high-risk operations then need his security key, which an agent working with his credentials can't touch. Decision in ADR 0062.

**awzy-reasoner**
- A new signal: resources a principal opened in the last day that neither it nor its team had opened in the month before. Two a day are ordinary; past that, 10 points each, up to 50.
- On its own it makes risk elevated, but never reaches the 80 that challenges everything.
- A new ClickHouse query loads who opened each recent resource, capped at 100 openers per resource.

**Policies**
- `elevated-risk-high-risk-operations-verify`: a person above risk 40 calling a `crown_jewels` MCP tool gets a security-key challenge.
- `it-calls-any-tool`: IT may call any MCP tool.

**Synthetic company**
- `larkspur-admin` is a stand-in MCP server with four admin tools, served at `/admin/mcp` next to larkspur-drive. IT runs them as routine work.
- The scenario: Lee reads seven of engineering's introductions for new starters and IT's runbook, then runs three crown-jewel operations within a minute.
- The end-to-end test scores the morning with the reasoner's own code and writes the scores to awzy-context. It checks that every scenario step gets the expected outcome and that no ordinary work is challenged.
- Two new tests check that nobody else's risk rises above 40, on the scenario day or on an ordinary day.

**Behavior changes**
- A scenario's own accessors don't count toward false positives on the day it runs.
- `AWZY_DRIVE_UPSTREAM` is removed; the driver picks the upstream from each call's tool.

**Docs:** the platform plan gets a row for awzy-reasoner (it was listed as not started), the demo plan's step 7 is updated, and the synthetic README and DEVELOPMENT.md describe the `larkspur-admin` upstream.

**Testing:** `bazel test --config=local-stack` passes for the synthetic, reasoner, and PDP packages, and `bazel build --config=lint //...` is clean.

**Known limitation:** a demo that replays the same scenario every day makes Lee's earlier reads familiar to him, so his score stops rising (ADR 0062, Consequences).

author: agoodkind
body:
### Problem

poweredge booted without SSH, the Proxmox API, and a login prompt from 2026-10-08 to 2026-10-10 because ifupdown2 3.3.0 treated `iface nic2 inet6 auto` as DHCPv6 and waited for a lease the provider never supplied. `networking.service` has no start time limit. DHCPv4 worked throughout. The kernel option `quiet` hid the waiting job. Configs defined neither `/etc/network/interfaces` nor the kernel command line.

The overlay module writes `/etc/default/grub.d/boot-messages.cfg` with `GRUB_CMDLINE_LINUX_DEFAULT="systemd.show_status=1"` for poweredge. The module runs `opentofu/overlay/files/refresh-grub.sh` through `remote-exec` after that file changes. The module writes `/etc/network/interfaces` from `opentofu/overlay/files/poweredge/interfaces` without a network reload. The module declares `inet dhcp` for DHCPv4, `accept-ra 1`, and `autoconf 1` on `nic2`. The host starts no DHCPv6 client. The module adds no resource for Vault or suburban.

poweredge already has both declared files. SSH, the Proxmox API, and the serial login work after an ordinary boot. Only the DHCPv4 client runs. DHCPv4 assigns `135.84.144.59/27` to `nic2`. `nic2` has only a link-local IPv6 address. Two router solicitations received no router advertisement. `tofu fmt -check`, `tofu validate`, `./configsctl lint`, and `shellcheck` pass. No plan ran.

author: frizynn
body:
## Por qué

Con el coordinador caído, apretar `g` en el popup y volver a la tab de origen congelaba Herdr hasta cerrar la terminal.

`g` corría `go_to_pane` dentro del popup. Eso abre el coordinador, que crea un workspace con `--focus` y espera `herdr agent start --timeout 20000`. Herdr mantiene el popup modal hasta que su proceso termina. Al volver a la tab de origen el popup reaparece congelado y se queda con todas las teclas hasta que vence la espera. El log del server real lo muestra dos veces hoy. `codex` salió con código 1 y el popup siguió vivo 20 s más. El selector `open` y crear un proyecto desde el popup tenían el mismo problema.

## Qué cambia

- `ui_ops::Jump` (ir a un nodo, abrir el coordinador). En el popup, esos tres casos guardan el salto y cierran. El dock no cambia porque no es modal.
- Al cerrarse, el popup lanza `herdr-organizations jump ...` en una sesión propia. Ese proceso espera a que el popup termine (fin de un pipe) y recién ahí mueve el foco. Un error llega como notificación de Herdr.
- `create_project` ya no abre el coordinador. `runner::new_session` reemplaza las dos copias de `setsid`.
- Docs: test manual del popup, arquitectura y la repro en `herdr-notes.md`.

## Validación

- Test rojo antes del fix (el popup llamaba a `workspace create --focus` antes de cerrarse), test de integración de `jump` (no llama a Herdr hasta que el popup sale y avisa los errores) y test de ida y vuelta de sus argumentos.
- `cargo fmt --check`, `clippy -D warnings`, `cargo test --locked` (468 tests) y `cargo build --release --locked` pasan en local.
- Herdr descartable con server 0.9.1 (como el real) y cliente 0.9.3 en un pty, coordinador con el workspace cerrado y un agente que sale con código 1:

| Caso | Antes | Después |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `g`, volver a la tab y tipear | sin eco en 5 s, Esc no responde | eco en 0,10 s |
| Selector `open` | sin eco en 5 s | eco en 0,10 s |
| Proyecto nuevo | sin eco en 5 s | eco en 0,10 s |

Con el coordinador vivo, `g` sigue llevando a él.

## Riesgo y rollback

Un error de `g` ya no se ve en el popup, llega como notificación. Rollback con `git revert` del merge.

Queda fuera: si el agente no arranca, `go_to_pane` igual espera 20 s y después enfoca el workspace del coordinador sin avisar. Ya pasaba antes.

author: cruisercohen
body:
## Problem / Motivation

**Goal:** A reasoning effort picked for a session reaches that session even when no model is pinned, and the spawn receipt reports the same outcome the provider produces.

With `agent.model` set to the empty string, the provider factory resolves no model id. Its effort gate needs one (`if m and _eff and ...`), so the per-model effort map stays empty and the level is dropped. After a restart the session runs the backend's own default effort while the dashboard still shows the level the operator picked. This happens on every backend: on the registry-gated ones the empty id also fails `model_supports_effort("")`, and on `pi` the `m and` guard is the only check left.

## Why it matters

The dashboard reports an effort level the session is not running. The operator gets no error and no log line on the advertised-option path, so the mismatch is invisible until someone notices how the model answers. The spawn receipt has the same problem in both directions once the level can be applied: it must not say "dropped" for a level the provider applied, or "applied" for one the provider could not apply.

## Not a goal

- Changing which model an unpinned session runs. An explicitly empty `agent.model` still lets the backend choose.
- Getting effort to apply on kiro-cli's `auto` model. kiro-cli refuses an effort level while the model is `auto`, so with nothing to bind to, the level is logged as not applied.

## What changed (motivation → approach → change)

Symptom: a level picked with nothing pinned is lost at provider construction. Root cause: every effort read and write is keyed by model id, and an unpinned session has no id until the backend answers `session/new`.

Approach (the shape suggested in the issue): carry the level unkeyed through construction, then bind it to the model the backend reports serving once the session is ready, before the initial effort push. The spawn receipt then asks the same question the provider asks.

- `config/loader.py`: when the resolved model is empty, the factory passes the level as `unbound_effort` instead of dropping it. A level that would be dropped for any other reason still warns there, as before.
- `providers/acp.py`:
  - `_effort_model` is the id every effort site keys on: the pinned model, or the served model (`served_model`, taken from `currentModelId`) when nothing is pinned. `supports_effort`, `_resolve_effort`, `_apply_effort_overlay`, `change_effort`, `clear_effort` and the `set_model` carry now read it instead of the raw client field, so a live change and a restart agree on the key.
  - `_bind_unbound_effort` runs on every (re)start before `_apply_initial_effort`. It stores the level under the served model unless a level is already stored there. On the config-option harnesses (claude, codex, deepseek, pi) the existing initial push then applies it. On the kiro family, whose level otherwise rides the spawn-time overlay, it pushes the level live through `change_effort`, which also writes the overlay for the next spawn. If the serving model takes no level, or no model was reported, it logs a "will not be applied" warning once per provider and leaves the level unapplied.
  - The kiro push is live code, not a corner case: an unpinned kiro session is launched without `--model` (`AcpRuntime` gets no model, and the provider only re-applies a configured model that is not `auto`), and kiro-cli then serves its own `chat.defaultModel` when one is set. The level is not stored before `change_effort` runs, so a push kiro-cli refuses rolls back to nothing instead of leaving the level in the map and the overlay for the next spawn.
  - `clear_effort` drops the unbound level so a later restart does not bring it back. `change_effort` replaces it, so a restart binds the level picked last.
  - kiro-cli reports `currentModelId` `auto` for an `auto` session, and `served_model` filters that to `""`. So an unpinned kiro session on `auto` still offers no effort, and a live change is still skipped instead of being pushed to a model that refuses it.
- `subagent.py`: an unpinned spawn gets neither verdict. `effort_drop_reason` reports no drop and `effort_applied_note` claims no delivery; a new `effort_pending_note` says the level is bound at start to the model the backend serves and applied only if that model takes effort, otherwise logged as not applied. This holds on every backend, the kiro family included, because the served model is not known at accept time on any of them. For a requested effort whose selection resolves, exactly one of the three is non-empty. A per-spawn `backend` keeps its own rules above that: one with no effort channel still reports the drop, and one that advertises its own levels still gets none of the three.
- `dashboard/messaging_api/spawn.py`: `/api/spawn` returns the pending note as a new optional `effort_pending` field beside `effort_dropped` and `effort_applied`.
- `mcp_tools/spawn.py`: `spawn_run` renders `effort_pending` as a neutral `ℹ reasoning_effort='<level>' for <ids>: <note>` line, with no `✓` and neither "applied" nor "dropped", because the outcome is decided after the tool returns.
- `docs/system-specs/modules/providers.md`: the reasoning-effort paragraph describes the unbound level, `_effort_model`, the kiro `chat.defaultModel` case and the drop log, which replace the factory warning for an unresolved model.
- `docs/system-specs/modules/subagent.md`: the `reasoning_effort` receipt paragraph describes `effort_pending` and the three-way rule.

Design choice: keep the kiro live push in the provider, and report an unpinned spawn's effort as pending on every backend. The receipt cannot know at spawn time whether kiro-cli will serve a configured default model or `auto`, and the provider already judges the level once the model is named and logs it when it is not applied. A third field, instead of a conditional `effort_applied` note, keeps the tool from printing a `✓ applied` line for a level that may be dropped.

Alternatives rejected:
- Delete the kiro `change_effort` branch and keep the kiro receipt's drop. That makes the two halves agree by keeping the bug on kiro: an operator whose kiro-cli `chat.defaultModel` takes effort would get the same silent drop this issue reports.
- Predict the served model in the receipt by reading kiro-cli's `chat.defaultModel`. That is a second resolver of kiro-cli's settings precedence (user file, workspace overlay, agent spec) that can drift from what kiro-cli actually serves.
- Split the receipt by backend capability. It says "dropped" for an unpinned kiro spawn whose served default model the provider then pushes the level to.
- Carry the conditional note in `effort_applied`. The tool renders every `effort_applied` as `✓ ... applied`, so an unpinned kiro spawn on `auto` would read as applied while its level is dropped.
- Report nothing for an unpinned spawn, the answer a per-spawn backend that advertises its own levels gets. The receipts exist so a requested effort never goes unreported in the tool result, and unpinned with no field is the default spawn: the caller would lose both the outcome and the hint the old drop line gave it (pin an effort-capable `model=` to know at spawn time). The advertised-option case keeps its silence; this change does not widen it.
- Treat an empty `agent.model` as `auto`, so it resolves through the agent spec or the bundled default. That changes which model the session runs, which is a product decision outside this bug, and it still leaves the `auto`-resolves-to-nothing case broken.
- Store the level under the `""` key. `_resolve_effort` looks it up by the client's model, which is `""` or `auto`, and `resolve_effort_for_model` returns nothing for an empty id. The level would still never be pushed.

## Backwards compatibility

Compatible: a pinned model takes the same path as before (the level is keyed by the pin and nothing is carried), and `unbound_effort` defaults to empty for every other constructor caller.

author: tfenne
body:
> Review-only PR within the fork, opened to get CodeRabbit feedback. Not for merging here.

## Summary

`conditioning_set::compactSelection` packs each common site's selected reference bits into `Hvar` one byte at a time. Every byte is an `unsigned char` store, which may alias any object, so the compiler re-read `H.HvarRef`, `Hvar` and `idxHaps_ref` through their members after each store: about 11 of the loop's 61 instructions per byte with Apple clang.

This reads the reference row, the `Hvar` row and the state list through local pointers instead, via a new `bitmatrix::rowBytes(row)` (const and non-const). The 8 bits stay written out: clang vectorises a loop over them into per-lane byte inserts, which was 8.6% slower overall. `setByte`, used only here, is removed. Output is unchanged.

## Results

Single-threaded, HGDP+1KG chr22 chunks 2, 7 and 12 (8,176 haplotypes, NA12878 removed), tutorial NA12878 BAMs, median of 5 interleaved reps on a pinned core (AWS `.large` spot) or 3 reps (M4). Wall-time change from this commit:

| Platform | On this base, 1x / 0.2x | On top of `tf_reduce_rss` + PBWT speed-up, 1x / 0.2x |
|---|---|---|
| AMD Turin (m8a.large, g++ 13.3) | -2.0% / -2.0% | -2.6% / -3.4% |
| Graviton4 (m8g.large, clang 23.1.2) | +0.2% / +0.1% | -1.2% / -1.5% |
| Apple M4 (Apple clang) | -1.6% (both) | not measured |

Instructions fall by 1.4-4.4% everywhere. On Graviton4 against this base the cycle count doesn't move. Output was byte-identical in all 12 AWS pairs and in 46 local cases (all 16 HGDP chunks at both coverages, tutorial chunks 2/7/15, `--Kpbwt 1000`, and a panel below `Kpbwt`, which takes the full-panel path). Neither g++ nor clang vectorises the new loop.

body:
Part of #527.

This adds the eval cases that #520 deferred because they needed new CLI snapshots, adds long-session variants of three ceiling cases, and adds scaffolding for a 2×2 ablation. Nothing here has run live; `claude plugin eval` can't run in this environment.

## New CLI snapshots (`test-cases/`)

| Snapshot | What it records |
| --- | --- |
| `136-fix-code-denied-reply-one-look-skip` | The REST tick after a denied reply. The denied thread is suppressed and only the new thread reaches the apply command. |
| `137-escalate-proxy-session-refusal-mark-ready` | A cloud-proxy refusal of mark-ready escalates as `transport-unsupported` (exit 13). |
| `138-ready-required-approval-gate` | `[READY]` with `Approvals: None [Required]` and "awaiting 1 approval". |
| `139-fix-code-rest-review-thread` | The first REST tick that 136 continues. |
| `apply-review-denied-reply`, `apply-review-session-refusal` | Real `apply review` output (exit 69 and exit 77), recorded by the new `apply-review.test.mts` through the REST mutation path against a local wire. |

The harness gains two fixture keys: `restErrorResponses` (non-2xx REST bodies by path) and `claudeCodeRemote`.

## New eval cases

| Case | Fixture | Rule under test |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `38-denied-reply-one-look-skip` | 136 | A denied reply is a one-look skip. Don't retry the denied ID, don't escalate, keep iterating. |
| `39-proxy-session-refusal` | apply-review-session-refusal | Exit 77: request `add_repo` with push access, then retry only the pending ID. Not a review denial. |
| `43-required-approval-gate` | 138 | The positive direction of `08`: the required approval is the blocker. No self-approval, no `--admin`, rerun after the ready delay. |
| `44-multi-pr-cancel-long-session` | 03 | `25`, after earlier ticks on both PRs. |
| `45-stack-handoff-long-session` | 102 | `15`, after a finished one-PR session. |
| `46-stack-all-owned-long-session` | 106 | `16`, after a finished one-PR session. |

- Numbers 40–42 are left for #530's `cloud.mjs`.
- New cases set `runs: 6` through a new per-case `runs` field.
- `39` is a regression guard. The plugin has no `add_repo` guidance, so expect Δ≈0.

## Multi-turn

`plugin eval`'s only history hook is `case.yaml` `context.history_file`, and its schema is unpublished. Instead, `transcriptShape` in `evals/lib.mjs` replays the earlier turns as a labelled transcript inside the prompt. Every history tool output is read from a snapshot with `historyText`, so the history stays in CI sync with the CLI.

## Ablation scaffolding

`node evals/generate.mjs --instructions playbook --out <dir>` writes the playbook arm outside `evals/`.

- It reads `<fixture>-playbook` snapshots and skips cases that have none. History turns stay inline.
- The default output is unchanged.
- EVALS.md documents the steps for when #523 lands: add the `-playbook` fixtures, generate, run both arms with `--ablation with-without`, then compare them with `analyze.mjs`.

docs: `evals/EVALS.md`, `evals/README.md` and `test-cases/README.md` are updated.

author: kleinc80
body:
Stopping the File editor app (configurator) makes Supervisor log a warning:

    App File editor did not handle SIGTERM and was terminated by the default signal handler (exit code 143).

After stopping the app it shows status "Error" (not "Stopped").

This was reported in #4756 (closed as stale).

## Root cause

hass-configurator only installs a handler for SIGINT. s6 stops the service with SIGTERM, so the process dies from the default signal action and the `finish` script records 128 + 15 = 143 as the container exit code.

## Change

- Add an s6 `down-signal` file so the service is stopped with SIGINT. The existing handler then closes the server and exits with code 0. Same approach as #4800 and #4801.
- Bump the app version to 6.2.1.

## Related

#4846  also bumps the version to 6.2.1 and contains the second part of the changes made in #4800 and #4801 ("Leave the 'Starting' state faster by checking readiness every 5 seconds during startup").

## Tests

I ran the image locally against a mocked Supervisor API. After the web server answered with HTTP 200:

| | exit code after `docker stop` | service log |
|---|---|---|
| without the changes of this PR | 143 | `Service exited with code 256 (by signal 15)` |
| with the changes of this PR | 0 | `Got signal: 2. Shutting down server` / `Service exited with code 0 (by signal 0)` |

`docker stop` takes about 3 s in both cases.

author: jaredlunde
body:
## What

The gateway becomes billing's source of truth: every `ai.usage` row now carries its price, computed by the reference pricer (`providers::pricing`, #162 and #164) from the row's own facts. Beyond only has to collect and batch the rows.

Built on #163 (the row contract) and #164 (the pricer aligned to it), both merged.

- **The call.** `logging` calls `pricing::price()` at row emission, after the response and off the relay path. It costs about 165 ns and no allocation per row.
- **The fields.** Beside the existing facts, every row now has:
  - `price_status`: `priced`, `estimated` or `unpriced`;
  - `price_reason`: the reason code when unpriced;
  - `price_micros` and `cost_micros`, both absent when unpriced (**never a zero**);
  - `cost_basis`: `tokens`, `reported`, `dearest_endpoint` or `cache_hit`;
  - `price_detail` and `cost_detail`: a `key=value` breakdown written straight into the log line with no heap allocation;
  - `rate_version`: which compiled rate table priced the row;
  - `start_unix_secs`: the request's start, which DeepSeek's off-peak tier is decided on, logged so a repricer reads the same second.
- **Same inputs for repricing.** `server_tools` is read back from its logged text, so a repricer working from the row sees what the gateway priced.
- **Unpriced rows are alertable.** Each one increments the new `ai_usage_unpriced_total`.
- **Cache hits** cost 0 and are priced 0. This is a fixed rule (owner decision), not a setting.
- **`web_search_preview`.** The pricer learns #163's new kind: $10/1K on reasoning models, $25/1K on the rest. Web search on gpt-4o and gpt-4.1 is now priced; gpt-4o-mini and gpt-4.1-mini are still refused because of their fixed 8K-token block. The golden vectors grow to 94, and `RATE_VERSION` becomes `2026-10-10.70d68df553023807`.
- **Docs** (`crates/gateway/ARCHITECTURE.md`):
  - The intro now says the gateway emits a priced billing row.
  - The row contract marks the price authoritative and keeps the token facts for audit and repricing.
  - A new section, "The price (authoritative)", lists the fields.
  - "Repricing stays possible" explains why: every input fact is kept, plus `rate_version`.
  - The cache-hit rule is stated.
  - "Why the catalog has a list price and the request does not" is replaced by "Why the gateway prices the row".
  - The metric is added to the metrics table.

## Pass-through pricing (owner decision, folded in)

The customer pays exactly what we pay for each request, fees included: `price_micros == cost_micros` on every row. Both come from the card of the host that served the request:

- OpenRouter: `usage.cost` plus the 5.5% credit fee;
- Bedrock `us.`: list +10%;
- each open-model host: its own rates.

An estimated row is priced from the same estimate as its cost. The gateway's own cache writes are priced as the 5-minute writes the vendor bills.

The customer card is renamed the list card (`RowRates::list`). It is still the ListPrice that `/v1/models` publishes.

`tests/pass_through.rs` asserts price == cost on all 95 vectors (recomputed by the independent implementation) and on every row × candidate × class × usage shape. Both ARCHITECTURE docs now state pass-through, and the "cost exceeds price" list is gone. `RATE_VERSION` is `2026-10-10.ad3fdef71820a687`.

## Tests

- **`tests/billing_price_vectors.rs`** (claim BIL-24) drives golden vectors through a real gateway. A mock upstream answers with each vector's usage, and the row must carry the vector's exact `cost_micros`/`price_micros` (or `unpriced` with its reason, and the counter at 1). The cases:
  - Anthropic: basic; cache read + 5m + 1h; fast × US-only × caches × web search; a refusal.
  - OpenAI: cached, priority.
  - OpenRouter: reported cost + fee, native search.
  - A slow upstream (2.5 s), which pins `start_unix_secs` to the request's start rather than its end.
- **Mutation, checked by hand** (per instructions). I flipped each new condition and confirmed a test failed:
  - the unpriced counter's `inc()`;
  - `saturating_sub` → `saturating_add` on the start time (this one survived until the slow-upstream test was added);
  - the breakdown's `Display` (a providers unit test pins it too).
- **Suites:** providers, gateway and verify all pass locally. Clippy `-D warnings`, fmt and dprint are clean, and `verify gate` is OK.

## Next

The reconciliation PR is ready on `jared/pricing-reconcile`, stacked on this one:

- live, key-gated cases per dimension;
- BIL-5 extended to money;
- BIL-25 invoice-level reconciliation.

body:
## Summary

Closes the loop on PR #44 (README data-sources accuracy). That PR explicitly deferred fixing the **matching in-code comment** at `app.js:11–13` because of cache-buster implications — this PR lands that fix.

## Diff (8 insertions, 6 deletions)

```diff
 app.js     | 8 +++++---
 index.html | 4 ++--
 sw.js      | 2 +-
```

### `app.js` — comment block

```diff
-     Stop coordinates (GMB / NLB / MTR) → third-party curated
-       dataset by hk-bus (https://data.hkbus.app/), packaged at
-       /assets/hk-stops.json (CC0-style compilation of TD sources).
+     Stop coordinates (bus / LRT / MTR / NLB) → curated bundle
+       at /assets/hk-stops.json (CC0-style compilation of TD sources,
+       third-party hk-bus dataset at https://data.hkbus.app/).
+       Per-operator catalogues live in /assets/mtr-stops.json
+       (MTR stations) and /assets/lrt-stops.json (Light Rail stops).
```

Brings the in-code attribution in line with the README. Also surfaces the per-operator catalogues (`mtr-stops.json` + `lrt-stops.json`) as the dedicated lookups, with `hk-stops.json` as the everything-else fallback — matches PR #44's wording.

### `index.html` + `sw.js` — cache-buster bumps

Per `docs/cache-strategy.md` (app.js changed → bumps apply):

| Knob | Before | After |
|------|--------|-------|
| `meta` | `55` | `56` |
| `app.js?v=` | `45` | `46` |
| `sw.js CACHE` | `buseta-v44` | `buseta-v45` |
| `planner.js?v=` | (unchanged) | (unchanged) |
| `planner.css?v=` | (unchanged) | (unchanged) |
| `style.css?v=` | (unchanged) | (unchanged) |

## Why this matters

The README and the in-code attribution comment had drifted apart — both described `assets/hk-stops.json` as primarily "GMB / NLB / MTR" content, but the actual file is ~92% bus stops of any operator (TD-assigned numeric IDs in the 20M-prefixed range). PR #44 fixed the README; this PR fixes the matching in-code comment so future contributors see consistent information in both places.

## Important context: main vs the Phase 1–37 stack

`main` is currently at v53 with cache-buster values `meta=55`, `app.js?v=45`, `sw.js CACHE=buseta-v44`. The Phases 1–37 enhancement work (tests/, scripts/, src/utils/, eslint config, .gitattributes, .nvmrc, dependabot.yml, etc.) sits on the `enhance/phase38-trams-stub` branch stacked on top of main, ending at `meta=75` / `app.js?v=64` / `sw.js CACHE=buseta-v64`.

- **PRs #39–#44** branch off that stack (they need `tests/`, `src/utils/trams.js`, etc.).
- **This PR (#45)** branches off main directly — the comment fix doesn't depend on the stack.

This PR's bumps start from main's actual values (55/45/44) rather than the stack's terminal values (75/64/64). The invariants `meta ≥ max(asset ?v=)` and `sw.js CACHE ≥ max(asset ?v=)` hold in both orderings:

| Merge order | End-state `meta` |
|-------------|------------------|
| This PR merges first, then stack | `meta=76` |
| Stack merges first, then this PR | `meta=76` |

Either way monotonic increase holds. This PR is safe to merge independently.

## Verification

```
$ git diff --stat
 app.js     | 8 +++++---
 index.html | 4 ++--
 sw.js      | 2 +-
 3 files changed, 8 insertions(+), 6 deletions(-)
```

No Prettier --write run — main hasn't been Prettier-formatted historically and introducing reformatting here is out of scope.

No cache-buster invariant tests exist on main (`scripts/check-cache-buster.js` lives on the `enhance/phase21-cache-buster-test` branch which is part of the unmerged Phase 1–37 stack). The bumps follow the pattern from `docs/cache-strategy.md` manually.

No tests added (no code change).

## Out of scope

- This PR does not touch the Phase 1–37 stack. The stack's eventual merge will continue its own +1 chain on top of these values.
- This PR does not introduce Prettier formatting to main. The unmerged stack has Prettier on `src/utils/` files but main itself doesn't.

## Merge order

Trivial, independent of all other open PRs (#39–#44 stack on `enhance/phase38-trams-stub`; this PR stacks on main). Safe to merge at any time.

- [PR #44 (README accuracy)](https://github.com/rollroyces/buseta-hk/pull/44) — the README half of this symmetry fix
- [`app.js:11–13`](https://github.com/rollroyces/buseta-hk/blob/main/app.js#L11) — the in-code attribution being corrected

author: gafferongames
body:
Fault 9 (c13, 2026-10-10): children on superman's `pro-deepseek-v4-direct` and `flash-deepseek41-direct` routes worked until the route deadline and never wrote RESULT.md. In one case a real commit had been pushed, and nothing reported it.

## What was and was not confirmed

- **The fault was not reproduced on superman.** In `~/nova-bench/results` I found no deepseek job that was missing its RESULT.md (the only directory without one was `ci/`), and `card-jobs/` was empty. The fault is taken from the seat's fault inventory, not from a job I saw.
- **The route deadlines were not read.** `nova-config route show` is refused on the Studio because no nova-config login is recorded for this account. This PR does not change either route's deadline.

## The design

The card already tells the child to finish at 80% of its wall (`member.WallText`, `WallFinishShare = 0.8`). That covers option (a), the margin before the deadline. This PR adds a backstop for a child that ignores that line and works on to the deadline:

- `watch` records `deadlined` when the deadline timer is what ended the run.
- When the run ends, `swarm.WriteDeadlineResult` writes a `RESULT.md` FOR the card if all three of these hold:
  - the deadline ended the run;
  - `./repo` holds commits past its base (`repoCommits`);
  - the card published no result (`FindCardResult`).

  The rule is the pure function `swarm.DeadlineReports`.
- The report names the branch, the commit count and the head. Its first line is `RESULT: BLOCKED <task>` with no findings head, so it is scored `plan-only` and never `ok`. It carries the same `written-by: nova-swarm native` line as the idle-end report, and it never overwrites a result the card wrote.
- No report is written for a run that ended any other way: idle, TERM, budget stop, wall refusal or lost response. Each of those already has its own end.

## Tests

- `TestDeadlineReportsOnlyAJobTheDeadlineEndedThatCommittedAndPublishedNothing`: a table test of the decision. Each row that writes no report differs from the reporting row in one condition.
- `TestWriteDeadlineResultNamesTheWorkTheCardCommitted` (functional tag, real git): the report's content, never overwriting a result, and no report when there is no commit or the deadline did not end the run.
- `TestWallTextFinishMinuteAtTheMarginBoundary`: the 80% finish minute at its rounding boundaries (149 s and 150 s, 599/600/601 s, and others).

Built and tested on hetzner2 (go 1.26.6), never on the Studio. There is no TLA+ module for the native wait's ends, so no model applies.

author: mikkoparkkola
body:
## What this changes

A Windows run failed `build_first::a_failed_replacement_keeps_serving_the_old_transport`: an approved login came back `AuthorizationCancelled` (login_window.rs:663).

**Cause.**
- The login fixture issued a token good for 65 s against the 60 s early-expiry margin, so it had 5 s of real use.
- On a slow runner it lapsed mid-start. The start's era probe (`src/backend/era.rs`, bounded at 2 s) then met an expired token, and its token step led a second login: a second browser open.
- The 2 s bound dropped the probe, and with it the login's lead. `Lead::drop` ended the login `Cancelled`, and the start behind it shared that outcome.
- It reproduces deterministically: a zero-margin token fails the same row in 2.2 s with the same two-login signature as the CI log.

**The product side.** The era probe's contract is that it can never fail a start. Yet a background request with a short bound could open the user's browser and abandon the login 2 s later. The same holds for the other bounded background upkeep: the event-listener session (open, refill, subscriptions) and task recovery's discover, query and cancel. Each now runs `non_interactive`, as the health probe already does. A lapsed token reads as "authorization required", and only a request a person is waiting on logs in.

**Task recovery, precisely.** Only recovery's query and cancel are background upkeep, so they run wholly non-interactive, including the discovery they trigger. The claim a task dispatch makes runs in its caller's own mode: run non-interactive, it was refused while a start held the backend, and the task was dispatched with recovery silently unarmed. The owner's upstream `tasks/cancel` is a row's one send, so before its non-interactive attempt it waits, within its own deadline, for any start in flight to finish (a restarted gateway reconnecting). Without that wait it was refused and never sent. The health probe keeps answering at once: it never queues behind a start.

**The test side.** `approved_start` now issues a long-lived token. Each row that needs a lapsed token ages it on demand (`token_lapse::lapse`), after waiting for any request the row must send first: a fill's second page, a probe's request. No row races a wall-clock window any more.

## Evidence (Spark)

- Red first (commit 1, the fix sites at base):
  - era probe: "the era probe opened a login";
  - task recovery: "sent these where a login may begin: [(server/discover, true), (tasks/get, true), (tasks/cancel, true)]";
  - event session: "the event session ran where a login may begin".
- Green (commit 2): full lib suite 10,511 passed, 0 failed.
- Clippy, all-features and no-default-features, on Linux and windows-gnu: rc=0.
- Review: design note to both reviewers, then code review on 9b036409d. Both SHIP.

## Test-only hooks

These are all `#[cfg(test)]`, and the `Transport` trait is unchanged:
- `OAuthClient::age_token_for_test`, which saves through the existing locked save path;
- `HttpTransport::oauth_client_for_test`;
- the `Backend::last_oauth_client` field, filled where the start builds the HTTP transport;
- the `Shared::ran_interactive` cell on the event session.

## Stated limits

- A request a person *is* waiting on (a fill deadline, a warm-start attempt) can still lose an in-progress login when its deadline fires. That needs request-time logins owned by a detached task, and is filed separately (B-class, v4.0.0).
- A claimed upstream `tasks/cancel` whose one send still fails (a peer down for the whole deadline, or a start that is a real login outlasting it) is logged and not retried. It can leave the upstream job running after the owner cancelled. Filed separately (v4.0.0).
- After a lapsed-token probe reads as silence, a modern-only peer gets the legacy handshake, as any silent peer does.
- Follow-ups from review (optional):
  - real-OAuth cases for the event and task-recovery rows;
  - a wire-level witness for the event session;
  - a start-completes assertion on the era row;
  - asserting the recovering probe's error type;
  - `age_token_for_test` failing loudly with no stored token.

Family: login-under-deadline (Refs MIK-8269)

author: indicaza
body:
## Summary
- **One connection.** `withGuildDatabase`/`withGuildTransaction` opened a new SQLite connection and re-ran the migration check on every call (81 call sites). The connection is now opened and migrated once per database file. It reopens if the data directory changes or the file is replaced (checked by inode, so restores and test directories still work). Nested transactions become savepoints.
- **Atomic ingest.** One telemetry ingest opened 7 connections and committed 6 times, so a failure part way left the raw record, latest state, read model and stream head out of step. It now runs as one transaction. Local benchmark: 14.2 → 1.6 ms per ingest.
- **Migration 8.** The Guildweaver tables (pairings, devices, telemetry records, stream heads, latest state, character aliases) and `game_data_catalog` move from create-on-first-use into a numbered migration. The SQL is unchanged and uses `IF NOT EXISTS`, so it's a no-op on production. `ensureQuestCompletionSchema` is removed because migration 6 already creates that table. The read-model tables keep their own versioned rebuild, by design. The legacy `character_snapshot_ingests` and `telemetry_*` projection tables are left alone; the legacy snapshot removal will delete them.
- **Payload stored once.** `guildweaver_telemetry_latest_state.envelope_json` no longer repeats the payload, which lives in `payload_json` (and raw in the record). Existing rows are slimmed once at startup, tracked in `app_meta`. On a local copy of the dev database, latest-state envelopes went from about 1.3 MB to 16 KB.

## Tests
- New `telemetryIngestStorage.test.js`: a failure injected during projection leaves no raw record, latest state or head, and the retry isn't mistaken for a duplicate (fails on `main`, passes here). Also covers savepoint rollback, the slimmer envelope, and the one-time startup slimming.
- Updated tests that called the removed `ensure*` helpers, or asserted that latest state held the raw payload (only tests read it).
- Backend: 379/379. Frontend tests and backend lint pass.

Bundles two pieces of Talos work (per request, one branch):

The `nextcloud` CloudNativePG `Cluster` had no backups while the shared `postgres` cluster did. This adds the same pattern:

## 摘要

台账 **#63 结清**：`encaps-tenant` 在 **prod profile 下起不来**（启动即 `Schema validation: missing table [api_definition]`）。

### 根因（不是"误扫"，是**有意复用**）

`encaps-tenant` 的 `ProjectController` / `TenantService` / `AdminController` 直接使用 encaps-layer 的 model/repository（`ProjectEntity` / `Tenant` / `ApiDefinitionRepository` / `AssetRepository` / `DataSourceRepository` / `SyncTaskRepository`），其持久单元因此**确实**包含 20 个共享实体；而本模块迁移只建了 2 张表（`quotas` / `workspaces`）。prod 走 `ddl-auto=validate` + 独立 schema（`encaps_tenant`）⇒ 少一张表就启动失败。

### 修法

- 新增 `V3__baseline_shared_model.sql`（**20 张表**）：由 `bash scripts/gen-db-baseline.sh platform/encaps-tenant` 按 Hibernate PostgreSQL 方言**导出后切片**（共导出 22 张；`quotas`/`workspaces` 留在 V1），**非手写**。
- `docs/prod-schema-coverage-baseline.yaml` 随之清零 ⇒ **全平台 0 条建表缺口**（门禁 16 个带迁移模块全绿）。

### 真机验收（本地 PG16 容器）

| 项 | 结果 |
|---|---|
| `SPRING_PROFILES_ACTIVE=prod` + `DB_URL=…currentSchema=encaps_tenant` | Flyway 应用 **V1 → V2 → V3**，`now at version v3` |
| Hibernate `ddl-auto=validate` | **通过**（修前：`wrong column type … invite_codes.tenant_id` / `missing table [api_definition]`） |
| 应用启动 | `Started EncapsTenantApplication in 36.7s` |
| 健康探针 | `/actuator/health` **200**、`/api/v1/health` **200** |

### 过程中两个坑（已记入 PR/台账）

1. `gen-db-baseline.sh` 读的是本地仓（`E:\dev-data\maven\repository`）里的 encaps-layer **旧 jar**（#56 之前 `tenantId` 还是 bigint）⇒ 首轮产出的 DDL 把 `invite_codes.tenant_id` 写成 bigint、validate 继续失败。**须先 `mvn -pl platform/encaps-layer -am install` 再生成**。
2. 迁移文件打包在 **exec jar 内**，改完迁移必须重新 `mvn package`（否则测的还是旧 DDL）。

台账：#63 行补记 + 标题销账；变更日志加行。

author: matthewt1
body:
## Problem
Items that need a big batch of an ingredient (the Advanced Atmospheric/Space Engine Overclocks need 125 Advanced Processor, Uncommon Power System and similar) never get made. The machine sits in "missing ingredient" and the transfer units stay idle.

## Cause
Both request tests are `databank.hasKey(k) == 1`. In the current game build `hasKey` returns `true`/`false`, so the test is never true. The chef writes every request into `needed1` (each one overwrites the last) and the transfer units never read a request, they only clear the keys.

## Fix
A small helper `dbHas(k)` that accepts both answers (`true` or `1`) replaces the two `== 1` tests (transfer-unit `getStack`, chef `addNeed`). It also works on a build that still returns 1/0.

## What it improves
The "ask a transfer unit for an ingredient" path works at all. This is what made the Advanced overclocks impossible to build.

## How to check
In game, after a chef pass the databank holds distinct `needed1..n` keys (before: only `needed1`). The transfer units take them within seconds.

## Tested
- Offline, fake databank that answers true/false: three requests end up in three keys (before: one key, overwritten).
- In game (Settlers, 2026-10-10): 9 distinct requests written in one pass, all taken 6.5 s later, an Electronics M went Running on an Advanced Atmospheric Engine Overclock. That run also had the two fixes in the PRs that follow.

body:
## Summary
- `/dashboard/messages`' two-pane split switched at `md` (768px), the same breakpoint where the dashboard shell (`app/dashboard/layout.tsx`) becomes a sidebar+main row. At that exact width the thread column's real available space drops to ~94px -- under the EmptyState's own ~176px floor (icon + padding, even with zero text) -- and the Card's own `overflow-hidden` clips the overflow invisibly rather than scrolling the page, so this was invisible to a page-level scroll check and easy to miss by eye.
- Same class of defect as #349: an inner element switching layout at a breakpoint that doesn't reflect its true container width.
- Fix: move the split to `lg` (1024px), where there is genuinely room for two columns, in lockstep across the grid (`md:grid-cols-...` → `lg:grid-cols-...`), both panes' visibility/border classes, the EmptyState wrapper, and both mobile-only back buttons (`md:hidden` → `lg:hidden` -- these would otherwise be hidden exactly when they're still needed, between md and lg, stranding a user on the thread pane with no way back).
- Nothing about the approved design changes: the range that was broken simply gets the single-pane behavior the narrow range already had.

Found via a full-range (320-1440px, 8px steps) re-sweep of the authenticated web app, after an earlier admin-console finding (#358, `PageHeader`) proved that five-point breakpoint sampling can miss a content-dependent threshold entirely. The original 5-point sweep and #356's own list-pane fix both missed this because they were looking at the list pane while the thread pane was the one breaking.

## Stacked on #356 -- merge order matters, read before merging either
**This PR's base is `fix/messages-list-grid-overflow` (#356), not `main`.** Both PRs rewrite the same line of `apps/web/app/dashboard/messages/page.tsx`, incompatibly, if applied independently in either order:
- #356 adds `grid-cols-1` as the explicit base column count below `md` (its own fix for the list-pane overflow).
- This PR (as originally written) moved the breakpoint from `md` to `lg` but carried no base class at all, which would have **silently dropped #356's fix** and reintroduced its exact mechanism (an unconstrained implicit grid track) across a *wider* band than before -- 768-1023px, not just below 768px, because this PR also moves the single-pane cutoff up to `lg`.

Rebased this branch onto #356's tip (`git rebase --onto`, resolving the textual conflict by keeping both: `grid-cols-1 lg:grid-cols-[minmax(0,22rem)_1fr]`) and retargeted this PR's base accordingly, so the diff above is this PR's own incremental change only, and the owner can merge #356 first, then this one, without an ordering trap.

**Verified #356's defect is absent in the newly-expanded single-pane band (768-1023px), not assumed:** ran #356's own mocked long-subject-conversation assertion at 768/800/900/1000/1023px against the rebased code -- both truncating nodes constrained (`clientWidth < scrollWidth`) and page overflow clean at every one. Then ran a full 320-1440px @8px stepped sweep with the same mock: **zero broken widths**. #356's fix holds across the whole range this PR newly makes single-pane, not just at its own five original sample points.

## Test plan
- [x] New regression spec (`apps/web/e2e/authenticated-dashboard-geometry.local-only.spec.ts`) straddling the measured defect window (768, 800, 840px) plus clean points (375, 900, 1024, 1440px) -- confirmed RED at 768/800/840 and GREEN elsewhere pre-fix, GREEN everywhere post-fix.
- [x] Full 700-1100px stepped sweep (8px) post-fix: EmptyState only renders at >=1024px (as designed), zero overflow at any rendered width -- confirms the window closed rather than moved.
- [x] After the rebase: full combined spec file (both #356's and this PR's blocks) -- 42/42 passed locally.
- [x] After the rebase: #356's own long-subject assertion re-run at 768/800/900/1000/1023px plus a full 320-1440px @8px sweep -- zero broken widths, proving #356's fix survives the breakpoint move.
- [x] `pnpm turbo run typecheck --filter=@bmpl/web`: clean after the rebase.
- [x] `pnpm --filter @bmpl/web test`: 58 files / 396 tests passed after the rebase.

Local-only per the spec file's own header (needs a live API + seeded dev DB, not provisioned in apps/web's CI job) -- same shape as #356 and #358.

author: drawmeanelephant
body:
## Summary - **#19 — silent data loss on seekable stdout.** `File.stdout().writer()` builds a *positional* writer in Zig 0.17: drains are `pwrite`s at `pos = 0` that never touch the fd's shared offset, so output to a file at a nonzero offset (grouped `{ a; b; } > out`, `>>` appends, pre-existing content) landed at offset 0 and clobbered it. All stdout writers — `render`, `init`, `template --list`, and `printStdout` (`--help`/`--version`/`template `) — plus the init stderr writer now use `writerStreaming`, which honors the fd offset. - **#21 — undiagnosed stdout write failures.** `render`/`init`/`template --list` used to `catch return 1` silently, and `printStdout` let the raw error escape `main`, dumping `error: BrokenPipe` plus a stack trace. Every stdout write/flush failure now prints a one-line `dogbed: cannot write to stdout: ` on stderr via the new `stdoutErr` helper (the `File.Writer` keeps the real errno in `w.err`; the writer interface only surfaces `WriteFailed`) and exits 1. `printStdout` now returns the exit code instead of throwing, so nothing escapes `main`. ## Test plan - [x] `zig build` — clean - [x] `zig build test` — 40/40 pass, including two new regression tests: - *fd offset*: spawns the installed binary three times with stdout wired to one shared open file pre-seeded at a nonzero offset — asserts `kept\n` + both renders + `--version` land in order (pipes can't reproduce the clobber; a real shared fd can) - *EPIPE*: spawns `--version` and `render` with stdout connected to a pipe whose read end is already closed — asserts exit 1 and exactly `dogbed: cannot write to stdout: BrokenPipe\n` on stderr, no stack trace - [x] `sh docs/build.sh` — renders clean; `git status` shows no changes under `docs/site` - [x] Issue repro, before → after: - `{ dogbed render t.knap -d a.json; dogbed render t.knap -d b.json; } > combined.html`: **13 bytes (`

BBB

` only) → 26 bytes, both renders in order** - `dogbed render … > log.html` then `>> log.html`: **clobbered → appends** - `dogbed --version | true`: **`error: BrokenPipe` + ~15-frame stack trace → `dogbed: cannot write to stdout: BrokenPipe`, exit 1** Closes #19 Closes #21 Generated with [Devin](https://devin.ai)
