author: adamcohen8
body:
Installation previously required downloading the source ZIP and preparing Python separately; startup accepted an empty downloaded runtime inventory, and the desktop had no reviewed-save control. This provides an application-local evaluation installer, a verified download-first curl bootstrap, complete startup integrity checks, and explicit desktop approval of new copies.

The public-release workflow generates a **single command to paste into native Windows PowerShell from any folder**. It uses `curl.exe` to fetch a versioned bootstrap, hashes it through a held read-only sharing handle, and keeps that handle through ordinary file execution. The standalone bootstrap embeds source archive size/hash and source manifest pins, downloads only through HTTPS redirects, checks the complete extracted source before running the installer, and rechecks cached source before reuse. Internet-zone markers are preserved; no `Invoke-Expression`, policy change, unblock or bypass operation is used. The repository is now public at `adamcohen8/SILO`; anonymous installation still requires publishing versioned release assets. **There is no live anonymous installation URL yet.**

The local release builder reads an exact Git commit, includes bounded reviewed source, and excludes dirty/untracked files, Git history/author metadata, local settings, model weights and dependency binaries. It rejects unexpected tracked file categories, links/submodules and unsafe paths. Generation does not upload assets, create releases/tags, alter visibility or run downloaded software. The public distribution repository can differ from private development. Prepared assets include `install.ps1`, a source ZIP, metadata pins and `INSTALL.md` with the exact command.

`installer/Install-Evaluation.ps1` supplies application-local CPython 3.14.8 and 42 pinned Windows wheels, verifies inference assets and prepares separate host and contained-worker trees without pip/setup hooks. Shared-cache assets are rechecked in private staging. A complete payload manifest and mandatory native GPU/document/token/cleanup preflight gate publication and launch, with metadata-only failure-stage reporting. Offline caches, resumption, idempotent reuse, repair, rollback and a current-user shortcut are supported. Existing versions/documents/preferences are preserved. No driver, global Python/PATH, firewall or network-adapter change is performed.

Startup binds the complete committed inference lock to a canonical SHA-256, rejects empty/incomplete/changed inventories and undeclared runtime files, verifies the pinned model, and checks installed interpreter/dependency/source assets before starting Python. Mutable preferences/grants stay outside the immutable payload.

The desktop's **Review draft → Review changes → Save reviewed copy** dialog shows concrete source/destination locations, source hash, editable text and plain-text diff. Background review stores exact bytes; edits invalidate approval. Changed sources, revoked grants, destination collisions and replayed approval fail closed. The model has no approval operation, and existing files are never overwritten.

SILO (Super Intelligence for Local Offline Operations) now appears in the app and README with the owner-selected tagline, “Local intelligence. Contained by design.” The original vault-window robot artwork is preserved unchanged, packaged in a seven-size Windows icon, and used by the app and current-user desktop/Start menu shortcuts. Unrelated shortcuts are preserved; owned legacy shortcuts are retired after a SILO shortcut is saved. State directories, launcher filenames and the internal package name remain stable. Both branding assets are explicit bounded release inclusions and part of installed payload integrity verification. Documentation describes the connected host/process containment design and retains evaluation-only status.

Validation:

- **321 synthetic tests: 205 passed, 116 platform-dependent skips** on macOS. Nine new bootstrap tests cover exact committed snapshots, dirty/untracked exclusion, safe packaging, repeatable generation, no output replacement, actual curl command status/hash gates with a controlled download fixture, and standalone source/archive/cache verification with an inert installer. Native path/ACL/Internet-zone behavior is explicitly mocked in those bootstrap tests.
- All 42 real Windows wheels matched pinned sizes/hashes, satisfied Windows CP314 dependency requirements and passed actual safe vendoring; no Windows binaries were executed.
- PowerShell 7.6.6 on macOS parsed eight installer/test sources, rejected 11 unsafe paths, exercised four synthetic archive cases, denied wrong-digest bytes before extraction and extracted the pinned official Windows interpreter ZIP. Actual generated bootstrap and one-command syntax were also parsed. This does not establish native PowerShell 5.1, ACL, Internet-zone or signing behavior.
- Prepared release assets were independently hashed and the full committed source manifest verified. Assets remain local/unpublished. The 22 installer/bootstrap/desktop tests also passed after the branding edits, including actual Qt icon decoding and rejection of altered icon bytes. Python compilation and `git diff --check` passed; no hosted CI was dispatched.

**Native Windows curl/fresh install/repair/rollback and the CPython 3.14 configuration remain unqualified.** Earlier CPython 3.12 workstation evidence cannot qualify this configuration. Full isolation/network-change acceptance, signing, redistribution/licensing review and organizational CUI authorization remain pending; readiness stays false. Restrictive policy requiring signed downloaded scripts will block this unsigned evaluation until the approved signing/execution requirements are satisfied.

See [`docs/PUBLIC-BOOTSTRAP.md`](docs/PUBLIC-BOOTSTRAP.md) for download-first distribution and [`docs/EVALUATION-INSTALLER.md`](docs/EVALUATION-INSTALLER.md) for the manual/offline installer. The earlier inert `Install-LocalAI.ps1` staging workflow remains separate.

author: thiesgerken
body:
[Funes (Dev)] 

⚠️ **Depends on #319** (`llm.py`), which is merged into this branch. Merge after it.

## TLDR

Before running extraction on real sessions, we want to see what it would cost and iterate on the prompt. `scripts/memory_eval.py` renders archived sessions exactly like the extraction handler and prints input sizes plus the per-session cost spread. Only with an explicit flag does it send them to a model. One file, argparse, no framework.

## Usage

```
uv run python scripts/memory_eval.py data/sessions                       # dry run (default)
uv run python scripts/memory_eval.py --test-model path/to/conversation.json
uv run python scripts/memory_eval.py --call --model anthropic:claude-haiku-4-5 --limit 3 data/
```

- Input: archived `conversation.json` files or directories (searched recursively). Sandbox workspaces hold clones of the knowledge repo, so one session appears many times. Each session id is kept once, the copy with the latest `last_active`.
- Dry run: per session the event count, rendered chars, input tokens and estimated max cost (input + full 4,000-token output cap). Then the totals: median/p90/max of the upper bound, plus the input share alone (the realistic floor).
- `--call`: real calls through `run_structured` (one request, capped output), printing the extraction JSON, usage and cost. The model is resolved with pydantic-ai's `infer_model` (API key from the environment), deliberately not carapace's registry, since this is a dev tool.
- `--test-model`: the same call path against `TestModel` with a minimal valid `SessionExtraction`. The smoke test uses it.

## Decisions

- **No real calls without `--call`.** Thies decides on model and budget before any real session goes to a provider (Leonard).
- Archives carry no event timestamps, so the session's `created_at` stands in for the first user message as the session date. The handler uses the first user message in the user's timezone.
- **Session ids from the DB are not supported:** the archives cover the eval and keep the harness free of server wiring. It's easy to add if needed.

## First dry run (local data dir, no calls)

320 unique sessions (from 9,054 archive copies), 1 without a user message:

| model | input tokens total | median / max per session | upper bound total (median) | input share total (median) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| claude-haiku-4-5 | 1.78M | 3.1k / 70.9k | $8.16 ($0.023) | $1.78 ($0.003) |
| claude-sonnet-4-6 | 1.78M | 3.1k / 70.9k | $24.49 ($0.069) | $5.35 ($0.009) |

Real outputs should land far below the 4,000-token cap, so a full haiku backfill should cost roughly $2 to $4. The cap dominates the upper bound, which matters for the budget gate's reservations, not for actual spend.

## Tests

`tests/test_memory_eval.py` runs the script as a subprocess: a dry run (dedup picks the newer copy, the empty session is skipped, no calls) and `--test-model` (extraction printed with usage).

author: enzoitaliano
body:
# Pull Request

## Description

Follow-up to #2189 for #2184. #2189 limited the SIGUSR2 hot-reload to Waybar's main process, which stops the other processes in the bar's unit from being killed. But fast layout switching still breaks the bar on current dev. On dev @ e3e45069 (includes #2189), switching `hyprdots/01` ↔ `macos` twice with `hyde-shell waybar --set`, 0.5 s apart, **failed in 4 of 4 runs**:

```
waybar[1472]: [info] Reloading...
waybar[1472]: [error] Error parsing JSON: * Line 1, Column 1
waybar[1472]:   Syntax error: value, object or array expected.
hyde-Hyprland-bar.service: Main process exited, code=exited, status=1/FAILURE
...
hyde-Hyprland-bar.service: Main process exited, code=killed, status=12/USR2
...
hyde-Hyprland-bar.service: Failed with result 'start-limit-hit'.
```

The causes that remain after #2189:

1. **Each switch reloads twice.** `--set`, `--next`, `--prev`, `--select-layout` and a theme's layout preset refresh the files and reload Waybar in `_apply_layout()`. Then `main()` falls through to the default path, which rewrites `includes.json`, `global.css` and `style.css` and reloads again about 20 ms later. The journal shows two `Sent signal SIGUSR2` per switch.
2. **Files are written in place.** The second round of writes empties the files while Waybar is still reading them after the first reload, which is the `Line 1, Column 1` above.
3. **SIGUSR2 can kill Waybar itself.** A Waybar started a moment earlier gets the signal before it has installed its handler and dies (`status=12/USR2`). `--kill-who=main` can't help, because Waybar is the main process.
4. A few failures in a row hit systemd's start limit, and the bar stays gone.

Changes (all in `Configs/.local/lib/hyde/waybar.py`):

- **`restart_waybar()`:** with systemd, runs `systemctl --user reset-failed` and then `systemctl --user restart` on the unit, and falls back to `run_waybar()` if the restart fails (the transient unit may have been collected, see #2160). systemd serializes overlapping restarts, and `reset-failed` keeps fast switching from hitting the start limit. Without systemd, the SIGUSR2 reload is unchanged.
- **`_atomic_write()` / `_atomic_copy()`:** write to a temp file in the same directory, then `os.replace()` it into place. They keep the old file's mode and write through a symlinked config (dotfiles managers). All live writes Waybar reads now go through them: `config.jsonc`, `style.css`, `includes.json`, `global.css`, `border-radius.css` and the initial `user-style.css`. The layout backup copy and `staterc` are unchanged.
- **One refresh and restart per switch:** `main()` skips its default refresh and restart when `_apply_layout()` already did both. With `--style`, it still runs, so `--set X --style Y` behaves as before.

`_signal_waybar()` from #2189 is kept; `--hide` (SIGUSR1) still uses it.

Fixes #2184

**Depends on / related:**
- Tests: HyDE-Project/tests#39 adds `test_waybar_restart.sh`, which covers the restart path, the atomic writes and the single restart per `--set`. It fails on current dev and passes with this PR.
- HyDE-Project/tests#36 (open) asserts in case 5 that `restart_waybar()` sends SIGUSR2 under systemd. That case will fail with this PR by design. If #36 is merged first, its case 5 needs the same update as in tests#39. I can send that change.

## Type of change

- [x] **Bug fix** (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)
- [ ] **New feature** (non-breaking change which adds functionality)
- [ ] **Breaking change** (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to not work as expected)
- [ ] **Documentation update** (non-breaking change; modified files are limited to the documentations)
- [ ] **Technical debt** (a code change that does not fix a bug or add a feature but makes something clearer for devs)
- [ ] **Other** (provide details below)

## Checklist

- [x] I have read the [CONTRIBUTING](https://github.com/HyDE-Project/HyDE/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md) document.
- [x] My code follows the code style of this project.
- [x] My commit message follows the [commit guidelines](https://github.com/HyDE-Project/HyDE/blob/master/COMMIT_MESSAGE_GUIDELINES.md).
- [ ] My change requires a change to the documentation.
- [ ] I have updated the documentation accordingly.
- [x] I have added a changelog entry.
- [x] I have added necessary comments/documentation to my code.
- [x] I have added tests to cover my changes. (in HyDE-Project/tests#39)
- [x] I have tested my code locally and it works as expected.
- [ ] All new and existing tests passed. (`sh tests/run.sh`: 59 cases, 1 failed, `test_binds`. It fails the same way on dev @ e3e45069 without this PR: `key_binds.lua:54: attempt to call a nil value (field 'exec')`, from #2192.)

## Testing

Same scenarios on dev @ e3e45069 and on this branch. After each run I checked `systemctl --user is-active`, `NRestarts`, the waybar layer on each monitor in `hyprctl layers`, the journal and `coredumpctl`.

| Scenario | dev (with #2189) | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| Fast switching, 2 rounds, 0.5 s apart | 4 of 4 runs failed (exit 1 on empty JSON, `status=12/USR2`, one `start-limit-hit` with no bar) | 7 of 7 runs clean (3 with the final commit) |
| Overlapping `--set` (two at once) | — | clean |
| `--set`, `--next`, `--prev`, no args, `--update` | 2 SIGUSR2 per `--set` | 1 restart each |
| Bar visible afterwards (`hyprctl layers`) | gone after `start-limit-hit` | on both monitors every time |
| Waybar memory | — | 57–73 MB |

On the "hiding bug" the hot-reload was added for (#1755): I checked `hyprctl layers` after every switch, on two monitors, and never saw an active but invisible bar.

**Clean install (HydeVM, dev @ e3e45069, one virtual monitor):**

| Scenario | dev (with #2189) | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| Single, fast ×3, overlapping `--set` | no crash, but memory grows with every reload: 71.6 → 81.8 MB over 5 runs | clean, memory flat at ~63 MB |
| 20 back-to-back switches (no pause) | Waybar aborted in its reload handler: `Fatal glibc error: pthread_mutex_lock.c:426 ... assertion failed`, `status=6/ABRT`, coredump, restarted by systemd | 20 switches → exactly 20 starts, 0 restarts by systemd, bar on screen, ~63 MB |
| Caffeine on, then a layout switch | — | still on; its `systemd-inhibit` survives the restart (own scope) |
| Theme change (`theme.switch.sh -n`) | — | 1 restart, bar on screen |
| Wallpaper change (`wallpaper.sh -n`) | — | bar untouched |

Machine: CachyOS, Hyprland 0.56.2, Waybar 0.15.0, amdgpu, two 1920x1080 monitors.

## Additional context

The non-systemd path still hot-reloads with SIGUSR2, to keep this PR focused. It has the same race but no cgroup, and I can't test it here.

  * Configuration and style updates are applied more safely, reducing the chance of incomplete files.

body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"PierreZ"} -->
_Requested by **Pierre** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01DS2jy7NSy5EfL5kQq5bWCJ?thread=cmsg_01DS2jy7NSy5EfL5kQq5bWCJLo5XQQS6bDyZqNdWyvs1fu)_

Closes #340 (trim-point jump mutation survivors).

Before: the mutation hunt's 300 seeds meet only 4 trim-point jumps (`Message::TrimmedTo`). The journal truncates little in the chaos window, and the attrition brings a node back fast. The `raise_next_slot` mutant is caught on one of those 4 jumps.

After: a per-seed **lagging-acceptor scenario** holds one acceptor down until a peer's floor passes the chosen prefix it holds, and every client compacts at every truncation step. The node then boots below every floor and jumps, with its allocator frontier far below the point.

How: `shape::lagging_acceptor` draws the scenario (never on a departed-straggler or bare-quorum seed). `world::lagging_acceptor` crashes one acceptor 0.8–2 s into the chaos window, once no budgeted commit is in flight on it (#332). It restarts the acceptor when `AuditWorld::floor_passed` says a peer's durable floor passed it, or at the latest `LATE_WINDOW` into the tail, like the silent machine (#211) and the late outage. `ChainWorkload` sets `compaction`, `compact_every = 1` and the `TRUNCATE` weight ceiling on a scenario seed. Only harness code changes. AGENTS.md records the new tail exception next to the other two.

## The three mutants, applied by hand at seeds `1..=300`

- `RepairProbe::blocked -> {0}`: caught in seeds 181..=200 ("a slot learned chosen leaves the repair probe"). The harness changed since #334 (first mutation run).
- `Proposer::raise_next_slot -> ()`: caught in seeds 1..=20 ("a trim-point jump carries the allocator past the dropped prefix").
- `Proposer::probe_retain_from -> ()`: survives. No seed meets a leader whose repair probe is blocked below a trim point. That needs a split floor, a faulty quorum and an outage in the tail. Follow-up: #409 (repair probe blocked below a trim point).

## Two harness fixes the hunts found

- The impatient re-send of an ambiguous write had no deadline. A node parks the duplicate until its slot is decided. The client that sent it can hold the static-stability crash (#247 (static stability)) of the grid column member that the slot needs, so the step waited to the cutoff and decided slots stayed unapplied. The re-send now stops after the request timeout (`chain_workload/write.rs`).
- The gate "system: a message from a not-yet-folded node is refused and later accepted" fired on about 3 in 1,000 seeds, so one sweep missed it. On a lagging-fold seed (#189 (node registry)) a client now registers at the ceiling weight, asks again a reconfiguration onto the joiner that no leader took, and reboots every member of one that started: 35 in 3,000 seeds, from 5 in 1,600.

A sweep also met a `cell_exists` refusal of `init`: a defect in shipped code (`paros::client::initialize`), filed as #413 (init stops at a founder admitted into its own cell).

## Validation

- Jumps in seeds `1..=300`: 4 without the scenario, 7 with it.
- `sim-paros-hunt main 2000`: 2000 ok, no violations. `canary 300`: no violations.
- CI green on the head.

Triage recorded in `docs/analysis/simulation/mutation-triage.md`.

author: ctc-kernel
body:
## Problem

FIM ignored any path that merely contained the word "sentinel". `is_ignored_path` tested `dir/**` patterns as substrings, and the self-exclusion `sentinel/**` is re-applied to every policy, so it meant "path contains `sentinel`" instead of "inside a directory named `sentinel`".

Observed on Ubuntu 24.04 with `/etc` watched: `/etc/sentinel-e2e-dropper.conf` and `/etc/hosts.sentinel-test` produced no FIM alert and no playbook trigger. An attacker could evade FIM, the YARA scan and playbooks with a name such as `/etc/cron.d/sentinel-update`.

## Fix

- **`dir/**`** matches only the content of a directory with exactly that name (whole path components, still case-insensitive, separators normalised). A *file* named `sentinel` stays monitored.
- **Plain patterns** had the same over-matching. They now name a file or directory instead of any path containing the text. An empty pattern used to match every path and now matches nothing.
- **`*suffix`** is unchanged.
- **Baseline** had its own copy of the substring matcher; it now shares the watcher's.
- **`SELF_EXCLUSION_PATTERNS`** lists the agent's directories by exact name. The substring match was covering several by accident, now added explicitly: the macOS fallback log directory, the temp fallback `sentinel-logs`, the GUI preferences directories and the three launchd log files under `/var/log`. `Sentinel/**` is dropped as redundant with case-insensitive matching.

## Behaviour changes to review

- `/usr/bin/sentinel-agent`, the systemd unit, the logrotate and AppArmor files and the macOS LaunchDaemon plist were only excluded by the bug. They are now monitored like any other file.
- A custom plain pattern that relied on substring matching (e.g. `.swp` instead of `*.swp`) no longer matches and will produce more alerts.

## Not addressed

- Exclusion is still by directory name, not by the agent's resolved directories. A *directory* named exactly `sentinel`, `sentinel-grc`, `SentinelGRC`, etc. under a watched tree is still unmonitored, including its creation.
- A data directory relocated with `SENTINEL_DATA_DIR` to a path without those names is not self-excluded (already the case before).

## Testing

- `cargo test -p agent-fim` and `cargo test -p agent-common` pass; clippy and fmt clean on both crates.
- The six new tests fail against the previous substring logic.
- Manual run through the real watcher on macOS with the default policy: alerts for `sentinel-e2e-dropper.conf`, `hosts.sentinel-test`, `cron.d/sentinel-update` and a file named `sentinel`; none for `sentinel/agent.json` or `sentinel/agent.db`.
- Not run on Linux or Windows. Windows paths, including the `\\?\` prefix, are covered by string-level unit tests only.

- **Public header (owner feedback A):** the header holds only the logo, Find Jobs, How CHARA Works, and Log in / Sign up (or Go to my area / Log out). The top bar keeps the account menu. Content uses a container up to 75 rem. Below 1024 px the existing menus are unchanged. The admin console uses the same layout.

author: zooldoo
body:
## What

FA's multifunction panel has a team-colour button: in retail, pressing it recolours every identified unit's strategic icon by how its army stands to the player's — your own in royal blue, allies dark green, enemies red, neutrals goldenrod — on the world view and on the minimap. Here the button raised a Lua error (`TeamColorMode` wasn't bound) and the icons kept their army colours. FAF's version of the button, and its "enable at start" option, call it too.

## Why

- **Moho's rule:** `TeamColorMode(bool)` (faf-re `cfunc_TeamColorModeL`) sets the session's `mTeamColorMode`; a non-boolean is a type error. `RenderUnitIcon` reads it: with the mode on and a focus army, an identified unit's icon takes `GameColors.TeamColorMode.Self` if it is the focus army's, else `Neutral`, `Ally` or `Enemy` by the focus army's alliance with the unit's army; without it, its army's colour. The four colours are read once from `GameColors.lua` (`StrategicIconAux`'s constructor). Blips keep `UnidentifiedColor`; nothing else reads the flag, so meshes and lifebars keep their army colours.
- **Retail Lua:** `/lua/ui/game/multifunction.lua` (the `teamcolor` button's `OnCheck`: `TeamColorMode(checked)`), `/lua/GameColors.lua` (`TeamColorMode = {Self, Enemy, Ally, Neutral}`).
- **FAF:** its exe also takes a string of per-army colours, `"aarrggbb,aarrggbb,..."` in army order, and colours each army's icons by its entry (FA-Binary-Patches `section/TeamColorMode.cpp`); FAF's `multifunction.lua` passes `calculateTeamColors()` and then `true`.
- **The engine** didn't bind `TeamColorMode`, and the snapshot's army record carried its allies but not its enemies, so the renderer couldn't tell an enemy from a neutral.

## Change

- **`TeamColorMode`** is bound: a bool sets the mode, a string sets FAF's per-army palette, anything else is a type error; the argument count is checked as Moho's is. A new map starts with the mode off and no palette.
- **`GameColors`** reads `TeamColorMode`'s four colours (retail's values by default).
- **The strategic icons** of identified units take the focus army's Self, Ally, Enemy or Neutral colour with the mode on, or the palette's entry for their army once FAF has given one; blips, maybe-dead darkening and badges are as before. The minimap's icons go through the same pass.
- **The snapshot's army record** carries an `enemies` mask beside `allies`.

## Tests

- **`--strategic-icon-test`** (gate), four new checks: with the mode on, the player's tank shows Self, a seen enemy tank Enemy, a never-seen blip stays unidentified, and the minimap's tank shows Self; after `SetAlliance` the same tank shows Neutral, then Ally; FAF's palette colours both armies' icons by index; with the mode off, the army colours are back. Without the change the first three fail.
- **Catch2** `TeamColorMode sets the session's mode and FAF's string its palette`: a bool sets and clears the mode, FAF's string fills the palette in order, a number and no argument are errors. Without the binding it fails at the first call.
- **Full suite:** data-free tests pass on GCC, Clang and ASan; the data tests pass.
- **Gates:** clang-tidy, formatting clean on changed lines, `-Werror`.

author: dlrivada
body:
Refs #751 (Phase 5 of 8), Fixes #2106

## Summary
- **Decision audit health, no write probe.** New `ABACDecisionAuditHealthState` singleton updated by the PEP after every audited write (including unbuildable records and caller cancellation). `ABACHealthCheck` adds an audit step when `DecisionAudit.Enabled`; the worse of engine and audit status wins. Unhealthy: no `IOperationAuditStore`, or a failed write within `HealthFailureWindow` (new option, default 5 min, validated > 0) under FailClosed. Degraded: BestEffort, an older failure, or `InMemoryOperationAuditStore`. Result data holds only `decision_audit` = ok | no_store | write_failed | in_memory_store; exceptions by type name only.
- **Transaction isolation proven** on real SQL Server (`EFCore-SqlServer`): a deny row survives rollback of the outer EF Core transaction and of an ambient `TransactionScope`.
- **#2106 one core tenancy marker.** `DeadLetterManager` and `QueryCacheInterceptor` now use `MultiTenancyMarker`; `Encina.Messaging.Tenancy.TenancyInUse` is deleted. An application with its own tenant provider and no `AddEncinaTenancy` registers `MultiTenancyMarker` itself (changelog fragment). DI tests (`ValidateOnBuild` + `ValidateScopes`): one marker even when called twice, both consumers deny without a tenant, single-tenant without tenancy, app-registered marker honoured.

body:
🛡️ Sentinel Security Fix:
- **Severity**: MEDIUM
- **Vulnerability**: Incomplete numeric input validation in `sanitizeFeedbackItem`
- **Impact**: Untrusted `localStorage` or `BroadcastChannel` events with `overallScore: Infinity` or out-of-bounds numbers bypassed sanitization, leading to metric corruption (e.g. `avgRating` becoming `Infinity` or `NaN`).
- **Fix**: Updated `sanitizeFeedbackItem` to check `Number.isFinite(fb.overallScore)` and enforce bounds `1 <= overallScore <= 5`. If invalid, it safely recomputes `overallScore` as the average of the sanitized individual ratings (`food`, `service`, `ambiance`).
- **Verification**: Verified using `pnpm lint` and `pnpm build`.

author: joaodobread
body:
## O que muda e por quê

### Máxima lê TODOS os arquivos de código
- Sem limite de arquivos, de tamanho, de chamadas por arquivo, de chamadas no total nem de locais por conexão (`SCAN_MAX`).
- Usa `allCodeFiles`: todo arquivo de código (inclui `scripts/`, `migrations/`, `generated/`…; ficam fora só testes,
  mocks/fixtures e dependências/builds). Mais extensões (jsx, vue, svelte, rs, scala, swift, dart, ex…).
- Repositórios muito grandes: quando a API do GitHub corta a árvore recursiva (`truncated`), percorre pasta por pasta.

### Retomar depois de uma falha
Com tudo sem limite a análise pode levar horas; agora uma falha não perde o trabalho.
- **Checkpoint** por repositório (**migração 5**, `introspection_checkpoints`, mesmo sha + profundidade): resultado da análise
  pelo LLM, arquivos lidos + chamadas/rotas encontradas (a cada 50 arquivos) e cada lote do LLM já respondido.
- Falhou: status de erro com **onde parou** ("Parou na etapa "mapeamento pelo LLM" (12/40): …") e o botão **Retomar**
  (linha da tabela e painel) continua do ponto salvo — não relê o código nem repete lotes.
- Erros transitórios do LLM (429, 5xx, sobrecarga, timeout, rede) são repetidos 3x com espera (2s, 8s, 20s).
- Na máxima, falha do LLM **interrompe** (para retomar) em vez de cair silenciosamente na heurística.
- Forçar ou commit novo descartam o checkpoint e recomeçam.

### Correções encontradas no caminho
- Varredura: a regra "não repetir chamada em linhas seguidas" descartava chamadas a 2 linhas de distância (comparava linha
  1-based com índice 0-based).

author: ndekocode
body: ## What `isActive` and `isArchived` are declared `nullable: true` on `BaseEntity`, with defaults that only apply on insert. A row in `organization_team_employee` or `organization_project_employee` can therefore hold `NULL` in those columns: rows created before the columns existed, imported rows, and rows written by a raw migration. `ManagedEmployeeService` matched memberships with strict equality: ```ts isManager: true, isActive: true, isArchived: false, ``` `NULL = true` is not true in SQL, so these rows were skipped. A real team or project manager on such a row: - got a 404 or 400 when editing, deleting or removing tasks from a member's daily plan (`canManageEmployee`) - was refused when reading or deleting a member's time logs (`canManageEmployees`) - saw only their own numbers in statistics and custom tracking (`filterAccessibleEmployeeIds`) A member on a `NULL` row was also left out of what their manager could see. `isMemberOfTeam` in the same file already used the tolerant predicate, so the service gave inconsistent answers for the same row. ### A manager of one team could read the members of every requested team `filterAccessibleEmployeeIds` asked whether the caller manages at least one of the requested teams or projects, then returned the members of all of them: ```ts const isManager = await this.isManagerOfTeamsOrProjects(currentEmployeeId, teamIds, projectIds); if (isManager) { const managedEmployeeIds = await this.getMembersOfTeamsAndProjects(teamIds, projectIds); ``` So a manager of team A who also named team B in the same request got B's members too. And when none of the requested employee ids belonged to a managed team, the filter returned `[]`, which the callers read as "no employee filter". ## How A small helper in `managed-employee.service.ts` builds the predicate that `isMemberOfTeam` already used: ```ts const activeMembershipWhere = () => ({ isActive: Or(IsNull(), Equal(true)), isArchived: Or(IsNull(), Equal(false)) }); ``` It replaces the strict flags in the eight membership queries: - `isManagerOfTeamsOrProjects` (team and project) - `canManageEmployee` (manager row and target row) - `canManageEmployeeInAnyTeam` (managed teams and target row) - `getMembersOfTeamsAndProjects` (team and project) `isMemberOfTeam` now uses the helper too. The helper builds a new object for every query because TypeORM can transform a `FindOperator` value in place. The generated SQL is `col IS NULL OR col = ?`, which behaves the same on PostgreSQL, MySQL and SQLite. The existing spec `managed-employee.service.any-team.spec.ts` asserts the full where clause on purpose, so its two expectations now use the new operators. For the second defect, `filterAccessibleEmployeeIds` first keeps the requested teams and projects the caller manages (`getManagedTeamsAndProjects`, same membership predicate), then returns the members of those only. A selection that leaves nobody returns `NO_ACCESSIBLE_EMPLOYEE_ID`, the id that matches nothing, instead of an empty list. ## Why it does not break anything else - No new kind of access. Rows explicitly set to `isActive = false` or `isArchived = true` are still excluded, and `isManager` is still strictly `true`. No code path deactivates a membership by writing `NULL`. - The narrowing only removes access. A caller who manages every requested team sees the same members as before. Ever Teams sends every team of the user in its activity report request (`use-activity-filters.ts`), so a manager of team A who is a plain member of team B now sees A's members and no longer B's. Callers with `CHANGE_SELECTED_EMPLOYEE` and `onlyMe` requests are unchanged. - `isManagerOfTeamsOrProjects` keeps its any-of meaning: its last caller is `ManagerOrPermissionGuard`, which is mounted on no route and is removed by ever-co/ever-gauzy#10500. - Callers checked: `DailyPlanService` (update, delete, `removeTaskFromManyPlans`, team read), `TimeLogService` (four checks), `StatisticService`, `CustomTrackingService` and `ManagerOrPermissionGuard`. Signatures and return types are unchanged. - No schema, DTO, route or contracts change, so the API clients are unaffected. - `canViewEmployeeProfile` is left as is. It is a deliberately strict check that also verifies the team's own flags, and it has its own spec. - Recognising project managers in `canManageEmployee` is not part of this change. It would give project managers write access to members' daily plans and time logs, which needs a product decision first. --- ## Summary by cubic Fixes `ManagedEmployeeService` so team and project managers are recognised even when their membership rows hold `NULL` in `isActive` or `isArchived`, and scopes statistics reads to only the teams and projects a manager actually manages. - Reuses the tolerant predicate `isMemberOfTeam` via a shared `activeMembershipWhere` helper across all eight membership queries. - `filterAccessibleEmployeeIds` no longer returns members of every team or project in a request just because the caller manages one of them; it now keeps only the ones the caller manages. - An empty result returns `NO_ACCESSIBLE_EMPLOYEE_ID` instead of an empty list, which callers would otherwise read as "no employee filter". - Explicitly deactivated or archived rows stay excluded; no new access is granted and no API or schema changes are made. Written for commit 1247534554c2d791ca9bd8d4e538da0df9e4bf8c. Summary will update on new commits.

author: couchriv
body:
### What

```text
AGC graphics: f16 rounding: vector 0 (0x00000000, 0x00000401, 0x000003ff) v_add_f16 is 0xabcd0800, expected 0xabcd0401
```

On `main`, scalar f16 add/mul/sub ignore `FLOAT_MODE` f16 denormal bits and keep denormals the hardware flushes. `float16Binary` now flushes inputs when denorm16 bit 0 is clear and results when bit 1 is clear (nearest-even, known float mode). Multiply checks tininess after rounding to 11 significant bits (`0x387ff000`); add/sub use `0x38800000`. `v_sub_f16` / `v_subrev_f16` share the same helper. Unknown float mode and other rounding modes stay as on `main`. NaN payload selection is unchanged (still driver-dependent).

### Tested

CachyOS Linux; RTX 4070 Ti (NVIDIA), Radeon 610M (RADV / gfx1036 hw-oracle), lavapipe (CI ICD).

- Replay of 1156 non-NaN-input operand pairs per mode (denorm16 = 0, 1, 2; ieee 1) through the recompiler on RTX 4070 Ti (NVIDIA), Radeon 610M (RADV) and lavapipe, against gfx1036 on the hardware oracle: v_add_f16 / v_mul_f16 rows that differed from hardware went from 800 to 0 on RADV and lavapipe with no regression on any of the 1681 rows; v_sub_f16 / v_subrev_f16 from 380 to 0. On NVIDIA 760 and 380 are fixed; the remaining 70 and 12 rows are NaN payloads (`7fff` vs hardware `fe00`), and 40 of the 70 (denormal x infinity in v_mul_f16) moved from an infinity to that NaN.
- `agc_driver_float16_rounding` (add and mul only) fails on main with the line above and passes on the branch on all three drivers.
- Live tininess on gfx1036: with denorm16 = 1 (output flush), `0x3bff*0x0400` → `0`, `0x3c01*0x03ff` → `0x0400` (after-rounding at threshold `0x387ff000`).
- `check_conventions.py --base origin/main`; `git diff --check`.

Not tested here: Windows, packed f16, ternary f16, directed `round16` ≠ 0. Sub and subrev are covered by the replay above, not by `agc_driver_float16_rounding`.

body:
## What this adds
A search control above the scatterplot (upper right on desktop, full width on phones) for finding and highlighting one or more schools.

- **Search:** focusing the empty box lists all 1,723 plotted schools alphabetically. Typing filters immediately by case-insensitive substring on the school name **or** the district name. Results are sorted by school, then district, and show both names. No matches shows "No matching schools".
- **Select several:** clicking a result (or pressing Enter) toggles it. The query and dropdown stay put so several schools can be picked in a row. Selections are tracked by the school's unique id (district number, district type and school number), never by name or position. The data has 33 repeated school names and 7 schools sharing a position with another.
- **Chips:** each selected school appears as a removable chip with a "N schools selected" count. The district is shown on the chip when the school name is not unique. Chips wrap and, past about three rows, scroll inside their own area, so the chart is never pushed off-screen.
- **Highlight:** while anything is selected, unselected dots fade and selected dots are drawn on top at full strength. Positions, sizes, tooltips, the 90% line and band, and the "≥90%" FRP treatment are unchanged. Clearing the selection restores every dot.
- **Clear all:** clears the selection and the query and closes the dropdown. It is disabled when there is nothing to clear.
- **Keyboard and screen readers:** Arrow Up/Down move through results (scrolling only the list, never the page), Enter toggles, Escape closes without clearing anything. Chip remove buttons are focusable and labelled ("Remove School, District"). The combobox and listbox use ARIA roles.

No changes to data, the build script, calculations, counts or exclusions.

## Files
- `site/search.js` (new): the filter and sort rules, with no page access, so they can be unit-tested.
- `site/app.js`: search control behavior and `applySelection()`. The chart's only change is two lines that re-apply the selection after a redraw (for example, on resize).
- `site/index.html`: search control markup, plus loading `search.js`.
- `site/style.css`: search, dropdown, chip and fade styles, using the existing light/dark color tokens.
- `tests/test_search.mjs` (new): 6 unit tests using Node's built-in runner, with nothing to install.
- `README.md`: adds the new test command.

## Testing
- `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests`: 5/5 pass, so the data is unchanged.
- `node --test tests/test_search.mjs`: 6/6 pass.
- Headless Chromium end-to-end run against the real page, all passing:
  - The focus list, case-insensitive school and district matching, and the empty message.
  - Select, multi-select, toggle-off, and keeping selections across query changes and closing.
  - Single-chip removal and Clear all.
  - Arrow keys, Enter and Escape without page scroll; chips reachable by keyboard.
  - Tooltip and "≥90%" behavior; identical-coordinate schools highlighted independently.
  - Unchanged counts and dot positions; no page errors.
- 30 schools selected by touch at 375 px wide in light and dark mode, and by mouse on desktop in dark mode: no horizontal overflow.
- Not tested: Safari/WebKit and real assistive technology such as VoiceOver.

author: iwyoo
body:
Closes #1921

Checked Blue Book rules: P-62.5 (class term oxide for one amine oxide, method 2 prefix for an oxide on a substituent nitrogen), P-44.1.2.2 (a ring parent outranks a chain), P-62.2.2 (N-substituted amines).

- A saturated ring nitrogen oxide beside a chain oxide: the multi-oxide namer names the contracted molecule with the polyfunctional ring route when the generic namer declines a ring parent.
- An aromatic ring nitrogen oxide beside a chain oxide: the charged atoms of an amine oxide on a non-ring nitrogen are cited as the prefix by the substituent engine, so they no longer stop the ring N-oxide route.

So [O-][N+]1(C)CCCCC1CC[N+](C)(C)[O-] is 2-{2-[dimethyl(oxo)-λ5-azanyl]ethyl}-1-methylpiperidine 1-oxide and [O-][n+]1ccccc1CC[N+](C)(C)[O-] is 2-{2-[dimethyl(oxo)-λ5-azanyl]ethyl}pyridine 1-oxide; single-oxide rings keep their names.

Test plan: fast set and the slow tests of the touched test files pass.

_Requested by **Erik** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01KzG9voPzhAGxpxt4doP1QN?thread=cmsg_01KzG9voPzhAGxpxt4doP1QNNWPMraDc3YsJez3N1Vi8nV)_

Before: rolling a cairn cluster to a new version meant running `clan machines update` per machine by hand, following the runbook's order and health checks yourself.

After: `nix run .#cairn-upgrade` in a consumer flake walks the cluster one machine at a time. It takes an etcd snapshot first. Before touching each machine it refuses to continue if any *other* etcd member or apiserver is unhealthy. It then cordons and drains schedulable machines, runs `clan machines update`, and waits for that machine's etcd member, `/readyz` and node Ready at the pinned minor. Control-plane machines go first, ordered by VIP priority, then workers.

This replaces #107, which was closed because the logic didn't belong in bash.

How:
- `flakeModules/cluster/plan.nix` (unchanged from #107) emits `cairn-upgrade-plan.<cluster>` from the same evaluated `cairn.clusters` value the machines are built from.
- `pkgs/upgrade/` is a Go module built with `buildGoModule`. It talks to the cluster through client-go, etcd's client and kubectl's drain library. It execs only `nix eval` (the plan), `clan` (the deploy) and `ssh` (`--rollback`).
- The rollout loop depends on two interfaces, `Cluster` and `Deployer`. The tests fake both to cover ordering, the quorum guard, uncordon on a failed drain, and post-gate timeouts. `nodeReady`, cordon and drain are tested against client-go's fake clientset. I also ran the etcd health, snapshot and `/readyz` paths once against a local TLS etcd and apiserver stub; that test isn't committed.
- `checks/flake-module.nix` asserts the plan's order and runs `--dry-run` against `examples/ha-cluster`. That build also runs the Go tests.
- `gofmt` is added to treefmt.

A Renovate bump to `pkgs/upgrade/go.mod` will need `vendorHash` in `pkgs/upgrade/default.nix` updated to match. AGENTS.md notes this.

author: rmakowiecki
body:
## Why

The Session Summary showed its result as a static screen, so finishing a session had no payoff and a Level-up was never visible. Builds on #164.

## What

**Behavior**
- **XP reveal**: when the score arrives, the XP lines appear one at a time under a total that counts up, or down for a loss. Confetti bursts from the total when it is positive.
- **Level card and pour**: the Level card drops in at the User's real starting position, and the earned XP pours into its bar. Every Level crossed fills the bar, resets it and pulses the Level number. Middle Levels show only the bar and the number. The pour stays within about 2.5 seconds.
- **Sheet and app bar**: the sheet rises and the app bar's title and close button fade in. During the sequence the app bar holds only a Skip button.
- **Skip**: Skip, a tap anywhere or the first system back jumps to the end. Confetti already in flight finishes.
- **Settled order**: the settled stack is now Level card, headline, total, stat pills. The total starts under the app bar and is pushed down by the card.
- **Direct and accessible paths**: a restore, rotation, an unavailable score or disabled system animations show the settled screen with no sequence. TalkBack gets one polite announcement of the total and any Level-up once settled.

**Implementation**
- **`SummaryPayoff`**: holds the animated values and runs the timeline from a `LaunchedEffect`. It is presentation-only and changes no screen state. A `rememberSaveable` flag keeps it from replaying.
- **`planPour`**: a pure function turns the before and after Level positions into pour segments, applying the duration floors and the cap. The timing constants live in `SummaryTimeline.kt`.
- **`SummaryXpTiles` and `SummaryConfetti`**: the tile list scrolls to keep the newest tile in view and goes compact above six lines. Confetti is one non-interactive canvas with 34 deterministic particles.
- **`core:ui`**: `FlashcardsLevelCard`, `FlashcardsXpBreakdownRow` and `FlashcardsGradientTopBar` each gain defaulted parameters, so other callers are unchanged. New `rememberAnimationsEnabled()`.
- **Docs**: `SYSTEMDESIGN.md` and `xp-leveling-system.md` describe the sequence as built.

## Edge cases handled

- Zero XP lines: no tiles and no confetti, the card drops in and the screen settles.
- Negative total: the counter and bar count down within the same Level, with no confetti.
- Level-up exactly to the boundary: the new Level starts on an empty bar with no extra wait.
- More Levels than fit the cap: middle segments shrink to 80ms first, then the first and last segments to their 520ms floor.
- Score arrives late: the spinner shows, then the sequence starts once, never restarts.
- Skip before the burst: no confetti.
- Rotation or process restore mid-sequence: settled, with no replay.

## Testing

- New `SummaryPourPlanTest` covers no crossing, a loss, a single and multiple Level-ups, the cap and floors, the boundary case and a missing threshold.

author: steimerbyte
body:
Fixes image attachments that overflow the request body

Attaching several full-resolution photos in one message failed with a bare `413` and no explanation. There are two independent causes, and this addresses both.

## Cause 1 — the client never resized anything

`ChatInput.tsx` read each picked file into a data URL at full resolution, so a 12 MP phone photo contributed ~3 MB to the request. Three of them are 8.1 MB of JPEG but **11.2 MB once base64-encoded** — and base64 is what the transport actually counts.

The CLI never had this problem: the harness normalizes its own attachments to a 2048 px longest side before sending. The browser path had no equivalent, which is why the same files worked in the terminal and not in chat.

`ChatInput` now downscales attachments before they go on the wire, targeting a 2048 px longest edge and 2 MB per image — the same normalization the CLI applies, so both surfaces send comparable payloads. An attachment that is already small enough is left untouched, and a platform without canvas falls back to today's behavior rather than rejecting an image the user can see working elsewhere.

## Cause 2 — the documented allowance was unreachable in principle

`proxy.ts` matches `/api/:path*`, so Next applied its default 10 MB body limit and refused the request *before any route handler ran*. The advertised allowance of 10 images × 10 MB could never actually be sent, since ten 10 MB attachments serialize to ~133 MB of base64.

- `next.config.ts` now sets `experimental.proxyClientMaxBodySize`, sized to the server-side budget rather than left at the framework default.
- A `Content-Length` guard in the route answers with the `prompt_rejected` shape the client already knows how to react to, instead of letting the proxy drop the connection with no reason.
- `validateAgentImages` gained an aggregate check, so a message that is over budget is refused with an API-safe message rather than by a layer that cannot explain itself.

Attachments are also no longer dropped silently when they do not fit: the composer keeps what it can, and a genuinely over-budget message now fails with something a user can act on.

## Verification

Measured in Chromium against the three original phone photos:

| | 164322935 | 164329928 | 164337838 |
|---|---|---|---|
| before | 2.00 MB | 3.40 MB | 2.66 MB |
| after | 0.43 MB | 0.68 MB | 0.51 MB |

Request body **10.74 MB → 2.16 MB** (80% reduction), which fits even the *old* 10 MB default — so the fix does not depend on the config change to work.

Quality holds up: 3072×4096 → 1536×2048 with a mean absolute pixel difference of **1.14–2.10 out of 255**, i.e. visually lossless.

Gates: `bun test` (660 pass; the 10 pre-existing auth/network failures are unchanged from `upstream/main`), `tsc --noEmit` clean, `eslint` clean on every touched file.

## Notes

- `lib/image-attachments.ts` stays the single source of truth for the budgets; `next.config.ts` cannot import it, so a test asserts the configured proxy limit covers the base64 expansion of the aggregate budget.
- Raising the cap is deliberate and bounded. The downscale is the real fix — it keeps normal traffic small — while the higher cap means the server-side allowance is no longer a promise the transport cannot keep. The route-level guard sits below the proxy limit so the handler answers with a reason instead of the proxy pre-empting it.

body:
## What broke
`main` went RED at `0b81b0c27`: the `test` job (kernel-tests.yml) failed, and `promote-and-prove` failed as its cascade.

## Why (bisected, evidence-backed)
- **PR #2173** changed `BRAIN/CURRENT-MISSION-STATE.md` (2330 → 8582 bytes) without re-running `tools/regenerate_brain_index.py`. The `test` job's last step — `python tools/regenerate_brain_index.py --check` — failed because `BRAIN/REAL-TREE.json` / `BRAIN/REAL-TREE.md` no longer matched the git tree. Deterministic, reproduced locally.
- **PR #2174 (kernel evidence-gate wiring) is NOT the breaker.** Full pytest green (2715 passed), node 599/599 green. Its own tests pass.
- **`promote-and-prove` needs no code fix.** At the tip it fails CLOSED via its required-workflow wait loop (kernel-tests red → fail). Its earlier failure at `e41e91f` was a timing race: #2172/#2173/#2174 merged 38s and 24s apart, and the job asserts `origin/main == GITHUB_SHA` after a fresh fetch — main moved under it. Self-inflicted, not a defect.

## The fix
Ran the official generator from git truth. 7 lines across 3 index files: receipt-basis stamps → `0b81b0c27`, `CURRENT-MISSION-STATE.md` blob SHA + size. **No test or gate code touched** — the `--check` assertion is byte-identical; only the generated artifact it verifies was refreshed. This is the 7th brain-index drift occurrence; the re-stamp should ride the changing PR, not a repair lane.

## Green proof (exact fix head `433b201f`, tree `1491f685`)
- `node --test tests/*.test.mjs`: **599/599 pass**
- `python -m pytest -q` (pytest+pyyaml+pglast, the workflow's exact install set): **2715 passed, 12 skipped, 2 xfailed, 0 failed**

author: gonxkz
body:
## Problema

El diagnóstico de #16 (PR #531) mostró que las colas del residual de US las dominan acciones muy poco líquidas: 19 de los 20 residuales mayores abren por debajo de 1 USD o negocian menos de 1.000 títulos, y una sola fila de KGJI pesa cerca de tres cuartos de la suma de cuadrados de 2022. Cualquier métrica o pérdida cuadrática queda decidida por esas filas. No había estratos de liquidez ni un registro del peso de las filas extremas.

## Cambio

- `evaluation/liquidity_strata.py` asigna cada fila evaluada a `liquid`, `low_price`, `thin_volume`, `low_price_and_thin_volume` o `unclassified` con la edición sin ajustar de #379. Usa la última sesión publicada en el instante de la predicción (cierre más cinco minutos), el último cierre verificado con volumen positivo y la mediana de 20 filas de volumen. Los precios preparados están ajustados hacia atrás, así que un umbral sobre ellos usaría splits futuros.
- Sección `liquidity_strata` declarada en las dos comparaciones de la campaña antes de cualquier resultado: umbrales, estratos, MAE y MSE por estrato con los contrastes, el bootstrap y Bonferroni de los estratos de modalidades, y el peso de las 1, 10 y 100 filas de mayor contribución por fila y por sesión. Es descriptiva y no selecciona nada.
- La comparación, los agregados por ventana de la retención v2, la matriz de comparaciones y la etapa de políticas reciben la edición. La matriz rechaza una vista con `mse` si un informe de origen no trae la sección, y los agregados incluyen la edición en su identidad.
- La comparación y la retención comparten una sola instancia del asignador para todas sus ventanas, con los mismos códigos.
- La cartera ya limitaba la orden al 1 % del volumen de la sesión publicada en la decisión. Una prueba nueva fija ese caso.
- `docs/research/metrics.md` documenta qué es cuadrático en la campaña, la asignación causal, las métricas, el coste y lo que no permite afirmar.

## Comprobaciones

- Datos reales sin modelos ni objetivos ([recibo](reports/engineering/liquidity-strata-20261010/README.md)): 16,1 millones de filas de US y 2,9 de CN asignadas, 400 activos truncados en una sesión al azar sin ningún cambio en las 778.631 filas anteriores y las 251 filas de KGJI en 2022 en `low_price_and_thin_volume`.
- Mutación dirigida: 36 de 36 mutaciones detectadas en `2cd8a352`.
- Coste: asignar un mes de US con una instancia nueva cuesta entre 17 y 21 s y con la instancia compartida entre 0,18 y 0,23 s, con 96,5 MB de caché. Puntuar los cinco estratos de 625.000 filas, 0,45 s.
- 1.294 pruebas en verde en CPU, en serie: `tests/evaluation`, `test_row_identity`, `test_score_recheck`, `test_adapter_campaign_stage`, `test_stage_comparison`, `test_campaign_a_joint`, `test_candidate_walk_forward`, `test_masked_campaign`, `test_modality_ablation_stage`, `test_rolling_retention`, `test_titans_walk_forward` y `test_portfolio`.
- `ruff check`, `ruff format --check` y `scripts/check_repository.py` correctos.

## Límites

No se ha ejecutado sobre predicciones de la campaña, que siguen bloqueadas. Los umbrales son los del diagnóstico de #16 en moneda local y en China apenas separan nada salvo las suspensiones. `unclassified` reúne entre el 13,5 % y el 16,2 % de las filas anuales de US desde 2018 y no es un estrato aleatorio. Cambiar la pérdida cuadrática de Ridge o XGBoost sería otra configuración de referencia con su propio presupuesto de búsqueda, y no se toca aquí.

Closes #532

## Why

Part A makes the epic's record the crew's memory. A1 to A3 built the record, the Architect's pass and the answers as rows. These four finish it:

- **A4: the merged tests an epic changes are C rows** (`record.TestRow`).

author: damianvtran
body:
# PR Description

## Summary of Changes

**U0: the i18n core mechanism, shipping dark.** The UI half of the merged RFC (`local-operator` [`docs/design/i18n.md`](https://github.com/damianvtran/local-operator/blob/main/docs/design/i18n.md), §3.2), built to the shapes that RFC measured — and mirroring the core's merged mechanism (local-operator #2127) rather than re-inventing it. Nothing translates yet, no user-visible string moves, and the `en` catalogue is deliberately empty; the extraction fan-out fills it namespace by namespace.

**The core (`src/i18n/`), per RFC decision:**

- **§2.4 — one generated key map + a two-overload `t()`.** `keys.gen.ts` is generated by `scripts/i18n/generate.mjs` from `src/i18n/catalogues/en/*.json` (empty stubs for the §5 namespace list: `ui.agents` … `ui.shell`). Each key's parameter shape is inferred from the message's own ICU placeholders; `messages.ts` declares the two overloads §2.4 proved. **The conditional-tuple variant is explicitly NOT the shape**, because the spike measured it *accepting* a missing params object.
- **§2.5 — locale resolution.** The backend's resolved `language` from `GET /v1/capabilities`, gated on `features.i18n`; the device locale (`navigator.language`, read raw and un-normalised — byte-identical to what every migrated site read) before any answer. The renderer mirrors the capabilities query into the store once, from `App`; `DesktopCapabilities.language` joins the wire contract as an optional post-contract field.
- **§2.6 — the envelope's fail-soft rule.** A missing or malformed message degrades to the key at render time, never throws through a render path; `registerCatalogue` is the seam the served `wire.*` slice will fetch into, with the bundled `en` map as the fallback for every lookup.
- **§2.8 — formatting.** The `Intl` layer (`format.ts` mirrors `local_operator/i18n/format.py`: numbers, dates, relative time, durations, byte sizes with per-locale caching) plus the migration of the sites §3.2 names: the shared date utils, the projects model and its five components, and the analytics panels' pinned `en-US`.
- **§2.7 — enforcement (this PR's scanner).** Below.

**Out of scope, deliberately:** main-process menus/dialogs/notifications (`ui.shell`) get their own catalogue slice — they cannot import renderer code (§3.2); no existing string is extracted or translated here.

Release: patch — no user-visible change yet: the i18n core lands dark (typed catalogue, `t()`, locale store, formatter layer, hardcoded-string scanner) ahead of the extraction fan-out.

## The typed-key spike evidence (§2.4, re-proven on the committed module)

`scripts/i18n/typed-keys.test.mjs` regenerates the types from a **fixture** catalogue and compiles the real `messages.ts` against them with the repo's own `tsc --strict`:

- **All four negative cases are rejected** — bad key, bad parameter type, missing required params, params on a no-params key. Each is a `@ts-expect-error` directive in `call-sites-negative.ts`, and an **unused directive is itself a compile error (TS2578)**, so the suite going green means every one of the four really errored.
- **A control compile pins it harder**: the same file with the directives stripped must FAIL, with ≥4 errors — proving the rejections are real rather than the directives being tolerated.
- **One claim the suite does NOT carry** (round-1 review, R1-4): swapping the overloads for a conditional-tuple variant does *not* fail this suite — re-measured, the variant rejects all four cases as retried here, so the shape's authority is §2.4's spike alone and the docstrings say exactly that. What is pinned is the SHIPPED shape rejecting all four.
- **A drift gate that is actually wired** (round-1 review, R1-2): `scripts/i18n/typed-keys.test.mjs` runs `generate.mjs --check` inside `test:desktop`, and `pnpm check-i18n` chains it ahead of the scanner.
- Positive call sites (every parameter kind, `Date | number` for date args) compile clean; the generated module's §2.4 shapes are asserted verbatim; the same generated catalogue is then **rendered at runtime** through the real `t()` (`{count, plural, …}` → `1 file`/`2 files`, interpolation, select, and the degrade-to-key path).

## The scanner and its negative fixture (§2.7)

`scripts/i18n/check-strings.mjs` runs on the **real TypeScript compiler API** (this repo's `typescript` is the native TS 7; `typescript/unstable/sync` is its programmatic surface, and this is the one file that touches it). It flags the two shapes the RFC's inventory measured — JSX text containing a letter, and literal `aria-label`/`placeholder`/`title`/`alt` attributes — and nothing else:

- **The ratchet mirrors the core's `check.py`**: per-file ceilings in `i18n/baseline.json` that may only stay equal or go down (`--update` refuses every raise and leaves the entry intact; a file with no entry starts at 0), a reason-REQUIRED allowlist (`i18n/allowlist.json`; exact paths or directory prefixes, no globs), and `// i18n: ignore <reason>` pragmas with both placements pinned (inside the finding's span, and the JSX block-comment spelling inside the enclosing element).
- **Enforcement is scoped** (RFC §9 P1): `src/i18n/` and `scripts/i18n/` block; everything else is **advisory** until an extraction slice activates its area's prefix in a reviewed change. The baseline records the tree as it stands: **240 files, 1611 literals, all advisory today.**
- **The negative fixture** (`scripts/i18n/fixtures/scan/violations.tsx`): every flagged shape AND its exempt neighbour (punctuation/digit whitespace, expression-valued attributes, the reasonless pragma that is NOT an exemption), with the fixture's exact findings **pinned by line number** so a walker that stops flagging — or starts over-flagging — fails the suite. The real-tree check CI runs is in the same suite: the tree must sit at-or-below its own baseline with nothing enforced failing.
- **v1's boundaries are stated in the module, not implied**: object-literal copy, expression-valued attributes and `+`-assembled strings are NOT counted; the slices that reach those shapes extend the walker with their counts. A false negative nothing reports is the one outcome the file must not quietly produce.

`pnpm check-i18n` is the developer entry point; `test:desktop` carries the four i18n suites (`check-strings`, `typed-keys`, `runtime`, `format`).

## Related Issue(s)

- Related: the RFC — `local-operator` `docs/design/i18n.md` (merged; §2.2–2.8, §3.2, §5).
- Related: the core-side mechanism it mirrors — `local-operator` #2127 and its neighbours (merged).

## Impact

- **No user-visible behaviour change; no version bump.** The mechanism ships dark and en-only; the migrated sites are pinned byte-identical to what they printed before (below).
- **Dependency update:** `intl-messageformat` + `@formatjs/icu-messageformat-parser`, both **devDependencies** (round-1 review, CI fix): the renderer bundle inlines the runtime, the generator is a script, and the repo's runtime-dependency gate reserves `dependencies` for main/preload packages shipped unbundled in `app.asar`. The lockfile delta is the importer move alone (**-3/+3 lines**, no other entry touched; the same edit `--lockfile-only` produces, verified with `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` under CI's pinned **pnpm 10.29.2**).
- **`navigator.language` semantics preserved**: pre-connection the store *is* the raw tag, read at format time; the analytics panels' deliberate pinned `en-US` is preserved verbatim through the layer.
- **No security implication**: no code-execution surface touched.
- **Evidence manifest**: the tree stamps are retired in this repository (the guard asserts their absence). The class the pair used to catch — a `src/` change that moves a surface the committed frames render, with no re-capture — is a review question, answered here: **no frame the sweep decodes is a picture of a surface this diff changes** (the mechanism ships dark; every migrated format site is pinned byte-identical). author: ndekocode
body: ## What The web app loads the team task list with a single `GET /tasks/team` that sends no `take` or `skip`. A team with a few hundred tasks gets all of them in one response, each with its 11 relations (tags, members, linked issues, children, estimations...). ```ts // task.service.ts, getTasks (before) const query = qs.stringify({ ...this.baseQueries, 'where[projectId]': projectId, 'where[teams][0]': teamId }); ``` Gauzy already supports pagination on that route. The web just never asked for it. ## How - `taskService.getTasks` takes optional `take` and `page`. When both are given, the request adds `take` (capped at 100), `skip = page` (at least 1, because Gauzy reads `skip` as a 1-based page number and `0` gives a negative offset) and `order[createdAt]=DESC&order[id]=DESC`. `findTeamTasks` has no default order, so without that sort the page boundaries would not be stable. Without `take` and `page`, the request is exactly the same as before. - `useTeamTasksQuery` uses `useInfiniteQuery`: pages of 50, `initialPageParam: 1`, and a next page while the loaded count is below `total`. Only the owner instance (the one in `InitState`) runs an effect that calls `fetchNextPage` while `hasNextPage` is true. It stops on error until the next refetch. Pages are joined and de-duplicated by id (`flattenTaskPages`, built on the existing `removeDuplicateItems`) before they go into `tasksByTeamState`, so every screen that reads the list still ends up with all the tasks. `querySuccess` is still true after page 1, so the shell does not wait for every page. - Pages are read one after the other, so a task created or deleted between two reads shifts the offsets: a task can be skipped while the count still reaches `total`. The list only counts as complete when every page reports the same `total`. When the totals differ, loading stops and the pages are reloaded from page 1, at most 3 times before waiting for the next refetch. - A new `teamTasksCompleteState` atom says whether every page is loaded. The owner writes it right after the list sync, so both atoms change in the same render. While it is false: - the active task is not cleared because it is missing from the list (`use-team-tasks-query`, and the two effects in `use-team-tasks-state`); - the task search does not show the create form, so nobody creates a duplicate of a task on page 3; - the open/closed counts in the task input are hidden until they are right. The assign task modal copies its task list when it opens, so it also records whether the team list was complete at that moment. A copy taken earlier never offers to create a task, even once the team list completes. - `useUpdateTask` applies its optimistic update and rollback to the `{ pages, pageParams }` cache. On failure it puts back only the edited task in the current pages, so pages loaded while the update was pending stay. `use-update-task.test.tsx` now seeds and reads that shape. - The Team's Task table shows 10 rows per page by default instead of 5. The 5 to 50 options are unchanged. A team with 50 tasks or fewer still makes a single request. A team with 200 makes 4, one after the other, and a refetch (polling, invalidation) reloads the loaded pages in sequence while keeping the old list on screen until it finishes. ## Scope - No Gauzy change, and nothing changes for mobile, desktop, the Angular app or the MCP: pagination is opt-in from the client. - `createTask` still calls `getTasks({ projectId })` with no pagination, so finding the created task by title after creation works as before. The server requests in `core/services/server/requests/tasks.ts` are untouched. The `app/api/tasks/team` proxy passes the query string through, so proxy mode gets the same pages as direct mode. - Other users of the `byTeamByScope` key only cancel or invalidate it, which works the same on an infinite query. The legacy `tasks.byTeam` key used by the unused `useTeamTasks` hook is a different key. - The kanban and profile tabs fill in as pages arrive. Tasks now come back newest first, where the order used to be undefined. - No new user-facing strings. Worth trying by hand before release: a team with about 250 tasks (page 1 SQL with the 11 relations, and an active task that sits on page 3 staying selected after a reload), and a search for a page-3 task, which should show the task and not the create form. --- ## Summary by cubic Loads team tasks in pages of 50 instead of one unbounded request, so large teams no longer get a single heavy response. - Pages are fetched with `take` capped at 100, a 1-based `skip`, and stable `createdAt DESC, id DESC` ordering; pages are joined and de-duplicated by id before the store is updated. - A new `teamTasksCompleteState` atom prevents clearing the active task, showing the create form, and displaying open/closed counts until all pages are loaded. The list only counts as complete when every page reports the same total; if page offsets shift, the sequence is reloaded from page 1 up to 3 times. - `useUpdateTask` now applies its optimistic update and rollback to the paginated cache shape; rollback restores only the edited task so pages loaded meanwhile stay in the cache. - The assign-task modal tracks when it copied an incomplete list and never offers to create a task from such a copy. - The Team's task table now defaults to 10 rows per page instead of 5. - The request is unchanged when pagination options are omitted, so `createTask`, server requests, and the proxy route work as before; no Gauzy changes. Written for commit 3a07bfb9b4b4a48cfaa7f150d9cf9927dfd3ec15. Summary will update on new commits.

author: singhharsh1708
body:
On a communicator, `autodiff = AutoForwardDiff()` was refused for a `DynamicalODEProblem` or `SecondOrderODEProblem` under an implicit method. The colouring from #135 seeds each rank's dual array with `colours[rstart .+ (1:n)]`, the colours of the columns numbered like the rank's block of PETSc's state. For these problems the prototype's columns number the whole velocity before the whole position while the state runs rank by rank as `[v; u]`, so past one rank those are other variables' colours: replaying the colouring in one process for a split of 7 and 16 rows, with tridiagonal `df/dv` and `df/du`, gave 121 wrong entries out of 157. The colours of the columns themselves and the mapping of the filled prototype onto PETSc's matrix through `_flat_columns` were already right, so the change picks each rank's seeds through the inverse of that column map and drops the refusal. The dual function is also guarded per part, so `f2` still runs when `f1` throws, and it is no longer wrapped as out of place.

This covers `TSAlpha2`, which reads `df/dv` and `df/du` from the `v` rows of the same first-order Jacobian a `jac` would fill, and the implicit methods on the first-order form. It needs the sparse `jac_prototype` of the first-order system, this rank's rows by the whole state: no prototype, a dense one, one of the acceleration rows alone, another backend and a mass matrix are still refused, each with its existing message. In one process on `MPI.COMM_WORLD`, the Jacobian of a nonlinear damped chain (45 entries, largest 62.8) differed from a hand-written one by 7.1e-15 and from the serial ForwardDiff one by 0, for `TSAlpha2` and `TSImplicit("bdf")`, and a partitioned problem with 4 velocities and 6 positions gave 0 for both. Solves with `TSAlpha2` at fixed and adaptive steps, `TSImplicit` (`"bdf"`, `"cn"`, `"beuler"`, `"theta"`), `TSRosW`, `TSARKIMEX` and `TSGeneric` (`"alpha"`, `"dirk"`), on both directions of the span, took the same steps (100 to 23603) and Jacobian counts as the `jac` solve and the serial ForwardDiff solve, with states within 1.4e-15 of the first and equal to the second; `TSIRK(2)` agreed with the `jac` solve to 2.0e-14, and a complex state under `"bdf"` and `TSAlpha2` matched both exactly.

test/mpi/second_order.jl now runs the `TSAlpha2` and `"bdf"` wave cases with ForwardDiff against the serial solve at the gaps of the `jac` cases, compares each rank's rows of the Jacobian with the `jac`'s and, on rank 0, with the serial ForwardDiff one, and adds a nonlinear chain as a `DynamicalODEProblem`, a rank with no rows and `f1` throwing on one rank. It passes in one process (210 tests) and at 2 ranks locally (210 and 168 on the two ranks); 3 ranks is left to CI, and only `TSAlpha2` and `"bdf"` ran on more than one rank. The new testset on `MPI.COMM_WORLD` in test/runtests.jl errors on main with the old refusal.

AI Disclosure: Claude assisted with the code. Testing and review by @singhharsh1708.

author: sethdford
body:
## Why

Phone calls arrive as 8 kHz PCMU over the Twilio SIP trunk. The cascade sends every caller's audio to Cartesia ink-2 at 16 kHz, so a phone caller's narrowband audio reaches ink upsampled. On the prod phone call (AJ_6gTw8RUcxwBC), Ferni misheard the caller twice.

## What (flag `PHONE_AUDIO_MODE=on`, default off)

For a LiveKit SIP caller (`ParticipantKind.SIP`, the same test `wantsPhonePreStt` uses for the AGC), the cascade STT is created with `sampleRate: 8000`. The plugin then resamples the AGC'd track to 8 kHz and opens ink with `sample_rate=8000`. App callers are unchanged, and with the flag off nothing changes.

Live path (grep):
- `persona-agent-factory.ts:162`: `phoneCaller: context.userParticipant?.kind === ParticipantKind.SIP`
- `agent-setup.ts:1136`: `createCallSession({ ...parts, phone: config.phoneCaller })`
- `call-session.ts`: `createProviderSTT(modelProvider, keyterms, { phone: phone === true })`
- `cartesia-cascade.ts`: `buildCascadeSTTOptions(env, caller)` adds `sampleRate: 8000` when `caller.phone && PHONE_AUDIO_MODE=on`

Only the multi-agent path is covered, which is the one prod runs. The legacy single-agent `voice-agent-entry/session-creator.ts` is unchanged.

## Phone detection (second commit)

Detection did catch the prod call. AJ_6gTw8RUcxwBC (phone_seth, outbound trunk ST_AEE6NnKE84XP) logged `Pre-STT: AGC + high-pass on phone caller audio` (sampleRate 24000), and that line fires only when `participant.kind === SIP`.

The `isTelephony:false` / `inputIs8Khz:false` lines come from two other places:
- The parallel monitoring analyzer in `audio-processor.ts` decides telephony from `frame.sampleRate === 8000`, but it reads a stream resampled to 16 kHz, so it is always false. It only monitors and never changes the audio sent to STT. Setting it true would be wrong: it would apply the 8 kHz Twilio preset to 16 kHz frames.
- The SIP frame processor runs the standard preset at the track's 24 kHz by design. That was measured earlier with stt-accuracy (bandwidth extension gave no gain).

To make detection robust anyway, `isPhoneParticipant` (`pre-stt-frame-processor.ts`) accepts kind SIP, **or** any `sip.*` attribute, **or** a `sip_`/`phone_` identity. Both the SIP pre-STT and `phoneCaller` use it (`persona-agent-factory.ts`). The test uses a participant shaped like the real one (`phone_seth`, kind SIP, `sip.callStatus`/`sip.phoneNumber`), with and without the kind. Reverting it to kind-only fails that test.

## Measurement

`scripts/audio-eval/stt-accuracy.ts` gains G.711 mu-law phone conditions, arms whose names end in `8k` (sent at 8 kHz) and `INK8K=1` (raw 8 kHz). Setup: real ink-2, 126 scenario utterances, 3 noise seeds (11/23/37). `agchp` is today's SIP pre-STT (AGC + high-pass).

| condition | raw 16 kHz | AGC+HP 16 kHz (prod today) | **AGC+HP 8 kHz (this PR)** | raw 8 kHz |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| mu-law, clean line | 4.5% | 4.6% | **4.4%** | 4.3% |
| mu-law, 15 dB babble+pink noise | 7.3% | 8.0% | **6.4%** | 6.1% |
| mu-law, soft line (-12 dB) | 12.4% | 5.3% | **5.2%** | 11.9% |

Per seed, noisy line, AGC+HP: 16 kHz 8.3/8.0/7.7% vs 8 kHz 6.2/6.5/6.5%. The 8 kHz arm wins or ties in every condition and seed. Raw 8 kHz does best on the noisy line, but without AGC it fails the soft line, so the AGC stays on.

Not changed here, for lack of evidence: endpointing/VAD thresholds for phone noise (needs dev calls), noise suppression (it hurt ink-2 badly before) and bandwidth extension (no gain before).

## Trade-off: about 160 ms slower turn ends (measured; decide on the dev A/B)

Ink-2 takes longer to end a turn on 8 kHz audio. `scripts/audio-eval/phone-endpointing.ts` (commit `a3c732faa`) streams 60 utterances in real time with the prod `responsive` thresholds (start 0.7, eager 0.6, end 0.3, timeout 4.5 s). It measures the time from the end of speech to ink's `turn.eager_end` and `turn.end`:

| arm | turn.end p50 / mean | eager_end p50 / mean |
|---|---|---|
| wideband 16k (app) | 956 / 961 ms | 783 / 761 ms |
| phone, sent at 16k (today) | 978 / 983 ms | 814 / 790 ms |
| phone, sent at 8k | 1139 / 1140 ms | 985 / 942 ms |
| phone + AGC/HP, 16k (today on SIP) | 949 / 953 ms | 788 / 752 ms |
| **phone + AGC/HP, 8k (this flag)** | **1114 / 1120 ms** | **959 / 920 ms** |

The 8 kHz delay roughly matches reply-speed's replay: about +160-170 ms on both turn end and eager end. The absolute times differ from theirs (their wideband was 574 ms) because the utterances and speech-end marking differ and mine include network round trips. Unlike their replay, I saw no phone-at-16k penalty against wideband (+22 ms vs their +263 ms).

So `PHONE_AUDIO_MODE=on` trades about 1.6 points of word error on noisy lines (8.0% to 6.4%) for about 160 ms more silence before each reply.

**Can we keep 16k for turn detection and 8k for words?** Not cleanly.
- Ink takes one rate per stream, so this means two Ink streams per phone call: 16k for turn events and 8k for text.
- At the 16k turn end, the 8k stream has only an interim transcript, which can lack the last words. Waiting for its final transcript costs the same ~160 ms.
- It would also double STT cost.

UNCONFIRMED whether 8k interim text is good enough at that moment; it would need its own replay.

**Cheaper alternative to test:** on 8k, raise the end threshold (for example `CASCADE_TURN_END` around 0.4 with eager 0.65) to win back the delay. That risks answering into thinking pauses, which 0.4 did on dev (2026-10-04), so it needs pause-bearing audio to judge.

**Recommendation:** keep the flag off and A/B it on the dev phone line, measuring WER and the gap callers hear.

## Tests

- `cartesia-cascade.test.ts`: 8 kHz only for a phone caller with the flag on. App callers stay unchanged with the flag on.
- `cartesia-stt-phone-rate.test.ts`: the real plugin connects to a local WebSocket server with `sample_rate=8000` for a phone caller and `16000` for an app caller.
- `call-session-phone.test.ts`: `createCallSession` passes `{ phone: true/false }` to the STT.
- Mutation check: reverting the `sampleRate` line and the call-session argument fails 4 tests. Restored, all pass.
- `vitest run src/agents/model-provider src/agents/multi-agent`: 43 files, 307 tests pass. `pnpm typecheck`: 0 `error TS`. Ratchet: no regressions (agent-setup.ts net 0 lines).

## Rollout

Set `PHONE_AUDIO_MODE=on` on dev and place a phone call. `Creating cascade Cartesia STT` should log `phone: true, sampleRate: 8000`.

author: hawabuilds
body:
Brings the USDC and fee work from `colosseum` to production. The delta is exactly the seven commits of #19 — everything else on colosseum already reached master in #18.

## What actually changes on trador.one

**The swap path moves to Jupiter Swap v2.** This is the only live change. v1 rejects a fee account on the input side of a trade with on-chain error 6014, which is what forced the move. The only API difference is `userPublicKey` becoming `taker`; every other option we send is unchanged.

**The fee stays off.** `NEXT_PUBLIC_TRADOR_FEE_BPS` and `TRADOR_FEE_WALLET` are not set on Production, so no fee is priced, no collection account is resolved, and the ticket reads "Not taken" exactly as it does now. Turning it on later is two env vars and the vault's two token accounts, not a deploy.

**The ticket gains the USDC pill**, the portfolio shows USDC beside SOL instead of counting it as a token nobody can price, and `npm run fee:accounts` is there for when the fee is switched on.

## Risk and rollback

`JUPITER_API_URL` has been unset on Production, so the swap host is now the default `https://api.jup.ag` with `JUPITER_API_KEY` — the same configuration every leg of this was tested against on Preview. Keyless, v2 is rate limited to roughly half of quotes, which is why the key matters.

It adds `workspace_compute` to owner chat turns. The model passes argv and exact workspace file revisions. These run in a single-use Cloudflare Container behind a private `COMPUTE` service binding (`examples/compute/`):
