author: augustas11
body:
Related: #1911
Related: #1749

This PR covers the two capacity items for the SPEC-049 privacy class in #1911. It changes coordinator ordering and waiting only. Eligibility, the wire format, schemas, disclosure strings and error codes do not change.

## Design (SPEC-049-R029, v0.2.6)

**1. Slot-aware private selection.** Since #1910 both reservation selectors run every SPEC-049-R013 check first. They then rank the surviving candidates of the requested model and key class: providers with an unclaimed free seat first, then busy ones. Each tier starts at a uniformly random provider.

This PR adds one input. The buyer account's own undispatched relay-blind and privacy reservations now count against a provider's free seats, so one buyer's concurrent private requests bind distinct providers deterministically instead of queueing behind one. The index is in memory and keyed by account. It holds at most 64 entries per account and has no shared cap, so one account's tracking never depends on another's. Entries are cleared when the chat reaches the slot wait, and a timer sweeps expired entries every 30 s while the index is non-empty. Selection is serialized per account up to recording the reservation, so simultaneous reservations from the same account see each other; other accounts are not blocked. The index affects ordering only.

The index is account-scoped on purpose. With a global index, any buyer could hold cheap undispatched reservations to make honest providers look busy, steer other buyers' private traffic, and learn other buyers' reservation activity.

Rotation stays a random tier start. Because the candidate list is already per model and key class, the rotation is per model and key class without any shared state. #1910's audit rejected a counter for this: requests of different sizes concentrate on one provider, and a counter would leak other buyers' reservation counts.

**2. Fair share for private waiters.** Before this change, a private chat waiting on its pinned session sat in the plaintext FIFO queue. It had these limits:
- at most `maxPending/4` private waiters per provider, which is 1 by default;
- no queue position at all once plaintext filled the queue;
- a wait of at most min(10 s, reservation expiry).

The per-provider slot queue now has two FIFO lanes: plaintext and pinned.
- Each lane has its own cap. The pinned cap is half the plaintext cap of max(configured cap, default 4, `slots_total`), and at least 1.
- A queue that is draining only pinned waiters still counts as draining for plaintext admission.
- While both lanes wait, grants alternate between them.
- A pinned waiter waits until its reservation expires (at most 30 s) as long as its provider keeps granting seats. It gives up as the existing retryable `relay_blind_provider_unsupported` only after one slot-queue deadline with no grant.

This is bounded and starvation-free for both classes:
- A pinned waiter at lane position k is served within 2k grants.
- The plaintext head is served within 2 grants.
- While both lanes wait, private traffic takes at most ceil(n/2) of any n consecutive grants.
- Plaintext admission, deadlines, direct dispatch and the capacity shed are unchanged.

SPEC-006 §7.8 (v0.9.50) and SPEC-002 (v1.6.14) now describe the two lanes. AUTHORITY adds SPEC-002 as a consumer of the privacy-class domain. CONFORMANCE adds the pending SPEC-049-R029 row. It is mapped to unit and integration tests, not to `JOURNEY-PRIVACY-CLASS-BETA-V2`, because that journey's contract fixes its own requirement set.

## Tests
- Ranking:
  - `TestPrivacySelectionSpreadsUndispatchedReservations`: 3 concurrent reservations land on 3 distinct enrolled providers, over 20 rounds.
  - `TestPrivacySelectionRotatesAndNeverChoosesIneligible`: 4 enrolled providers get 10 of 40 each. A provider without posture and one without a privacy key are never chosen, even when they are the only free ones.
  - `TestPrivacySelectionSpreadsSimultaneousReservations`: 4 concurrent reservations from one account land on 4 distinct providers. This test fails without the per-account serialization.
  - `TestPrivacySelectionPrefersFreeEnrolledProvider`.
  - `TestPrivacySelectionIgnoresOtherAccountsPending`.
  - `TestRelayBlindPendingExpiresAndIsBounded` and `TestRelayBlindPendingSweepsWithoutTraffic`.
  - `TestPrivacyReservationPendingClearsAtDispatch`.
- Fairness:
  - `TestSlotQueueAlternatesLanesWhenBothWait`.
  - `TestSlotQueueSustainedPlaintextLoadGivesPinnedFairShare`: 2000 grants with a saturated plaintext lane. Every pinned waiter is served within 2k grants, the pinned class gets close to half, and plaintext gets at least half.
  - `TestSlotQueueSustainedPinnedLoadDoesNotStarvePlaintext`.
  - `TestSlotQueueLanesHaveSeparateCaps`.
  - `TestSlotQueuePinnedWaitersCountAsDraining`.
  - `TestPrivacyChatWaitsThroughSustainedPlaintextLoad`: a real privacy chat behind two private waiters and a full plaintext lane keeps waiting past one stall deadline while seats free every 60 ms. It is served with HTTP 200 at its share.
  - `TestRelayBlindSlotWaitersAreCappedPerProvider` and `TestRelayBlindQueuesWhenQueueHasOnePosition` were updated to the new lane caps.
- Integration: `TestPrivacyClassSpreadsAcrossEnrolledProviders` runs two auto-enrolled Swift privacy fixtures behind the real gateway and coordinator. Sixteen private requests are served by both providers. The harness can now connect a second provider identity.

Local runs, all passing:
- `make test-coordinator`
- `make test-gateway`
- `make vet`
- `make lint-coordinator` (0 issues)
- `make test-integration` (EXIT 0)
- `make test-dist-python` (EXIT 0)
- `go test ./internal/buyer -race` on the relay-blind, privacy and slot-queue tests
- `check_spec_governance.py`
- `gen_spec_index.py --check/--lint`

## Audit
Three-lane Codex audit. The prompts are in `audits/2026-10-11-privacy-slot-aware/`. The gate (0 CRITICAL, 0 HIGH, 0 MEDIUM) was met in round 3.

| Round | Code | Security | Architecture |
|---|---|---|---|
| r1 | 0C 2H 2M 3L | 0C 0H 1M 1I | 0C 0H 3M 1L |
| r2 | 0C 0H 1M 2L | 0C 0H 0M 1L 1I | 0C 0H 0M 4L |
| r3 | **0C 0H 0M 2L** | **0C 0H 0M 2L 1I** | **0C 0H 0M 2L** |

Fixes, round 1:
- Simultaneous reservations from one account could both bind the same provider. Selection is now serialized per account.
- A queue draining only pinned waiters shed plaintext. It now counts as draining.
- The shared cap on the pending index broke isolation between accounts. The cap is now per account only.
- SPEC-006 had a contradiction about pinned requests entering the queue. It is fixed.

Fix, round 2: expired pending entries of idle accounts were swept only when new reservation traffic arrived. A timer now sweeps them.

Carried LOW findings:
- The integration spread assertion is probabilistic: about a 2^-15 chance that all 16 requests land on one provider.
- Private queue dwell is not in the `queue_wait_ms` telemetry. This predates the PR.

Carried INFO: toolchain dependency advisories that predate the PR, for a separate change.

## Deploy
This is a coordinator-only change: no provider, CLI, gateway, wire or catalog change. It is **not deployed by this PR**. It ships in a later Pearl runtime train through `scripts/ops/pearl-runtime.sh` (`status`, then `next`). After that train, a live probe must show more than one enrolled provider serving private traffic through the gateway; that is the remaining #1911 capacity proof.

{
  "schema_version": "spec-pr-governance-v1",
  "behavior_change": "yes",
  "contract_change": "yes",
  "specs": ["SPEC-049", "SPEC-006", "SPEC-002"],
  "requirements": ["SPEC-049-R029", "SPEC-049-R013"],
  "authority_domains": ["operator-constrained-privacy-class"],
  "arbitration": ["CODE_BUG"],

body:
## Summary

Internal-only tooling to detect routes whose OSM source relation disappeared upstream. **Nothing user-facing changes**: no template, view, static or locale file is touched, public route/stop pages render byte-identical to master (the provenance line and "Source under review" banner from earlier revisions were removed on 2026-10-11 to keep SEO untouched). **Flag only**: nothing deletes, hides, redirects or `noindex`es a route. Write-up: `docs/research/p0/p0-6-provenance-osm-check.md`.

```diff
 Recorrido
+  osm_checked_at   # last comparison against OSM (migration core 0030, nullable, no default)
+  osm_gone_at      # first check in which the relation was missing; cleared when it reappears

 apps/core/management/commands/check_osm_existence.py   (new)
 apps/core/admin.py
+  OsmSourceStatusFilter (gone / present / unchecked / no osm_id) = the review queue; both columns in list_display, read-only
```

`check_osm_existence` state machine (same for both sources):

```text
--source extract (default, 0 API calls): ids = route relations in /tmp/osm-<king>.pbf (pyosmium)
--source api: bounded GET /api/0.6/relation/<id>.json, cap 500/run, 1 req at a time, >=1 s apart, identifying UA

present  & gone_at null -> checked_at=now                      (present)
present  & gone_at set  -> gone_at=NULL, checked_at=now        (reappeared)
absent   & gone_at null -> gone_at=now, checked_at=now         (newly_gone)
absent   & gone_at set  -> keep gone_at, checked_at=now        (still_gone)
API 429/5xx/timeout     -> write nothing                       (inconclusive)
```

Writes are `QuerySet.update()` on those two columns only. `apps/editor/models.py` copies only fields that exist on both `Recorrido` and `RecorridoProposed`, so no editor migration is needed and the check fields stay out of the proposal flow.

Migration is `0030_recorrido_osm_checked_at_osm_gone_at` on top of P0-3's `0029_horario_secuencia_rol` (branch merged with master through #355).

## Evidence

- **Before:** relation `3443708` (Barcelona L61) returns HTTP 410 from the OSM API (checked 2026-10-10) while its page is live and nothing in the DB records it.
- **After:** `manage.py test apps.core.tests_osm_provenance apps.core.tests apps.core.test_route_meta apps.core.test_osm_tags apps.catastro` OK on a local PostGIS 16/3.4 (`config.settings.test`); the 2 `apps.core.test_paradas` failures seen locally also fail on `origin/master` (uncompiled `.mo`), unrelated. `makemigrations --check` reports nothing pending for `core`. `git diff --merge-base origin/master --stat` touches only `apps/core/{admin,models,tests_osm_provenance}.py`, the command, the migration, `apps/editor/models.py` and the write-up.

## Merge Danger

**Door:** two-way (revert the PR; the two nullable columns can stay or be dropped by reverse-migrating 0030).

**Blast Radius:** admin changelist of `Recorrido` and the new command. Public pages unaffected.

- Migration applies itself at container start since master's badd0c9 (`gunicorn.sh` runs `migrate --noinput`); if that is reverted, run `manage.py migrate` by hand. A deploy before the migration would only break the admin changelist, not route pages.
- The command is **not** scheduled here. Run it after each import (P0-0b owns the cron): `check_osm_existence --source extract --king <king>` (use `--pbf <file>-cropped.pbf` for clipped kings). Spot check: `--source api --osm-id 3443708`.

Open in Devin Desktop: https://app.devin.ai/desktop/session/58662e0457a24701a4f19584c9547d8f?variant=devin

body:
Sign split: name the halves original / inverse (review on ns-pond-ingestion-workflow#69).

`SignSplit` was `{group, direction: positive|negative, rule, primary}`. The halves describe the contrast, not the sign of a value: if a table already reports decreases, its "positive" half is the decreases and its "negative" half the increases. Now:

- `half`: `SplitHalf` = `original` (the analysis as named) | `inverse` (the reversed contrast, which a consumer records as the original's conditions with negated weights). Replaces `SplitDirection`.
- `original_analysis`: on the inverse half, the **key** of the original analysis in the same parse. Absent on the original half and on an inverse half whose original is not in the parse.
- `group` and `primary` are gone: `primary` was `half == original`, and `group` was the original's key on both halves.
- positive/negative stay only where they mean the sign of a statistic value (`StatisticKind`, `SplitRule`'s text now says negative values form the inverse half).

author: justinelliottcobb
body:
## Problem

Every PR touching public API surface regenerates the 18 MB monolithic `amari-discovery/catalog/generated.json`; concurrent PRs on disjoint crates (audit/core vs. rewrite features) always conflicted on it. PR #285 paid that merge tax twice (#283, #284). The pattern continues to 1.0.

Operator decision (2026-10-10): option **C — per-crate split only**. Merge queue, regen bot, and build-time generation explicitly deferred.

## Design

- `catalog/manifest.json` — every non-crate `StructuralCatalog` field (aggregate `content_hash`, cross-crate edges, totals) + ordered crate file refs.
- `catalog/crates/<name>.json` — 28 per-crate files, canonical bytes.
- Generated `catalog/index.rs` — documented compile-time include table; the loader composes the split and takes the **unchanged** `from_sources` path, so the `content_hash` recipe and validation semantics are identical to the monolith (round-trip byte equality is pinned by test).
- Generator removes the monolith and stale per-crate files; `verify_checked_in` is split-aware and names drifted files, **including the generated index** (single shared `render_index_rs`/`manifest_bytes` source for generator and verifier); CI drift check covers the whole catalog directory.
- `compose_structural` rejects duplicate manifest references and unreferenced bodies.

## Proofs (docs/plans/core-matrix-evidence/catalog-split/SUMMARY.md)

author: brg8607
body:
## Origen

Revisión de errores de la app de tablet en el emulador (2026-10-10, Pixel 7 / Android 16, backend local contra el Postgres local al día con `main`). Se midieron cinco errores; este PR arregla dos de ellos (E4 y E5). Los otros tres (E1 kilometraje que nadie guarda, E2 vender con el día cerrado, E3 "1 registro por subir") van en `feature/t-38-jornada`, que se abre aparte.

Spec con las decisiones: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-10-sync-segundo-pull-y-textos-design.md`. Plan: `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-10-10-sync-segundo-pull-y-textos.md`. Ejecutado con subagentes (3 tareas, cada una con su revisión, más revisión final de la rama).

## E4 · Una venta a crédito recién subida no aparecía para cobrar hasta la SEGUNDA sincronización

**Medido antes:** venta a crédito `TJ261010DM01` → *Sincronizar ahora* → "Se bajaron 0 y se subieron 1"; Cobranza decía "no tiene notas pendientes". Segunda sincronización sin cambios → "Se bajaron 1". Causa: el motor corre pull **antes** del push a propósito (`motor.ts`, si se corta la red a la mitad mejor tener catálogos frescos), y nadie volvía a bajar después de subir.

**Arreglo (D1):** paso 5 del motor: si el push aplicó algo o subió alguna foto, un pull incremental más al final; sus filas se suman al resumen. Si ese segundo pull falla por red/sesión/contrato, la sincronización sigue `ok` (lo subido ya está a salvo) y queda `pullPosterior: 'fallo'` en el resultado; un error desconocido se propaga, como en los demás pasos. 6 pruebas nuevas en `motor.spec.ts`.

**Medido después:** venta a crédito `TJ261010DM04` → una sola sincronización → "Se bajaron 1 registro(s) y se subieron 1" → la nota aparece en Cobranza.

## E5 · Tres textos que confundían al vendedor

- **5.1** "Catálogos bajados: 2026-10-10T18:02:54.922Z" (ISO cruda y en UTC) en el menú de la jornada y en la lista de clientes. Ahora `formatearMomento` (`src/ui/momento.ts`, sin `Intl`, hora local del dispositivo): "Catálogos bajados: 2026-10-10 21:40". Medido en el emulador.
- **5.2** En *Abrir el día* el error "El kilometraje inicial debe ser un número…" se quedaba después de corregir el valor. Ahora se borra al escribir (también en *Cerrar el día*). Medido.
- **5.3** En *Cobranza*, la ayuda de *Fecha de pago* decía "Entre 2026-10-10 y 2026-10-10." Ahora "Solo hoy (2026-10-10)." con `ayudaRangoFecha` (función pura con prueba). Medido.

## Verificación

| Chequeo | Resultado |
|---|---|
| `npm run typecheck --workspace=apps/tablet` | limpio |
| `npm run lint --workspace=apps/tablet` | limpio |
| `npm test --workspace=apps/tablet` | 36 suites / 435 pruebas (antes 35 / 422) |
| Emulador, los cuatro escenarios de arriba | en verde |

Solo `apps/tablet/`. Sin cambios de contrato, backend ni migraciones locales.

## Decisiones tomadas por el agente (Mario puede revertirlas)

- El segundo pull va al final (después de las fotos) y solo si hubo algo que subir; `cursor` es el del segundo pull, `completo` el del primero.
- Un fallo de campo del segundo pull no vuelve roja la sincronización; un bug sí se propaga.
- Helper de fecha sin `Intl`, en archivo propio `momento.ts` (jest de la tablet solo transforma `.ts`).

## Pendiente que deja este PR (no bloquea)

- Cuando `pullPosterior === 'fallo'` (WiFi inestable justo al final), la tarjeta de sincronización todavía dice "completa" y la nota recién vendida no está para cobrar hasta la siguiente. El campo ya existe para que la tarjeta lo avise; conviene un ticket junto a T-44.
- Una prueba intermitente que ya existía en `main` (`motor.spec.ts` "el cursor NO se guarda si aplicar el snapshot falla") falló una vez de ocho corridas; no la toca este PR.

author: ndekocode
body: ## What When a teammate starts or stops their timer, other people on the team view may not see it for up to 60 seconds. The only source for other members' status is the team detail query owned by the shell. It refreshed on the same 60 s interval as everything else: ```ts // init-state.tsx detailRefetchInterval: autoRefreshEnabled ? SHELL_REFRESH_INTERVAL : false // 60_000 ``` There was also a 5 s loop, but it was gated on the viewer's own timer: ```ts useTimerPolling(autoRefreshEnabled && teamReady && timerOwner.rawTimerRunning); ``` So a viewer who was tracking saw changes within 5 s, and a viewer who was not tracking waited up to a minute. The loop also had three side effects: - It invalidated the whole `['organization-teams']` prefix and the working-employees list, so the full team list was refetched along with the detail. - It kept running in a background tab. - Even once fresh data arrived, the detail's dedup signature only looked at `activeTaskId`, roles, member count and `updatedAt`. A start or stop made from the desktop app, the agent or Gauzy web could change `timerStatus` or `employee.isTrackingTime` without changing any of those, and the store was never updated. ## How - New constant `TEAM_PRESENCE_REFRESH_INTERVAL = 25_000`. That is Gauzy's `BACKGROUND_SYNC_INTERVAL`, the value its web and desktop apps use to resync a timer changed from another device. - A small Jotai counter, `teamPresenceViewCountState`, plus `useTeamPresenceView(enabled)`. `TeamMembers` calls it with `!publicTeam`: +1 on mount, -1 on unmount. - In `InitState`, the team detail refetches every 25 s while the counter is positive and every 60 s otherwise. It is still `false` under `NEXT_PUBLIC_DISABLE_AUTO_REFRESH`. - `useOrganizationTeamsQuery` gets a `detailRefetchOnWindowFocus` option. When the team view is mounted, the detail uses `refetchOnWindowFocus: 'always'`, so coming back to the tab refreshes right away. `refetchIntervalInBackground` stays `false`, so a hidden tab makes no calls. - The detail signature now also includes each member's `timerStatus`, `employee.isOnline`, `employee.isTrackingTime` and `employee.isActive`. - `useTimerPolling` is removed from the shell and deleted. The dead `useSyncTimer` hook, its only other user, is removed too. Its two barrel exports are added to `tools/preservation/ever-teams-preservation.allow.json` so the preserved-surface check accepts the removal. Unchanged: the teams list (60 s), the viewer's own timer status (60 s), tasks, daily plans and statistics. ## Why it does not break anything else - `InitState` is the only caller that passes options to `useOrganizationTeamsQuery`. The other callers get the new option's default (`false`), which is the previous behaviour. - `TeamMembers` is rendered only on the main page. That page is in the `(main)` group, so it shares the Jotai provider with `InitState`. The counter goes back to zero when you leave the page, and the detail falls back to 60 s. - `useSyncTimer` had no caller in the repo. - The working-employees query the 5 s loop used to invalidate is only used by the invite modal, which fetches when it opens. - The endpoint (`GET /organization-team/:id`) and the request are the same in direct and proxy mode. Only the cadence changes. - Expected load, worked out from the intervals: - A non-tracking viewer with the team view open goes from 60 to 144 detail calls per hour. - A tracking viewer goes from about 720 detail calls plus 720 list calls per hour to 144 and 60. `init-state.test.tsx` mocked the removed `use-timer-polling` module and asserted `polling(true)`. That mock, the `polling` spy and the assertion are removed; the rest of the test is unchanged. --- ## Summary by cubic Refreshes teammates' presence status on the team view every 25 seconds so a timer started or stopped from another device shows up promptly, regardless of the viewer's own timer. Before, non-tracking viewers waited up to 60 seconds, while tracking viewers got a 5-second loop that refetched the full team list and kept running in background tabs; that loop is now removed. **Notes** - The 25-second cadence applies only while the team view is mounted and the tab is visible, with an immediate refresh on window focus; everywhere else stays at 60 seconds, and `NEXT_PUBLIC_DISABLE_AUTO_REFRESH` still disables it. - The detail signature now includes each member's `timerStatus`, `isOnline`, `isTrackingTime`, and `isActive`, so changes made from the desktop app, agent, or Gauzy web reach the store even when `updatedAt` and `activeTaskId` don't change. - The unused `useSyncTimer` hook and its polling wrapper are deleted, and the test mock of the removed hook is dropped. Written for commit 11a8e2bcdd9b69188c43e4b12e363bb033f26c5d. Summary will update on new commits. ## Summary by CodeRabbit * **Improvements** * Team details refresh every 25 seconds while a private team view is active and refresh when you return to the window. * When no team view is active, team details refresh every 60 seconds without refreshing on window focus. * When automatic refresh is off, team details no longer refresh on a schedule or window focus. * Running timers synchronize every 60 seconds when automatic refresh is enabled and the team is ready.

author: xxfran10xx
body:
## Problem

At 16:27 on 2026-10-10, Paper's watchdog on Main caught the server thread stuck in `StealManager.getStealGuiHolder` (`StealManager.java:115`). Every inventory click and close ran `inventory.getHolder()` in several Thievery listeners. For a block inventory that copies the whole block state, so a barrel reloaded all of its items just to learn it was not a Thievery menu. This is the same kind of slowdown #25 fixed for hoppers.

## Changes

- `StealManager.getStealGuiHolder` (click, close, and every tick per open steal session), the loadout click/close handlers, and the steal title refresh now use Paper's non-snapshot `getHolder(false)`.
- `ContainerManager.onInventoryClick` uses `getHolder(false)` / `getLeftSide(false)`. It also checks the cached owner (from #25) before reading the container's data file, so takes from unowned containers skip the disk read.
- Tests: MockBukkit does not implement `getHolder(boolean)`, so tests that use its inventories wrap them in `TestInventories.withHolderLookup`. Without that, 10 tests were silently skipped and the coverage gate failed. A new test checks that an unowned container click reads neither the data file nor a block snapshot.

## Testing

- `mvn clean verify`: 822 tests, 0 skipped, 100% coverage gate passes.
- TFMCDev01 bot test (`~/holder-test/test.js` on the host), 23/23 checks:
  - Barrel and double chest: the owner claims and later privates the container while a thief has it open. The thief's take alerts opted-in staff, and the double chest reports the left-side location.
  - Loadout GUI: a category click toggles, the click is cancelled, and confirm saves the category.
  - Robbery GUI: accept opens it, a click moves one ingot from victim to robber, and closing the GUI ends the session.
  - No Thievery exceptions or warnings in `latest.log`.

body:
## Summary

This follows up on PR #2685 by replacing duplicated numeric kernels with the libraries already used by the project, while keeping optional diagnostic dependencies optional.

- Use Shapely/GEOS for point-to-segment distance and closest authored-segment mapping. Sample each authored curve once per mapping pass, and reuse the same geometry-preparation helpers in the FreeCAD adapter.
- Use NumPy vectorized cross products/norms for fallback triangle areas and SciPy sparse connected-components for edge-connected mesh components.
- Prefer `trimesh.contains` for watertight point-in-mesh queries when the optional spatial-index backend is installed; retain the NumPy ray-parity path for environments without that accelerator or for open meshes.
- Validate point coordinates and mesh face connectivity with the existing Pydantic schemas before either containment backend, and replace remaining Euclidean square/sum/square-root loops with `math.dist`.
- Add Hypothesis properties for GEOS distance invariants and triangle area, plus regressions for edge-based components, containment parity, and invalid containment inputs.

## Verification approach

CrossHair remains focused on pure-Python contracts it can symbolically explore. The GEOS-backed distance contract is exercised with Hypothesis instead of pretending CrossHair can symbolically model GEOS. The canonical repository CI checks are requested by this PR; results will be reported after they finish.

No solver parameters or cloth-physics behavior are intentionally changed.

The known-input pairing control exercised plain FASTQ files and bypassed gzip recovery. Extend the native Docker matrix to plain and gzip sources with identical known reads, then execute a fresh replay for each. Both cases require exact preservation of all six read identities, sequences, qualities, mate orientation, singletons, per-mate reports and repair diagnostics.

The replay checker also recognizes a relocated guarded source bundle without losing support for downloaded original evidence. Wrong origins, wrong observed engines and failed replay outcomes remain rejected.

author: oldsj
body:
Every first Claude turn in a Mainloop workspace failed after #26: the driver refuses to start with any pre-existing child processes, the harness is PID 1, and git 2.47+ `fetch` detaches `git maintenance`, leaving zombies under PID 1.

- Workspace checkout runs git with `-c maintenance.auto=false -c gc.auto=0`.
- Before the process census, the harness reaps only exited orphans that are its direct children *outside* its own process group. Each wait goes through a pidfd opened before the identity recheck. No `exec.Cmd` that Go still waits on can be reaped, and a reused PID can't be hit. Live orphans still fail closed.
- Admission and start failures reach Mainloop as `TerminalFailure` with the real, content-free cause instead of "Harness runtime execution failed".

Root cause proven live (hidden ateom log). Fix proven with unit, race and regression tests (trace2 maintenance check, an orphaned zombie between turns). Not yet proven on a live gVisor turn. Reviewed by Claude Opus xhigh: accepted, with 4 P3 follow-ups.

author: vikrantb
body:
## The blind spot

The founder's course 8a64fcff shipped four repaired lessons on 2026-10-08. The acceptance gate scored all four `PASS_DETERMINISTIC` with no issues (`gate-<id>/gate.log`). That same day, hero critic Elena reviewed the same frames and found text cut on all four (review section 2):

- a central question ending "...when does it create avoidable…";
- myth/reality cards cut by their own box;
- a takeaway that never finishes ("...this plan often produces");
- titles cropped by a camera push ("hoosing Your Strongest Major", "ifficulty Bonus Myth").

The gate's only text rule is `_pixel_invariants`' EDGE-CLIP. It cannot see this class, for two reasons:
- It reads 12 of ~250 frames and fires only when a third of the frames it checks show edge structure (main `acceptance_gate.py:241`, `edge_clip >= max(2, edge_checked // 3)`).
- It knows only the FRAME edge. Text cut by a word budget, by a length cap's "…", or by its own card box never reaches the frame edge.

The pipeline fix is workers #3278 (text) plus a camera PR from the same lane. This PR is the instrument.

## What the gate now reads

`scripts/text_integrity.py` OCRs every non-photo gate frame with the tesseract CLI. That is $0 and the same binary `kitesforu_qa.harness.checks.visual` already shells out to. Each frame can raise three findings:

| finding | rule |
|---|---|
| `EDGE` | a word with confidence ≥ 40 and 2 or more alphanumerics touches the frame edge (cut by the frame or by a camera move) |
| `ELLIPSIS` | a line ends in "…" or "...", preceded by a real word (3+ alphanumerics): a length cap on screen |
| `PREFIX` | a text block is the OPENING of a line the job itself authored (blueprint `central_question` / `takeaway` / `worldview_shift` / `succes_plan.concrete` / `must_cover`, or one sentence of a segment's `text_full`), and it stops where that line does not end: no sentence or clause boundary, not inside an open parenthesis. The line's next words also appear nowhere on the frame, nor on the next 3 frames, because a reveal is not a cut. |

How findings become issues:
- A kind seen on 2 or more frames is a MAJOR issue that names its frames.
- Photo frames (`scene_image`) are skipped by the same predicate as the pixel rule. That predicate is now one function, `_is_photo_frame`, shared by both rules.
- OCR that cannot run is reported as MAJOR "NOT checked". It is never a pass.
- `run_gate` calls the probe after the pixel invariants and returns a `text_integrity` summary.

`PREFIX` is the finding OCR alone cannot produce, because the clipped half-line is never on screen to be read. It needs the authored line to compare against.

## Evidence (all $0, local, no provider call)

**1. The four lessons, both arms, on the same frames and machine.** Command: `python tools/main_arm_pixel.py <scripts> <label>`. Main is a `git archive` of c0a3fee; head is 7a84c20. OCR rows come from cached TSVs of the same frames.

| lesson (frames) | main c0a3fee | head 7a84c20 |
|---|---|---|
| ep2 2eddeaaf (247) | PASS_DETERMINISTIC | REVIEW: TEXT-CUT PREFIX 20/198, ELLIPSIS 17/198, EDGE 6/198 |
| ep5 56f276db (257) | REVIEW: EDGE-CLIP 3/7 | REVIEW: EDGE-CLIP 3/7, TEXT-CUT PREFIX 14/135, EDGE 6/135 |
| ep6 c6c180c8 (268) | REVIEW: EDGE-CLIP 3/8 | REVIEW: EDGE-CLIP 3/8, TEXT-CUT PREFIX 25/170, ELLIPSIS 6/170 |
| ep4 cdcf1150 (231) | PASS_DETERMINISTIC | REVIEW: TEXT-CUT PREFIX 6/172, ELLIPSIS 20/172 |

Caveat on the main column:
- The recorded gate run on 2026-10-08 said PASS on all four. My re-run today said REVIEW on two of them.
- `acceptance_gate.py` was last changed on main on 2026-09-01, so the code is the same. The frames are the same files.
- The input that differs is the job doc the clip list was read from: I used a snapshot taken later. **That is not root-caused.**
- Either way, main's EDGE-CLIP is a pixel count that names no text and no frame.

**2. Against the review's witnesses.** Commands: `python tools/eval_text_integrity.py <scripts> text_integrity_eval.json`, then `python tools/score_witness_groups.py text_integrity_eval.json`.
- **Population:** every gate frame of the four lessons, 1,003 frames. 675 were OCR'd; 328 were photo frames, skipped.
- **Witness groups:** 17 groups. Each is the frame range where a cited defect is on screen. I located each range by eye on the frames, from the review's citations. Where the review gives frame numbers (f_211-f_219, f_225-f_234, f_168-f_178, f_192-f_200, f_211-f_214, f_261-f_268), I used them.
- A group counts as flagged when 2 or more of its frames carry a finding (a one-frame group needs its one frame).
- **Result: 15 of 17 groups flagged, and 0 flagged frames outside every group.**
- Every finding inside a group names the cited text: the takeaway, the myth cards, the central question's "avoidable…", the cut labels, and the pan-cropped title fragments ("100sing", "ifficulty"). The list is in `scratch/group_texts.log`.

💡 What: Moved the array copy (`[...runners]`) and `new Map()` initialization out of the `while` loop inside `runRaceToCompletion`. Pre-allocated an array, sorting it in-place every tick, and reused the same `Map` instance using `.clear()`.

author: enriqueagv
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"EnriqueAGV"} -->
_Requested by **Enrique** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01KGRnrfo7Nwo5jUJsKeASVy?thread=cmsg_01KGRnrfo7Nwo5jUJsKeASVyUpCmgEuCoQ8RA5JyZ9odgD)_

Before: whoever wrote from a phone number that staff had typed into a record (a typo, an old or recycled number) could ask the assistant for that patient's name, saved answers and appointments, and could change them. The assistant could also overwrite a name or DUI that staff had already confirmed. The only thing stopping medical advice was the prompt. Patient conversations, DUIs included, could reach any OpenRouter provider.

After: a number staff typed in stays unverified until the person writing gives a matching birth date or DUI. Until then the assistant shows and changes nothing on the record. Confirmed names and DUIs go to staff review instead of being overwritten. A second, tool-less call checks every reply before it goes out, and the model never sees a DUI.

This fixes all nine findings from the agent security review (`/mnt/project-files/ikarus/agent-security-review.md` in the project).

**How**
1. **Unverified numbers.** New columns `clients.wa_verified_at` and `wa_verify_failures`. A number that writes in first is verified when its record is created. Records created by staff, or whose phone staff changed, start unverified. In that state the prompt carries no names or appointments, only the read-only tools run, and the new `verify_identity` tool compares the answer in code. After three wrong answers the conversation goes to the team. The patient page shows "Sin verificar" with a "Marcar como verificado" button. The migration marks every holder that has already written in as verified, so existing conversations carry on.
2. **Name and DUI.** New column `identity_reviewed_at`, set whenever staff create, edit or review a record. After that, `save_client_info` only fills empty fields. A different value goes to `data.nombre_whatsapp` or `data.dui_whatsapp`, and the existing intake review (now extended to names) lets staff accept it.
3. **Patient text in the prompt.** Saved answers are gone from the prompt; only missing fields are listed. Names are JSON-quoted and labelled as patient data. Profile names, names, answers and handoff reasons are reduced to one line with a length cap, and every free-text tool input has a max length.
4. **Reply check** (`src/lib/agent/guard.ts`). The reply is checked for medical advice, leaked instructions or off-topic content, using `LLM_GUARD_MODEL` (defaults to `LLM_MODEL`). A reply containing a UUID is blocked without that call. A blocked reply, or one the check can't judge, sends the holding reply and hands off with the reason. The prompt also gains an explicit rule against role-claims.
5. **Provider and DUIs.** OpenRouter calls ask for `data_collection: "deny", zdr: true`. DUIs in the history become `[DUI n]` tokens, which the tools turn back into the real number. A call without tools sends neither `tools` nor `tool_choice`.
6. **Volume.** More than 30 outbound messages to one number in an hour pauses the assistant and hands off. A number can hold at most 10 patients.
7. **Errors.** A failing tool returns a generic message; the detail goes to the logs.
8. **Replays.** An inbound message whose Kapso id is already stored is skipped. A new non-unique index backs this lookup. There is no unique constraint, because existing rows might already hold duplicates.
9. **Staff-facing text.** Handoff reasons are capped and kept to one line.

Tests: 12 new cases in `test/agent.test.ts`, `test/records.test.ts` and `test/llm.test.ts`. Locally, typecheck, lint, all 176 tests and `next build` pass.

Deploy notes: set `LLM_GUARD_MODEL` if you want a cheaper checker. On OpenRouter, a model with no zero-retention provider will now fail instead of falling back.

body:
## Summary

About half of today's PR runs were cancelled at the 15-minute job limit because one browser test in the Desktop lite suite never returned. This change makes such a test fail after 60 seconds with its own name, and removes the most likely thing it was waiting on. I could not reproduce the hang locally, so the cause below is inferred from the code, not observed.

## Changes

- `apps/desktop/test/live-reload.test.mjs`: every test has a 60 s `timeout`; browsers a test launched are closed when it ends, so a stuck `page.evaluate` is cancelled and the process exits (checked with a simulated never-settling evaluate: fails by name, run exits).
- `boot()` no longer waits forever on `handle.ready`. That promise settles only after the engine reports a paint following the render, and `startup/measure.ts` documents that it never resolves where no paint arrives. `page.evaluate` has no timeout, so the wait was unbounded. It is now bounded at 15 s; each test already waits on its own condition.
- `changelog.d/F-30.md`.

## Evidence

- Cancelled runs 38088243517 and 38084654597: last completed test is in the F-19.3/F-23 series, then roughly 11 minutes of silence. Other cancelled runs' logs were not usable for this.
- Locally, 20 serial runs of the file, six busy loops running: 0 failures or hangs before, 0 after. So the hit rate is below about 1 in 20 here and the diagnosis is not confirmed.
- Not changed: the product's unbounded paint wait, which is by design for a reader on a locked screen.

## Verification

- `MARXY_BROWSER_TESTS_REQUIRED=1 node --test --test-concurrency=1 test/live-reload.test.mjs` x20 under load: 20/20 pass (27 tests each, 28-40 s).
- `pnpm precheck`: 7/7 passed.

author: orenhacham-lab
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"orenhacham-lab"} -->
_Requested by **oren** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01N1rjLCUuakrwGVxEKYUs4N?thread=cmsg_01N1rjLCUuakrwGVxEKYUs4NB8uyT8uZXarsPx6qTXp9A3)_

Before: the forty-odd pages that carry the software keywords — ten features, four solutions and the free check, in four languages — had no structured data of their own. All they shipped was the site-wide `Organization` and `SoftwareApplication` from the root layout, identical on every URL, so a crawler could not place any of them in the site, and the questions each page answers in plain sight were not declared as questions anywhere. Every article page carried **two conflicting `BreadcrumbList`s**: the listing's two-step trail lived in the articles layout, which wraps the whole segment, so it was rendered next to the article's own three-step trail, with the article's title in only one of them. The price in the markup was shekels on every language, so an English page displayed $79 and told a crawler 249. The English, Spanish and Portuguese home pages declared no canonical at all, and `url` in the markup pointed at the Hebrew root whatever language the reader was on.

After: each feature and solution page states the route it serves, and the template turns that into a breadcrumb — home, then the page — in the reader's language. The questions already on the landing, pricing and feature pages are declared as an `FAQPage` built from the same copy the reader sees. One `WebSite` node names the publishing `Organization` by `@id`, so the four language trees are one graph. The offer is the real plan range in the currency that language is quoted. The listing's trail belongs to the listing page alone, so an article page has one breadcrumb. The three home pages name themselves.

Google retired FAQ rich results in May 2026 and this does not pretend otherwise; Bing and the AI engines still read `FAQPage`, and these are the answers we would want quoted. No rating, review or customer count is introduced, and nothing is served to a crawler that a reader cannot see.

How: `lib/seo/page-schema.ts` holds the three builders. `FeaturePage` takes the page's path and emits the trail and the FAQ itself, so the 56 route files each state one path and nothing else. The home-page canonical is on the **page**, not on the language layout — a layout's canonical is inherited by every route under the prefix, which would point the legal pages that declare none of their own at the home page.

Verified: `node scripts/qa/verify.mjs` — tsc 0 errors, ESLint 0 findings on touched lines, no new QA failures; the new `lib/seo/__qa__/marketing-page-schema.qa.ts` is 59/59, and its detectors were proved by breaking a page's path and the layout's offer on purpose. `bash scripts/qa/journeys.sh` builds clean, and the rendered HTML of the built site was checked directly: one breadcrumb per article page, USD 79–649 and the locale home `url` on `/en`, `/es`, `/pt-BR`, ILS 249–1999 on Hebrew, and a self canonical on all four home pages.

author: gzotti
body:
The latest master does not launch on Windows. One could create a wrapper .bat file into the venv/scripts, but IMO it's even cleaner to let the pip install build the proper .exe adapter: move the main scripts from bin to fchart3 and rename them.  This install code was mostly made by Google Gemini. It is now working on Windows, untested on Linux! After any edit, `pip install .` is needed.

Apart from this, I fixed the tikz building (redundant parameter) and ensured utf-8 encoding. (This could be enhanced by another config var `--output-encoding` if ever needed, but I need UTF-8 in my Almanac.)
When building a tikz, it has a clip that trims away most of the caption. Adding no-margin now also hides the captions. 

The sigma character in star maps is AFAICS always the 'internal' σ, not ς. I removed the σ/ς which looked even like σ/σ in tikz/LaTeX output.

The trajectory code computes points at regular intervals and connects them with straight segments. I suggest a bit shorter intervals for a smoother curve. Future extension may be an argument like `--trajectory-label-every=5` that computes denser intervals but labels only every 5th.

author: rsocko
body:
## Why

A GitHub create with an unknown post-dispatch outcome is intentionally quarantined as `push_failed`, but local-only tasks bypassed that terminal-state fence because `source_id LIKE 'local:%'` independently qualified them for every scheduled push. In production this caused the same safely fenced task to be reclaimed hundreds of times.

## What changed

- Exclude `push_failed` local-only tasks from push candidate selection in both SQLite and PostgreSQL.
- Apply the same exclusion when atomically claiming a task, preserving race-safe behavior.
- Add shared persistence contract coverage proving terminal local creates are neither listed nor claimed.

This does not automatically reconcile unknown GitHub outcomes or identity collisions; those remain explicitly operator-controlled.

body:
## 目标

增强通用整圈旋转搜索的覆盖范围，同时保留原有水平旋转总量。该默认行为同时作用于战斗结束后的目标搜索，以及普通导航连续丢失后的旋转兜底搜索；导航状态机的其它状态转换保持不变。

## 变更

- `rotate_search()` 从单层水平旋转改为平滑正弦俯仰扫描。
- 默认将每个原水平分段拆成 2 个检测采样点，检测次数翻倍。
- 水平累计位移保持与旧实现的 `segments * max(1, int(width * step_ratio))` 一致，只重新分配每次 `dx`，不改变整圈 yaw 总像素量。
- 俯仰默认使用 1080p 基准 ±30px、每圈 2 个正弦周期，并通过 `scale_distance()` 做分辨率缩放。
- 完整扫描未命中时，累计俯仰位移回到起始值；中途命中时立即返回并保持当前视角，避免再次把目标转出画面。
- `delay` 与 `between_delay` 都按检测倍数均分，保持整圈鼠标移动等待预算和额外等待预算与旧实现一致；检测调用自身的耗时不包含在这两项等待预算内。

## 测试

- 为 `TestDailyBattleToEnd` harness 提供 1080p 的俯仰距离桩，并为新增轨迹测试补齐 `_executor.method` 的分辨率属性，修复读取 `BattleTask.width` 时的 CI 报错。
- 新增单测验证：检测次数翻倍、水平总 dx 不变、完整正弦扫描后累计 dy 归零、1080p ±30px 俯仰幅度命中、鼠标移动等待预算与额外等待预算均不变。
- 保留既有“首次检测命中立即停止旋转”覆盖。
- 本地执行 `uv run --locked python -X utf8 -m unittest tests.TestDailyBattleToEnd -v`，9 个测试全部通过；`git diff --check` 通过。
- 新增轨迹单测使用 1080p 距离桩，不声称覆盖其它分辨率的缩放；完整测试结果以 PR CI 为准。

body:
Tom: "yes", to a prediction horizon for the trick-shot game. The predictions were committed before each run (ff319e1 and 7f95a49 for run 8, 37d0867 for run 9).

**Run 8: how many levels of aim one contact costs**
- Derived: a contact turns an aim error by A = s/(2r·cos φ), where s is the run to the contact and φ the cut. For a full hit, A = 2^L − 1, where L is how many levels the pair started from contact (h + v read from the striking ball's start). This corrects the log₂(2d/r) I gave in conversation.
- P19 and P20 killed: only 92 of 180 contacts were within 15%, and 19 of 60 chains within 0.3 levels. P21 (linear) not killed.
- After the run, the cause: the engine found contact at a fixed tick, with the balls already overlapping by up to 0.077 (2r = 0.9). That made thin cuts cos²φ less sensitive than the geometry, and up to a few degrees off at full power.

**Run 9: contact made exact, in the situated way**
- Each ball works out, in its own units, how long ago the pair's reading was exactly h + v = 1. It uses the other's direction, the pair's readings and the told motion. It responds along the line of centres at that moment, then corrects its place by its change of motion times that time. Cushions are handled the same way.
- P22, P23 and P24 not killed: all 180 contacts and all 60 chains match the prediction to rounding, and every contact sits on h + v = 1 to 2e-16.
- Measured:
  - On an open table, a contact costs 1.5–2 levels of aim, so a 0.1° aim error passes half a pocket by the third contact.
  - Inside a rack, errors shrink: balls struck from a few hundredths away have A ≪ 1.

**The game (`play-trick.html`)**
- Contact is exact (run 9).
- New "see" control, default 3 deep: each ball's motion is shown only while it is at most k contacts from the white. Past that the path stops with a "?", and the readout counts the contacts past sight.
- The row of four shows the horizon: its pot is 4 contacts deep, so it is hidden at "see: 3" and appears at 4.
- Fixed a load-order race in the test hook (the screen mapping is now set up at load).

**Also**
- `plans/pol-plan.md`: runs 8 and 9 (predictions, output, readings).
- `plans/pol/pol8.mjs`, `pol8-posthoc.mjs`, `pol9.mjs` and their outputs.
- `CLAUDE.md` and the demos card updated.
- Smoke step 11 checks exact contact and the horizon.

body:
The baseline of #270's step 3: measure how often the current tree lands on a state other than the two known 1.20.6 ones, so the experiment branches have something to compare against.

The detector: `4.png` and `5.png` accepted, and the rare cold rounding dropped on this branch, so any capture that matches neither accepted state is a flip.

- `4.png` is pass 1's cold state.
- `5.png` is the state every pass after the first lands on, deterministically. This file was `6.png`; the first attempt deleted the old `5.png` and the validator rejected the resulting non-contiguous directory, so the warm state was renumbered down instead.
- The cold rounding is not accepted, and a capture that lands on it is a flip.

What the baseline showed, across three repeats dispatches (runs 38091484679, 38101900182, 38103096566) and the branch's pull request runs:

- Five valid pass 1 samples, two of them flips, both the same 22 pixels at the crop's top-right corner. The rate is commoner than #263's one in six, and the flip is a piece of the crop's 452-pixel cold-warm difference rather than a state of its own.
- `a1.1.2_01-ornithe` crashed in the first dispatch's pass 12, which is #275, fixed by the grug-rs pin bump (PR #279); its later passes and dispatches are clean.
- The other three loaders never flipped in any pass.

The experiment branches (the wall's size, the remesh, the view distance, the time of day, the assets) and the step 4 experiments are recorded on #270, with the step 5 verdict that keeps this detector as the accepted workaround.

author: fiftybengt
body:
## Problem
The need list named every unfilled formation need up front, even while almost every spot was still open to anyone, e.g. `need: rsham, hpal, rog, sham, all`. The line was long and confusing early in forming.

## Need list (`Comp.NeedString`)
Classes from the formation list are only named once they're all that's left:
- roles are counted with their reserved needs included (`6 heal`, not `rsham, 5 heal`);
- a role's count becomes its need names (`rsham`, `2x hpal`) only when every open spot of that role is reserved;
- when every open spot in the raid is reserved, exactly the remaining needs are listed. That's also the only time needs fitting several roles (e.g. "any shaman") are named;
- `all` / `N dps` still bundle roles shown as counts.

Over a raid: `Need: all` → `Need: 6 heal, 17 dps` → `Need: rsham, 17 dps` → `Need: rsham, rog`.

Who gets accepted is unchanged: `Comp.CanAccept` still reserves spots for formation needs, and refusal whispers still give the reason. The /raid "still need" message and refusal whispers use the same shorter list.

## Announcement styles (`Comp.BuildAnnouncement`, Setup tab)
New "Announcement style" dropdown next to the preview (profile `lfmStyle`, `lfmIcon`):
- **Clean dashes** (default): `LFM TOC25N 18/25 - GS 5.3k+ - Need: 2 heal, 5 dps - B+O+P RES - fast run - /w spec + GS`
- **Raid icons**: `{skull} LFM TOC25N 18/25 {skull} Need: … {skull} …`, with the icon chosen in a second dropdown
- **Brackets**: `[TOC25N] LFM 18/25 - [Need: 2 heal, 5 dps] - GS 5.3k+ - B+O+P RES, fast run - /w spec + GS`
- **Need first**: `TOC25N needs 2 heal, 5 dps (18/25) - GS 5.3k+ - …` (`needs ALL` early on)

The ending is now `/w spec + GS`. The 255-char limit still shortens the need list first and keeps the free text and ending.

## Testing
Offline suites with Lua 5.1.5 against stubbed WoW APIs (test files live outside the repo):
- Logic tests: 409 passed. New cases cover each phase of the need list, partly reserved roles, `2x` labels, "any shaman" only at the end, every style with and without optional parts, and the 255-char limit per style
- End-to-end simulation: 237 passed, including the chosen style reaching the posted line
- GearScore parity with GearScoreLite: 5000 gear sets, 0 mismatches
- Mutation checks: naming needs early again fails 4 tests; ignoring the style setting fails 5

Not yet verified in the live 3.3.5a client (raid icons rendering in Trade/LFG, dropdown layout in Setup).

author: frederikgeth
body:
Replaces the September–October timing-campaign apparatus for exact IVR with a lightweight benchmark, a measured cost model, named profiles and two performance fixes. Details: `docs/src/ivr_findings.md` and `docs/src/ivr_benchmarking.md`.

## Findings
- **Ipopt time ≈ number of KKT factorizations × MUMPS factor size** (log-linear fit, R² = 0.994). Function evaluation is 3–5% of Ipopt's time.
- **Per-voltage-zone coordinates (`transformer_scaling=:nominal`) decide performance.** On their own they give 0.43× time, because Ipopt drops from about two factorizations per iteration to about one. Composed rows and ground scaling add nothing.
- **`mumps_pivtol=1e-3` removes most of the penalty of poor scaling.** It gives 0.50× on its own, which confirms the mechanism is conditioning rather than model size.
- **Eliminations and lifting are second-order.** With scaling fixed they save 15–25% on the French MV/LV feeders. Without scaling they often slow Ipopt and fail at 1,000–1,600 buses. Broad observation lifting was the slowest option under both solvers.
- **MadNLP was about 3.5× faster than Ipopt on the French feeders, but not at 22k buses.**
- **External baseline:** BMOPFTools was faster than the old FormulationLab default. The scaled model is 1.35–3.4× faster than BMOPFTools.

## Changes
- **`examples/ivrbench/`:** run, analysis and BMOPFTools baseline scripts, plus gzipped raw results and generated reports. Runs use near-default Ipopt and MadNLP, a duplicate arm to measure the noise floor, performance profiles that count failures, and the cost-model fit.
- **`IVRNLP(profile=:scaled | :fast | :reference)` and `ivr_ipopt_options()`, with tests.**
  - `:scaled` is the recommended default. On the 22k-bus network it solved in 8.0 s against 26.8 s for the old control under default Ipopt.
  - `:fast` adds the safe reductions. It was 13% faster on the French feeders but 2.1× slower at 22k buses.
  - `IVRNLPOptions` defaults are unchanged.
- **Performance fixes:**
  - The per-solve network digest now hashes bytes instead of a String: about 570 s → milliseconds per solve at 22k buses.
  - Per-bus voltage-map loops no longer recompute the neutral map, which had made builds quadratic: a 22k-bus reduced build went from about 15 minutes to 79 s.
- **Docs:** new findings and methods pages; the selection guide now opens with the recommendation; the performance page is marked superseded; the 63 campaign pages move to an archive section of the navigation.

## Verification and limits
- The full test suite passes (244,591 tests).
- The docs build reports one error: the HTML size limit on `tutorial_exact_ivr.md`. That page is not modified in this PR; whether `main` already fails the same way has not been checked.
- **Evidence limits:**
  - All but one timed network are French MV/LV feeders, and the 22k-bus case ran once per cell.
  - SAPN networks are refused by the compiler (bus field `grounding_assumption`).
  - No licensed HSL or GPU solver was tested.
  - Many 1.5× and 2.0× load instances are infeasible for every arm.

author: achrafreyani
body:
### What

ProsperoRadio (PPSA99001) stops at start-up on the missing `libSceOpusCeltDec.prx` module. It's listed under "No PR found" in @babyhuey's catalog table in #1578 (runs on `main` 197ffac9 / cf8b129e, `libSceOpusCeltDec.prx` module: ProsperoRadio). The title imports six functions from it: `sceOpusCeltDecInitialize`, `Terminate`, `GetSize`, `CreateEx`, `Decode` and `Destroy` (`VMOyIG83Jtg`, `pkri5OAPsJk`, `xUp4-mftj5I`, `z6eJnrUEaVY`, `6fxZHeuNhIA`, `Sn-MpfGTN9w`).

[ProsperoRadio opens this decoder](https://github.com/blackbearreloaded/ProsperoRadio/blob/2c4029c3a8f43e9e1dfef98374d94d99b14d745d/src/radio_service.cpp#L2072-L2080) only as a fallback, when `sceOpusDecDecode` returns a retryable error for a CELT packet. AnyPS5's libSceOpusDec (FFmpeg) decodes CELT packets and throws instead of returning that error, so the fallback isn't reached here.

The module is therefore added without an implementation, like `sceSaveDataCancel` in ec2bb21e: each function throws `<name> not implemented` if called. The signatures are libSceOpusDec's, from [ProsperoRadio's `opus_decoder.cpp`](https://github.com/blackbearreloaded/ProsperoRadio/blob/2c4029c3a8f43e9e1dfef98374d94d99b14d745d/src/opus_decoder.cpp). The sysmodule table already maps `0x80000044` to `libSceOpusCeltDec`. TechnicalDebt records the six functions under unknown function info.

### How the module is reached

No registration is needed beyond the new directory: `core/libs/CMakeLists.txt` globs `core/libs/prx/` and adds each subdirectory, so `libSceOpusCeltDec/CMakeLists.txt` is enough to build `libSceOpusCeltDec.prx`. The sysmodule loader's `kModuleTable` (`libSceSysmodule/ModuleTable.hpp`) already maps `0x80000044` to `libSceOpusCeltDec`, and the title's own modules are found by scanning `sce_module/`.

### Tested

Windows 11, WinLibs GCC 15.2.0 r7, Release, `-DBUILD_TESTING=ON`, on `main` 2b831510:
- `guest_opus_celt_dec` checks that each of the six reports `not implemented` and passes 3/3. A function that returned instead would fail it.
- `libSceOpusCeltDec.prx` (patched) exports exactly the six NIDs above.
- ProsperoRadio 01.000.010 (catalog sha256 checked; `eboot.bin` and `sce_module/libc.prx` unwrapped), relinked with `--registry` and checked with `tools/import_audit.py` against these libraries: the six `libSceOpusCeltDec` imports move from absent to stub, and no module is missing. I did not run the title.
  - The remaining absent imports are `_umtx_op`, `pthread_set_name_np`, `getcontext`/`setcontext`/`makecontext`, `realpath`, `memrchr`, `getprogname`, `malloc_usable_size` and some math functions.
  - Most of the libc ones are covered at run time by the bundled `libc.prx` shim (#2652), so the next stop is likely in libkernel.
- `ctest -E "^agc_|video_out"` passes 395/395. `check_conventions.py`, `check_test_registration.py` and `pr_overlap.py --branch` pass.

### Checklist
- [x] Based on current `main`; no other open PR implements the same functions
- [x] One topic per PR; follow-ups go in a new PR
- [x] No comments in code except [technical debt](https://github.com/boykopovar/AnyPS5/blob/main/docs/dev/CONVENTIONS.md)
- [x] Unimplemented paths throw (`NotImplemented_nid_no_patch`); silent stubs are listed in [TechnicalDebt](https://github.com/boykopovar/AnyPS5/blob/main/docs/dev/TechnicalDebt.md#silent-stubs)
- [x] No notes, investigation `.md` files or images added to the repository (attach them to this PR)

author: burnouttrader
body:
A `WeightPools` registry owns no clock. Each client charges the pool's fixed, aligned venue windows at the instant its own `Config::clock` reports, so clients of one registry given different clocks charge different windows of one pool. In production every client uses wall time and the windows agree; the mismatch can only arise from injected clocks.

This documents the requirement instead of adding a clock to the registry:

- `WeightPools` docs state that clients drawn from one registry must be given one clock (the same `Arc<dyn Clock>`, or wall time for all).
- Every `Config::clock` doc (Spot, Spot SBE streams, Spot FIX, USDⓈ-M, COIN-M, Options, SAPI wallet/convert, Margin, Margin WebSocket API) carries the same requirement.
- The README Budgets section states it.
- `margin_clients_of_one_key_share_its_native_order_windows` built a separate `ManualClock` for each client of one registry; it now gives every client one shared clock. The other shared-registry contract tests already shared one clock.

No behaviour changes, so no new test: a test of this text would only restate documentation.

Validation: every command in CONTRIBUTING.md passes locally (codegen check, CI unit tests, fmt, SPDX, clippy `-D warnings`, `cargo test --all-targets`, doctests, rustdoc `-D warnings`, `cargo package`, `cargo deny`, `cargo audit`, markdownlint, gitleaks).

author: telagomidia
body:
Closes #27.

## Diagnóstico
Cadastro interrompia antes da gravação quando signup não retornava sessão. Não havia retomada autenticada e retry repetia signup. Não foi encontrada anamnese órfã; nenhum registro clínico real foi alterado.

## Correção
Login explícito após confirmação ou para acesso existente; respostas mantidas no formulário, validação reutilizada do portal, PAR-Q sem respostas presumidas e revisão obrigatória. Sessão isolada, getUser + e-mail + perfil ativo de aluno. UUID estável, upsert confirmado com id/student_id e submitted_at; bloqueio de duplicação na mesma página e orientação para editar registro existente no portal. Tratamento de falhas e aviso antes de fechar página com envio pendente. Sem armazenar dados clínicos em Auth metadata/localStorage e sem reduzir RLS/confirmação de e-mail.

## Validação
223 testes Node e DOM de portal/painel/cadastro passaram localmente. QA SQL real em transação com ROLLBACK confirmou leitura pelo professor, isolamento entre alunos, reenvio sem duplicação e bloqueio de perfil inativo. CI inclui testes Chromium do fluxo em quatro larguras, além da regressão de layout e backup.

## Limite de recuperação
Respostas que não chegaram ao servidor não podem ser vinculadas por SQL. O aluno deve reenviar a anamnese pela conta existente. Instruções e plano em docs/onboarding-anamnesis-fix.md.

## Revisão visual
Direção LG atual preservada; alterações limitadas aos controles necessários ao fluxo. Sem novo hero, grade, paleta ou reestruturação do painel.

ImageSharp 4 looks for `sixlabors.lic` only **below each project's folder** (`**/sixlabors.lic` from `src/DipsyPaint.Engine/`), so a git-ignored key at the repo root was never found and Release builds still failed.

- `Directory.Build.props` sets `SixLaborsLicenseFile` to the root file when it exists and nothing else is configured. The `SixLaborsLicenseKey` environment variable, used by CI, still takes precedence.
- CLAUDE.md and ADR-0020 now say where the file goes.

Verified locally with the maintainer's key: `dotnet test -c Release` passes (186 engine + 56 shell tests). The key file is git-ignored and not part of this PR.

`ATC Test Suite` passed both `cargo-tests` and `npm-tests`, then failed in `evidence` because `actions/checkout` checked out the pull-request merge ref in detached HEAD state and the job attempted `git push`.

- Generate the test evidence bundle only after both test jobs succeed.
- Bind the artifact to `github.sha` and `github.run_id`, require exactly one `bound_commit` field, and upload the evidence YAML as a 90-day workflow artifact.

author: petri-koistinen-refineid
body:
Step 5 of the remote-card state simplification (bugs 4 and 9).

- The card-not-ready warning was hard-wired off, so a card that never got an identity showed "Reading the card…" forever. ActivationWatch now starts a 10 s SettleDeadline when a card is present without an identity and warns after it; the warning needs a card in the reader (the phone path has its own timeout and Retry).
- ActivationWatch (and its TKTokenWatcher) was rebuilt on every StatusView init via a @State default; there is now one shared watch.
- LoginIdentityModel's software card reinsertion (attemptRecovery/cancelRecovery/touchPresentCard) had no callers and is removed with its state.

agy review (Gemini 3.8 Flash and 3.1 Pro), checked against the code — all rejected:
- Actor isolation / lazy-init races: ActivationWatch is @MainActor.
- Timer not cancelled when the identity publishes: reconcile() moves the state to idle on .ready, which clears the deadline.
- No warning for a phone without a reader card: intended.
- Singleton coupling in the view: the chosen design for this migration.
- Missing positive warning test: covered by "reader card not ready" in IdentityLineTests.

`Scripts/test.sh pr` passes; SettleDeadlineTests 3/3, IdentityLineTests and VirtualIDCardMacOSTests pass (12 tests in 3 suites).

author: jlobue10
body:
Two remaining IME queue defects affect normal text entry and reconnects:

- `commitText` schedules text on a Handler, but `deleteSurroundingText` sends backspace immediately. A commit/delete/replacement sequence can therefore delete before the committed text reaches the host. Deletions during a multi-chunk paste also overtake its remaining chunks, and the requested following-character deletion (`afterLength`) is ignored.
- The separate commit-text Handler is not cancelled by stream teardown. Its retained Game/NvConnection keeps sending the remaining paste after disconnect; JNI input addresses the process-wide native session, so delayed work can reach a later stream.

Text chunks and deletions now share one ordered main-thread queue. Both backward and forward deletions are honored. Disconnect and onDestroy cancel callbacks, clear queued payloads, and permanently close this activity's IME queue; late callbacks cannot revive it.

Also pins common-C `f698f68cd4cc0e00beb1e861a2ee60f13c48f1de` from https://github.com/jlobue10/moonlight-common-c/pull/21, which preserves mouse movement ordering around clicks, keys, and scrolling. Merge common-C #21 before this PR.

Validation:
- Extended `tools/regression/test_commit_text_queue.py` runs the actual queue, enqueue, deletion and stopConnection methods with a fake main-thread Handler/native input sink: 11 checks, 6 failures before, zero after.
- Covers IME ordering before the first flush and mid-paste, forward deletion, disconnect cancellation, subsequent native-session input, late callbacks, and existing chunk/Unicode-boundary cases.
- All 25 portable Android regression scripts passed; JNI/HDR fixtures rerun with the newly pinned common-C source. Common-C's full ASan/UBSan suite passed separately.

Baseline `f406538a08fe44f4250d301d0b1daca033a06a81`; no open Android PRs at audit start. Physical Android/IME and live streaming tests were not available locally; PR CI performs the Android build.

author: d-martian
body:
The rebuilder named its hash list and its key after the machine (`SHA256SUMS.rebuilt-nova`, `rebuilders/nova.pub`). A signature should say who vouches for the bytes, and a machine isn't an identity.

## What
- **Lists are named for a person and an architecture:** `SHA256SUMS.rebuilt-<name>-<arch>`. The name comes from `--as`, defaulting to the repo's git `user.name`, never the hostname. The same person can co-sign amd64 and arm64 from two machines without one list overwriting the other.
- **Signed with that person's PGP key** from `rebuilders/<name>.asc`. The maintainer's is a link to `dMartian.pub`, the key that already signs the project. The script picks whichever of those keys has its secret half in the local gpg. Signing goes through gpg-agent, so it works without a terminal. Before, minisign failed with `get_password()` when the script ran without one.
- **The separate minisign key is removed.** rc6's existing co-signature still verifies against `rebuilders/nova.pub` at the `v0.2.0-rc6` tag.
- **The script runs on aarch64,** where it rebuilds the arm64 `kind-minerd` .deb, the one file only an arm64 machine can make. It downloads with `curl` when `gh` isn't installed, so a Nodo needs only podman, git and curl.
- **`--sign-file FILE`** signs (and with `--upload`, uploads) a list made on another machine. The Nodo rebuilds; the key never has to be copied to it.
- **A rebuild that differs is no longer signed.** Before, it was signed and then only the upload was refused.
- **REPRODUCIBLE.md** documents the per-architecture flow and how to verify a co-signature. It also says nothing enforces co-signatures yet.

## Tested
- **Signing:** `--sign-file` with a throwaway key in a temporary GnuPG home; the signature verifies with `gpg --verify`.
- **Refusals:** a list named for someone else, a name ending in `-arm64`, and a name with spaces.
- **Full suite:** passes.
- **Not yet run:** the aarch64 rebuild on a real arm64 machine. It uses the same recipes as CI's arm64 .deb job.

author: alexisbeaulieu97
body:
Before: S32 checks that the store sets `gc.pruneExpire` at repo scope, but no test shows what the key protects.

After: two scenarios under the hostile HOME, where the global config sets `gc.pruneExpire=now`. In each, a prefetched handle reads a tree, another process deletes the ref it read, gc runs, and the read still succeeds.

- **Fetched objects:** they live in promisor packs. Every git the store supports keeps those on repack, whatever `gc.pruneExpire` says (measured on 2.43 and 2.55). This case is a guard against a future git that prunes them.
- **A commit made in the store** (a worktree's commits are made this way): it sits outside any promisor pack, and the key decides it today. With the repo-scope key the read succeeds. With only the global setting, the read fails.

How: the tests are in `test_hostile_home.py`. The comment on the policy key now reads like `gc.auto`'s: it is git's default, restated so that a global value cannot switch it off.

## Drift review

- Docs, skills and READMEs: n/a. No repo doc names `gc.pruneExpire`; the design's S32 and §12 text is updated outside the repo.
- Changelog: none, a test and a code comment
- Duplicated helpers: reuses `_store`, `git` (which gains an `input=` parameter) and `all_refs`
- Repo rules: checked
- Issues: follow-up to #572

author: lsm
body:
A send card claimed queued until its message was seen landing, but a landing can scroll out of an adapter's window. 9a92c410 landed on Oct 8, outside the 4 MB tail of a 98 MB Codex rollout.

- `planNeoDriverSettlement`: once a card's landing is still unconfirmed 24 h after it was sent (`isNeoCardUnconfirmed`), its live status is the session's own instead of queued. A later confirmed landing takes over as before.
- `NeoWorkDriverReceipt.unconfirmed: true` is derived (queued work, no started_at, live status not queued), so the UI can say "not confirmed it got this". There's no new column, cache or scan.
- The card's work status doesn't change; only its live display does.

Closes #6300

author: courthive
body:
Merges **before** #675(courthive-components), whose first CI run exposed this bug; #675 is then re-run (CA, 2026-10-11).

## The bug

When the free-score approach opens, it schedules `setTimeout(…, 100)` (`freeScoreApproach.ts:686`), and that timer still fires after its dialog has closed. It then runs the **closed** dialog's `handleScoreChange`. That handler finds Submit by the page-wide id `submitScoreV2`, which is by then the **next** dialog's button, and disables it from the closed dialog's stale, empty state.

In TMX, an operator who closes one score dialog and opens another within about 100 ms gets a Submit that does nothing.

## How it was found

#675 is the first CI run to execute play functions. In it, `reasonCodeRoundTrip`'s "A full round trip through the dialog" sometimes submitted nothing: it failed once, then passed on a rerun. Logging in the dialog showed the order of events:

| | passing run | failing run |
|---|---|---|
| earlier story's free-score dialog (RETIRED) opens, then is closed | t=3023 | t=2990 |
| this story's dialog opens | t=3053 | t=3030 |
| Submit clicked | t=3123, emits | — (button disabled) |
| the CLOSED dialog's late update fires | t=3130 | **t=3099** |

It reproduced in 2 of 12 local runs under parallel load.

## The fix

Each dialog records that it has closed (in its `cModal` `onClose`) and ignores outcome updates after that. The deferred Clear restyle checks the same flag. `onClose` callers are unaffected: theirs is still called.

## Tests

`__tests__/closedDialogLateUpdate.test.ts` reproduces the bug with fake timers. Dialog A (free score) opens and closes, then the operator declares a walkover in dialog B. When A's late timer fires, B's Submit must stay enabled and must submit.
- **Fails without the fix** (B's Submit is disabled).
- **Passes with it.**
- **Without dialog A,** the same flow passes, which isolates the cause.

I also wrote a Clear-side test, but it passed with or without the fix (B's own deferred restyle runs later and overwrites A's), so it was dropped rather than kept as a vacuous test.

Gates pass under the linked and the published (7.9.0) factory: lint, check-types, build, and test at 155 files / 2885 tests (2884 + 1).

The existing `scoringModal.ts` imports are reordered longest-first, with the type import in its own section. That's the only other change.

author: skvorikovcode
body:
## What and why

In the model picker (the chip next to the composer), the selected row's text was pushed to the right of the dot, and the other rows lost their padding and got divider lines.

Cause: a CSS class collision. The picker and the model price table in Settings both used `.mp-row`, `.mp-group` and `.mp-empty`. Stylesheets are global, so the table's three-column grid, borders and negative margins were applied to the picker rows too: the dot landed in the wide first column and the text in the second.

- The picker's classes are renamed to their own `mpk-` prefix (`ModelPicker.tsx`, `providers.css`, and the three `composer.css` selectors that style the chip).
- Side effect, intended: the prices table no longer inherits the picker's `.mp-group + .mp-group` margin and `.mp-empty` padding.
- New test `css-collisions.test.ts`: fails if two stylesheets define the same bare class (`.a`, `.a:hover`). Modifiers and rules scoped under a parent are ignored. Four classes that are layered on purpose (base in `styles.css`, refinement in the component file) are listed explicitly.
- `vitest.config.ts` gets `css: { include: /.+/ }`, because vitest otherwise returns empty strings for `?raw` CSS imports and the test would pass without checking anything.

## How to check

Reproduced the bug in the demo build before the change (same layout as the report), then confirmed after it: dot, name and check on one line for the current row, equal padding for the rest, and the Settings → Models price table is unchanged. Reverting the fix makes the new test fail and name `.mp-row` and `.mp-empty`. `tsc` clean, 452 tests pass.

## Checklist

- [x] `npm run build` and `npm test` pass
- [x] Test added for the changed behaviour
- [x] No secrets or personal data

author: sjefsharp
body:
# Pull request

## Summary

PR #107 adds an offline, deterministic selector for choosing one approved Project planning context linked to an exact source Issue. Repository-name casing is normalized only for identity comparison; repository IDs, Issue numbers, and Issue node IDs remain part of the exact source identity. The result remains planning-only and untrusted; no live Project integration or execution authority is added.

## Source

- Source issue: Refs [#107](https://github.com/agentic-delivery-lab/agentic-delivery/issues/107).
- Project context: The inventory found no live Project association or approved topology for this selection. Tests use synthetic identities only and make no Project changes.
- Strategic alignment: This implements the Control Plane selection contract while requiring Architecture #11 and ADR-0023 to enter a reviewed immutable Architecture release path, and preserving Architecture #15 as the human topology decision.
- Related work: Control Plane PR #102 provides the single-context normalizer; merged PR #104 provides the offline evaluation router. Issue #108's fixtures remain independent and do not activate this selector.

## Plan

- Implementation plan: Validate a versioned policy and separately supplied SHA-256 pin, bind each candidate to stable repository and Issue identities, collapse identical Project-item observations, choose by explicit policy priority, and fail closed for inaccessible, unapproved, or ambiguous candidates.
- Plan deviations: Because no approved topology release exists, this PR introduces no real Project identity or policy. The caller must supply a policy digest from a separately validated immutable release; this helper does not authenticate policy approval or enable runtime access.

## Changes

- Add strict policy and result schemas plus an offline selector that reuses the existing Project planning normalizer.
- Reject malformed normalized source-Issue identities before candidate comparison; compare repository full names case-insensitively while retaining the stable repository, Issue, and node IDs.
- Register the versioned selection policy in the domain language and guide; keep fields from unselected Projects separate, collapse identical repeated items, and hold on conflicting observations or multiple items in one Project.
- Preserve planning-only authority, untrusted-data marking, and independent source-Issue authorization when Project reads are unavailable.
- Add synthetic unit tests, harness mappings, traceability metadata, and a changelog entry.

## Verification

- Focused selector tests: 18 passed, 0 failed, including a regression test for case-variant repository names. The domain-language validator passed.
- `pnpm control-plane:boundary`, `pnpm control-plane:check`, `pnpm metadata:check`, `pnpm traceability:check`, `pnpm migration:check`, `pnpm lint:branch`, `pnpm lint:commits`, and changelog validation passed.
- Local `pnpm test`: 567 tests, 534 passed, 0 failed, 33 skipped. The nested worktree lacks split-repository checkouts and private operator/database fixtures required by those skipped cases.
- `pnpm acceptance:check` completed its offline checks; private publication-boundary verification was unavailable because `.github-private` is not adjacent to this nested worktree. Live GitHub verification was not run.
- The release-chain validator reports existing Control Plane/Architecture pin drift tracked by Distribution Issue #2; this PR changes no release pins.

## Evidence

All policy and Project identities used by tests are synthetic. The selector makes no GitHub calls, Project or Issue writes, model calls, or runtime decisions. The expected digest only verifies policy bytes; a separately reviewed immutable release must supply the trusted policy and digest.

## Risk and delivery

- Risk level and impact: Low operational risk; this adds offline selection code, schemas, tests, and documentation without a runtime consumer.
- Security and privacy: No credentials or personal data are used. Candidate content stays untrusted and cannot authorize execution.
- Breaking changes and compatibility: No existing runtime contract changes; the selector is additive and versioned.
- Deployment or migration: Not applicable. Live Project access and runtime adoption remain disabled.
- Rollback: Revert this proposal through a reviewed PR; no production state depends on it.
- Dependencies and follow-up work: Runtime use requires Architecture #11 and ADR-0023 to enter a reviewed immutable Architecture release path, plus Architecture #15's human topology decision and separate Project configuration/access. Distribution Issue #2 tracks unrelated release-pin alignment.

## Review guidance

- Review focus: Verify source identity binding, case-insensitive repository-name comparison, policy digest canonicalization and pin checks, deterministic priority selection, duplicate/ambiguity holds, and the absence of execution authority.
- Suggested review order: selector and schemas; focused tests; selection contract documentation; changelog and harness mapping.
- Out of scope: Choosing or creating Projects, approving a topology, changing permissions, enabling live Project reads, activating a participant, merging, or releasing.

## Author checklist

- [x] The source issue and Project-association gap are recorded above.
- [x] The plan, deviations, verification limits, and skipped tests are stated.
- [x] Tests, schemas, documentation, traceability, and changelog are updated.
- [x] Risk, compatibility, deployment, rollback, and follow-up gates are assessed.
- [x] No live Project, Issue, model, release, or production side effect is introduced.
