author: mr-quin
body:
## Summary
- The providerConfig migration chain is now one plain translation from the v1.5.0 shape. v2 translates each record on its own and validates it against the flat schema, so a bad entry is dropped and the rest survive.
- Removed the v2 and v3 try/catch fallbacks to the default providers, and the v4 and v5 try/catch wrappers. A store whose migration still throws (in practice, a store that is not a list) now goes through `OptionsService.upgrade`'s normal path: it resets to `[]`, and seeding recreates the built-ins for an install that was never seeded.
- Removed `ensureBuiltinProviders`. v1.5.0 never let users delete a built-in: the UI hid the delete action for them, and `deleteFromStorage` and `create` both refused built-ins (checked with `git show v1.5.0:` on `providerConfig/schema.ts`, `service.ts`, `ProviderConfigList.tsx`, `ProvidersPage.tsx`). So every v1.5.0 list already contains them. If a list is malformed or incomplete, it keeps its surviving entries, and the user can add a missing source back.
- v3 is now a plain prefix strip. Its de-duplication only repaired collisions caused by appending bare-id defaults next to `builtin:` ids. v3 and the bare ids landed in the same commit, and stores still at v2 hold only prefixed ids, so no shipped store has such a pair.
- v5 (dropping `impl`/`isBuiltIn`) is now a no-op. Leftover unused fields are harmless, and v1.5.0 stores lose them anyway when v2 parses through the schema. The version number stays because stores already at v5 exist.
- Also dropped: inferring a missing `type` from `impl` (every shipped schema required `type`), the already-flat passthrough (v2 only ever sees version-1 data, which is in the union shape), and defaulting a missing `enabled`.
- Kept: custom DanDanPlay options including auth, the Bilibili `danmakuTypePreference` to `danmakuFormat` rename, the MacCMS legacy config, and stripping a trailing `/api` from DanDanPlay base URLs.

## Test plan
- Verified: lint (biome + lint:specs) pass · type-check pass · `packages/danmaku-anywhere` unit tests 812 passed · e2e `e2e/specs/migration/` + `e2e/specs/providers/` 17 passed (`--workers=1`, under the shared e2e lock)
- Red before green: the new chain test `providerConfig upgrade chain > drops a bad entry and keeps the rest without adding defaults` failed on master. It feeds the real v1.5.0 list with a corrupt Tencent record, and master returned a default `tencent` config appended at the end. The tests for records with no type, no id or an empty name, and the test that a non-list store throws, also failed on master.
- The migration unit tests now assert the exact translation of the real v1.5.0 provider list from the migration e2e fixture (secrets and hosts redacted), run through the service's actual version chain.
- No e2e assertion needed changing. The migration smoke spec's provider-id check already expected exactly the stripped seeded ids.
- [ ] `pnpm --filter danmaku-anywhere exec vitest run src/common/options/providerConfig`
- [ ] `cd packages/danmaku-anywhere && pnpm exec playwright test e2e/specs/migration/ e2e/specs/providers/ --workers=1`

## Notes
- v3 and v4 no longer guard against non-object records. They only see records that v2 has validated. The exception is a nightly store or backup already at v2 or v3 that holds a corrupt record, which the old unvalidated v2 could write in theory. That store would now reset to `[]` instead of skipping the record. I judged this too unlikely to keep guards for.
- With the current restore path (set, then `upgrade()`), a backup whose providerConfig payload is not a list now restores as an empty list instead of the defaults.
- Self-review: a clean subagent did the review, KISS and comment-sweep passes. Its findings are applied: dropped the flat passthrough and the `enabled` default, trimmed comments, and added a missing-`options` test.

author: tannevaled
body:
This repository pins Go **1.27.1** in `ci.yml` — **2** occurrence(s). This moves them to **1.27.2**.

## Why move a pin that is already explicit

Pinning was the right thing: an alias has no version to review. But a pinned fleet cannot move, and a Go patch release is usually a **security** release — the standard library is compiled into every binary, so the toolchain that built it is the toolchain it carries.

Check what this one fixes with `govulncheck ./...` against both versions, rather than taking the release notes' word for whether it reaches this code.

## It moves an exact version, and only that one

`-from 1.27.1` names the version to move. "Anything older" cannot tell a stale pin from a deliberate one, so a job held back on purpose at some other version is not a candidate here and is left exactly as it is.

`go.mod` is **not** raised. The directive is a minimum for consumers; the workflow pin is what builds the artefacts.

Every policy is scored on the same 10 seeds and the per episode returns are committed in verify/data/episode-metrics.csv, so python -m dgno.ablations --paired now writes docs/paired-returns.txt: each policy's return minus backpressure's, paired by episode, with a 95% percentile bootstrap interval.

author: elliyeen
body:
Draft. Stacked on #1 (base is that branch).

## Why
The reference implementation had never been executed: dependency pins did not exist, tests imported the wrong paths, `chain-validator.ts` used an API `@peculiar/x509` does not have, and the vitest config was for a newer major than pinned.

## Security-relevant bugs found and fixed
- **Logout did not revoke sessions.** `validateAndRefreshSession` only looked at the signed cookie. It now requires the server-side store and rejects unknown or revoked sessions.
- **CRL parser was a placeholder returning an empty list**, so any real CRL would report nothing revoked. Now parsed with @peculiar/x509 and signature-verified (Node crypto over the original DER, because the library's own CRL verify does not match the signed encoding).
- **`requireMtls` fell through to IP matching.** It now fails closed. The CIDR check was exact-match only; now real IPv4 CIDR.
- CRL cache: stale-while-revalidate branch was unreachable; cache-miss failure silently returned 'not revoked'. Default is now fail-closed (configurable).
- chain-validator: signature checks were skipped for the last link, CA constraints were not enforced, and a catch block would re-throw. Rewritten.

## Evidence
- `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm test` (60 passed, 5 todo), `pnpm demo` run locally on Node 24 / pnpm 10.
- Cross-check: `openssl verify` agrees with the validator on valid, expired and untrusted-issuer certificates generated by `pnpm certs:generate`.

## Honest notes
- Five tests that only asserted against inline objects were converted to `it.todo`; they need an application layer this reference does not have.
- Not implemented: OCSP, name constraints, policy mapping, AIA chasing, IPv6 CIDR, CRL signature check unless the issuer is supplied.
- `next`, `react`, `better-auth`, `iron-session`, `prisma` were declared but unused and are removed; the reference is a library plus tests, not a running app.
- CI itself is unverified until it runs on GitHub.

Adds **`vimPlugins.vim-dadbod-manager-ui`**,Vimscript plugin that turns a                    
                                                  
 [vim-dadbod-ui](https://github.com/tpope/vim-dadbod-ui) connection into a server → database → table tree, with per-database administration and backup sections on top of the drawer.                 
                                                  
   - upstream: <https://github.com/sergioia-dev/vim-dadbod-manager-ui>                                          
   - version: `0-unstable-2026-10-10` (upstream publishes no tags, so it is pinned to the commit the updater resolved)          
   - license: MIT                                 
                                                  
   Two things are not plain `vim-plugins-updater add` output:                                     
                                                  
   * `overrides.nix` adds `dependencies = [ self.vim-dadbod ]`. vim-dadbod supplies the `db#url#*` helpers and the adapters the plugin drives.                                   
   * `vim-dadbod-ui` is deliberately **not** a dependency. The drawer this plugin extends is vendored in-tree, and upstream states that a separate vim-dadbod-ui "must not be installed next to it" (`README.md` §Requirements,`UPSTREAM.md`). author: chiru-allvest
body:
# AI assist, learning insights and agents

Stacked pull request 9 of 11 (see the note at the end for the base branch).

## What

- **Reply assist**: a suggested answer inside the inbox when a customer writes in; the person presses Send. Handover detection on inbound messages.
- **Agents workspace**: drafts waiting for review (one at a time, keyboard friendly), what was sent, rules and each assistant's kill switch.
- **Insights** (`/agents/insights`): reply, conversion and cost-and-quality views from what the assistants did and how customers answered.
- **Evaluation suite** (`npm run evals`): benign and hostile messages checked against the guardrails, the handover rules and the PII scrub, with the known gaps listed.
- Service-window rule for WhatsApp (24 hours) behind its own flag.

## Why

Assistants are useful only if a person stays in the loop and the team can see whether they help. Every draft is draft-only, passes the guardrails and a judge, and needs per-message approval.

## Flags

Everything defaults off or unset; a flag is on only for the exact value `1`. `NEXT_PUBLIC_*` values are read at build time.

| Name | Default | Effect |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `WA_ASSIST_ENABLED` | off | Suggested replies and handover detection (also needs the `wa_reply` kill switch on) |
| `WA_ASSIST_AUTO` | off | Draft a suggestion when an unanswered thread opens |
| `WA_META_WINDOW` | off | Enforce the 24-hour service window |
| `AGENT_NUDGER_ENABLED` | off | Draft-only nudger job |
| `NEXT_PUBLIC_INSIGHTS` | off | Insights page |
| `AI_PROVIDER`, `AGENT_MODEL` | `anthropic`, default model | Provider switch |
| `EVALS_REAL_PROVIDER` | off | `npm run evals` only: also run the real judge (never in CI) |

## Migrations

`20261210000000_learning_insights_indexes`: three plain indexes (`IF NOT EXISTS`). Additive and safe to drop.

## Screenshots

Synthetic data, every flag on. One set per screen in dark, light and 390 px, kept outside the repository:

Files are `<id>-dark.png`, `<id>-light.png` and `<id>-mobile.png` in `screens/ultimate/`; `screens/ultimate/index.html` is a self-contained gallery with a plain-English caption and the enabling flag for each.

- Agent insights: `insights-default`
- Agent insights: Replies: `insights-replies`
- Agent insights: Conversion: `insights-conversion`
- Agent insights: Cost and quality: `insights-quality`
- Agent drafts: `agents-default`
- Agent drafts: Sent: `agents-sent`
- Agent drafts: Rules: `agents-rules`
- Inbox: `inbox`

## Test evidence

```

prisma generate ok
build ok
```

author: zonuexe
body:
**Depends on #1808 (#1800).** This branch is cut from `keyword-overload-over-positional`, so until #1808 merges this diff also shows #1808's commits, which arrive here by merging its branch (no rebase). The commits for this PR are the ones after `Add changelog fragment for #1800` other than #1808's `Prove a keyword overload only by a yes acceptance…` and the merge of it.

With

```rbs
class S
  def ph: (a: Integer) -> Integer
        | (Hash[Symbol, String]) -> String
end
```

`S.new.ph(*xs, a: "s").upcase` reported `undefined method 'upcase' for Integer` on correct code. The selector saw the splat as one untyped positional, so it ruled out the one-parameter `(Hash)` overload by arity. That overload takes `{ a: "s" }` when `xs` is empty: `def ph2(h) = h; ph2(*[], a: "s")` returns `{ a: "s" }`. No overload was left, and the first-overload fallback answered `Integer`. #1791 fixed this only in the keyword-distribution path.

- `RbsDispatch` passes the splats' indices to the selector (`splats:`). It does so only when the call node's arguments are exactly the argument list, as for `keywords_last`. The return path, the keyword distributions and the block-parameter probe all receive them.
- `OverloadSelector#matches?` reads a splat as any number of untyped elements. `SplatArity.expansions` spells out each count, from none up to what the overload's positional parameters can take, or one past filling them when it declares `*rest`. An overload matches when some count fits its arity and every argument is accepted at the parameter that count binds it to. Past 32 argument lists, an overload matches when every argument other than a splat is accepted by some positional parameter of it, wherever a count would place it: `rest3("s", *xs, *xs, *xs)` against `(Integer, Integer, Integer, *Integer) -> Integer | (String) -> String` is `String`. A call without a splat adds no key to the selector's bundle.
- A splat's element is untyped, so the call was already imprecise. Every overload some count reaches therefore joins, as #521 joins them.
- Without a keyword hash, the block-parameter probe of a splat call binds block parameters only where every overload some count reaches agrees. Before, it took the first gradual match.

Results:

- `ph(*xs, a: "s")` and `ph(*xs, { a: "s" })` are `String`. `ph(a: 1)` and `ph(*xs, a: 1)` stay `Integer`.
- `ph(*xs, **opts, a: "s")` is `Dynamic[Integer | String]` (was `Integer`).
- `two(*xs)` against `(Integer, Integer) -> Integer | (String) -> String` is `Dynamic[Integer | String]` (was `String`).
- `two("x", *xs)` is `String` (was `Integer`, through the fallback).
- `ph(**o, a: v)` from the issue already joins on #1808.

- rigor-activerecord keeps the policy its bundled `Relation#find` documents, counting a splat or a `**` hash as one argument: a new plugin-side answer (`relation_splat_find_return_type`) types a block-less relation-side `find` with a splat by argument count, as the class side's `finder_return_type` already types `Post.find`. Without it, `user.posts.find(*ids)` joined to `Dynamic[Array[Post] | Post]`, on which a following `update` or `save` no longer resolves on the model. `user.posts.find(*ids)` and `where(...).find(*ids)` stay `Post`, while `find(id, *ids)` and `find(*args, **opts)` stay `Array[Post]`. The existing `find(*ids)` pin is unchanged, and a new example pins the other forms.

The internal spec's arity bullet states the rule.

## Known limits

- A splat of a known tuple (`xs = [1, 2]; two(*xs)`) is still read as untyped elements of unknown count. Expanding it statically is a follow-up.
- The `Dynamic` joins follow the #521 policy, so some true positives behind them are lost: `1.5.round(*xs).nope` and `s.blk(*xs) { |v| v.nope }` no longer report.

## Changed existing expectations

- `keyword_overload_selection_spec.rb`, "splits the values behind a splat whose count may reach a positional Hash": `ph(*xs, a: int_or_str)` and `opt_hash(*xs, a: int_or_str)` were `Dynamic[top]` and are now `Integer | String`. Before, the `String` member's list matched no overload, because the splat ruled out the `(Hash)` overload. That list now reaches it, and the answer equals `ph(a: int_or_str)`'s. The block form stays `Dynamic[top]`. The test still checks that the splat call splits the value and reaches the `(Hash)` overload.
- `spec/integration/fixtures/kernel_functions.rb`: `p(*xs)` was `Dynamic[top]` and is now `Dynamic[Array[Dynamic[top]] | Dynamic[top] | nil]`. The fold still declines to the RBS envelope, and the envelope now joins `()`, `[T] (T)` and `(untyped, untyped, *untyped)`. The snapshot is updated.
- `spec/integration/fixtures/method_type_param_binding.rb`: the same `p(*xs)` value, and `Ractor.make_shareable` of it, change the same way. To keep the "no evidence leaves `T` unbound" check, the fixture adds `Marshal.load("")`, a bare `Dynamic[top]`, and `Ractor.make_shareable` of it still answers `Dynamic[top]`. The snapshot is updated.

## Precision

I compared #1808's branch against this branch over 77 stdlib calls with keywords (no type changed) and 70 calls with splats. Every change is a wider or `Dynamic`-joined answer:

- `[1, 2, 3].first(*args)`, `sample`, `min` and `max` change from `Array[1 | 2 | 3]` to `Dynamic[1 | 2 | 3 | Array[1 | 2 | 3]]`. The old answer was wrong for an empty `args`.
- `[1, 2].first(*args, *args)` changes from `1 | 2` to `Dynamic[1 | 2 | Array[1 | 2]]`.
- `[1, 2, 3].fetch(*args)` changes from `1 | 2 | 3` to `Dynamic[1 | 2 | 3 | Dynamic[top]]`. `dig` and `Hash#fetch` change alike.
- `s.gsub(*args)` changes from `Enumerator[String, String]` to `Dynamic[Enumerator[String, String] | String]`.
- `10.5.round(*args)` changes from `Float | Integer` to `Dynamic[Float | Integer]`, and `10.0.floor(*args)` from `Integer | Numeric` to `Dynamic[Integer | Numeric]`.
- `Rational(*args)` changes from `Dynamic[Rational?]` to `Dynamic[Dynamic[top] | Rational | nil]`.
- `[1, 2].zip(*args)` and `product(*args)` gain the tuple arms for zero and two arguments.

These calls kept their types: `JSON.generate`, `CSV.new`, `File.open(*args, mode:)`, `system(*cmd, exception:)`, `Struct.new(*names, keyword_init:)`, `Time.new`, `Integer(s, exception:)`, `format(*args)`, `format(s, *args)`, `File.join(*args)` and `Array#push(*n)`.

Fixes #1801

author: junruxiong
body:
## What and why

Selecting text opens a menu under it, replacing the format menu. Closes #91.

- **Text ›** turns the selected Notes into text, Heading 1/2/3, a bulleted or numbered list, or a quote. Citations stay inside the text (unit-tested through every conversion). It is offered only over Notes of text, not Questions, Answers, code or formulas.
- **Format buttons:** bold, italic, underline, strike, link (a small address field), code, formula (the selected text becomes an inline formula and its LaTeX field opens), highlight, clear formatting. Underline was already a mark of the Mind and already exported to Word and dropped from Markdown (covered by the existing export tests).
- **AI section slot:** `SelectionMenu` takes `ai: SelectionAction[]`; with none, the section is hidden. #93 and the others add their entries there without reworking the menu.
- Keyboard: ⌘/ (Ctrl+/) moves from the text into the menu, arrows go through it, Enter acts, Esc closes the innermost thing (Turn into list, then the menu, back to the text). Esc in the text closes the menu too.
- Each menu action is its own Undo step, so ⌘Z takes back exactly it rather than the typing before it.
- Input methods: the menu waits while composing, no action runs while composing, and it closes after a composition ends over a collapsed cursor. The menu also waits for the mouse button to be let go, so it doesn't chase a dragging selection.

Convention followed: Notion's selection menu (Turn into, format row), as the design boards show.

## How it was tested

- `npm run typecheck`, `npm run lint`, `npm test` pass locally; new `tests/renderer/selectionMenu.test.ts`.
- `e2e/selectionMenu.spec.ts` (new): selects with a sliding mouse and with Shift+arrows, turns a paragraph into a heading and a list, applies bold and underline, checks Undo, Esc order, and an input-method composition. `e2e/notes.spec.ts` ran too: its format-menu test now looks for `selection-menu` and `aria-checked` (the buttons are menu items, not toggle buttons).
- By hand in the built app (temporary data folder), English and Chinese, at 900 and 1280 wide. No AI feature in this change, so no model was used.

## Differences from the design boards (Final-18-Selection-Menu, Final-18-Selection-Font, Selection-Bar)

- No "Aa" font button: fonts per selection are a separate ticket.
- No To-do and Table in Text ›: the schema has no task list yet, and tables come with #92.
- The AI section and "Edit with AI…" field are not drawn: they have no actions until #93 and the others; the slot is ready.
- The "Text ›" row shows what the selection is now (e.g. "Heading 2"), not always "Text", so the row says what it will change.
- Icons are text glyphs (B, I, U, S, </>, ∑, T×, ↗) instead of drawn icons.
- Not in ⌘K: the command list does not exist yet; every action has a keyboard path.
- No link shortcut: ⌘K is reserved for the command list.

## Interaction checklist (UI)

- [x] Gestures follow Notion's selection menu
- [x] Nothing replaces the Mind the User is in
- [x] Reversible actions: ⌘Z undoes each as one step
- [x] Every action works by keyboard; focus is visible; Esc closes the innermost thing
- [x] Responds within 100 ms (menu opens 50 ms after a keyboard selection)
- [x] Words in English and Simplified Chinese
- [x] Layout holds at a narrow and a wide window
- [x] Adds nothing to first run or onboarding
- [x] Tested like a person in the built app, with the mouse and the keyboard
- [ ] ⌘K entries: no command list exists yet

Screenshots (after, EN and ZH, 900 and 1280 wide) are saved locally; the PR has no before shots.

author: zepocas
body:
## Summary

A JPEG export now carries the design, as the PNG does (D45). Dropping it back reopens the design at its exported size.

```text
export (worker)
  canvas.convertToBlob → jpeg
  embedJpegDesign(jpeg, envelope)       # XMP APP1, after the JFIF header, via Blob.slice
drop (App)
  readExportedDesign(file)
    readPngDesign(file) ?? readJpegDesign(file)
      readJpegInfo: walk segments to the image data → size + cromatica:design
```

```diff
 src/export/
+├── jpeg.ts           # splice and read the XMP segment
+├── design-image.ts   # readExportedDesign: PNG, then JPEG
 ├── export.worker.ts  # jpegSink embeds the design
```

The envelope is 0.6 to 2 KB over 3000 shuffled designs, about 30 times under one segment's 64 KB. A design that would not fit is exported without it. Details in D72.

## Evidence

- **Before:** a dropped JPEG fell through to palette from image (`readPngDesign` returned null).
  **After:** the e2e drop test passes for both formats, through Chrome's real JPEG encoder.

```text
✓ an exported PNG dropped back reopens its design at its size
✓ an exported JPEG dropped back reopens its design at its size
```

- 323 unit tests pass (new `tests/unit/jpeg.test.ts`), plus `npm run check`, ESLint and Prettier.
- A real export (3840×2160, 424 KB) has JFIF first, then a 1.3 KB XMP segment, and macOS `sips` decodes it.
- **Not checked:** which services and editors keep the segment. Anything that re-encodes strips it.

## Merge Danger

**Door:** two-way.

JPEGs exported after the merge carry the extra segment, and those files stay as they are if the PR is reverted. Reverting makes the app ignore the segment; the files stay valid.

**Blast Radius:** JPEG export and drop

The splice runs after encoding and leaves the image data untouched. A file that is not a JPEG, or a design too large for one segment, is returned unchanged. PNG export and the drop of other images follow the same path as before.

author: parkertrue
body:
Fixes the approved findings from the 2026-10-10 security audit (SEC-1, 2, 6, 7, 9) and records the accepted ones in `DECISIONS.md`.

## Changes
- **SEC-1: targeted login lockout.** The tight login limit (5 failures/min) is now keyed on account *and* IP, so someone guessing a user's password only locks out their own address. A new per-account cap (100 failures/hour, any address) bounds distributed guessing. Both count only failed logins (`deduct_when` 401), so the owner's successful logins never use up the budget. The 20/min per-IP limit is unchanged.
- **SEC-2: absolute session lifetime.** Login puts an `auth_time` claim in the refresh token, and every rotation copies it forward and sets `exp = auth_time + 30 days` (the Redis TTL matches). A session now ends 30 days after login however often it refreshes; after that, refresh gets the existing 401 `AUTH_TOKEN_EXPIRED`.
- **SEC-6: `Cache-Control: no-store`** on every API response (a Flask `after_request` hook; a route can still set its own).
- **SEC-7: `__Secure-refresh_token`.** The refresh cookie has the `__Secure-` prefix, and `JWT_COOKIE_SECURE` is on in every config (browsers drop a `__Secure-` cookie without it). Browsers treat `http://localhost` as secure, so dev keeps working.
- **SEC-9:** `NotesListQuery` refuses unknown keys (`?befor=` is a 422, not a silent first page).
- **DECISIONS.md:** SEC-4 (composition rules kept), SEC-5 (scrypt cost until real hardware), SEC-8 (unreachable CVEs in the `db`/`redis` images), and the distributed lockout the hourly per-account cap still allows.
- CLAUDE.md and README describe the new limits, the session lifetime, the cookie and `no-store`.

## Deploy note
The cookie rename signs every user out once, since the old `refresh_token_cookie` is no longer read.

## Verification
- Backend unit: 475 passed, 100% line and branch coverage; ruff clean.
- Backend integration: 44 passed.
- Frontend: 345 passed; lint clean.
- E2E: 35/35 on a freshly built test stack, including a new `nginx.spec.js` check that `no-store` survives the proxy.
- Dev check: in Chromium, through Vite's proxy on `http://localhost:5173`, register, login and refresh all work, and the `__Secure-` cookie is stored with `Secure`. Firefox and WebKit are not installed here, so they weren't checked.
- Each new test was mutation-checked (11 mutations, all caught). One mutation that would go unnoticed: dropping `deduct_when` from the hourly cap only (catching it would take 101 successful logins).

A retro RPG-style XP bar under the dashboard's top bar, to bring creators back.

- **Bar:** LV badge, a 24-block Klein-blue bar, the XP count, and what was earned since the last visit (daily visit, streak, score points, on-brand post).

- **Reduced motion:** jumps straight to the end; the label and sound still play.
- **XP model:** `src/lib/xp.ts` holds the XP rules and level curve (250 × level XP per level).

author: aritracodesbad123
body:
Adds model-written probes, a hard probe freeze rule, and a `--baseline` switch for ablations. Schema rev 7 is additive only.

## 1. Model provider and model-written probes

- `poc/model_provider.py`: three providers.
  - **nebius**: Nebius Token Factory (`https://api.tokenfactory.nebius.com/v1`, OpenAI-compatible, structured JSON output via `response_format: json_schema`, temperature 0). Model ids are set with `--claims-model` / `--probe-model`; both default to `nvidia/nemotron-3-super-120b-a12b` (NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Super 120B, REQUIREMENTS section 4a).
  - **recorded**: answers from `evals/fixtures/model_responses/<owner>/<repo>/<pr>.json`, used by tests and CI. Every file there must say it is a TEST FIXTURE, and the provider refuses files that do not.
  - **none**.
- `--model-provider {nebius,recorded,none}`, default `none`. With `none`, or with `nebius` and no key, the run falls back to fixed probes only, and the record (`model_provider.note`) and the report say so.
- **Key handling.** `NEBIUS_API_KEY` is read by the orchestrator process only. The untrusted-process allowlist does not contain it, and its secret-name check refuses it. New tests check this in a real sandbox: a hostile build backend and a probe started while the key is set in the orchestrator cannot see it, and the key never appears in a request body or an error message.
- `poc/model_probes.py`, in order:
  1. Claims are read from the PR text. Each claim must quote the title or description exactly, otherwise it is rejected.
  2. Probe code is written from the claims plus base-side code only.
  3. The code is validated: at most 20,000 characters, it must parse, it must not define `PROBE`, and its claim ids must be known.
  4. The validated code is written as a normal probe file and frozen.
- **Model code is untrusted.** It runs only in the side's sandbox, without network, with a 60 s timeout.
- **Output contract** (all probes, `poc/probes.py`):
  - at most 256 kB of stdout and at most 200 observation names;
  - stdout and stderr go to temporary files under a file-size rlimit, so a noisy probe cannot fill the orchestrator's memory;
  - probe timeouts are capped at 300 s.

## 2. Probe freeze rule (`poc/freeze.py`)

- Probes are generated only from the PR title and description and from **base-side** code. Any generation input under a PR-side root is rejected (`FreezeError`).
- Before the first PR-side execution (its install, build or patch), every probe is frozen. Its content sha256, generator, time and the sha256 of its generation inputs are recorded (`probe_plan`, and `freeze` on each probe result). The record also stores `pr_side_started_at`.
- The runner re-checks the freeze before **every** PR-side run. A probe whose content changed, or that was frozen or written after PR-side execution started, is refused (`probes.refused`), is not run, and appears in the report.
- **Generator labels:**
  - `fixed (post-hoc, written after results were known)`: the existing mlxtend #1229 probe now carries `"provenance": "post-hoc"`, which is also the default.
  - `model (<id>, live)`.
  - `model (recorded fixture, not blind)`.
  - `diff (auto-derived from base-side code, model-free)`.
- **Blindness:** only a live `nebius` probe that passed the freeze rule is blind.
  - `evals/pr_metrics.blind_score` refuses records whose verdict a non-blind probe could decide.
  - `score_records` scores those in a separate, labelled NOT BLIND column.
  - The golden mlxtend case now also checks `blind: false`.

## 3. `--baseline {tests,tests+diff,tests+probes,full}`

| Baseline | Decides the verdict |
|---|---|
| `tests` | test comparison only (no probes, coverage gate or claim flagging) |
| `tests+diff` | tests + differential probes (`poc/diff_probes.py`) |
| `tests+probes` | tests + claim probes (fixed and/or model-written) |
| `full` (default) | tests + claim probes + coverage gate + claim flagging; differential probes run and are shown, but do not decide |

- **Differential probes** are a deliberately simple, model-free baseline:
  - they target the module-level public functions whose base-side lines intersect the diff's old-side line ranges;
  - each is called with the same simple inputs on both sides (`1, 0, -1, 2.5, "abc", [1, 2, 3], None`), with `random` and NumPy seeded;
  - results are compared as canonical summaries;
  - they have no claims, so under `tests+diff` any difference needs attention.
- Each record stores its `baseline`, and records without one are treated as `full`.
- **Baseline awareness:**
  - `--rejudge` and the coverage gate respect the baseline.
  - The reviewer report prints the baseline under the title, labels every probe with its generator, and marks informational probes.
  - Evals check that a record's baseline matches its contents; the golden mlxtend case is re-derived under all four baselines (verified, verified, needs_attention, needs_attention).
- `evals/ablation.py` runs (`--run`) or scores (`--records-root`) a labelled PR set under each baseline. It writes a markdown and a JSON table: catch rate, false alarms and could-not-verify rate (blind), plus a separate NOT BLIND column.

## Schema rev 7 (additive)

- **New optional pr_run properties:** `baseline`, `model_provider`, `probe_plan`, `pr_side_started_at`.
- **Probe results:** items gain `generator` and `freeze`; `source` gains `diff`; probes gain `refused`.
- Nothing becomes required, and rev 1-6 records stay valid.

## Checks

ruff, the no-external-side-effects guard (the one inference POST is marked), public hygiene and docs commands all pass. pytest: 338 passed, 4 skipped. New tests in `tests/test_model_probes.py` (25) cover:

- tamper detection, ordering, a rewritten file with the same content, and PR-head generator inputs being rejected;
- a probe that rewrites itself on the main side being stopped before the PR side;
- provider fallback and the structured-output request;
- fixture labelling, claim grounding and code validation;
- output caps, differential probes, verdicts per baseline, blind scoring and the ablation table.

`tests/test_sandbox.py` adds the `NEBIUS_API_KEY` check in a real sandbox. Strict golden evals: 28 pass, 3 skip, APPROVE.

## Follow-up

- **Live model runs need the key.** With `NEBIUS_API_KEY` set, `--model-provider nebius` is ready, but no live model call has been made yet. The model ids should be confirmed with `GET /v1/models`.
- **Blind metrics need live runs.** Until live probes exist, every probe-decided verdict is NOT BLIND, so the blind columns of the ablation reflect test-only and claim-flag verdicts.

## Follow-up commits

- `evals/ablation.py`: rates are computed only over labelled cases that have a record; unlabelled records are counted separately.
- Source-pair installs: files under `src/<package>/` count as package code, and PEP 735 `[dependency-groups]` named test/tests/testing are installed (option-like strings are dropped).
- Test runs: if pytest-xdist stops with "Different tests were collected", that run is repeated without workers instead of being counted as flaky.
- Decision log: `docs/decisions/2026-10-11-model-probes-freeze-baseline.md`.

## Smoke checks (recorded provider, sandboxed)

| PR | Baseline | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| rasbt/mlxtend#1229 | tests | verified |
| rasbt/mlxtend#1229 | tests+diff | verified |
| rasbt/mlxtend#1229 | tests+probes | needs_attention |
| rasbt/mlxtend#1229 | full | needs_attention |
| marshmallow-code/marshmallow#3026 | tests | needs_attention |
| marshmallow-code/marshmallow#3026 | full | needs_attention |

All probe-decided verdicts above are NOT BLIND (post-hoc fixed probes or recorded fixtures).

Known follow-up: test ids built from the current time (e.g. `datetime.now()` in a parametrize) change between runs and are reported as flaky.

author: sergiogd112
body:
Stacked on #66. Scripts and a receipt only; no model data or figures are committed (provider redistribution terms are unclear).

- `scripts/waccmx/extract_regional_daily.py` (+ SGE wrapper):
  - one stored year per task, with each member's CRC re-checked;
  - daily forcing series, 126-level profiles, and fixed-geopotential-height
    values interpolated per hour and cell;
  - stored for the central column and the 25-cell mean.
- `scripts/waccmx/co2_lag_analysis.py` (+ SGE wrapper):
  - tracer age against the prescribed surface `co2vmr`, using deseasonalized
    monthly means that never bridge the 2022 gap;
  - block-bootstrap intervals;
  - depletion ratios above 80 km;
  - solar-adjusted CO₂ growth by height.

  It recovers known lags exactly on synthetic data.
- Receipt `docs/research/waccm-x-co2-transport-lag-2026-10-11.md`:
  - **Run structure:** the archive holds 3 runs (bases 1949/1973/1997); run 3's
    2023–24 output is a continuation of the same run.
  - **Restart artifacts:** each run starts with physically impossible negative
    ages from its scaled year-2000 initial CO₂, and needs 6–8+ years to settle.
    Run 1 never fully does.
  - **Equilibrated ages (runs 2 and 3):** ~1.1 / 3.0 / 3.0–3.3 / 4.1 years at
    20 / 40 / 60 / 70 km.
  - **Cooling region:** 100–140 km CO₂ grows at ~55–75% of the surface rate
    after a solar adjustment. The raw trends are aliased by the solar cycle.
- `scripts/waccmx/co2_transport_tigramite.py` + receipt `docs/research/waccm-x-co2-transport-tigramite-2026-10-11.md`:
  - **Method:** tigramite ParCorr lag profiles (0–96 months, identical samples)
    with 1,000-surrogate calibrated significance, plus PCMCI+ and a synthetic
    recovery check.
  - **Result:** no lag is significant once autocorrelation and the lag search
    are accounted for. 20 km (~1 year) and 40 km (~3.3 years) peak where the
    tracer ages predict. The apparent ~5.7-year thermospheric lag is solar
    aliasing and vanishes when F10.7 is removed.
  - **Conclusion:** tigramite can't time CO₂'s arrival in the thermosphere with
    this data. The tracer-age estimate (~4–5 years, via the upper mesosphere)
    stands.

body:
## Summary

There was no way to manage an instance short of writing SQL, and a closed instance (`SIGNUP_MODE=closed`) had no way to get accounts at all. `bun run admin` covers that until there is an admin page.

## Commands

```
bun run admin users                                   # accounts, active keys, last request
bun run admin users add <email> [--name N] [--password P]
bun run admin users verify <email>
bun run admin users delete <email> --yes
bun run admin keys <email>
bun run admin keys revoke <key-id>
bun run admin usage [--days 30] [--csv]
```

- `users add` creates an account with a confirmed email and a credential password, hashed with Better Auth's own `hashPassword`, so it signs in like any other account. Without `--password`, a random password is printed once.
- `users delete` and `keys revoke` clear the gateway's Redis key cache, so keys stop working at once. Deleting requires `--yes`.
- `usage` reports requests, decisions, branches and input tokens per account and model, as a table or CSV. This is also a first usage export.

The CLI is a new workspace, `apps/cli` (Bun): `commands.ts` holds the logic and `main.ts` parses arguments and prints output.

## Testing

- `bun run typecheck` (5 packages)
- `bun run test`: cli 5 (new), gateway 16, shared 7. The cli tests cover:
  - account creation with a password that verifies;
  - refusals for a taken address, a short password and a bad address;
  - confirming an account;
  - revoking a key and clearing its cache;
  - the usage report;
  - deleting an account with cascade and cache cleanup.
- Manual check: an account created with `bun run admin users add` signs in to the dashboard with the printed password.

author: nweddle
body:
## Summary

Follow-up to #948, addressing [CodeRabbit's review comment](https://github.com/tronbyt/server/pull/948#discussion_r4239040033).

When `EnsureRepo` finds a URL or branch mismatch, it deleted the working clone *before* cloning the new source. If that clone failed, for example because of a mistyped `#branch` suffix, a deleted branch or a network error, no repository was left, and apps installed from it stopped working until the URL was fixed.

The validation block now re-clones through the existing [`recloneRepo`](https://github.com/tronbyt/server/blob/3ec20f9be755e71af7dd28b005b4e20676e5a01d/internal/gitutils/git.go#L345-L368), which clones into a temporary directory and swaps it in only on success. A failed switch returns the error and keeps the previous clone. This applies to URL changes as well, which had the same delete-first behaviour before #948.

It also closes the remaining gap inside `recloneRepo` ([CodeRabbit's second comment](https://github.com/tronbyt/server/pull/949#discussion_r4239419613)): the old clone was deleted before the new one was renamed into place. The swap now lives in `replaceRepoDir`, which moves the old clone aside, restores it if the rename fails, and deletes it only after success.
